item:99-year-old-port.text: 99-Year-Old Port. The 99-Year-Old Port is an exceptionally rare bottle of vintage liquor shipped from Booty Bay as a personal gift for Gazlowe. After a cargo accident on the Ratchet docks, it was snatched away by a lunatic named Mad Magglish, who fled into the twisting tunnels outside the Wailing Caverns. Transporting precious freight across the Great Sea always carries risks, but Crane Operator Bigglefuzz made things far worse during a routine morning unloading in Ratchet. Attempting to clear an overwhelming shipment from Booty Bay, the goblin overloaded his crane and brought a mountain of crates crashing down onto the docks. In the chaos, the town eccentric—a troublesome figure known as Mad Magglish—snatched an extraordinarily aged bottle of 99-Year-Old Port and bolted into the hills toward the Wailing Caverns.

item:a-bloodstained-journal-page.text: A Bloodstained Journal Page. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has a torn, bloodstained journal page examined during the investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle. A few words remain legible, and she asks Clerk Daltry to compare the handwriting with the Town Registry. Commander Althea Ebonlocke watches over Darkshire and asks that the handwriting on a torn, bloodstained page be examined. Though thick blood covers it, a few words remain legible for Clerk Daltry to compare with the Town Registry.

item:a-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text:
A Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, A Clue to Sanders' Treasure leads seekers farther along Captain Sanders' trail. It marks the second step in a hunt across the bluffs and coastlines. After following Captain Sanders' first treasure map, you find a parchment pointing farther inland into Westfall. Its scrawled note sends you east from the coast and up the bluffs toward the main road.

Near crumbling stone ruins and an abandoned chimney, an old barrel marks where Sanders hid the next clue. The trail leads deeper into the troubled farmlands.

item:a-dusty-unsent-letter.text: A Dusty Unsent Letter. In Westfall, a dusty letter sheds light on Stalvan Mistmantle’s past in Moonbrook. The unsent parchment was found in an old footlocker and confirms that he lived there before his disappearance. Investigators searching for Stalvan Mistmantle’s past find an unsent letter in an old footlocker in Moonbrook. Darkshire’s town registry still gives his last address as the Moonbrook Schoolhouse, and Clerk Daltry wants to know whether he truly lived there. The letter confirms that Stalvan resided in the Westfall township for a time. Finding it disturbs a vengeful Forlorn Spirit, which guards the remnants of Stalvan’s past with bitter malice.

item:a-faded-journal-page.text: A Faded Journal Page. In eastern Elwynn, an old page points toward Stalvan Mistmantle's grim history. The Faded Journal Page lay for years in an old trunk at Marshal Haggard's home near Elwynn Forest's eastern border. Haggard had retired there, but his failing eyesight kept him from reading the weathered parchment. The page stayed neglected until investigators seeking the truth about Stalvan Mistmantle retrieved it.

item:a-letter-to-grelin-whitebeard.text: A Letter to Grelin Whitebeard. A letter from Ironforge reaches Grelin Whitebeard at his camp in Coldridge Valley. Its news and instructions bring the mountain capital close to the snowy frontier. Grelin Whitebeard receives a dispatch from Ironforge at his camp in Coldridge Valley. Anvilmar offers shelter, but the valley lies far from its safety. Letters link scouts and scholars in the field with the halls of the mountain capital. This one has come south along the mountain paths to reach him.

item:a-mysterious-message.text: A Mysterious Message. In Westfall, a courier's intercepted message gives the People's Militia proof of who directs the Defias Brotherhood.

item:a-simple-compass.text: A Simple Compass. At the burned Alexston Farmstead in Westfall, A Simple Compass lies in a small chest. It belonged to Baros Alexston before he became Stormwind's City Architect. Baros Alexston grew up working his family's farm in Westfall. His first instrument for finding his way was a simple compass. It may have kindled his interest in geometry, drafting, and exploration. Then the Defias Brotherhood raided and burned the farmstead, leaving the compass in a sturdy chest among the ruins as bandits overran the farmland. Baros's father escaped the destruction, but could not carry the family's possessions to safety. Inside Stormwind City's stone walls, the compass has little use to a master builder. Yet it means much to Baros. Its return would restore a rare, intact link to his humble beginnings and the peaceful countryside of his childhood.

item:a-stack-of-letters.text:
A Stack of Letters. In Coldridge Valley, a stack of letters has come through the mountain pass for scouts in the snowy wilderness. Letters for Coldridge Valley come from Anvilmar by way of travelers crossing the pass. The road to the remote camps in Dun Morogh's mountains is hard, so postal runners rely on travelers to carry each bundle onward. This one is bound for scouts deeper in Coldridge Valley.

Until the letters are sorted, Talin Keeneye at his lakeside camp is thought to be the only recipient. Among them is a missive for Grelin Whitebeard, a mountaineer.

item:a-torn-journal-page.text: A Torn Journal Page. In Stormwind, A Torn Journal Page links an old crate to Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Its worn script points toward records kept in Elwynn Forest. A Torn Journal Page lies in a sealed storage crate beside Stormwind City's canals. Old books, family heirlooms, and a ceramic vase surround the worn fragment among forgotten personal effects. Its distinct handwriting points to Stalvan Mistmantle's past, though the page is damaged and hard to read. Who in the kingdom might recognize the hand that wrote it?

item:abercrombie-s-crate.text: Abercrombie's Crate. Near the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, Abercrombie's Crate lies abandoned after ogres drove off its owner. The crate holds delicate tools and gathered herbs belonging to the eccentric hermit. Abercrombie left his shack in western Duskwood to gather vegetation. Far from home, he met a hostile band of ogres and fled for his life, leaving behind his crate of instruments and harvested plants. The ogres carried it to the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, where the heavy chest rests near the cave mouth.

item:admiral-proudmoore-s-orders.text: Admiral Proudmoore's Orders. Kul Tiras forces keep their coastal positions in Durotar, and Admiral Proudmoore's Orders lay out their plans. The documents were written before Daelin Proudmoore fell at Theramore and describe a campaign against the Horde. Admiral Proudmoore's Orders show that the Kul Tiras forces at Tiragarde Keep still mean to fight. Lieutenant Benedict's garrison holds the papers, which detail long-term maneuvers and fortifications against the Horde. The plans show that Daelin Proudmoore's offensive in Durotar was an organized campaign, built to continue after his death. For the Horde, the documents reveal Kul Tiras operations and possible reinforcements threatening its borders.

item:ados-fragment.text: Ados Fragment. At Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, Ados Fragment lies among three lost pieces of the Goaz Stone. Together, the four shards make an ancient relic carved with Titan inscriptions. The Ados Fragment is one of four pieces Prospector Whelgar needs to restore the Goaz Stone at Whelgar's Excavation. Before raptors overran the dig site, Whelgar began translating the main tablet and found its inscriptions broke off at crucial moments. The four pieces, named Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru, were lost across the ruins in ancient containers and dirt mounds, among prowling beasts.

item:agamand-family-axe.text: Agamand Family Axe. In northern Tirisfal, the Agamand Family Axe remains among the family's ancestral arms. Once a symbol of the wealthy mill owners, it is now sought by Coleman Farthing to strip the undead Agamands of their remaining dignity. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty owned land across Tirisfal Glades' northern hills and kept vast mills and a family crypt. The Agamand Family Axe rested with the ancestral arms, beside the buried patriarchs and warriors. The Scourge overran the estate and slaughtered its inhabitants, but the weapons remained on racks underground. The Scourge raised the fallen Agamands as mindless thralls to the Lich King. Their former servant Coleman Farthing survived in undeath, bitter toward his old masters. Farthing blames the family for his own death and sends Forsaken wanderers into the crypt to take the axe, sword, mace, and dagger from the racks. He wants the last traces of the Agamand heritage erased.

item:agamand-family-dagger.text: Agamand Family Dagger. In northern Tirisfal, the Agamand Family Dagger rests among the weapons in the family crypt. Coleman Farthing seeks it and the family’s other arms to strip his former masters of their legacy and honor. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held vast estates and grain mills in the rolling meadows of northern Tirisfal Glades. The Scourge destroyed their power, but their weapons endured in the family crypt north of Agamand Mills. Restless undead members of the household and mindless servants of the Lich King guard the dagger. It recalls the martial heritage and standing the family once held above its servants and tenants. Coleman Farthing resides at Brill, but he once died in the Agamands’ service. He blames the family for his death, and the dagger means resentment to him, not noble lineage. Farthing sends adventurers into the Agamand Family Crypt for the dagger, sword, axe, and mace. By taking these arms from the tomb, he seeks to rob the Scourge patriarchs of their last dignity and extinguish the Agamand name.

item:agamand-family-mace.text: Agamand Family Mace. At Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Mace remains locked in the family crypt. Once a proud heirloom of northern Lordaeron, it is now sought by their former servant, Coleman Farthing. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held vast farmlands and windmills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Like the region’s other aristocrats, they fell to the plague of undeath. The Scourge raised them as mindless thralls in service to the Lich King, and they wander their ruined estate. Their ancient treasures remain locked in the family crypt. Among them rests the Agamand Family Mace, a remnant of a lineage reduced to shambling undead.

item:agamand-family-sword.text: Agamand Family Sword. In northern Tirisfal, the Agamand Family Sword remains in the family crypt. The tarnished blade once marked the wealth and standing of the mill-owning dynasty, and Coleman Farthing now seeks it to erase their legacy. The Agamands once held great wealth and influence through their mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, the family met a gruesome end, and their bodies rose as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Their ancestral weapons, including the ceremonial sword, were sealed inside the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern edge of the mills. Taking these blades from their burial racks is an act meant to break the memory and noble standing of the fallen household.

item:ahanu-s-leather-goods.text: Ahanu's Leather Goods. Ahanu's Leather Goods carries Thunder Bluff's leatherwork to the Crossroads. Ahanu sends finished leather armor and supplies to the Barrens for travelers there. Ahanu prepares leather goods for trade beyond Mulgore. In Thunder Bluff, the leatherworker turns raw hides into finished apparel and gear for Jahan Hawkwing, a merchant at the Crossroads in the Barrens. The plains make overland travel slow, so the tauren send the parcel by air. Tal and Devrak's trained wind riders carry goods swiftly across long distances.

item:alaric-s-remains.text: Alaric's Remains. Alaric's bones lie in a shallow grave in Silverpine Forest, far from Fenris Isle. His spirit asks travelers to carry them past the Rot Hide gnolls and directly into Fenris Keep. Alaric's bones were unearthed from a shallow grave in Silverpine Forest. He was once a resident of Fenris Isle, and his spirit longs for the place he cherished in life. He asks whoever finds his bones to leave his ill-fitting boots behind and carry his remains directly into Fenris Keep, far from the scavengers prowling the mainland.

item:alien-egg.text: Alien Egg. The Alien Egg is an unusual and mysterious clutch found guarded by local wind serpents across the canyons of Thousand Needles. Despite its unfamiliar appearance, the native serpents protect the egg fiercely as if it were their own. Its presence has aroused the curiosity and concern of the tauren scouts stationed atop Freewind Post. Discovered resting at the base of the towering spires south and northeast of Freewind Post, the Alien Egg stands out dramatically from the typical fauna of the canyon floor. Rather than abandoning or destroying the odd clutch, the native serpents of the needles fiercely guard it alongside their own nests. Hagar Lightninghoof, a tauren brave keeping watch from the heights of Freewind Post, sought to retrieve the specimen to determine whether it represented a threat to the mesa settlements or merely an unusual variation of local reptilian life.

item:alterac-granite.text: Alterac Granite. Near Darrow Hill in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Alterac Granite draws master stonecutters with its resilience and grain. King Magni Bronzebeard’s royal mason insists on the stone for a tribute to fallen soldiers. King Magni Bronzebeard ordered a monument to Sully Balloo, a brave dwarven defender who died in the tragedy at the Thandol Span. Grand Mason Marblesten was charged with sculpting it in Ironforge. He insisted on Alterac Granite instead of ordinary quarry stone. Few stones in the Eastern Kingdoms are finer, and its durability keeps a fallen hero’s likeness and memory untarnished for generations. Alterac Granite lies around Darrow Hill in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, near the ruined territories of Alterac. Hostile wildlife, syndicate brigands and lingering strife make the journey perilous. To bring unblemished slabs to Ironforge’s artisans, you must venture deep into contested lands.

item:altered-snapjaw-shell.text: Altered Snapjaw Shell. At the Lushwater and Stagnant Oases, snapjaws bear altered shells that draw a druid’s attention. Their carapaces may reveal what the fissures beneath the Barrens are doing to local wildlife. Oasis snapjaws have changed in ways that trouble those who study the land. The freshwater turtles of Lushwater and Stagnant Oases are believed to drink from springs fed by mysterious underground fissures. Their altered carapaces have caught the attention of researchers at the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem, a tauren druid, gathers the shells as he seeks to understand the land’s health. He wants to learn whether energies rising from deep below are an unnatural blight or something stranger.

item:ambercorn.text: Ambercorn. Across Mulgore, Ambercorn falls beneath the ancient trees. Tauren gather it for the Water of the Seers, a brew used in the Rite of Vision. Ambercorn falls beneath Mulgore's great trees, where tauren gather it from the grass. To the tauren, these nuts carry the land's spiritual vitality and latent magic. Tauren mystics have understood and used that power for generations. Young hunters and wanderers learn to watch the ground beneath the canopy and honor the Earth Mother's gifts. In Bloodhoof Village, seer Zarlman Two-Moons prepares young tauren for the Rite of Vision with ambercorn. He combines it with stones gathered from the plains' water wells to make the Water of the Seers. Initiates drink the ceremonial brew before the ancestral flames. Their senses shift, revealing a guiding spirit animal meant to lead them to their next destination.

item:amethyst-phial.text: Amethyst Phial. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Amethyst Phial to travelers in Dolanaar. They carry it to the Oracle Glade to gather water from the moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Amethyst Phial to travelers on Teldrassil. It is the final vessel used in the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage. They carry it to the far northwest of the boughs, to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the ancient canopy of the Oracle Tree lies the island’s first and most potent moonwell. The phial is dipped into its radiant waters to gather the essence of Elune’s grace. Druids and priestesses study and tend to the World Tree’s unpredictable growth with that water.

item:an-undelivered-letter.text: An Undelivered Letter. Long-forgotten mail lies in Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn, carrying a critical clue to Stalvan Mistmantle's past. Years ago, a storm sent a traveling courier to the Lion's Pride Inn for shelter. Near midnight, the frightened messenger fled downstairs in his sleeping clothes and vanished into the pouring rain, never to return. On the second floor, he left a chest of belongings, including a letter from Stalvan Mistmantle addressed to an estate in Stormwind City's Canal District.

item:anaya-s-pendant.text: Anaya's Pendant. Across Ameth'Aran, Anaya's Pendant remains with the restless ghost of Anaya Dawnrunner. Cerellean Whiteclaw carries grief for the love he lost when the Sundering shattered their world. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the ancient kaldorei city of Ameth'Aran fell into ruin. Cerellean Whiteclaw believed his beloved Anaya had perished, and carried his grief into a long sleep beside Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage. After waking, he wandered Darkshore and found Anaya's tormented apparition still drifting through Ameth'Aran, bearing the pendant. Cerellean cannot raise a hand against her himself, so he asks travelers to free her spirit and recover the heirloom.

item:ancient-moonstone-seal.text: Ancient Moonstone Seal. The Ancient Moonstone Seal holds Asterion captive in the ruins of Bashal'Aran. Forged by the Highborne long before the Sundering, it binds his spirit with arcane magic. The Ancient Moonstone Seal binds Asterion's soul to the pillars of Bashal'Aran. His former master, the Highborne sorcerer Athrikus Narassin, forged it as an unbreakable anchor while the Well of Eternity still stood and Queen Azshara reigned. More than ten millennia later, Asterion remains a spirit bound by its magic. No strength or spell he commands can break the ward.

item:ancient-statuette.text: Ancient Statuette. Along Ashenvale's northwestern shore, Talen seeks the Ancient Statuette he recovered from Zoram's sunken ruins. The night elf effigy came from a city lost beneath the waves. The sunken ruins of Zoram lie off northwestern Ashenvale. The pre-Sundering night elven city was lost beneath the waves ten thousand years ago. Recently, the explorer Talen surveyed the ruins from a small craft, searching for historical relics. Naga attacked and drove him ashore. In his flight, he left most of his belongings behind, including the ancient statuette he had dredged up. It lies on the tideline sand near his scuttled skiff. Talen calls the statuette his most prized possession and the reason he braved the monster-infested coast. He believes the effigy can help decipher Zoram's architecture, history, and arcane secrets, all hidden beneath the surf of Zoram Strand.

item:andron-s-ledger.text: Andron's Ledger. In the Undercity, Andron Gant's ledger draws the Deathstalkers' attention. They seek it as an operative gathers information for the Forsaken.

item:another-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Another Clue to Sanders' Treasure. In Westfall, a scrap of Captain Sanders' parchment points toward his next hidden marker. Captain Sanders hid his stolen riches across Westfall, leaving riddles and buried markers instead of one map that could be seized. This scrap carries the trail onward from the previous hiding place. It says to turn north and seek a discarded jug beside a lonely windmill above the sea cliffs.

item:arikara-serpent-skin.text: Arikara Serpent Skin. At Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arikara is summoned and slain, leaving a scaled hide behind. Carried to Whitereach Post, the skin proves the wind serpent was defeated. Arikara is a formidable wind serpent tied to ancient tauren legend. Rumor says she seeks retribution against Cairne Bloodhoof as tauren ways change. Under Elder Magatha Grimtotem's direction, champions prepare enchanted Incendia Powder. They light the sacred fire atop Darkcloud Pinnacle's burial bluffs, drawing the spirit-beast into the physical realm. Stripping Arikara's hide leaves the Arikara Serpent Skin, proof of her death.

item:arnak-s-hoof.text: Arnak's Hoof. Arnak's Hoof is the macabre proof of death taken from the criminal Arnak Grimtotem. Hunted down on the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arnak was marked for execution by the defenders of Freewind Post after murdering a fellow tauren and kidnapping his sister. Arnak Grimtotem earned notoriety throughout Thousand Needles as an outlaw whose brutality crossed even the contentious lines of tauren clan politics. After murdering another tauren and abducting the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong, a formal bounty was posted for his death. Arnak holed up on the heights of Darkcloud Pinnacle, surrounded by Grimtotem guards. Slaying him and claiming his severed hoof serves as undeniable confirmation for Cliffwatcher Longhorn at Freewind Post that the murderer has finally answered for his crimes.

item:astor-s-letter-of-introduction.text: Astor's Letter of Introduction. Astor Hadren carries a letter between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. Deathstalkers use it to pose as the courier and investigate Andron Gant, a shopkeeper suspected of leaking Forsaken intelligence. Astor Hadren carries messages between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. His letter of introduction gives its bearer credentials with illicit contacts in the city. Mennet Carkad, a Deathstalker handler, needs to investigate suspicious leaks in the Undercity, and Astor's travels make him a target. An operative can eliminate Astor and take his papers, then assume his identity and intercept the covert messages meant for him.

item:ataeric-s-staff.text: Ataeric's Staff. At the Sepulcher, Ataeric's Staff marks the archmage's defeat. Archmage Ataeric, a senior Dalaran wizard in Silverpine Forest, wielded it to command local ley lines. Shadow Priest Allister feared Dalaran's growing reach in magic and ordered Ataeric killed. He also demanded the staff. Once Ataeric was slain and the staff recovered, the concentrated ley energies sank back into dormancy. Carrying the staff to the Sepulcher marked a clear victory over Dalaran's ambitions. Yet power still lies latent in the earth, and the Forsaken remain watchful.

item:athrikus-narassin-s-head.text: Athrikus Narassin's Head. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Athrikus Narassin's Head proves the ancient warlock's death. The coven's demonic activity in northern Darkshore has been disrupted.

item:bag-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Bag of Empty Ooze Containers. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle supplies empty jars for his study of Azeroth’s oozes. He means them to hold clean slime gathered in the wild. Laris Geardawdle studies the strange biology of Azeroth’s oozes. He found that they quickly take on the corruption around them, including Felwood’s tainted residues. So he commissioned sturdy jars that can hold acidic specimens without harming them. The bag carries enough jars to gather clean slime in wild regions, especially Un’Goro Crater, where ancient glutinous oozes live free of demonic taint.

item:balnir-snapdragons.text: Balnir Snapdragons. At Balnir Farmstead, vibrant snapdragons grow where the Scourge's corruption presses toward Tirisfal Glades. The Forsaken study their sensitivity to magic to watch for that corruption's spread. Balnir Snapdragons still bloom in the garden of Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. The homestead lies in ruin after the fall of Lordaeron and the rise of the Scourge. The Plaguelands border Tirisfal to the east, and the garden sits where the Lich King's blight presses against the region. Its flowers give the Forsaken a place to watch for the spread of that corruption. Balnir Snapdragons are unusually sensitive to atmospheric magic, making them living barometers for magical blights. Anastasia Hartwell and the Forsaken mages in the Undercity seek fresh flowers from the farmstead's window boxes. They send the plants to the Royal Apothecary Society for study, hoping to measure how far the Lich King's plague has seeped across the border into Tirisfal's soil.

item:baron-longshore-s-head.text: Baron Longshore's Head. Along the Merchant Coast, Baron Longshore's Head proves the pirate captain's death. Gazlowe posted a public bounty for Longshore's identifiable remains to protect Ratchet's commercial shipping. Baron Longshore led Southsea Freebooter raids from camps along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. His flagship, the Heedless, threatened goblin trade lanes between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Gazlowe, Ratchet's Chief Engineer, offered a bounty for identifiable proof of Longshore's death. The port authority pays a monetary reward when the pirate's head is delivered.

item:barrel-of-barleybrew-scalder.text: Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder. At Kharanos, Marleth Barleybrew sends a cask of Scalder toward the Thunderbrew Distillery. He means to prove his brewing can rival the Thunderbrews, his chief competitors. The Thunderbrews and Barleybrews contend fiercely over brewing in Dun Morogh. The Thunderbrews are renowned for their busy distillery in Kharanos. Marleth Barleybrew will not live in their shadow. So he brews fiery Scalder to show his recipes can rival theirs. He hopes those who taste it will see the Thunderbrews do not own the art of fine dwarven drink.

item:barrel-of-shimmer-stout.text: Barrel of Shimmer Stout. In Dun Morogh, a barrel of Shimmer Stout is bound for the mountain watch. Rejold Barleybrew sends his experimental ale to the high passes, where drinkers say it brightens their vision. Rejold Barleybrew made Shimmer Stout from ingredients gathered across Dun Morogh. The recipe is the newest work of the Barleybrew family. Its dwarven brewers vie to make ales hearty enough for the mountain cold. Rejold brewed this stout to warm the gut and sharpen the senses of those posted in the wind. The barrel is bound for Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew at the southern tower on the pass into Loch Modan. Mountaineers there endure cold and long watches between skirmishes with troggs and wildlife. A cask of family ale brings a taste of home. Its kick can leave a tired sentry feeling able to see clearly in the dark.

item:barrel-of-thunder-ale.text: Barrel of Thunder Ale. In Kharanos, the Thunderbrew Distillery has lost a barrel of Thunder Ale. Marleth's Barleybrew Scalder was meant to take its place, turning a brewing feud into foul play. The Thunderbrews of Kharanos and the Barleybrews of Brewnall Village are bitter rivals. Marleth Barleybrew tried to slip a barrel of his Barleybrew Scalder into the Thunderbrews' cellar. He hoped their patrons would choose his brew. The Thunder Ale barrel was seized in the exchange, proof that the switch succeeded despite the local guards.

item:barrow-key.text: Barrow Key. Deep beneath Stonetalon Peak, the Barrow Key lies locked in the Talon Den. It is one of three druidic keys guarding the ancient treasures sealed within the den's hoard. Night elf druids placed wards throughout the Talon Den's underground barrows to protect their relics from intruders. The Barrow Key is hidden in a cache among the passages, one part of that layered defense. The cache opens only with the Gatekeeper's Key, so a seeker must know the druids' defenses to reach it.

item:bartleby-s-mug.text: Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Burlguard asks a young warrior to win Bartleby's Mug from its stubborn keeper. Bartleby surrenders it only after a tavern fight leaves him beaten. Bartleby clings to his beloved mug until a fight leaves him beaten. Even then, he drains every last drop before handing it over. The mug proves the warrior could force an uncooperative opponent to yield.

item:bathran-s-hair.text: Bathran's Hair. Among the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in northwestern Ashenvale, Bathran's Hair remains a rare herb. Night elf healers value its power against afflictions of the flesh and spirit. Bathran's Hair grows among the ancient ruins north of Maestra's Post, where night elf healers have long valued it. Common herbs soothe wounds of the body, but Bathran's Hair is said to restore the spirit as well. When a young night elf in Astranaar falls gravely ill, herbalist Orendil Broadleaf seeks the rare plant to prepare a remedy.

item:battleboar-flank.text: Battleboar Flank. In Mulgore, young hunters gather Battleboar Flanks from beasts threatening tauren hunting grounds. The meat feeds the tribe's youth. Bristleback quilboar train battleboars in Brambleblade Ravine to enter tauren hunting grounds. Their attacks threaten the young tauren at Camp Narache. Grull Hawkwind sends novice hunters to take the flanks and snouts from the beasts they kill. The flank meat is cooked into stew for the tribe's youth, feeding them with what the quilboar sent against their people.

item:battleboar-snout.text: Battleboar Snout. Young tauren hunters gather Battleboar Snouts near Red Cloud Mesa as the Bristleback press into their hunting grounds. The snouts also go into stews for the young in Camp Narache. Bristleback quilboar train battleboars in Brambleblade Ravine, in the shadow of Red Cloud Mesa, to probe tauren hunting grounds. Grull Hawkwind sends young braves to push back against the encroachment. A snout proves that a battleboar has been brought down. The tauren use the snouts with cuts of flank in rich stews for their young.

item:battleworn-axe.text: Battleworn Axe. In Redridge, Battleworn Axe blades mark the Blackrock orcs invading the mountains. Marshal Marris accepts the recovered weapons in Lakeshire as proof of the threat to its people. Blackrock reavers carry these heavy, nicked axes as they push south from the Burning Steppes into Redridge. Marshal Marris and Lakeshire's hard-pressed town watch collect the blades to confirm another marauding orc has fallen and to show how well armed the advancing warband is. Blackrock invaders have fortified Stonewatch Keep and taken footholds in southeastern Redridge, trapping townspeople in Lakeshire. Taking their battleworn weapons reduces the arms available to the warband and clears roads for Alliance travel.

item:berard-s-journal.text: Berard's Journal. In Pyrewood Village, Berard's Journal holds research the Royal Apothecary Society needs. Berard studied an ancient plague that wiped out the aquatic life of Lake Lordamere. Before Arugal's shadow magic spread across Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard was one of the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising minds. From Pyrewood Village, he studied an ancient blight that had wiped out all aquatic life in Lake Lordamere centuries earlier. When Arugal's curse gripped the settlement, Berard lost his mind and became a thrall. His detailed field notes remained on a bookshelf in his quarters at the Pyrewood Village Inn.

item:bernice-s-necklace.text: Bernice's Necklace. At Stonefield Farm in Elwynn Forest, Bernice keeps her late husband's necklace close. Auntie Bernice Stonefield keeps her husband's necklace at Stonefield Farm. He was a veteran of Stormwind's military campaigns and carried the charm into battle for good fortune. Bernice says tragedy came only in his final campaign. That was the one expedition when he forgot to bring it. Since his death, the keepsake has remained among her most cherished possessions.

item:besseleth-s-fang.text: Besseleth's Fang. In Sishir Canyon, Besseleth's Fang marks the end of a deadly spider's threat. Besseleth and her brood make Sishir Canyon dangerous for travelers. At night, the giant spider turns the Webwinder Path into a death trap for those crossing the gorge. Her fang measures nearly two feet and drips with potent venom. Local defenders have suffered her venomous strikes, and presenting the fang brings them relief.

item:bethor-s-scroll.text: Bethor's Scroll. Bethor Iceshard writes counter-incantations to help Apothecary Renferrel brew a protective draught against Thule Ravenclaw's dark sorcery. The scroll holds the key to facing the Scourge necromancy guarding Fenris Isle.

item:bingles-blastencapper.text: Bingles' Blastencapper. Troggs hold Bingles' Blastencapper after his gyrocopter fell into the Loch. Without it, Bingles' plans to aid Gnomeregan's liberation are in danger. Bingles Blastenheimer built the Blastencapper to strike from the air at the troggs and leper gnomes who overran Gnomeregan. Mechanical failure sent his gyrocopter into the Loch, but Bingles survived. Troggs from the northern islands raided the wreckage and carried the volatile weapon to their camps. Bingles needs the Blastencapper to help retake Gnomeregan. The exiled gnomes are preparing to reclaim their radioactive home, and he counts on his gyrocopter and signature munitions for the air assault. In trogg hands, the explosive could accidentally cause a catastrophe in Loch Modan. Recovering it would preserve a valuable weapon for the gnomish resistance.

item:bingles-hammer.text: Bingles' Hammer. At his crash site in Loch Modan, Bingles Blastenheimer needs Bingles' Hammer back from the troggs. With his gear restored, he can repair his flying machine and help free Gnomeregan. Troggs raided Bingles Blastenheimer's crash site on the freshwater islands. They took his hammer and high-potency explosives. The hammer is needed to repair the dented airframe and adjust the gyrocopter's mechanical parts. Without his equipment, Bingles cannot fly support runs for the gnome forces fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

item:bingles-screwdriver.text: Bingles' Screwdriver. Across Loch Modan's northern islands, Bingles' Screwdriver lies among the gear lost in a crash. Troggs carried it off with the tools of pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. When Bingles Blastenheimer crashed into Loch Modan, he lost the tools needed to repair his gyrocopter. Troggs on nearby islands carried off his tool buckets, and the screwdriver was packed in one of them. Bingles needs it for fine adjustments as he repairs the craft and handles its armaments. Bingles works to free Gnomeregan from troggs and leper gnomes. He means to join his flying skill with volatile Blastencapper munitions in an aerial assault. The screwdriver, wrench, and hammer will help him rebuild his gyrocopter and keep the airborne counteroffensive alive.

item:bingles-wrench.text:
Bingles' Wrench. In the Loch, Bingles' Wrench is missing with the pilot's other tools. Troggs took it after Bingles Blastenheimer crash-landed his flying machine. Bingles Blastenheimer survived when his gyrocopter crashed into the Loch. Then the troggs raided the crash site on the small northern islands. They took his specialized supplies and scattered his tools among buckets in their camps.

Bingles' Wrench is one of three critical hand tools, alongside his high-yield Blastencapper explosives. Without the wrench, Bingles cannot repair his downed gyrocopter. His planned aerial offensive to aid the exiled gnomes fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan must wait.

item:black-claw-stout.text: Black Claw Stout. Beneath Stormwind, Zardeth of the Black Claw prepares a drink for Lord Wishock. The stout reaches him as an ordinary tavern beverage.

item:black-feather-quill.text: Black Feather Quill. The Black Feather Quill lies in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, needed to wake the Druids of the Talon. The Black Feather Quill is one of four sacred focuses used to wake the Druids of the Talon from hibernation. The others are the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. The rite calls slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Without these items, a druid may remain trapped in the Dream and unable to return to their waking body. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Ban'ethil Barrow Den, putting the chests that held the relics in danger. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar ordered their swift recovery, before the captive druids were lost to the Dream.

item:blackened-skull.text: Blackened Skull. At Agamand Mills, Blackened Skull trophies mark the fight against the Scourge. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill wants them as proof that the Darkeye Bonecasters are being destroyed. Darkeye Bonecasters haunt the Agamand Mills. These skeletal spellcasters turn their necromantic malice against the living and the Forsaken, seeking to secure a forward base for the Lich King's armies in northern Tirisfal. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill asks for their ruined skulls as proof that the Scourge's mystical vanguard is being beaten back.

item:bloodfeather-belt.text: Bloodfeather Belt. In northern Teldrassil, Bloodfeather harpies wear crude leather belts as they crowd the Oracle Glade. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak collects them as proof that the nearby nests have been cleared. Bloodfeather harpies have built aggressive nests in the boughs around the Oracle Glade. Their presence threatens the ancient Oracle Tree and blocks travel through northern Teldrassil. After the flock ambushed and killed a runner carrying reports to Darnassus, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak called on travelers to strike at the nests. The belts taken from fallen harpies show that their numbers are being culled and the paths are being secured, so messages can reach the capital again.

item:bloodfury-ripper-s-remains.text: Bloodfury Ripper's Remains. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder seeks Bloodfury Ripper's Remains as proof that the Bloodfury harpy leader is dead. Her death strikes at the threat to the tauren settlement. Bloodfury Ripper leads the harpies of the Charred Vale with fierce, territorial aggression. They nest among the scorched ruins and threaten travelers and shamans across the Stonetalon Mountains. Culling the flock eases the danger for a time, but Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat knows that lasting relief means removing its leader. Bloodfury Ripper rules almost like a queen, directing the harpies' attacks on their territory. Her remains prove she is dead, leaving the flock in disarray and giving the tauren who seek to heal and secure their rugged lands greater peace of mind.

item:bloodstone-choker.text: Bloodstone Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder’s Bloodstone Choker binds a warlock’s rite to the void. His apprentice stole the talisman and fled to the Defias Brotherhood. Carved from bloodstone, the choker bridges the mortal world and the twisting shadows of the Twisting Nether. In the crypts beneath the tavern, Gakin channels its magic at the summoning circle. A hostile Voidwalker answers from the void. A warlock must face the furious creature in direct combat and subdue it while wielding the talisman. Only then is the will to command such a guardian proved.

item:blueleaf-tuber.text: Blueleaf Tuber. Beneath Razorfen Kraul, Blueleaf Tubers grow hidden from the surface. Their rarity draws wealthy gourmands and traders from across the world. Blueleaf Tubers grow beneath Razorfen Kraul in the Barrens. Dense roots and quilboar briars hide them from casual foragers. Though the ground is harsh, wealthy gourmands and traders across the world pay an exorbitant price for their distinct flavor. In Ratchet, the goblin Mebok Mizzyrix devised a way to find the hidden roots. He trains native snufflenose gophers to scent tubers from fifty paces away. Guided by specialized command sticks, adventurers can unearth them before quilboar patrols catch wind of the intrusion.

item:book-from-sven-s-farm.text: Book from Sven's Farm. In Duskwood, Sven's ruined farm holds a dirt-stained journal with no title. Its fragments record an unknown onlooker's glimpse of the attack on Sven Yorgen's family. A loose mound of dirt among the charred remains of Sven's farm in southern Duskwood hides a weather-damaged journal. Its anonymous writer left frantic, incomplete notes about the tragedy at the homestead. The pages support Sven Yorgen's suspicion that someone watched from the shadows while his family was slain. The account breaks off without explaining who the writer was or what happened next. Sven's clue leads investigators to carry the book to Darkshire, hoping someone there will recognize the handwriting.

item:book-stresses-of-iron.text: Book: Stresses of Iron. In Stormwind Keep, Margulf Blaggon’s book on metallurgy is away at Northshire Abbey for copying. Margulf Blaggon wrote about metallurgy in practice and in theory. Milton Sheaf cared for the volume in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep. The library lent it to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton copied it by hand for his own collection. The work took far longer than expected. So Brother Kristoff waited anxiously in Cathedral Square for the book to return to the city.

item:bottle-of-disease.text: Bottle of Disease. Forsaken alchemists brew disease near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in Ashenvale. The bottles hold virulent concoctions found at their encampment. Near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Forsaken alchemists brew contagions in an outpost beyond the Warsong Outriders' front lines. The bottles give night elves at Forest Song evidence of an offensive aimed at sickening the woodland soil and wildlife instead of meeting their sentinels in open combat.

item:bottle-of-moonshine.text: Bottle of Moonshine. In Darkshire, a bottle of moonshine is sought for Lakeshire’s tavern. Barkeep Daniels needs one while Blackrock orc incursions keep regular supplies from reaching town. Blackrock orcs have cut off Lakeshire’s regular supply caravans. Barkeep Daniels seeks regional drinks to restock the tavern for the guards and townsfolk. One is brewed and sold at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire, where locals favor strong drinks.

item:bottle-of-zombie-juice.text: Bottle of Zombie Juice. In Darkshire, a Bottle of Zombie Juice is bound for Abercrombie, a reclusive hermit in Duskwood. The potent liquor is brewed from rot blossom, and Abercrombie says he needs it to keep warm. Rot blossoms gathered in Duskwood go into this harsh brew. The bartender in Darkshire warns that it is potent enough to raise the dead. Most folk want nothing to do with such a vile drink, but Abercrombie, an eccentric hermit, says it is the only thing that keeps him warm on the damp, cold nights by his lonely shack.

item:bottom-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. Along Darkshore, the Bottom of Gelkak's Key is one of three fragments of a shattered winding key. It belonged to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast, and reef crawlers scavenged it from the shore. Threshadons sank Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore, casting the gnome and his belongings ashore. Among them was the winding key that activated his mechanical first mate. The key broke against the coastal rocks into three pieces, and local scavengers descended on the debris. Reef and tide crawlers seized the bottom fragment as they searched the tideline.

item:branch-of-cenarius.text: Branch of Cenarius. In eastern Ashenvale, Geltharis holds the Branch of Cenarius, sacred to the dryads. Anilia died defending the relic, and her dying wish was to see it recovered. The Branch of Cenarius is sacred to the dryads who follow the Forest Lord. Anilia and her sister Illiyana treasured it until corrupt satyrs ambushed them. Their leader, Geltharis, seized the branch and mortally wounded Anilia near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. As she lay dying, Anilia pointed north toward the arch where Geltharis lurks. She pleaded for a champion to take back the bough and return it to the dryads at Forest Song.

item:brass-collar.text: Brass Collar. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Princess wears the collar Ma Stonefield wants as proof the sow is gone. Princess is the Brackwell family’s huge, prize-winning sow. She roams east of the Maclure homestead, and her hunger often carries her into Stonefield Farm’s crops. After losing valuable vegetables to Princess, Ma Stonefield seeks someone willing to slay her. The collar proves the sow has been put down, so she can no longer raid Stonefield’s fields.

item:bristleback-attack-plans.text: Bristleback Attack Plans. Bristleback Attack Plans warn of a planned siege on Camp Narache. Quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine drew crude maps and tactical notes for an assault meant to overrun the tauren settlement. The Bristleback quilboar plan a sustained assault on Camp Narache. Their leadership means to push beyond skirmishes along the borders of the Red Cloud Mesa and wipe out the young tauren training there. The plans lie deep within a dirt cave in Brambleblade Ravine. Chief Hawkwind can send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements, giving Camp Narache a chance to blunt the invasion before it begins.

item:bristleback-belt.text: Bristleback Belt. In Camp Narache, young tauren gather Bristleback Belts to prove their valor. The belts come from quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine and mark a step in the Rite of Strength. The Red Cloud tribe tests youths who seek respect in Thunder Bluff through the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. The first trial, the Rite of Strength, asks each initiate to protect the tribe from threats. Bristleback quilboar raid food supplies and ambush hunting parties outside Camp Narache. Chief Hawkwind demands their belts in return. Bringing him twelve proves an initiate can face danger and help defend the tribe. Bristleback warriors and shamans in Brambleblade Ravine wear belts made from rough hide, twine, and scrap. A tauren warrior has little use for one as apparel, but its quilboar make marks it as evidence of a slain enemy. Bringing the belts back to the camp circle fulfills the rite's proof.

item:bristleback-quilboar-tusk.text: Bristleback Quilboar Tusk. Across the northern and central Barrens, Bristleback Quilboar Tusks are taken from slain quilboar. Mankrik gathers them as proof of slaughter and tokens of vengeance. Bristleback quilboar defend their territory across the Barrens against Horde expansion. Their jagged ivory tusks serve as weapons in close combat. Mankrik, a veteran orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads, lost his wife in a vicious quilboar ambush. He gathers dozens of tusks as retribution, a bloody count of the suffering he means to return to the Bristlebacks.

item:brock-s-list.text: Brock's List. At Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker sends a list of mining pupils honored with picks from Ironforge's guild halls. In Khaz Modan, apprentices must prove their skill before taking on serious work in the mines. Brock records those who excel in their lessons. He entrusts the list to travelers bound for Ironforge, where the honored names can be engraved on the picks. A gryphon carries Brock's List from Thelsamar's roost to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Deep Mountain Mining Guild in Ironforge's Great Forge. There, the students' names are engraved on their honorary picks.

item:broken-and-battered-samophlange.text: Broken and Battered Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, Venture Company machinery lies battered after a failed inspection. The damaged samophlange must reach goblin experts in Orgrimmar, where someone may understand how it works. The Venture Company made samophlanges for its resource work in the northern Barrens. Wenikee Boltbucket tried to inspect and modify one, adding gauges, levers, and dials to measure its stability. Her tinkering weakened the mechanism instead, leaving it battered and close to ruin. Knowing more additions might make it fail completely, she sent the fragile device to someone with factory experience. Repairing the device calls for someone who has worked on Venture Company production lines. Rilli Greasygob, a former Venture employee, works at Nogg's Machine Shop in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. The battered apparatus catches the engineer's eye. Anyone who scavenges from goblin operations may seem daring, or simply foolhardy.

item:broken-samophlange.text: Broken Samophlange. In the northern Barrens, a broken samophlange draws the notice of curious engineers. Its gears and shifting parts hint at a purpose no one has uncovered. The broken samophlange is a baffling contraption from the northern Barrens. Its moving assemblies and fine gears show careful workmanship, even in ruin. Sputtervalve, a goblin in Ratchet, damaged the delicate device by accident before anyone could document how it worked. The finder hoped to send working results to curious colleagues in Undermine, so they sought someone able to repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket, a clever tinkerer near the border outpost of Mor'shan Rampart, was the one they turned to. Wenikee Boltbucket cannot tell what a samophlange is meant to do, even after examining its ruined parts. Its clockwork sounds and shifting motion catch her interest, though. Rather than discard it as junk, she sets out to repair the device and see its mechanisms working at full capacity.

item:broken-tools.text: Broken Tools. At the dig northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven picks lie broken on the forge. Baine Bloodhoof wants proof that the excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has been stopped. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators dig into Mulgore's hills in search of ancient history. The tauren see their work as a defilement of the Earth Mother. The digging's noise and destruction agitate the local wildlife, especially the roaming kodo herds. Young Baine Bloodhoof orders defenders to take the prospectors' iron picks and break them at a forge. With their picks ruined, the expedition cannot gouge further into the earth.

item:bundle-of-crocolisk-skins.text: Bundle of Crocolisk Skins. In the Wetlands, hunters prepare crocolisk skins for Menethil Harbor. The hides are valuable trade goods for local leatherworkers. Crocolisk hides are an essential trade good for coastal Menethil Harbor. Hunters gather and cure the tough, water-resistant skins in the Wetlands before sending them west to artisans such as James Halloran. Einar has gathered this bundle, but asks a traveler to carry it into town. He wants to avoid returning home to face the temper of his frustrated wife, Sida.

item:bundle-of-hides.text: Bundle of Hides. Across the Barrens, a Bundle of Hides travels toward Thunder Bluff with the Horde’s wind riders. The cured skins are a straightforward courier shipment for the leatherworkers, and their delivery introduces travelers to the wind rider network. Hunters skin the beasts of the Barrens for cured hides. The plains hold vast herds of kodo, prowling lions, and roving raptors. These skins supply the leatherworkers of Thunder Bluff, who turn them into gear, pouches, armor, and bindings for the Horde. Couriers carry the bundle from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff on Devrak’s trained wyverns. Overland travel through the Barrens and into Mulgore is slow and dangerous, with roaming quilboar and centaur raiders. Handing the hides to a wind rider courier shows how swiftly air travel can cross Kalimdor’s fractured terrain.

item:bundle-of-wood.text: Bundle of Wood. Eastvale Logging Camp needs wood sent west for Stormwind's rebuilding. Eastvale Logging Camp sends freshly chopped timber west for buildings and other construction in the Kingdom of Stormwind. But bears and wolves have entered the groves northwest of camp. The frightened loggers fled, leaving their Bundles of Wood among the trees. With the shipment deadline near, overseer Raelen needs travelers to recover the timber before the lumber contracts are breached.

item:burning-blade-medallion.text: Burning Blade Medallion. Cultists in the Valley of Trials carry the Burning Blade Medallion. Yarrog Baneshadow holds it deep in the Burning Blade Coven, where its dark magic threatens Durotar's young warriors. Zureetha Fargaze's divinations point to the medallion in the Burning Blade Coven. Yarrog Baneshadow, an agent of the Burning Blade cult, carries it deep inside the winding caverns. The trinket channels dark power among the cult's impish familiars and felstalkers. Defeating Yarrog and taking the medallion ends the cult's attempt to undermine the Horde's training grounds from within Durotar.

item:burning-blood-quest-item.text:
Burning Blood (quest item). In Duskwood, Nightbane worgen blood draws Grimand Elmore's interest. He needs twenty vials for experiments in smithing. Nightbane worgen prowl Duskwood in a strange fury. Their blood burns with real heat. It can be drawn from worgen haunting the timberlands and Roland's Doom. Armorers seek its heat to temper resilient plate. Grimand Elmore is an armorer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He wants to test smithing methods devised by his former student Furen Longbeard.

For the experiment, Elmore needs Burning Blood and a dense burning rock held by the worgen chieftain Gutspill. Bring him the bubbling fluid, and he promises sturdy warrior armor from his forge.

item:burning-rock.text: Burning Rock. In Duskwood, Burning Rock smolders within Roland's Doom. Gutspill, leader of the Nightbane worgen, carries it, and Grimand Elmore in Stormwind needs it with fiery worgen blood to forge enchanted armor for promising warriors. Gutspill carries Burning Rock through the shafts of Roland's Doom. Grimand Elmore in Stormwind wants its heat for armor made with fiery worgen blood. He tests smithing techniques developed by his peer Furen Longbeard, hoping to make tough plates for veteran fighters.

item:cache-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. At the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen, a stockpile of potent poison lies locked away. The mixture bears the name of Zanzil, a jungle troll witch doctor, and draws the Shattered Hand's attention. North of the Sludge Fen in the Barrens, the Venture Company holds a tower outpost. At its summit, Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix keeps a cache of altered mixture bearing the name of the troll witch doctor Zanzil in his private strongbox. A poison has weakened everyone in the tower, leaving its goblin inhabitants vulnerable to a bold intruder.

item:cactus-apple.text: Cactus Apple. In the Valley of Trials, Cactus Apples offer orcs a rare source of moisture in Durotar's dry heat. Cactus apples grow in clusters around the thick cactuses scattered across the Valley of Trials. Gathering them means working among the thorns, but the fruit gives welcome hydration in Durotar's heat. Galgar, an orc in the valley, gathers the apples to make Cactus Apple Surprise, a cooling treat for recruits enduring their early training.

item:calor-s-note.text: Calor's Note. In Duskwood, Calor's Note carries a woodsman's recommendation to Master Jonathan Carevin. Calor writes it on a scrap of faded parchment for a tested adventurer, opening a path to a hidden band that fights beside Darkshire's militia but remains apart from it. Calor is notoriously hard to impress, and Duskwood offers strangers little warmth. When an adventurer survives the bloodthirsty worgen stalking the woods, Calor's respect is earned, and he writes a brief message. The faded note travels to Darkshire, where it introduces the outsider directly to Jonathan Carevin. Darkshire relies on the Night Watch for public defense, while Calor and Carevin pursue a grimmer, hidden fight. Calor laments that the town guard outnumbers them and hopes to find enough capable fighters to advance their private war. When the note is handed over, it grants entry to Carevin's campaign against demons, undead, and the hidden sympathizers aiding Duskwood's decline.

item:candle-of-beckoning.text: Candle of Beckoning. On Brightwater Lake, Gunther Arcanus keeps an enchanted candle for a summons. Light it on a nearby islet, and the restless spirit Lillith Nefara answers. Gunther Arcanus keeps the Candle of Beckoning in a crate beside him on his island in Brightwater Lake. The candle is an instrument for a ritual of summoning. Gunther is a fiercely independent undead sorcerer who broke free of the Lich King's command on his own, and he remains wary of both the Scourge and the Forsaken. To show Gunther that you are not loyal to the Lich King, carry one of the candles southwest to a smaller islet. Set it on an old, bloodstained table and light it. The flame pierces the veil between worlds and beckons the dormant, restless shade of Lillith Nefara, a powerful Scourge agent, so she can be destroyed.

item:cantation-of-manifestation.text: Cantation of Manifestation. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell gives apprentices a scroll to reveal unseen magical beings in Algernon's shop. The Cantation of Manifestation reveals beings hidden by magic. Anastasia Hartwell keeps the scroll in the Magic Quarter and entrusts it to capable mages sent to contain rogue magical anomalies. Read aloud where arcane instability troubles the air, such as Algernon's alchemical workshop in the Apothecarium, its words force stray rift spawns into sight. The caster can then subdue them and trap them in containment coffers for further study.

item:canvas-scraps.text: Canvas Scraps. At Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow gathers Canvas Scraps to make travel sacks for new Horde recruits. The cloth comes from human invaders and centaur tribes in Durotar. Kul Tiras marines and sailors carry canvas along Durotar’s eastern shore. Their gear and sails leave scraps behind. Inland, Kolkar centaur reuse coarse cloth taken from supply caravans and past conflicts. Their camps and gear hold scraps that can be salvaged. Furl Scornbrow watches for invaders from the Razor Hill watchtower. The aging veteran has left his fighting days behind, but puts salvaged enemy cloth to use. He stitches it into sturdy carrying bags for younger soldiers, helping the new generation defend the Horde’s borders.

item:cask-of-merlot.text: Cask of Merlot. In Stormwind, Cask of Merlot supplies Lakeshire while Blackrock orcs cut its trade routes. Harvested and fermented in the heart of the kingdom, the merlot comes from the Galina Winery's cellars. The winery lies along the canals bordering Stormwind's Trade District, where winemaker Roberto Pupellyverbos tends its vintages for the capital's refined tastes. Unlike Duskwood moonshine or Elwynn spirits, this wine reflects the craft of human vintners working within the city's walls. When the Blackrock clan invaded the Redridge Mountains, supply routes failed and Lakeshire lost its usual merchant shipments. With locals parched and terrified, Barkeep Daniels sends willing couriers across the kingdom to refill his tavern's cellars. The cask gives defenders and refugees by Lake Everstill a gentle drink to wash down their rations.

item:cask-of-scalder.text: Cask of Scalder. In Stormwind, a cask of Barleybrew Scalder is bound for an old acquaintance. The fiery ale carries a favor between dwarves. Travelers who have proved themselves across the Rethban Gauntlet bring Barleybrew Scalder to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Furen is an artisan shieldsmith, and he finds dry times intolerable. The cask gives Yorus Barleybrew a way to call in an old favor and secure fine dwarven craftsmanship.

item:cask-of-shimmer-stout.text: Cask of Shimmer Stout. In Dun Morogh's cold heights, Cask of Shimmer Stout is bound for the eastern mountains. Rejold Barleybrew brewed the potent new ale, and his brother sends a cask east as a gift for fellow dwarven mountaineers. Rejold Barleybrew brews Shimmer Stout in Brewnall Village. Local patrons and mountaineers who brave Dun Morogh's biting frosts take to it quickly. Impressed by the brew, his brother Mountaineer Barleybrew commissions a cask for the journey through the eastern pass into Loch Modan. Dwarves prize strong drink for company and warmth in the mountain chill. Sharing fresh ale with comrades on distant patrols is a military tradition. During his watch in Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell opens the cask and samples the brew. Shimmer Stout lives up to its name: one draught is said to lighten the limbs and make a soldier feel as though he could fly. A dwarven scout on a long, lonely patrol along the high roads might welcome such an invigorating drink.

item:cats-eye-emerald.text: Cats Eye Emerald. In the northern Barrens, the Cats Eye Emerald has drawn the eye of Ratchet's Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Venture Company bosses keep the fist-sized gem under guard at Boulder Lode Mine. Venture Company laborers struck a massive emerald at Boulder Lode Mine, northeast of the Sludge Fen. Word of the find spread quickly across the savanna. In goblin country, rare gemstones seldom stay secret. Trade gossip carried news from Ratchet's docks to Booty Bay, and Wharfmaster Dizzywig heard of the prize. He began plotting to send it to the open market in Undermine. Venture Company management keeps the emerald inside the mine under heavy guard. Overseers, Enforcers, and chief operators such as Boss Copperplug defend it from rival cartels and fortune-hunters. Dizzywig has promised a fifty-percent cut to those who help him secure the gem.

item:cenarion-lunardust.text: Cenarion Lunardust. Turak Runetotem gives Cenarion Lunardust to young tauren druids on Thunder Bluff. They use it to awaken Lunaclaw at an ancient Moonkin Stone between Mulgore and the Barrens. Cenarion Lunardust carries the Cenarion Circle’s blessing for druids ready to join the Druids of the Claw. At the Moonkin Stone west of Camp Taurajo, the dust calls Lunaclaw, a sacred beast bound to test each initiate. Defeating the guardian tests strength and resolve. The trial teaches the young druid the strength of body and heart needed to take the form of a bear.

item:cenarion-moondust.text: Cenarion Moondust. At the Moonkin Stone east of Auberdine, Cenarion Moondust calls forth Lunaclaw. Night elf druids use the sacred powder in their trial to become Druids of the Claw. Mathrengyl Bearwalker gives Cenarion Moondust to young druids in Darnassus for their final trial of heart and body. To face Lunaclaw, the guardian, an initiate travels to the moonkin dens east of Auberdine in Darkshore. Scattered on the ancient Moonkin Stone, the powder summons Lunaclaw to test the druid in combat. Through the trial, the initiate takes in the enduring strength needed to channel the bear form.

item:centaur-bracers.text: Centaur Bracers. Across the Barrens, Centaur Bracers are stripped from slain Kolkar warriors. Regthar Deathgate gathers them west of the Crossroads as proof that centaur raiders have been culled. Kolkar raiders threaten the Horde’s foothold across the Barrens. Their fallen warriors leave behind leather and iron bracers, proof that a raider has been removed from the trade roads. Regthar Deathgate, an orc scout stationed on the bluffs west of the Crossroads, offers a standing bounty for these trophies to curb the tribe’s aggression.

item:charred-horn.text:
Charred Horn. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard needs Charred Horns from young chimaeras in Stonetalon. Their resistance to flame, blunt force, and harsh elemental forces makes them useful in strong armor. Fledgling and young chimaeras in the Stonetalon Mountains provide Charred Horns. Their resistance to flame and blunt force makes them useful to Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorsmith at his forge in Stormwind. He needs twelve horns to make fire-hardened mail.

Furen combines them with venomous spider fangs from the Wetlands, phlogiston from Razorfen Kraul, and the galvanized horn of a chimaera matriarch. The Charred Horns reinforce the mail's rings and plates with heat-treated material.

item:chest-of-containment-coffers.text: Chest of Containment Coffers. Mages in the Undercity keep the Chest of Containment Coffers close at hand. Its enchanted vessels can secure unstable magical phenomena. Invisible arcane creatures can emerge from experiments or sudden rifts between planes. Ordinary cages cannot hold beings made of magic. The Chest of Containment Coffers holds enchanted vessels that bind subdued creatures alive. Senior instructors keep the chest nearby, including Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity and Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. They give initiates the coffers for surveying anomalies before those forces can unsettle their surroundings.

item:chief-sharptusk-thornmantle-s-head.text: Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head marks the end of a threat to Red Cloud Mesa. The Bristleback leader threatened the young tauren braves, and his head was recovered from deep in Brambleblade Ravine as proof of victory. The Bristleback quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine have attacked the tribes of Camp Narache. Their chieftain, Sharptusk Thornmantle, urges them on. The tauren seek to protect their homeland in Mulgore with vigilance and strength. Sharptusk's head proves he is dead and warns the surviving quilboar clans against encroaching on the mesa borders. Brave Windfeather demands Sharptusk's head as a rite of passage for young hunters and tribal defenders. Facing an enemy clever enough to strike back and lead a war band tests a young combatant's martial skill. Presenting the head fulfills that trial and earns the young fighter a reputation among the braves of Red Cloud Mesa.

item:chok-sul-s-head.text:
Chok'sul's Head. In Thelsamar, Chok'sul's death is proved by the head Magistrate Bluntnose demands. The local dwarven authorities set a bounty, and he requires this proof before paying it. Ogres from Mo'grosh Stronghold threaten Loch Modan's settlements. They strike Thelsamar, excavation sites, and the Stonewrought Dam. Magistrate Bluntnose placed a bounty on Chok'sul, the brute believed to direct these attacks.

The northeastern hills are in turmoil, so the magistrate demands proof before releasing township funds. Chok'sul's severed head gives the dwarven council the certainty it needs to mark the bounty fulfilled.

item:clarice-s-pendant.text: Clarice's Pendant. In the Pools of Vision in Thunder Bluff, Clarice Foster keeps a bitter reminder of the family she lost. Her pendant came from her former husband, Yuriv, whose devotion to the Light left Clarice and their children behind. Clarice's Pendant recalls the life Clarice Foster lost before she became Forsaken. Before the Third War consumed Lordaeron, her husband Yuriv left her and their children to fight the undead. He believed devotion to the Holy Light came before all else. Yuriv died, and his family was left to fall to the very Scourge he had set out to fight. Clarice does not treasure the pendant he gave her. To her, it is an insult, a reminder that she and the children came second to his zeal and duty.

item:claw-key.text: Claw Key. Within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak, three druidic keys open the enchanted hoard. High on Stonetalon Peak, night elf druids built the Talon Den as a sanctuary and a storehouse for powerful relics. They hid the treasures behind several layers of protection. Three enchanted locks seal the hoard: the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key, and the Claw Key. Each key lies in its own druidic cache, shaped like a torch and hidden in the winding tunnels of the barrow den. The druids kept the keys guarded and out of easy reach. Near the barrow entrance lies the Gatekeeper's Key, needed to open the cache that holds the Claw Key. The Claw Key is vital to breaking the druids' seal and claiming the riches hidden deep within the mountain.

item:cliffspring-river-sample.text: Cliffspring River Sample. In Darkshore, foul water gathers at the base of the Cliffspring River waterfall. Drawn for Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, the vial shows that corruption is moving toward the coast. The Cliffspring River runs from Darkshore's eastern heights, past ancient stone bridges, and into the sea at Mist's Edge. Its clear waters have turned foul and visibly corrupted. Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine, fears the tainted flow will reach the settlement's shore and water supply. He sent travelers to draw water from the pool beneath the river's lower waterfall. The sample confirms that unnatural rot is moving downstream toward the coast.

item:cloth-request.text: Cloth Request. At the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, Rema Schneider receives Harlan Bagley's request for fresh cloth and knitted goods. His shelves are emptying quickly. Harlan Bagley asks Rema Schneider for fresh cloth and knitted garments. Trade has surged without warning. Citizens and travelers buy armor and sturdy clothing as if a brutal season were coming. The rush leaves Rema puzzled and wary. The House of Nobles has announced no open war, so she wonders why city folk are quietly armoring themselves and whether the crown's leaders are hiding unrest.

item:cloven-hoof.text: Cloven Hoof. Deep in Thousand Needles, the Galak centaur guard the Cloven Hoof within a sacred flame at Splithoof Hold. Tauren scholars seek to understand the strange energy rising from the relic. At the heart of Splithoof Hold, the Galak centaur keep the Cloven Hoof in an ancient brazier. Magical fire surrounds the relic, and blessed water must quench the flame for a moment before anyone can handle it. The centaur clans are divided and violent, yet their care for the brazier points to a ritual bound to their origins. At Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner and other tauren observers hope the strange aura of the hoof will teach them about the centaur who have long troubled Kalimdor's plains.

item:comar-s-heart.text: Comar's Heart. In the Undercity, warlocks seek Comar's Heart to draw a succubus into their service. The heart belonged to Comar Villard, a human searching the Wetlands for his lost wife. Comar Villard keeps searching the Wetlands for his lost wife. Though turmoil has swept the Eastern Kingdoms, he refuses to abandon the search. Carendin Halgar's disciples in the Undercity judge his fidelity among the rarest and purest. To bind a succubus, a creature both capricious and predatory, warlocks need devotion like his as bait. Comar's steadfast love marks him for slaughter, and his heart becomes the lure for a demonic servant.

item:consecrated-rune.text:
Consecrated Rune. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, the Consecrated Rune calls fledgling dwarven paladins to their formal duties as Knights of the Silver Hand. Among the Knights of the Silver Hand, a Consecrated Rune marks a novice dwarf’s place. Dwarven paladins receive one in Coldridge Valley after proving their basic skill in arms. Sacred words are inscribed upon it, and the Holy Light blesses the rune.

Bromos Grummner, the paladin trainer inside Anvilmar, sends it as an official summons. Dwarves greatly respect the Holy Light traditions their human allies introduced to them. Reading the rune confirms a novice’s place in the order and marks the beginning of service.

item:console-key.text: Console Key. At the Venture Company digsite in the Barrens, Tinkerer Sniggles holds the Console Key. It unlocks the main control terminal and lets the samophlange be removed once the apparatus is shut down. The Venture Company runs an industrial outpost in the northern Barrens. Its steam-driven machinery depends on a device called a samophlange. The console is locked against unauthorized hands, and only Tinkerer Sniggles, the chief technician on site, carries the Console Key. The key opens the terminal casing so the rig can be powered down.

item:control-console-operating-manual.text: Control Console Operating Manual. At the Venture Company site southwest of Sludge Fen, the Control Console Operating Manual guides workers through the machinery. It explains how to close the valves and disengage the samophlange. Southwest of Sludge Fen, the Venture Company runs a drilling and research site in the northern Barrens. Its machinery links gauges, pressurized valves, and mechanisms to a device called a samophlange. Without the right instructions, working the volatile controls can cause a dangerous failure or lock the system. The manual gives the valve sequence for disengaging the core apparatus without triggering an explosive failure.

item:corroded-shrapnel.text: Corroded Shrapnel. In Stonetalon, jagged metal remains lodged deep inside corrupted treants. The Venture Company’s retreating munitions left fragments in the forest’s protectors, now sought for study. When the Venture Company was driven from Stonetalon’s groves, its goblins used reckless munitions to cover their escape. Explosive shrapnel tore into the valley’s defending treants, lodging deep within their bark and core. The ancient guardians slowly succumbed to corruption. Their wood blackened, and their fury turned against anyone entering the vale. Kaela Shadowspear seeks the rusted fragments so Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome, can study how the weapons brought on the treants’ corruption.

item:corrupt-manifestation-s-bracers.text: Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers. Tainted bracers lie on the coast of Silverpine Forest, remnants of a corrupted water elemental. Shaman initiates recover them during the Call of Water and cast them into the Brazier of Everfount with pure water to cleanse the shrine and summon a pure water spirit. The Scourge's plague reached the spirits of Lordaeron. Along Silverpine Forest's misty coast, west of the Sepulcher, a sacred water shrine fell to corruption. Its water manifestation became an aggressive shade. Shaman initiates must defeat it and recover its bracers. At the Brazier of Everfount, they cast the bindings into the flame with pure water, lifting the corruption and calling forth an unblemished water spirit.

item:corrupted-brain-stem.text: Corrupted Brain Stem. In Blackfathom Deeps and along Ashenvale's coast, Corrupted Brain Stem specimens come from twisted naga and satyrs. Gershala Nightwhisper of Auberdine studies the deformities caused by reckless magic. Night elf scholars hope the findings can help keep the blood elves from suffering the same fate. Naga and satyrs bear the marks of forbidden magic and demonic pacts. Long ago, reckless kaldorei highborne became serpent-like aquatic beasts and demonic horned fiends. Their brain stems show heavy physical mutation, proof of how deeply corruptive energies altered the nervous systems of beings who were once elves. Gershala Nightwhisper watches troubling rumors about the blood elves of the Eastern Kingdoms from Auberdine. She fears their use of demonic sorcery will create another generation of monsters on Azeroth, so she sends adventurers into Blackfathom Deeps. By examining naga and satyr tissues, she hopes to trace magical degeneration before another elven culture is lost.

item:corrupted-kor-gem.text: Corrupted Kor Gem. Around Blackfathom Deeps, naga rites leave Kor gems corrupted. Spellcasters prize the stones for holding arcane force, but this taint must be cleansed before a gem can be used in righteous smithing. Kor gems can capture and hold great stores of magic, making them prized by sorcerers and enchanted smiths. Near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, naga oracles and tide priestesses claim the stones for their shadowy rites. Their foul enchantments warp each gem with corruption from the sea. The taint does not drain the stone's latent power, so those who need a potent focus still seek gems among the naga.

item:cougar-claws.text: Cougar Claws. Across Mulgore’s central plains, tauren hunters gather Cougar Claws for a cleansing ritual. The claws come from flatland cougars, among the grasslands’ apex hunters. Flatland cougars rank among the apex hunters of Mulgore’s grasslands, stalking prey by instinct. For the tauren, taking their claws is neither casual slaughter nor trophy hunting; it gathers the beast’s natural spirit. When goblin operations defile the plains’ ancestral waters, Mull Thunderhorn asks young hunters to collect Cougar Claws alongside prairie stalker claws. The tauren believe native beasts’ pure predatory instincts can be woven into a ritual totem. They mean to use it to scour unnatural toxins and foul sorcery from the poisoned Thunderhorn Water Well.

item:courser-eye.text: Courser Eye. Coursers roam the highlands of Stonetalon, where Courser Eye is gathered for a troll witch doctor's brew. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin wants many eyes for a concoction he calls forest magic.

item:covert-ops-pack.text: Covert Ops Pack. In Stonetalon, the Covert Ops Pack equips Alliance agents to sabotage Venture Company sites and steal their plans. Its charges and schematics target the company’s work in Windshear Crag. The Covert Ops Pack carries charges and plans for strikes inside Venture Company territory. Red and blue NG-5 explosives pair with remote detonators, while Plan Alpha and Plan Beta give agents instructions. The explosives target the Cragpool Lake lumber mill and the eastern mine. As goblins rush to fight fires and inspect broken machinery, an infiltrator can slip through the confusion and take documents and schematics. The pack serves both the night elf Sentinels and Alliance engineers in Stonetalon. Its blasts and theft hinder the clear-cutting and excavation of the sacred mountainside. The stolen Venture Company engineering plans also offer insight into goblin heavy machinery. They show where the machines can fail and give Alliance engineers ideas to adapt for their own designs.

item:crate-of-crash-helmets.text: Crate of Crash Helmets. A heavy supply shipment of dwarven Siege Engine headgear destined for the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. The sturdy helmets are urgently required by the Brassbolts brothers to protect test drivers from concussions caused by their experimental rocket cars. Out across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, gnome engineers test the absolute limits of mechanical propulsion. Unfortunately for the test pilots, the experimental rocket cars designed by the Brassbolts brothers move far faster than their steering can reliably handle. With drivers routinely suffering violent crashes and head trauma, ordinary leather caps no longer suffice. To prevent their roster of willing daredevils from vanishing entirely, heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets are packed and dispatched across the sea to keep drivers conscious—and alive.

item:crate-of-horseshoes.text: Crate of Horseshoes. In Elwynn, Crate of Horseshoes carries fifty iron shoes toward Lakeshire. Smith Argus forged fifty fresh horseshoes in Goldshire, then packed them into a crate and hammered it shut. Verner Osgood ordered them for Lakeshire, where pressure from gnolls and orcs leaves local craftsmen reliant on Elwynn for essential metal goods. The delivery meets Verner's desperate need for equipment, and Argus includes a stern bill of sale so the Redridge craftsman knows frontier survival comes at a steep price.

item:crate-of-inn-supplies.text: Crate of Inn Supplies. In Coldridge Valley, the Crate of Inn Supplies waits for a journey to Kharanos. Troggs have cut off the mountain pass, so the Thunderbrew Distillery depends on travelers to carry its goods. The Crate of Inn Supplies is waiting near Anvilmar for a safe way through Coldridge Pass. Troggs have cut off the route, stopping civilian couriers until Mountaineers can clear the road. Hands Springsprocket packed the crate with tavern provisions for Tannok Frosthammer in Kharanos, where the supplies are needed.

item:crate-of-lightforge-ingots.text: Crate of Lightforge Ingots. In Stormwind, the Crate of Lightforge Ingots carries Duskwood's hope against Morbent Fel. Lightforge iron is rare, and its consecrated metal channels holy power against dark entities. Morbent Fel's protections turn aside ordinary steel, so Duskwood looks to these ingots against the necromancer. Only an artisan who knows the metal's temper and honors its sacred nature can work it.

item:crate-with-holes.text: Crate With Holes. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix prepares a crate for a Snufflenose Gopher.
