Mebok Mizzyrix sends trained Snufflenose Gophers to find Blueleaf Tubers in Razorfen Kraul. The gophers cannot follow an adventurer across the Barrens on foot, so Mebok places each one in a wooden crate with air holes. Inside the quilboar stronghold, the crate is opened and the gopher follows its keen nose toward the buried tubers.

item:crawler-leg.text: Crawler Leg. Along Darkshore’s misty coast, crabs lose legs that most travelers have no use for. Their tough limbs can help keep a gnome’s communication device working. Darkshore’s crabs leave sturdy limbs along the shore, from pygmy tide crawlers to reef crawlers. Night elf sentinels pay them little mind, but the gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle has found a use for them. Working from Auberdine, Wizbang designed his prototype long-distance communication devices, called buzzboxes, to run on improvised local components. Crawler legs’ segmented joints and durable chitin provide the friction and leverage needed to repair Buzzbox 827, along the shoreline just south of town.

item:creeper-ichor.text: Creeper Ichor. Across the Hillsbrad forests, rare, virulent Creeper Ichor is harvested from moss creepers. The Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill seeks it as a biological agent for formulating novel plagues against the living. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon seeks natural toxins and biological catalysts to craft deadly new toxins and eradicate the surrounding human population. The clean air and vibrant life of the foothills offend him. Among the forest’s giant arachnids, mature moss creepers hold an elusive ichor that makes an ideal base for his Elixir of Suffering. Mixed with other reagents, including gray bear tongues, the fluid helps the Forsaken perfect their lethal alchemy.

item:crocolisk-skin-classic.text: Crocolisk Skin (Classic). At Farstrider Lodge in Loch Modan, hunters brave the Loch’s crocolisks for hides sought by merchants and leatherworkers. Crocolisks make dens along the islands and shores of the Loch’s cold waters. Their sharp teeth and thick scales make them dangerous quarry. Still, hunters based at Farstrider Lodge pursue them for their tough skins. Tailors and distant merchants seek the hides for sturdy garments and armor, so an undamaged skin brings a good price nearby.

item:crocolisk-tear-classic.text: Crocolisk Tear (Classic). At the Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir needs Crocolisk Tear to counter Dark Iron explosives. Crocolisk Tears come from reptiles in Loch Modan's waters. Chief Engineer Hinderweir found another use for their secretions. Mixed with potent spider venom and resonant ogre minerals, a tear gains the chemical properties needed to counter the volatile Dark Iron demolition charges threatening the Stonewrought Dam.

item:crossroads-supply-crate.text: Crossroads Supply Crate. Stolen provisions for the Crossroads lie scattered among Razormane camps in the Barrens. A raided caravan left the settlement short of food, tools, and necessities. Razormane quilboar raided a caravan carrying supplies to the Crossroads. The crates were dragged into nearby camps among the underbrush and dirt dens. Thork, the settlement's commander, seeks their return before the outpost runs dangerously low on food, tools, and necessities.

item:crude-flint.text: Crude Flint. Across the Wetlands, Mosshide gnolls carry Crude Flint to kindle fires with freshly hewn marsh timber. Their fires anger Rethiel the Greenwarden, protector of the marsh.

item:crystal-kelp-frond.text: Crystal Kelp Frond. Murlocs carry Crystal Kelp Fronds from the ocean to Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. William Pestle in Goldshire seeks them for an invisibility liquor. Crystal Kelp Fronds come from saltwater oceans, which makes them unusual in Elwynn Forest’s fresh water. Along Crystal Lake’s shores, murloc tribes gather and keep the fronds for reasons of their own. Alchemists value the fronds for their strange power to distort sight. William Pestle in Goldshire uses them as the chief ingredient in an invisibility liquor meant to help sweethearts slip past watchful family eyes.

item:crystal-phial.text: Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, Tenaron Stormgrip entrusts young night elves with a Crystal Phial. They carry it to a nearby moonwell to draw sacred water for rites honoring and nourishing Teldrassil. Young night elves receive a Crystal Phial atop Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip sends them to the moonwell just north of the bough to gather its glowing waters. The delicate vessel holds water touched by the sacred legacy of the Well of Eternity. Returning with a Filled Crystal Phial begins the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage, teaching the young kaldorei about the balance of magic, history, and nature in their new island home.

item:crystalized-scales.text: Crystalized Scales. Basilisks in harsh Kalimdor lands yield Crystalized Scales for arcane work. The mineralized hides come from the Charred Vale and Thousand Needles, and Collin Mauren seeks them in Stormwind. Basilisks endure heat and ash in Stonetalon's Charred Vale and the salt flats of Thousand Needles. Their hides harden beneath a crystal crust, and the scales hold latent arcane resonance. Wizards across the Great Sea prize them for experiments in rare spellcraft. In Stormwind, the mage Collin Mauren seeks travelers bound for Kalimdor to bring him these scales. Mauren pulverizes their crystalline mineral layers into dust, then uses the powder as a reagent for newly conceived spells and his own arcane research.

item:curative-animal-salve.text: Curative Animal Salve. Across Darkshore and the Barrens, druids use Curative Animal Salve to treat sick wildlife. Herbalists prepare it in both lands, while the Cenarion Circle sees the animals’ afflictions as signs of a wider blight. Druids use Curative Animal Salve to ease sick wildlife in Darkshore and the Barrens. Alanndarian Nightsong directs young druids to treat sick deer between the Cliffspring River and the borders of Ashenvale. In the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem brews the same remedy for sick gazelles grazing north of the Crossroads. Each herbalist prepares the salve from locally gathered herbs in batches of ten doses. Field practitioners apply it directly to the animals, while both herbalists work with local authorities to produce larger supplies. The salve eases an animal’s suffering, but the Cenarion Circle sees the afflictions as signs of a wider disturbance. In Moonglade, Dendrite Starblaze observes that the afflicted deer on the coast and the suffering gazelles on the savannah are no random casualties. They are unwitting victims of a blight spreading across Kalimdor from multiple directions. For initiates, treating the animals tests their dedication to protecting nature and their skill in cleansing poison.

item:daffodil-bouquet.text: Daffodil Bouquet. In Lakeshire, Guard Parker sends a bouquet to thank Darcy for packing his lunch. Martie Jainrose gathers the flowers, and their choice stirs gossip between the two women. Guard Parker wants to thank Darcy at the Lakeshire inn for packing his daily lunch. He asks the town herbalist, Martie Jainrose, to prepare a bouquet of daffodils. Martie says they are her favorite flowers. Darcy recognizes them as Martie’s signature bloom and suspects jealousy. Half-joking, she wonders whether Martie poisoned the stems out of spite.

item:daggerspine-scale.text: Daggerspine Scale. Along Hillsbrad Foothills' southern shores, Daggerspine Scale comes from tough reptilian scales harvested from prowling Daggerspine naga. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks them to activate virulent brews in the Forsaken's ongoing plague experiments. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks reagents for its toxins, plagues, and concoctions. While refining the experimental Elixir of Agony, its apothecaries found that scales from the local Daggerspine naga react in a useful way. Combined with troll regenerative elixirs and murloc organs, the scales chemically activate dormant contaminating agents suspended in raw mixtures. Gathering them means hunting along the rocky coastline east of Southshore, near both the vicious naga tribe and Alliance forces. The apothecaries need these scales for their research.

item:dal-bloodclaw-s-skull.text: Dal Bloodclaw's Skull. In northern Ashenvale, Dal Bloodclaw's Skull marks the end of a threat to Astranaar. Raene Wolfrunner receives it as proof that an attack on the night elf settlement has been averted. The Thistlefur furbolgs north of Astranaar have grown in number and aggression. Like much of Ashenvale's ancient forest, they have been corrupted. Raene Wolfrunner, a night elf sentinel, fears they will soon march on Astranaar. She orders their ranks culled and their leader, Dal Bloodclaw, slain. His skull gives grim proof that the tribe's leadership has been shattered, buying Astranaar's defenders precious time.

item:dalaran-mana-gem.text: Dalaran Mana Gem. Near Ambermill, Kirin Tor mages carry Dalaran Mana Gems to replenish their power. Forsaken tailors use the gems to weave enchanted robes. Kirin Tor mages, conjurors, and guards around Ambermill carry mana gems to focus and replenish their arcane power. In the Undercity’s Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners prize the gems as a ready supply of concentrated magic. Some undead mages share an academic heritage with Dalaran, but survival comes first. To the Forsaken, the Kirin Tor are rivals whose magical stores can be taken. Forsaken bring mana gems taken from fallen Kirin Tor operatives to tailors such as Josef Gregorian in the Undercity, along with simple linen. A tailor cannot channel arcane power directly, but can bind a gem into the cloth. The magic then strengthens the wearer’s connection to the arcane.

item:dalaran-pendant.text: Dalaran Pendant. In Ambermill, Dalaran Pendants focus the Kirin Tor's magic. The Forsaken seek them to hinder the wizards' work and trace the source of their power. Kirin Tor sorcerers, conjurers, and protectors weave powerful spells in Ambermill, threatening Forsaken control of southern Silverpine Forest. Each carries an attuned Dalaran Pendant. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister sends Forsaken operatives to recover the pendants, slowing the mages' efforts and uncovering who guides their magical weave.

item:dalaran-status-report.text: Dalaran Status Report. At Ambermill, the Kirin Tor watch Dalaran as the city is rebuilt in the open. Their report carries intelligence the Deathstalkers seek. The Scourge sacked Dalaran, and Archimonde brought down its towering spires during the Third War. Early in the rebuilding, the surviving magi removed the city's protective shield and began their work in the open. The Kirin Tor also keeps enclaves such as Ambermill in southeastern Silverpine Forest. Its wizards compile the Dalaran Status Report, which holds intelligence about the city's condition and draws the Deathstalkers' attention.

item:dalin-s-heart.text: Dalin's Heart. Near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine Forest, Dalin Forgewright patrols with an honorable heart. Undercity warlocks seek hearts from truly virtuous mortals to call and bind a succubus to their service. Dalin Forgewright spends his days defending desperate Lordaeron refugees kept from safety by the sealed Greymane Wall. His selfless devotion marks him as a rare offering of unblemished purity, and his heart is carved for the rites held in the Temple of the Damned.

item:darkhound-blood.text:
Darkhound Blood. In Tirisfal's fields and forests, tainted darkhounds yield Darkhound Blood, a bodily fluid. The Royal Apothecary Society gathers it as an early reagent for experiments to engineer a lethal new plague. Under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Royal Apothecary Society seeks a virulent contagion that can wipe out Arthas and his Scourge. Apothecary Johaan is stationed in Brill. He theorizes that local beasts, corrupted by dark energies and resilient to the surrounding decay, possess unusual biological properties.

By distilling wild darkhound blood, Johaan hopes to uncover compounds that can resist or spread virulent necrotic strains.

item:darkshore-grouper.text: Darkshore Grouper. Along Darkshore, grouper are a familiar catch, though murloc attacks have driven fishermen from their boats. The fish is prized for food and sport, and a good haul is harder to find. Darkshore Grouper are a welcome catch in the cold waters off Darkshore. Anglers around Auberdine value them for the simple dishes they make, and travelers and residents alike enjoy those meals. A fishing line and basic gear are enough to bring one in. For many fishermen, the pleasure of catching a grouper matches the pleasure of eating it. Fishermen such as Gubber Blump once took small boats into deeper waters and brought back grouper by the dozen. Coastal murlocs have grown more aggressive, grounding most boats around Auberdine. Anglers now fish from shore and dock, where locals suspect the murlocs are eating the grouper. A good haul takes patience.

item:darksoul-shackle.text: Darksoul Shackle. In Silverpine Forest, Moonrage Darksouls wear enchanted fetters forged under Archmage Arugal’s direction. Forsaken mages at the Sepulcher seek them to learn how the magic gripping the region can be undone. Archmage Arugal’s magic could not fully command or sustain the worgen he unleashed upon Silverpine Forest. He bound enchanted implements such as Darksoul Shackles to the beasts to make up for that failing. The fetters channel outside sorcery into the Moonrage Darksouls, strengthening them and anchoring the curse that keeps them thrall to Shadowfang Keep.

item:darnassus-marzipan.text:
Darnassus Marzipan. At Hallow's End, Darnassus innkeepers offer visitors marzipan after a dance. Made in the night elven capital for the autumn celebration, it is one of four treats Jesper needs. At Hallow's End, Alliance capitals share a lighthearted trick-or-treating custom. Dwarves offer sharp mints, Stormwind makes chewy nougat, and Darnassus innkeepers prepare delicate marzipan. Dance when an innkeeper asks, and you receive a piece.

Jesper needs the sweet as one of four regional treats. He is a sick orphan in Stormwind's Cathedral Square and cannot go out to collect them himself.

item:darthalia-s-sealed-commendation.text: Darthalia's Sealed Commendation. At Tarren Mill, Darthalia sends word of victories against Hillsbrad's humans to Undercity's high command. After the fighting across the Hillsbrad Foothills, High Executor Darthalia seals a dispatch recording victories against Hillsbrad's human defenders and the ruin of their positions. She addresses it to Varimathras, the dreadlord who advises Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. In the Royal Quarter, the report gives Forsaken leaders proof that Alliance enclaves south of Lordaeron can be broken, leaving northern garrisons free to face the Scourge.

item:deadmire-s-tooth.text: Deadmire's Tooth. In Dustwallow Marsh, Deadmire stalks the murky waters, and his tooth marks an honorable hunt. Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff receives it as proof that the ancient crocolisk's suffering has ended. Tauren hunters on Hunter Rise see the hunt as a bond of balance, reverence, and mercy. Deadmire was once among the most magnificent crocolisks in Dustwallow Marsh. Great age turned his final years to torment, though he kept the fierce spirit of his prime. His massive bones and failing body had become a prison of pain. Deadmire's Tooth gives Melor Stonehoof proof that an honorable hunt has ended the beast's suffering.

item:death-cap.text: Death Cap. In Darkshore, Death Cap grows in the cave behind Cliffspring Falls. Night elf herbalists seek the scarce fungus, but the Grove of the Ancients warns against approaching the falls. Death Cap grows in the damp cave behind Cliffspring Falls, along Darkshore's northeastern mountain ridges. Scaber stalks carpet the cavern floor, but Death Cap is scarce. Night elf herbalists such as Barithras Moonshade value it for experimental brewing. Finding even one means entering a cavern the Grove of the Ancients warns against, where corruption is taking root.

item:deathstalker-report.text: Deathstalker Report. Deathstalker Rane Yorick sends word of Scourge resistance in Silverpine Forest to High Executor Hadrec. Deathstalkers Rane Yorick and Quinn Yorick faced a deadly ambush in northern Silverpine Forest. Pinned down by Scourge in the pine woods, they gathered their findings into a hurried dispatch. It describes stronger resistance than the Forsaken expected as they seek to claim the region. Quinn was grievously injured, so Rane entrusted the report to passing allies, who must carry it to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher without delay.

item:deepfury-s-orders.text: Deepfury's Orders. Beneath the Thandol Span, Deepfury's Orders lie with the fallen Ol' Rustlocke. The crumpled parchment carries grim instructions from the Dark Iron dwarves who ambushed the scouting defender. Ol' Rustlocke, a dwarven bridge defender, was scouting the foundations of the Thandol Span when Dark Iron dwarves cornered and slew him. Beside his clenched fist lay crumpled orders drafted by their leader, Deepfury. The parchment is direct proof of a coordinated plot against the bridge linking the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands.

item:deepmoss-egg.text: Deepmoss Egg. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Deepmoss Eggs draw goblin merchants from Ratchet. Deepmoss spiders lay clustered clutches in the crags and canyons, and Booty Bay pirates prize them for omelettes. Deepmoss spiders nest across the Stonetalon Mountains, especially in Sishir Canyon and beneath the surviving trees of Windshear Crag. They leave clustered clutches of viable eggs in thick webbed sacks, sheltered by damp mountain moss. Most travelers have little use for them, but goblin traders see a chance to profit. Booty Bay has taken to spider egg omelettes, an eccentric culinary fad among wealthy pirates and adventurous diners. Local supplies cannot satisfy their appetite, so Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet arranges shipments through Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Collectors brave Stonetalon's venomous broods for fresh clutches, which become valuable cargo.

item:defias-docket.text: Defias Docket. Defias operatives hid their orders at Addle's Stead in western Duskwood. The docket gives Stormwind's search for its missing emissary a lead into the Brotherhood's plans. Master Elling Trias points investigators toward Duskwood as they follow leads on the kingdom's missing diplomat. Watcher Backus has tracked unusual Defias movements converging on Addle's Stead, the derelict farm south of the road from Westfall. A strongbox there holds the Defias Docket. Its records trace the Brotherhood's movements and show that their work reaches beyond highway robbery and local banditry.

item:defias-tower-key.text:
Defias Tower Key. In Westfall, the Defias Tower Key marks a quiet passage past Klaven's Tower's sentries. Stormwind operatives need it as proof that an infiltrator slipped by unseen. Klaven's Tower is a Defias Brotherhood stronghold on the Westfall coast. Recent shipments from Duskwood brought malformed Defias drones to guard it. The drones are undead and covered in spikes.

SI:7 watchers direct field agents to pick the sentries' pockets instead of fighting them. That way, no alarm sounds as the tower's defenses are breached.

item:deliah-s-ring.text: Deliah's Ring. A grim trail begins with Deliah's Ring, found among the Rot Hide gnolls’ corpse piles in Silverpine Forest. Its inscription, “For Deliah,” points back to a plague victim taken from Tirisfal’s mass graves. Among the gnoll mounds in Silverpine Forest, a ring rests on the pockmarked hand of a relatively fresh corpse. The band bears a simple inscription: “For Deliah.” The Rot Hide gnolls are doing more than scavenging battlefields. They raid the mass graves of Tirisfal Glades and carry human and Forsaken corpses south to Fenris Isle for their own purposes.

item:delivery-to-mathias.text: Delivery to Mathias. Keryn Sylvius sends a sealed parcel from Goldshire to Master Mathias Shaw in Stormwind. The delivery offers a promising rogue a first look at SI:7's inner workings. From the Lion's Pride Inn, a parcel must reach the Stormwind Barracks. For a young rogue, the journey is a test for Stormwind Intelligence. Keryn Sylvius entrusts the package to novice cutpurses, giving them their first meeting with Master Mathias Shaw. They must cross the capital quietly, keep a low profile, and follow discreet orders without questions. The handoff brings an operative to SI:7 headquarters in Old Town. Mathias Shaw uses these deliveries to tell pretenders from true talents. Those who present the parcel without faltering receive field assignments. First come covert reconnaissance and infiltration against Defias smuggling networks in Elwynn Forest.

item:deviate-hide.text: Deviate Hide. Deviate Hides are the mutated skins stripped from the beasts dwelling within the Wailing Caverns. Warped by the corrupting dream of the druid Naralex, these otherworldly pelts are sought by druids looking to repurpose the nightmare's taint into durable leather goods. When the night elf druid Naralex entered his deep slumber beneath the Barrens, his dream turned into an Emerald Nightmare that warped the local cavern ecology. The beasts lurking in the depths transformed into unnatural deviate predators with tough, mutated hides. While inherently touched by evil, these pelts possess unusual, supple resilience that makes them uniquely suited for leathercrafting. Nalpak, perched high above the cavern mouth in the skull-shaped rock formation, collects these hides to study their properties and fashion them into sturdy utility packs.

item:devlin-s-remains.text: Devlin's Remains. Near Agamand Mills, Devlin Agamand’s bones carry a bitter legacy. The younger son of the wealthy family that owned the mills, he roamed the road by his ruined home as a mindless Scourge thrall. A traveler struck him down and brought his remains to a survivor in Brill, who sought vengeance. Devlin Agamand lived in the shadow of his elder brother Thurman. Thurman was gentle and tall, while Devlin was frail and sharp-tongued. When the Plague of Undeath swept through northern Tirisfal Glades, the Agamand family failed to protect its lands and laborers. Devlin was among the first to fall. The Scourge raised him as a ravenous ghoul, and his mad chattering haunted the roadside leading to Agamand Mills. Coleman Farthing lives in Brill and holds a deep grudge against the Agamand bloodline. He blames the family for failing his own when the plague came. Farthing sent travelers to lay Devlin to rest and gather his remains. He wanted Devlin’s bones on his mantle, to savor how his former masters had been reduced to dust and shattered fragments beneath his heel.

item:dirt-caked-pendant.text: Dirt-Caked Pendant. In the Barrens, a captive orc gives up the Dirt-Caked Pendant he carried. The keepsake reaches Gan'rul Bloodeye in Orgrimmar, where it is used to draw a succubus.

item:disarming-colloid.text: Disarming Colloid. At the Stonewrought Dam, Disarming Colloid could keep Seaforium from exploding when wet. Ashlan Stonesmirk provides it in the Wetlands for a mixture that can neutralize the powder. Ashlan Stonesmirk recognized the powder left by Dark Iron sappers at the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan as Seaforium. Its scent and fine silver crystals gave it away. The powder is harmless while dry, but moisture makes it immensely destructive, a grave danger at the waterlogged dam. Stonesmirk provided Disarming Colloid to stop the reaction before detonation. Mixed with lurker venom, crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and a crocolisk tear, the colloid neutralizes Seaforium's explosive properties.

item:disarming-mixture.text: Disarming Mixture. At Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares Disarming Mixture to stop a Seaforium charge planted by Dark Iron saboteurs. The heavy Seaforium charge lies beneath the dam’s foundation, and no Mountaineers are close enough to help. Hinderweir turns to ingredients named by explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk. He stirs them into a chemical neutralizer, then mixes it with the powder keg underwater. The reactive compounds are neutralized, and the charge is left harmless.

item:divined-scroll.text: Divined Scroll. At Silverwind Refuge, the Divined Scroll can expose the mage behind Ashenvale's troubled waters. Night elves use magic from intact water elemental bracers to reveal the summoner's identity. Mystral Lake's tainted waters trouble the Sentinels guarding Ashenvale. Sentinel Velene Starstrike gives travelers an uncharged divining scroll to trace whoever manipulates the water elementals infesting the lake. Gather intact bracers from slain elementals and use them as an arcane reagent; their latent bindings pass into the parchment. The Divined Scroll then reveals the magical signature of the rogue wizard behind the infestation.

item:divining-scroll.text: Divining Scroll. At Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike gives investigators the Divining Scroll to trace the corrupted elementals to their creator. Corrupt water elementals rise from Ashenvale’s pools, and the Sentinels know the disturbance is unnatural. Sentinel Velene Starstrike obtains a scroll to find who is responsible. With intact elemental bracers as a focus, its magic draws out the summoner’s signature. The blank parchment becomes a Divined Scroll and names the guilty party.

item:dogran-s-pendant.text: Dogran's Pendant. Dogran's Pendant draws a succubus toward the warlocks of Orgrimmar. Dogran, a wounded orc, carries it while separated from his mate, Zankaja. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks turn the sorrow bound to it into a lure. Dogran's Pendant carries the sorrow of an orc separated from Zankaja. Captivity and crippling wounds have overshadowed their love. The warlocks of the Cleft of Shadow know that demons such as succubi prey on love, yearning, and vulnerability. They use the pendant's grief to draw a succubus across the Twisting Nether and into Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle.

item:dolanaar-delivery.text: Dolanaar Delivery. In Shadowglen, young travelers carry harvested herbs south to Dolanaar. Porthannius entrusts them with the bundle for Innkeeper Keldamyr. Fresh herbs from Aldrassil are bound for Dolanaar. Porthannius is occupied with matters among the druids of Shadowglen, so he entrusts the bundle to young travelers heading south along the road. They carry it to Innkeeper Keldamyr. The parcel brings you to Dolanaar's inn, where Keldamyr receives it with gratitude. The inn offers weary travelers rest, peace of mind, and sanctuary before they venture deeper into Teldrassil.

item:dragonmaw-war-banner.text: Dragonmaw War Banner. Dragonmaw War Banners rise over orc encampments in the Wetlands. Their clan markings give the dwarven defenders of Menethil Harbor proof of the growing threat. After the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan was shattered when they lost control of their enslaved red dragons. The enraged drakes turned on their captors and drove the survivors from Grim Batol into the eastern hills. Now the remaining orcs gather strength under Chieftain Nek'rosh and raise their banners over camps northeast of Menethil Harbor. Those rough standards mark their defiance and threaten the settlements in the marsh. Captain Stoutfist at Menethil Harbor sends Alliance adventurers into the marsh camps to bring back Dragonmaw banners. Raiders, centurions, and bone-warders carry these trophies, which confirm to the dwarven garrison that the camps are being broken before the clan can launch coordinated raids.

item:dried-seeds.text: Dried Seeds. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem gives travelers Dried Seeds to test the life-giving power beneath the Barrens' waters.

item:durnan-s-scalding-mornbrew.text: Durnan's Scalding Mornbrew. Inside Anvilmar, Durnan Furcutter waits for his mug of mornbrew as the mountain cold threatens to cool it before it arrives. A courier delayed on the way to Grelin Whitebeard leaves the fresh cup at risk in Coldridge Valley's frost. Carry it up the snowy path to the mountain hall within a few minutes, or Durnan's brew will go cold.

item:durotar-tiger-fur.text: Durotar Tiger Fur. Across the Echo Isles off Durotar's southeastern coast, tigers supply fur for the Darkspear, whose refugee population keeps growing. The trolls use the pelts for blankets, tents, and armor. In Sen'jin Village, the Darkspear must make scarce supplies last. They let the local tigers thrive until their growing needs call for a cull. Trolls cure the thick hides into goods their settlement needs, including protective armor and warm blankets for changing seasonal weather. The Echo Isles lie south of Durotar, across open water. The Darkspear once called the archipelago home, until the witch doctor Zalazane drove them out. Hunters face dangers from Zalazane's thralls and from tigers waiting among the thick foliage. Experienced hunters such as Vel'rin Fang speak of spending entire days motionless in the jungle brush to secure a single clean kill.

item:duskbat-wing.text: Duskbat Wing. Duskbats circle Deathknell, and local tailors turn their wings into makeshift armor for newly risen soldiers. New Forsaken claw from Deathknell’s soil with little more than rags and brittle bones. With mindless Scourge and hostile wildlife nearby, they must gather what protection they can. Novice Elreth, assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis, collects Duskbat Wings and wolf paws to piece together and strengthen clothing and armor for freshly raised warriors before they enter the wilderness to fight.

item:dusky-crab-cakes.text: Dusky Crab Cakes. In Darkshire, Chef Grual prepares Dusky Crab Cakes for the hungry Jitters. The dish is a local delicacy, and Jitters finds it exquisite.

item:dust-devil-debris.text:
Dust Devil Debris. Across Westfall, Dust Devils leave charged grit behind. Mages use it to enchant parchment and bind messaging spells into scrolls. Dust Devils sweep across Westfall’s plains as violent whirlwinds. When one falls, the living storm collapses into charged dust and grit called Dust Devil Debris. A faint trace of the elemental vortex lingers in the residue.

In Stormwind, arcane practitioners such as Collin Mauren prize the grit for specialized sorcery. Mixed into enchanted ink and parchment, it helps a wizard bind an airy messaging spell to a scroll, carrying words across the kingdom.

item:dwarven-tinder.text: Dwarven Tinder. In the Wetlands, Dwarven Tinder gives Alliance saboteurs a way to burn Dragonmaw siege engines before they reach Menethil Harbor. When Alliance scouts found Chieftain Nek'rosh's heavy catapults inside the Dragonmaw encampment, Menethil Harbor faced a crisis. Fighting in Dun Algaz had cut off the harbor from southern reinforcements, and its defenders could not withstand a long siege. They chose to sabotage the catapults before they could be used. Volunteers carrying Dwarven Tinder into orcish territory could light it with a struck spark. Its flames burned through the reinforced wooden engines in minutes.

item:ear-of-balgaras.text: Ear of Balgaras. At Dun Modr, Balgaras the Foul's ear marks the warlock's end. Recovered from the Dark Iron commander's corpse, it gives Ironforge's mountaineers proof of his death. Balgaras the Foul commanded the Dark Iron assault on Dun Modr. The invaders sabotaged the Thandol Span and destroyed the local dwarven garrison, leaving the outpost in ruins. A scheming warlock, Balgaras directed his troops from the shadows and shunned personal combat. Longbraid the Grim, the mountain king's officer stationed outside the ruins, wants proof that the ringleader has fallen. Balgaras's severed ear confirms the warlock's reign at the northern border is over. Dun Modr's fall cost Longbraid his brother and dozens of stout soldiers in the collapse of the West Bridge. The ear cannot mend the span or revive the fallen. With Balgaras unable to direct them, the surviving Dark Iron forces scattered through the northern Wetlands become easier for Ironforge's scouts to contain before another commander arrives from the south.

item:ebonlocke-s-response-to-solomon.text: Ebonlocke's Response to Solomon. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sends Solomon a refusal from Darkshire. His letter rejects the plea for Night Watch aid in Redridge. Magistrate Solomon asked Duskwood for reinforcements against the blackrock orcs after Stormwind ignored his petitions. Lord Ello Ebonlocke answers with anger and no promise of aid. He reminds Solomon that the Night Watch exists because Stormwind abandoned Darkshire when corrupting magic first gripped the woods. If its defenders leave to help Redridge, Duskwood will be left defenceless and fall to evil before the militia reaches the forest's edge.

item:echeyakee-s-hide.text: Echeyakee's Hide. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits the pale hide of Whitemist, the legendary white lion of the Barrens. Tauren honor the beast as an embodiment of mercy and death, while hunters bring the pelt as proof of their prowess. Echeyakee means Whitemist in the Taur-ahe tongue. The lion earned that name among the savannah's predators for his stealthy white coat and swift kills, ending prey's lives before fear or pain could take hold. A hunter summons the elusive cat near the giant kodo bones northeast of the Crossroads with a ceremonial horn, then claims his pelt. Bringing it to Sergra Darkthorn proves martial skill and honors Whitemist's silent, merciful end.

item:egalin-s-grimoire.text: Egalin's Grimoire. In the Undercity, Egalin's Grimoire holds the rites for summoning and commanding a voidwalker. A master warlock wrote it as a teaching text for the Temple of the Damned. Egalin's Grimoire records how to call a being of chaos from the Nether. Egalin was a master summoner, renowned for his effortless command of voidwalkers. He passed that skill to his students, including Carendin Halgar. Without the formulas and channeling methods in the book, an unprepared summoner risks being torn apart by the being they call forth.

item:electropeller.text: Electropeller. In Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle's electropellers lie scattered in freshwater rivers after a failed night outing. Wizbang Cranktoggle built the electropeller to propel an experimental exploding duck decoy. The gnome inventor works out of Auberdine. While scouting Darkshore's waterways after too many drinks, he blacked out. Hours later, he woke with singed hair and an empty pack. His electropellers had tumbled into Darkshore's freshwater currents, where they remain scattered through rivers and lakes until patient anglers recover them.

item:elixir-of-pain.text: Elixir of Pain. Forsaken apothecaries at Tarren Mill brew the Elixir of Pain for dangerous experiments. The mixture tests biological agents meant to advance Lady Sylvanas's darker ambitions. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks formulas to strengthen the Forsaken against their mortal neighbors and the Scourge. The Elixir of Pain is one such trial, made with freshly harvested ingredients from around the Hillsbrad Foothills. Its living subjects matter little to its makers; the potion tests volatile substances meant to aid the Dark Lady.

item:elixir-of-suffering.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon brews an experimental draught for the Royal Apothecary Society. Its work aims to create a virulent plague against living humans and the Scourge. Apothecary Lydon gathers raw reagents from the wilderness around ruined Tarren Mill and combines them into toxic draughts. The work follows the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching mandate to formulate a new plague that will exterminate the living and the dead alike. To test the brew's potency, Lydon gives it to his assistant, a frog named Umpi.

item:elune-s-tear.text: Elune's Tear. On Ashenvale's central island, Elune's Tear offers night elf healers a sacred means to cleanse corruption and sickness. Elune's Tear rests on a small islet in Iris Lake, east of Astranaar. Night elves believe the stone carries the Moon Goddess's purity. Corruption has turned the lake green, and twisted bog beasts roam its shores. Local herbalists and healers, including Orendil Broadleaf, seek the stone as an emergency remedy when ordinary woodland poultices cannot wash away deep corruption.

item:embalming-ichor.text: Embalming Ichor. In northern Tirisfal, Rot Hide gnolls carry a fluid that preserves their decaying bodies. The Forsaken Apothecaries seek to study it against the Scourge. Rot Hide gnolls at Garren's Haunt and the nearby mass graves are rotting thralls sent by the Scourge to dig up plague victims. Embalming Ichor flows through their decayed veins, preserving their flesh and sustaining their unlife. Magistrate Sevren in Brill wants vials recovered from these grave robbers. The Royal Apothecary Society will use fresh specimens to study the fluid and seek ways to turn it against the Lich King's minions.

item:emerald-dreamcatcher.text: Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Starbreeze Village, the Emerald Dreamcatcher lies forgotten after the Gnarlpine furbolgs drove out its people. Druids of Ban’ethil Barrow Den gave it to Tallonkai Swiftroot, hoping it would draw vigor from the Emerald Dream. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druidic warden of Ban’ethil Barrow Den, oversaw the making of the Emerald Dreamcatcher. The druids gave the enchanted amulet to only a chosen few. It draws ambient energy from the Emerald Dream, bringing fortune and protection to whoever carries it. When the maddened Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Starbreeze Village, the amulet remained inside a dresser, stranded in hostile, corrupted territory.

item:empty-blue-waterskin.text: Empty Blue Waterskin. Brine sends the Empty Blue Waterskin north from the Barrens to gather sacred water. The liquid will help her prepare the draught needed to summon and appease the water spirit. Brine gives the Empty Blue Waterskin to a shaman initiate at her hilltop hut in the southern Barrens. The vessel marks the final and most perilous gathering task of early training. To commune with the spirit of water, the initiate must seek pure, undisturbed sources across Kalimdor. The waterskin is meant for a secluded fountain deep within the Ruins of Stardust, along Ashenvale's contested borderlands. The initiate must leave the safety of Horde territory and travel into ancient groves guarded by nature beasts and night elves. At a fountain in the ruined sanctuary deep within the Ruins of Stardust, the waterskin is filled and becomes a Filled Blue Waterskin. With water samples from the Barrens and Tarren Mill, its contents let Brine brew the draught needed to summon and appease the elemental spirit of water.

item:empty-brown-waterskin.text: Empty Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, Brine gives an empty waterskin to a shaman initiate. Brine gives a shaman initiate an empty leather skin for the opening trial of the Call of Water. The initiate must carry it to the watering hole beneath her dwelling and return with it full. The pool is guarded by local quilboar, who prize its water. In the Barrens, where water is scarce, even a small oasis can sustain life and spark violence.

item:empty-cleansing-bowl.text: Empty Cleansing Bowl. At Auberdine, the Empty Cleansing Bowl carries moonwell water against the Blackwood corruption. Mixed with food samples, the water makes a meal that briefly breaks the satyrs’ demonic sway over the furbolgs. Thundris Windweaver gives the Empty Cleansing Bowl to adventurers in Auberdine to carry sacred water from the local moonwell. The night elves have learned that satyrs use enchanted talismans to drive the northern Blackwood furbolgs into demonic madness. Dip the bowl into the moonwell, then mix the water with nuts, grains, and fruits gathered from the furbolgs. The blessed meal briefly restores the afflicted creatures’ sanity and reveals the satyr overseer responsible.

item:empty-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Empty Cliffspring Falls Sampler. At Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, young druids gather water to investigate a poison killing local wildlife. The Cenarion Circle gives them empty samplers for water from the cave mouth. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore, so trouble in its headwaters threatens the local wildlife. When a wasting poison began killing the region’s deer, Dendrite Starblaze of the Cenarion Circle gave empty samplers to young druids sent from Moonglade. They must reach the cliffs by the falls and gather water at a cave entrance overrun by hostile naga.

item:empty-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Empty Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, druids seek tainted water in an empty Cenarion vessel. The sample may help diagnose and cure the blight spreading among wildlife in the northern Barrens. Dendrite Starblaze suspects the pools atop Dreadmist Peak are at the heart of a sickness afflicting gazelles and unsettling the northern Barrens. The pools influence the weather, and the druid fears they are tied to the spreading blight. He sends druid initiates with empty samplers to brave the mountain heights and draw water from the peak. The Burning Blade, a demon-worshipping cult, now infests the mountain.

item:empty-leaden-collection-phial.text:
Empty Leaden Collection Phial. Ozzie Togglevolt gathers Gnomeregan’s radioactive fallout in a leaden phial. He hopes the residue may help cure his afflicted kin, or make an extraordinarily potent drink. Ozzie Togglevolt made a leaden phial to gather the radiation left in Gnomeregan. The city’s vents once flooded its tunnels with toxic radiation to purge the trogg menace. The surviving defenders became leper gnomes, and the invading beasts were irradiated.

Green light still clings to Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers prowling the ruins. The lead shields the handler as the phial draws in the dangerous residue. Once sealed, the collection becomes a Full Leaden Collection Phial for Ozzie’s experiments.

item:empty-red-waterskin.text: Empty Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, an empty red waterskin is bound for a well untouched by blight. Brine gives it to shaman initiates for their elemental trials. Brine gives shaman initiates this plain red skin for the Call of Water trials. They carry it across the sea to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The Forsaken occupy the town, but its central well still draws fresh spring water. The filled skin brings a sample to Brine, who blends the water into a vial of purest water for the initiate’s trial.

item:empty-sampling-tube.text: Empty Sampling Tube. Thundris Windweaver gives an Empty Sampling Tube in Auberdine to gather water from the Cliffspring River. Night elf scholars study the taint threatening Darkshore. Darkshore's waterways are turning foul as blight spreads through the wilderness. Thundris Windweaver, an investigator in Auberdine, gives you an empty glass tube to collect water from the Cliffspring River. Take the sample from the pool beneath the first waterfall north of town. Night elf naturalists examine it to learn about the corruption flowing toward Mist's Edge.

item:empty-water-tube.text: Empty Water Tube. In Auberdine, the Empty Water Tube is ready to gather sacred moonwell water for the red crystal on Darkshore’s eastern cliffs. Sentinels and scholars seek pure lunar essence to study the mysterious red crystal along Darkshore’s eastern ridge. Ordinary glass or flasks can contaminate consecrated water, so investigators visiting Auberdine’s moonwell receive this sealed vial for the work. They carry its filled contents up the mountain slopes to learn how the alien mineral responds to Elune’s magic.

item:enchanted-gaea-seeds.text: Enchanted Gaea Seeds. At Sun Rock Retreat, Enchanted Gaea Seeds are prepared for the Charred Vale. Druidic magic gives them strength to take root in ash-choked soil and begin restoring Kalimdor's ravaged land. The Horde's druids are trying to heal the deep scars across Stonetalon Mountains. At Sun Rock Retreat, Tammra Windfield enchants raw Gaea Seeds so they can withstand corruption and elemental blight. Planted in the fertile dirt mounds beneath the Charred Vale's soot, they take root despite the harsh land. Hostile fire elementals and invasive harpies still dominate the vale. Planting the seeds is part of the struggle for Stonetalon's future. Their enchanted husks resist lingering corruption and give native plants a foothold. The returning vegetation is meant to soothe agitated fire elementals, crowd out feral harpies, and counter the deforestation caused by the Venture Company's relentless logging.

item:enchanted-resonite-crystal.text: Enchanted Resonite Crystal. In Stonetalon, Mor'rogal has altered resonite crystals with shamanic magic. The Enchanted Resonite Crystal is made to break the cask holding Goggeroc. Deep in the caverns of the Stonetalon Mountains, raw resonite crystals carry unusual harmonic and earthen properties. Shaman Mor'rogal sensed danger sleeping inside a sealed underground cask and altered the minerals with his elemental powers. The Enchanted Resonite Crystal can break the reinforced Resonite cask and rouse Goggeroc, a giant Earthen, while he is still dazed from his long sleep.

item:encrypted-memorandum.text: Encrypted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, the Encrypted Memorandum quietly guides new rogues to their trainer. Solm Hargrin disguises his invitation as official communication and calls scoundrels in exile to stand together. In Anvilmar, rogues keep their presence quiet. Their trainer, Solm Hargrin, reaches recruits through the Encrypted Memorandum instead of approaching them in plain view. The coded parchment looks like a directive from distant superiors. It tells fledgling rogues where to find a mentor while keeping local guards and suspicious townsfolk from noticing.

item:encrypted-parchment.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment guides young orc rogues toward the Den. Gornek hands it to recruits who show promise, and its cipher points them to Rwag, the hidden trainer. Young orcs prove their strength in the Valley of Trials under the open sun. Those who show a gift for stealth, deception, and bladecraft draw different notice. After facing the local wildlife, promising orc rogues receive Encrypted Parchment from Gornek. Its coded words call to those who can read a message meant to stay hidden. The cipher leads a novice into the Den, past the other clan trainers, to find Rwag. The recruit learns there that the Shattered Hand arranged the summons. The order works within the Horde's covert network, and answering the call begins a rogue's training in espionage and shadowcraft.

item:encrypted-rune.text: Encrypted Rune. In Coldridge Valley, the Encrypted Rune calls promising new rogues to Anvilmar. Its message bids them decipher the words and seek out Solm Hargrin. A new rogue must read thieves' cant to understand the rune. In doing so, they meet the shadowy craft needed to survive Dun Morogh's harsh wilderness. Its ciphers bear a private summons from Solm Hargrin, the rogue mentor in Anvilmar, for those who show promise in stealth and cunning. Deciphering the rune leads new rogues to Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. He hopes to strengthen the valley's covert ranks as local tensions rise. Solm teaches bladecraft and stealth, but also vigilance and camaraderie. With peace strained, rogues need to stand together.

item:encrypted-scroll.text: Encrypted Scroll. In Deathknell, an Encrypted Scroll calls a newly risen rogue to training. Sealed by David Trias, it directs its bearer to meet him at the inn and begin training among the Forsaken’s covert operatives. In Deathknell, a newly awakened Forsaken with a gift for stealth draws notice. The Encrypted Scroll is handed over after a scout proves capable against the mindless Scourge in the nearby graveyard. Sealed by rogue trainer David Trias, it tells the bearer to find him at the local inn. The summons points a fledgling operative toward the discipline needed to serve the Dark Lady, rather than spend a second chance at life as a pickpocket. The scroll’s brief message tells the rogue to make contact in Deathknell before traveling deeper into Tirisfal Glades. Trias watches for promising talent on behalf of the Shadowstalkers, the Forsaken’s covert arm. In Lordaeron, the Forsaken rely on silent blades and cunning scouts against the Scarlet Crusade, surviving Alliance enclaves, and the Scourge left behind. Answering the ciphered summons begins the path toward joining that covert network.

item:encrypted-sigil.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Encrypted Sigil carries a summons to newly awakened night elf rogues. Frahun Shadewhisper calls them to begin training as dangers gather around Teldrassil. New night elf scouts and infiltrators in Shadowglen receive the Encrypted Sigil through discreet means. A quiet messenger delivers it on behalf of Frahun Shadewhisper. Its contents are hidden instructions that tell the initiate to report to Frahun near Aldrassil. Reading and delivering the token shows Frahun that an initiate can follow subtle directions and handle covert messages. Frahun uses the summons to explain why rogues matter in an unsettled world. Tensions simmer between the night elves and the distant Horde, but open warfare is not the only danger facing their people. Rogues must gather intelligence across Teldrassil as the Kaldorei’s unseen eyes and blades, and learn to strike before threats take root in the World Tree’s boughs.

item:encrypted-tablet.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Encrypted Tablet sends novice troll rogues to Rwag. The rogue trainer inscribes its coded message and keeps his post inside the Den. Novice troll rogues receive the Encrypted Tablet when they arrive in the Valley of Trials. Its ciphered words direct them to Rwag, an orc trainer who lives in the Den’s shaded caves. The slate keeps the local shadow operatives’ business discreet while testing whether new recruits can understand its message. Deciphering the tablet brings recruits into contact with the Horde’s wider shadow network. When they report to Rwag, scouts learn that syndicates such as the Shattered Hand watch their progress. The syndicates rely on valley trainers to judge whether prospective cutpurses, spies, and assassins are sharp enough to serve the new nation.

item:essence-of-nightlash.text: Essence of Nightlash. At the Dead Fields, Nightlash's defeat leaves a trace the Forsaken can carry away. High Executor Hadrec needs it as proof that the Scourge force behind the rot hide gnolls has been broken. At the abandoned farmstead called the Dead Fields in northern Silverpine, packs of undead rot hide gnolls have dug in under Scourge command. Forsaken assaults have failed again and again, not because of the feral gnolls, but because their spectral commander, Nightlash, turns them back. Her wailing magic strengthens the gnoll lines and routs forces sent from the Sepulcher. When Nightlash is slain, her incorporeal form dissolves into dust, leaving a crystalline magical essence behind. Banshees leave no bodily corpse, so Nightlash's essence is the only physical proof that the spirit has been destroyed. High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher needs it to confirm that the Scourge foothold has fallen. With that proof, the Forsaken can secure their northern perimeter and suppress the rot hide threat.

item:essential-artificial.text:
Essential Artificial. In Ironforge, Essential Artificial parts help gnomish tinkers and engineers rebuild after exile. The gnomes left stockpiles behind when they fled Gnomeregan. Before Gnomeregan fell, tinkers relied on the Essential Artificial as a component for many uses. Gnomish engineers fitted it into contraptions, clockwork wonders and heavy machinery throughout the subterranean halls. Its standard design let smiths and machinists exchange parts with confidence. The trogg invasion and radiation disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan in a desperate rush. Large stores of Essential Artificial parts remained in heavy, steam-powered dispensers called artificial extrapolators, scattered through the deeper passages.

In Tinker Town, master craftsman Klockmort Spannerspan seeks daring adventurers to return to the contaminated ruins and recover the parts. He needs them so research and invention can continue.

item:etched-note.text: Etched Note. At Camp Narache, the Etched Note calls a young tauren hunter to begin training. Lanka Farshot, the camp's hunter trainer, welcomes the novice to the traditions of the hunt. At Camp Narache, a runner brings young shu'halo a message from Lanka Farshot, the camp's hunter trainer. The note names the hunter the heart of the tribe. It also warns that natural instinct needs rigorous instruction and deep respect for Mulgore's wilderness. For the tauren, hunting is a sacred discipline and a way of survival, woven into tribal life. Hunters join the work of warriors, shamans and druids, and the tribe looks to them for guidance and protection. The student presents the note to Lanka to begin learning weaponcraft and how to understand beasts, preparing to defend and sustain the tribes.

item:etched-parchment.text: Etched Parchment. Gornek gives hunters in the Valley of Trials a summons from Jen'shan. The Etched Parchment points them toward their first lessons in Durotar. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls begin their rites in the Valley of Trials. As recruits prove themselves against the local vermin, Gornek guides them toward their calling. He gives the Etched Parchment to those who will wield bow, gun, and fang. Its message comes from Jen'shan, a skilled hunter trainer seeking fresh eyes and steady hands. Taking the parchment to Jen'shan begins a hunter's training in Durotar. She teaches that the wild path takes dedication: mastering the beasts of the desert demands as much effort as an arcanist's magic or a shaman's work with the spirits. Her summons brings new hunters to lessons in marksmanship and wilderness survival.

item:etched-rune.text: Etched Rune. In Coldridge Valley, the Etched Rune calls promising dwarven hunters to Anvilmar. Hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson sends it to begin their instruction in the wilderness. Dwarven runes mark the Etched Rune, sent to novices who show promise in Coldridge Valley’s snowdrifts. Mountaineer and hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson calls fledgling trackers to Anvilmar. There, they move beyond basic survival and learn the hunter’s craft: respect for Dun Morogh’s beasts, tracking mountain predators, care for ranged weapons, and endurance in the harsh elements.

item:etched-sigil.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls new night elf hunters to their trainer. Newly awakened night elf hunters receive the Etched Sigil as they enter Shadowglen. Its carved marks of the hunt carry a welcome and summons from Ayanna Everstride, the hunter trainer who lives high in Aldrassil’s hollowed boughs. The token sends each novice to seek her out and begin instruction in archery, wilderness tracking, and the night elf bond between stalker and beast.

item:explosive-stick-of-gann.text: Explosive Stick of Gann. In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire turns stolen dwarven plans against Bael Modan. He built the charge to sabotage the dwarves’ flying machine. When Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor, the dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm’s blueprints to avenge his displaced and fallen kin. He studied the plans and assembled a charge with enough force to wreck heavy machinery.

item:faded-shadowhide-pendant.text: Faded Shadowhide Pendant. A voice now comes from the Faded Shadowhide Pendant, found in the Redridge Mountains. The Shadowhide gnolls wore it to receive orders from Morganth, and the delayed message is a spell cast by Theocritus. The Shadowhide gnolls of the Redridge Mountains follow Morganth and coordinate their movements through enchanted pendants. From his sanctuary at Tower Azora, High Mage Theocritus studied the talismans and devised a spell to breach their magical link. His broadcast took weeks to appear. This faded pendant proves the gnolls’ communication can be intercepted, giving Theocritus a way to disrupt Morganth’s reach.

item:fallen-moonstone.text: Fallen Moonstone. At Fallen Sky Lake in Ashenvale, night elves gather luminous, magically charged Fallen Moonstones from its tranquil waters. Sacred lunar energy gives the stones restorative power that can renew vitality and cure severe frailty. Southeast of Astranaar, Fallen Sky Lake once yielded many stones along its shores and shallows. Night elves prized their restorative magic and lunar blessing when ordinary remedies failed. Gathering them grew dangerous after corrupt Shadethicket bog beasts overran the lake. Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, hoarded every stone it found on a small island at the lake’s center, cutting the local Kaldorei off from a vital source of healing.

item:fandral-s-message.text: Fandral's Message. In Darnassus, Fandral Staghelm sends a message across the sea to Onu in Darkshore. The sealed dispatch carries news about Oracle Glade in Teldrassil. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm writes from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. His sealed dispatch is addressed to Onu, the Ancient of Lore who dwells in the Grove of the Ancients. Reports have reached Fandral about the state of Oracle Glade in Teldrassil, and he sends a courier south of Auberdine with word for Onu. The journey crosses the waters to Darkshore, carrying a message from the heart of the new World Tree to Kalimdor’s older, shadowed mainland.

item:fang-of-vagash.text: Fang of Vagash. In Dun Morogh, Vagash stalks the rams above Amberstill Ranch. His fang proves the deadly predator has been slain. Above Amberstill Ranch, Vagash hunts the rams under cover of darkness. The high crags shelter fierce predators, but none has troubled the local ranches as much as he has. Ironforge’s troops are stretched thin, so the herdsmen go without the city guard’s protection. His severed fang gives the breeders proof that Vagash is dead and their pasturelands are safe again.

item:fangore-s-paw.text: Fangore's Paw. In the Redridge Mountains, Lieutenant Fangore leads the Shadowhide gnolls against Lakeshire. His severed paw proves his death to Magistrate Solomon, whose bounty seeks to end the threat Fangore poses to the besieged town. Lieutenant Fangore is a primary field commander among the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching across the Redridge Mountains. He serves the renegade mage Morganth and directs attacks on trade roads, outlying farms, and the defenses around Lake Everstill. Gnoll raiders leave no uniforms, official seals, or banners to confirm their dead, so the township authorities rely on physical proof. Magistrate Solomon demanded Fangore's paw to prove he had been executed, giving Lakeshire some relief amid the dangers closing around the town.

item:farren-s-report.text: Farren's Report. In Southshore, Farren's Report carries Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's findings on the local naga. He hopes the dispatch will win him a return to Stormwind. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew tired of Southshore's embattled coast, its local leadership, and its remote frontier. He had adventurers hunt the Daggerspine naga to gather proof of their threat, then gathered the findings into a formal report. Farren plans to send it to Major Samuelson, captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep, rather than to his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath. Samuelson trained Farren, and Farren hopes the report will show his competence and earn him an immediate transfer back to Stormwind City's comforts.

item:fathom-core.text: Fathom Core. Beneath the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core records the elements at work in Blackfathom Deeps. The Earthen Ring seeks it to learn how the Twilight's Hammer is manipulating those forces. The Fathom Core rests inside an ancient fathom stone beneath the Moonshrine Ruins. It records shifts, disruptions, and surges in the elements over time. Je'neu Sancrea, an Earthen Ring shaman at Zoram'gar Outpost, seeks the core to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cultists are turning the region's elements to their own ends.

item:feather-charm.text: Feather Charm. In Anvilmar, Feather Charms catch a warlock instructor’s eye. Frostmane novices carry these crude trinkets, which hold a faint magical power. Southwest of Anvilmar, Frostmane novices carry feather charms through snowy caverns. Their tribe is known for territorial savagery, yet its young trolls practice primitive spellcraft. The charms hold a faint but unmistakable power. Alamar Grimm, the warlock instructor in Anvilmar, studies this crude trollcraft with interest. He uses the charms to test fledgling warlocks as they seek to bind their first imp.

item:fel-cone.text: Fel Cone. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones carry corruption into the forest. Night elf defenders put the pods to use against nearby tricksters. Beneath Teldrassil's boughs, Fel Cones show that corruption has reached the young tree. Gnarled and fallen, the pine cones billow foul green smoke. They lie scattered just east of Dolanaar. Tainted magic has warped the surrounding flora, and the pods are dangerous to touch or eat without caution.

item:fel-moss.text: Fel Moss. Fel Moss spreads through Teldrassil’s forests, its insidious corruptive energies carried by hostile grell and grellkin. The taint threatens the World Tree’s wildlife and native furbolg tribes. Corruption has reached Teldrassil’s boughs, though the World Tree was planted to restore the night elves’ immortality and heal the natural world. Fel Moss is one clear sign of that decay. Impish grell and grellkin infest Shadowglen, with the unnatural, wicked magic of the moss clinging to them and radiating from their growth. The dryad Tarindrella gathers samples to measure how deeply the rot has entered the sacred woodland canopy.

item:felix-s-box.text: Felix's Box. In Frostmane camps southwest of Anvilmar, Felix's Box lies far from the gnome refugee who lost it. Radiation swept through Gnomeregan during the failed attempt to purge the trogg menace. Felix Whindlebolt fled with the gnomes into Coldridge Valley, leaving his possessions and crafting gear along the snowy road to escape the fumes. Frostmane trolls plundered the goods before he could return. They carried his box, chest, and bucket of bolts to their settlements southwest of Anvilmar. Felix is unused to violence and poorly suited to Dun Morogh's wilderness. He needs passing adventurers in Anvilmar to help recover his belongings. Their return would restore some normalcy and give the displaced artisan the means to earn a living. He lost everything when Gnomeregan fell.

item:felix-s-bucket-of-bolts.text: Felix's Bucket of Bolts. In Dun Morogh, Frostmane trolls carry Felix's Bucket of Bolts to their camps. Felix Whindlebolt is missing the tools he brought from Gnomeregan. Felix Whindlebolt fled Gnomeregan with his tools after the disaster with the troggs. Radiation drove thousands of gnomes into Dun Morogh's freezing wilds with whatever they could carry. Felix headed for Anvilmar, but Frostmane trolls from the crags southwest of town ambushed him. They seized his belongings, including his bucket of bolts and parts, leaving the artisan without the materials he needs for his craft in exile.

item:felix-s-chest.text: Felix's Chest. In a Frostmane camp southwest of Anvilmar, Felix's Chest holds what he lost fleeing Gnomeregan. When troggs and toxic radioactive fallout drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan, refugees crossed snowy Dun Morogh carrying what they could. Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook scattered survivors. They took Felix Whindlebolt's sturdy chest to their camps in the crags, where his toolkits and personal belongings remain among their supplies.

item:felstalker-hoof.text: Felstalker Hoof. In Durotar's Valley of Trials, young shaman face demonic felstalkers as a test of readiness. Their hooves are brought to Canaga Earthcaller before they learn to commune with the earth spirits. Canaga Earthcaller sends young shaman against the demonic taint threatening Durotar. The Burning Blade Coven lies north in the Valley of Trials, where felstalkers roam among the coven's vile familiars. Taking a felstalker's hoof tests a shaman's endurance, resolve, and spirit. Those who subdue the beasts prove ready to receive the secrets of the earth and prepare the ceremonial sapta for communing with elemental spirits.

item:fenwick-s-head.text: Fenwick's Head. Forsaken rogues seek Fenwick Thatros along the shores of Lordamere Lake. His head is proof of his execution, claimed on orders passed down from Lord Varimathras. Mennet Carkad acts from the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity on urgent intelligence from dreadlord Varimathras. Fenwick Thatros, a hostile undead leader, has established a foothold near the decaying docks along Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. To keep him from rallying hostile undead against the Forsaken, Carkad sends promising Deathstalkers to find and kill him, then bring back his head as proof. For Deathstalker operatives, bringing Fenwick's Head to Carkad is a trial beyond collecting a bounty. The severed head proves a rogue's skill in infiltration and assassination. Success opens the way to deeper, more specialized instruction in the shadow arts from Forsaken masters.

item:fey-dragon-scale.text: Fey Dragon Scale. Around Stonetalon Peak, faerie dragons yield scales coveted by Jin'Zil. The Darkspear witch doctor uses one as a reagent in a brew that mocks night elven nature magic. Around Stonetalon Peak, faerie dragons haunt the wild groves of Kalimdor. Their scales gleam with natural magic. Night elves revere them as harmless woodland spirits and allies, while outsiders prize the scales as rare magical ingredients.

item:filled-amethyst-phial.text: Filled Amethyst Phial. In Teldrassil, water from the Oracle Tree's moonwell fills an amethyst phial. Corithras Moonrage receives it for the Cenarion druids to study the World Tree's troubled growth. The Oracle Glade lies in northwest Teldrassil, where the oldest and most potent moonwell rests beneath the Oracle Tree. Other moonwells across the boughs meet the night elves' daily needs, but the water here carries the raw essence of Elune's grace. Druids who watch over the World Tree's health collect it in amethyst phials, preserving it for testing and ritual cleansing.

item:filled-blue-waterskin.text: Filled Blue Waterskin. Shamans gather water for their trials at the Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale. The Filled Blue Waterskin carries a pristine sample from the ancient fountain. Call of Water initiates cross north from the Barrens into Ashenvale's dense forests. Beyond Lake Mystral, the Ruins of Stardust lie against the mountains dividing Ashenvale from Stonetalon. Fierce forest beasts guard the secluded elven sanctuary. At the center of its lake, an untouched fountain holds water untainted by corruption or drought. A blue waterskin filled from its basin carries the sample sought by shaman masters for ritual attunement. Brine, a hermit and water expert, lives on a hill in the southern Barrens and needs this final sample. He combines it with water from contrasting wells and springs, then distills the pure essence into an offering. The offering can manifest and soothe the elemental spirits of water, completing an initiate's trial.

item:filled-brown-waterskin.text: Filled Brown Waterskin. In the Barrens, the Filled Brown Waterskin carries fresh water from the pond below Brine's hut. Aspiring shaman bring it to her to begin brewing sapta, used to commune with water spirits. The pond beneath Brine's hut is a rare source of fresh water in the Barrens. Nearby quilboar fight fiercely over it, and a novice shaman sees how scarce water can drive creatures to defend what sustains them.

item:filled-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler. Near Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore, the Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler holds foul water drawn from the headwaters. The Cenarion Circle needs it to study the sickness striking local deer. Cliffspring Falls feeds much of Darkshore with water from the eastern highlands. Local deer have recently fallen ill with an unnatural sickness. At Dendrite Starblaze’s request in Moonglade, druidic initiates draw water from a cave mouth where hostile naga dwell. The liquid in the vial is visibly foul, showing that the fresh water supply is tainted.

item:filled-containment-coffer.text: Filled Containment Coffer. In the Undercity, Forsaken spellcasters use Filled Containment Coffers to capture erratic magical entities. A Cantation of Manifestation reveals and weakens rift spawn in the Apothecarium, so mages can seal them inside for examination. Magical disturbances have appeared in Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium. The Forsaken mage Anastasia Hartwell has called on arcane practitioners to capture the entities behind them. Rift creatures are living magical energy and cannot be seen, so ordinary cages cannot hold them. Spellcasters reveal them with a Cantation of Manifestation, defeat them in combat, and snap prepared coffers shut around them. The sealed boxes protect their carriers from volatile magical backlashes and keep the creatures intact for magical dissection. Living mana creatures in the Undercity pose a serious threat. Once sealed inside containment coffers, the beasts are carried to Anastasia Hartwell and the city's scholars. Forsaken mages seek to learn whether the intrusions come from natural rifts in Azeroth's magical fabric or are preliminary probes in a calculated magical assault on the kingdom.

item:filled-crystal-phial.text: Filled Crystal Phial. In Shadowglen, the Filled Crystal Phial holds water drawn from the moonwell north of Aldrassil. Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to gather it as a first lesson in Teldrassil’s sacred power. Tenaron Stormgrip sends young night elves to gather moonwell water before they venture into the wider world. The moonwell lies in Shadowglen, and its waters hold more than spring water: they carry energies traced to the ancient Well of Eternity. Sentinels honor moonwells as shrines of Elune, while druids use their restorative power to tend nature. The arcane sorcery of old remains forbidden. Gathering the water begins a lesson in the sacrifice at Mount Hyjal and the care needed to nurture Teldrassil.

item:filled-cursed-ooze-jar.text: Filled Cursed Ooze Jar. In Felwood, a Filled Cursed Ooze Jar carries a sample for Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. The gnome scholar seeks the ancient origins of slimes across Azeroth. Laris Geardawdle, a gnome researcher, sees mystery in the vile puddles and caustic slimes others pass by. Slimes thrive across Azeroth, and Forsaken apothecaries gather them with care. These sights led Geardawdle to a bold theory: oozes may be primordial secretions bound to Azeroth's creation. To gather a sample, brave Felwood's blighted woods and defeat a cursed ooze. Scoop its acidic remains into an empty jar before they dissolve. Laris Geardawdle hopes his ooze samples will bring knowledge and a lasting name. A major discovery could secure his reputation in the dwarven-led Explorers' League. Since Gnomeregan fell, many gnome refugees in Ironforge have felt pressed to prove their worth to their dwarven hosts. Geardawdle believes that uncovering ooze's ancient secrets will show them that welcoming gnomes was no mistake.

item:filled-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler. At Dreadmist Peak, a filled sampler holds water gathered by Horde druids from the summit pools. The Cenarion Circle studies the sample to learn what is poisoning wildlife in the northern Barrens. Dreadmist Peak’s high crags hold pools whose mists shape weather and rainfall across the northern Barrens. The Burning Blade, who worship demons, made their coven atop the summit, and the water soon soured. Cenarion druids suspect demonic rites poisoned the vapors that feed the surrounding savanna. They send initiates to collect a sample in a special sampler. The foul liquid confirms their fears: its corruption can sicken the herds below.

item:filled-etched-phial.text: Filled Etched Phial. In Thunder Bluff, the tauren seek a dryad phial filled with moonwell water. Its rare spiritual power can quench the eternal flame shielding a sacred centaur relic. To fill the phial, you must enter night elf territory deep in Ashenvale. Dryads around Raynewood Retreat carry the empty vessels, crafted to hold pure restorative draughts. A sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River fills the phial with water rich in celestial and nature-bound power. Night elves regard taking it without leave as desecration. The tauren see the water as vital to meeting a threat farther south.

item:filled-jade-phial.text: Filled Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, the Filled Jade Phial is carried back with sacred water from Starbreeze Village. The water helps replenish the central wells while young night elves learn their people's history. Druids in Darnassus draw sacred moonwell water from across Teldrassil to replenish their central wells. Corithras Moonrage entrusts young travelers in Dolanaar with a jade phial made to hold the pure water safely. The moonwell outside Starbreeze Village lies east of Dolanaar. Initiates collect its water as they tend the World Tree. When you bring the Filled Jade Phial back to Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage shares another chapter of kaldorei history. He tells of the years after the Third War, when Nordrassil burned, night elves lost their immortality, the Betrayer was released, and Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared.

item:filled-pure-sample-jar.text: Filled Pure Sample Jar. In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle studies how corruption changes living matter. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze from the remote wilds, giving him a clean specimen for comparison. Laris Geardawdle studies oozes across Azeroth and how corruption changes living matter. He found that these shapeless creatures absorb the magic and conditions of their homes, then reflect them. After cataloging tainted slimes in Felwood, he sought a clean sample for comparison. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze gathered from the wilds of Un'Goro Crater, away from corrupted strains. Oozes change readily, so Laris cannot find pure samples near civilization, demonic blights, or necromantic fallout. The glutinous oozes of Un'Goro Crater's untamed basin remain relatively isolated from outside corruption. That makes them a useful standard for scholars in Ironforge.

item:filled-red-waterskin.text: Filled Red Waterskin. In Tarren Mill, a well gives clear spring water for a shaman’s trial. The Filled Red Waterskin carries water drawn from the village well, amid ruins held by the Forsaken. Brine, a hermit in the Barrens, sends shaman initiates to Tarren Mill for water training. The journey leads to the Hillsbrad Foothills, where decay and the dead surround the town. Yet the central well still draws clear spring water. Brine sees this pure water as a sign of endurance in an unhallowed land. She compares the uncorrupted spring with Warchief Thrall’s resolve through hardship. Gathering the water tests an initiate’s respect for its purity, even in hostile surroundings.

item:filled-tainted-ooze-jar.text:
Filled Tainted Ooze Jar. In Felwood, a Filled Tainted Ooze Jar carries samples of corruption to Ironforge. The samples may help explain how life began on Azeroth. Across northern Kalimdor, tainted oozes bear Felwood’s lingering corruption. Gnomish researchers provide jars to hold them safely. Most travelers keep clear of these noxious creatures, yet their remains yield samples for natural philosophy and biological study far from the blighted woods. Laris Geardawdle, a gnome scholar with the Explorers' League in Ironforge, gathers the samples. The commonness of slimes fascinates him, and he has seen the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society take an interest in them too.

Many scholars dismiss Geardawdle's theory. He believes slimes and oozes may be primal secretions tied to Azeroth's creation. He seeks proof, and a place among dwarven scholars after Gnomeregan's tragic fall.

item:filled-tourmaline-phial.text: Filled Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, the Filled Tourmaline Phial carries moonwell water for Corithras Moonrage. Its waters help him watch the health and balance of the growing World Tree. The Filled Tourmaline Phial draws water from a moonwell southeast of the road to Darnassus, on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. Reaching the shrine has grown dangerous as the Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful neighbors, turn violently mad. Corithras Moonrage asks travelers to brave the hostile groves and bring back the water. He hopes it will help him find the deepening corruption unsettling the land.

item:filled-vessel.text: Filled Vessel. At Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage gathers sacred waters for Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. The Filled Vessel carries samples from Teldrassil’s moonwells to aid his study of the World Tree’s ailments. Night elf acolytes gather water from moonwells across Teldrassil. The tree was planted without the blessings of the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu, leaving its boughs open to corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes. Corithras Moonrage gathers the phials in Dolanaar and pours them into the Filled Vessel for the journey to the capital. Together, the waters offer a vital sample of Teldrassil’s vitality. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm studies them in the Cenarion Enclave, seeking a remedy for the Great Tree’s flaws.

item:final-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure. Along Westfall’s coast, Captain Sanders’ final directions send scavengers out to sea. A note in an old jug points west toward his buried treasure. Captain Sanders left his final directions in an old whiskey jug on the Westfall coast. The pirate had scattered cryptic notes along the shoreline, and this one completes the trail. From the jug, the directions point due west into the ocean. Follow them through the surf to a lonely offshore rock, where his ironbound sea chest lies.

item:fine-crab-chunks.text: Fine Crab Chunks. Fine Crab Chunks come from the Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers along Darkshore's coast. Gubber Blump seeks them for his cooking. Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers roam Darkshore's shores. Travelers may see them as pests or dangers by the water, while cooks prize their meat. The chunks can be boiled, broiled, fried, or added to stews.

item:fine-moonstalker-pelt.text: Fine Moonstalker Pelt. In southern Darkshore, mature moonstalkers carry the hides Terenthis needs. Their Fine Moonstalker Pelt is thick and healthy enough for an enchanted cloak that helps searchers pass the region’s hostile beasts unnoticed. Moonstalker sires and matriarchs have coats dense and healthy enough to yield a fine pelt. They hold territories along the Wildbend River and farther south toward Ashenvale’s borders, where they hunt with patience. Common moonstalkers prowl across Darkshore’s forests, but their hides are not fine enough.

item:fire-tar.text: Fire Tar. Across the eastern Barrens, Razormane spellcasters carry Fire Tar. Horde shamans use it to brew the Fire Sapta, which lets them commune with fire spirits. Razormane geomancers, mystics, and thornweavers carry Fire Tar. The quilboar use the flame-tuned substance in their harsh magic and rituals. Shamanic instructors prize it as a worldly reagent that helps mortal senses reach the raw fury of the elements.
