Young orc and troll shamans travel to Telf Joolam, high among Durotar's crags, to forge their fire totems. Telf asks them for a reagent pouch taken from Burning Blade cultists and Fire Tar gathered from the Razormane. He brews the two ingredients into a fire sapta. Drinking it lets a shaman perceive the fire spirits waiting atop the nearby peaks.

item:fizzle-s-claw.text: Fizzle's Claw. In Thunder Ridge, Fizzle Darkstorm’s claw is carried to Razor Hill as proof of his death. The goblin warlock was a dangerous Burning Blade conspirator. Orgnil Soulscar sent forces to root out shadow cults threatening the orcish homeland. He identified Fizzle Darkstorm as an instigator spreading corruption in Thunder Ridge. The claw gives Horde commanders proof that the warlock, who operated under the Burning Blade’s banner, has been slain. Thunder Ridge lies just northwest of Razor Hill, close enough to threaten the surrounding lands. Horde scouts took Fizzle’s claw back to Razor Hill, confirming that his rituals and attempt to establish a Burning Blade foothold had been stopped.

item:flagongut-s-fossil.text: Flagongut's Fossil. At the Wetlands dig, Flagongut seeks answers in an ancient fossil. The Explorers' League keeps the specimen, and Flagongut believes the Stone of Relu can help him decipher its secrets. Prospector Whelgar keeps the fossil at his excavation site in the southern hills of the Wetlands. Dwarven expeditions across Khaz Modan unearthed it, and Archaeologist Flagongut believes its ancient stone holds forgotten powers. He sees a kinship with artifacts found across the sea in Darkshore.

item:flatland-cougar-femur.text: Flatland Cougar Femur. Across Mulgore, cougars prowl the plains, and Maur Raincaller needs one of their bones. A Flatland Cougar Femur is part of the remedy he seeks for a venomous bite. Flatland cougars rank among Mulgore's most dangerous native stalkers. They blend into the dry brush, then spring upon unsuspecting prey. Hunters take their pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies, while their heavy, marrow-rich bones have use in local medicine. Maur Raincaller of Bloodhoof Village suffered a venomous wound from Mazzranache, a monstrous pink strider. He urgently asked for a cougar femur and parts from other local beasts. Crushed or boiled, the bone yields properties for an antitoxin poultice meant to draw fever and necrotic venom from a festering bite.

item:flatland-prowler-claw.text: Flatland Prowler Claw. Across Mulgore's plains, Flatland Prowler Claws mark a young hunter's trial. Hunters gather them to prove their resolve and fieldcraft to the elders of Thunder Bluff. Flatland prowlers stalk Mulgore's plains, quick to ambush prey in tall grass. Their cunning and territorial nature makes them dangerous to travelers and a hard test for young hunters. Gathering their claws is a recognized tradition. Skorn Whitecloud sends promising wanderers to bring the claws to Melor Stonehoof at Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff, proof that they have the resolve and fieldcraft to follow the hunter's way.

item:foreman-s-blackjack.text: Foreman's Blackjack. Foreman's Blackjack keeps peons at work in Durotar's Valley of Trials. Foremen use the leather-wrapped cosh to wake laborers who fall asleep during the Horde's early construction. Durotar's rugged desert needs stockpiles of lumber for the Horde's new home. In the Valley of Trials, the work falls to the peons, and Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the crews moving with Foreman's Blackjack. The weighted bludgeon delivers a jarring wake-up call to laborers caught napping beneath the valley's shade trees, rather than a lethal blow. Peon life in the new Horde means grueling, unglamorous work under an iron fist.

item:forged-steel-bars.text: Forged Steel Bars. In the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze's steel bars are missing. Recovering them will prove a warrior's resolve to reclaim stolen property. Thun'grim Firegaze, a visually impaired orc smith, keeps a camp in the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar took his iron chest during a night raid, distracting him with grunts and snorts while thieves slipped away. Unable to work fine steel, the quilboar left the unopened chest near a ruined wagon in their encampment to the northwest. The bars remain intact for warriors willing to recover them.

item:fragments-of-rok-alim.text: Fragments of Rok'Alim. Fragments of Rok'Alim are the shattered stone remains of a primeval earth elemental roaming the canyons of Thousand Needles. Brought to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, they serve as undeniable physical proof that a warrior has bested an ancient terror in single combat. While most elementals faded from Azeroth following the banishment of the Old Gods, a handful possessed enough raw power to endure on the surface without being summoned by mortal magic. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such survivor, wandering the canyon flats south of the main thoroughfare. Local centaur know him by the thunderous crashes of his stony fists pulverizing anything foolish enough to wander into his path. Striking down this living remnant of the primordial world yields jagged pieces of dense, animated rock—a trophy fit to prove unmatched physical prowess. For the tauren hermit Dorn Plainstalker, recovering the fragments is the decisive component of the Test of Strength. As part of a series of spiritual and martial rites conducted high within the Weathered Nook, the trial demands that an initiate face an entity of unyielding brute force. Delivering the battered rubble of Rok'Alim proves that an adventurer possesses the bravery and physical might required to survive the harshest perils of Kalimdor.

item:frostwolf-banner.text: Frostwolf Banner. In Alterac Valley, Horde initiates seek the Frostwolf Banner in Wildpaw Cavern. Recovering it is an ancestral rite of passage that awakens their battle spirit and earns their first clan insignia. Horde warriors seeking a place among the Frostwolf clan face a trial of grit in Alterac Valley. Warmaster Laggrond sends new recruits south into Wildpaw Cavern, where territorial gnolls fill the damp, hostile corridors. Reaching the hidden banner and bringing it back unbroken proves their courage and shows their battle rage has awakened. The trial earns each warrior the Frostwolf initiate's insignia.

item:full-leaden-collection-phial.text:
Full Leaden Collection Phial. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt seeks a sample from Gnomeregan’s troggs. He hopes it will cure irradiated leper gnomes, or perhaps make a dangerously potent rum. A lead lining shields the bearer from the volatile green fallout saturating Gnomeregan. High Tinker Mekkatorque’s advisors flooded the lower corridors with toxic radiation to stop the invading troggs. Instead, the disaster corrupted troggs and surviving gnomes into maddened, irradiated horrors.

Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers leave fluid residue for refugee tinkerers in Kharanos. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket use it as raw material in their experiments on remedies.

item:fungal-spores.text: Fungal Spores. Around the Barrens' oases, Fungal Spores gather in swollen mushrooms. The waters quicken the life around them, and the Royal Apothecary Society seeks the spores for its alchemy. The Barrens' oases bring unusual life to the dry plains. At the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis, the water does more than ease thirst. It quickens and changes the plants and wildlife nearby. Mushrooms along the damp shores swell with spores, carrying the waters' concentrated power to spur growth. Naturalists study this change, while the Royal Apothecary Society gathers the mushrooms for its alchemy. Apothecaries abroad gather unusual local ingredients for their laboratories and colleagues. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim sends such reagents onward, including to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The spores are valuable for brewing potent chemical mixtures. Their natural properties have already been altered by the mysterious forces beneath Kalimdor's soil, making them useful to the Forsaken.

item:furen-s-instructions.text: Furen's Instructions. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard gives tested Alliance warriors the list of materials for fire-hardened mail. Furen Longbeard offers a resilient suit of mail to a warrior who has proved himself at simpler smithing work. The dwarven armorer requires the warrior to fetch the rare components himself. His parchment records what is needed and sends the warrior across continents to gather it. The parchment calls for a dangerous journey through the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Dozens of scorched spider fangs come from damp caves in the Wetlands. The hardened links also need horns from fire-breathing chimaeras in the crags of Stonetalon Mountains. The list asks for a galvanized horn from the chimaera matriarch and a vial of volatile phlogiston held deep within Razorfen Kraul, a quilboar bastion.

item:furen-s-notes.text: Furen's Notes. In Stormwind, Furen's Notes carry his discoveries in metallurgy and armorsmithing to Alliance craftsmen. Furen Longbeard forged protective gear for veteran warriors, then sent copies to help fellow smiths refine their work. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Furen Longbeard forges specialized armaments for warriors. As he works, he records his methods and discoveries. Dwarven metalworking keeps changing, so he makes several copies for other smiths to use and build upon. His notes describe ways to temper, reinforce, and shape armor against deadly blows. Furen sends copies to trusted contacts among the Alliance's craftsmen. Grimand Elmore may scoff at a smith he claims to have taught, but the notes still hold useful insights. Some copies cross the Great Sea to night elven craftsmen, including Mathiel on Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace. Shared needs in battle bring their different traditions together.

item:furlbrow-s-deed.text: Furlbrow's Deed. Beside their broken wagon near Westfall's border, Theodore and Verna Furlbrow have lost their farm to the Defias Brotherhood. Their land deed is in bandit hands, and with it went their home and livelihood. Theodore Furlbrow and Verna signed the deed to secure their family farm in Westfall. After the Defias Brotherhood overran the region, bandits drove them from home and carried the deed into Elwynn Forest. Notes on its back show the thieves planned to copy it and forge claims to other properties. The Furlbrows lost their livelihood and took to the road, with no home to return to.

item:furlbrow-s-pocket-watch.text:
Furlbrow's Pocket Watch. In Westfall, Farmer Furlbrow searches for the pocket watch he lost when Defias bandits drove him from home. Verna’s father gave it to him on their wedding day. Defias bandits drove Farmer Furlbrow and Verna from their home at the Furlbrow Pumpkin Patch in the night. In their flight, he left the watch in a wardrobe in the overrun farmhouse. Benny Blaanco and his cutthroats keep watch nearby.

The couple now camps along the road. The watch is one of the few pieces of their former life the outlaws have not ruined.

item:gaea-seed.text: Gaea Seed. Along Mirkfallon Lake, Gaea Seeds offer a way to heal Stonetalon's wounded land. Tauren shamans value the hardy kernels for restoring places scarred by war and industry. Gaea Seeds wash ashore or grow along Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Small and fibrous, they look like coconuts, yet endure harsh conditions. As conflict and industry scar the land, shamans see the seeds as a means to heal it.

item:gaffer-jack.text: Gaffer Jack. Off Auberdine, Gaffer Jack parts lie beneath Darkshore's waves. Wizbang Cranktoggle lost a crate of them during his voyage across the sea. Gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle booked passage to Auberdine, seeking quiet away from Ironforge's forge-works and taverns. During the voyage, he drank too much and fumbled an entire container of gaffer jacks over the railing. The small fasteners sank into Darkshore's coastal waters, leaving Wizbang without the parts he needed to tune his stintle pegs. The gaffer jacks sank in the surf along Darkshore's shore, where patient fishermen sometimes snag them on their hooks. Recovering the parts lets Wizbang assemble his strange contraptions. Finding tiny metal hardware in the open sea takes patience and luck.

item:gallywix-s-head.text: Gallywix's Head. In Orgrimmar, Gallywix's Head proves that a Venture Company overseer was executed. The Shattered Hand demands the trophy as proof of the killing. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix directed the Venture Company's work from its tower north of the Sludge Fen. When word arrived that the Venture Co. planned something on a grand scale, the Shattered Hand sent operatives to dismantle the facility. Bringing Gallywix's head to Shenthul in Orgrimmar proves the overseer was executed and secures the rogue's standing within the guild.

item:galvanized-horn.text: Galvanized Horn. In the Charred Vale, armorers seek Galvanized Horns from chimaera matriarchs. Their hardened growths go into specialized armor for warriors. Chimaera matriarchs prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains. Ash, flame, and survival harden their horns. Fledgling chimaeras yield brittle, blackened horns, but a matriarch’s is strong as treated metal. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff each seek one as a test of martial valor and an ingredient for exceptional mail armor.

item:gargantuan-tumor.text: Gargantuan Tumor. In Teldrassil, a great growth was torn from Oakenscowl, the corrupted timberling by Lake Al'Ameth. The tumor bears witness to sickness spreading among the creatures there. Oakenscowl lurks in a cavern near Lake Al'Ameth's southern bank. Once a noble timberling elder, the creature has fallen to a vile affliction. A huge growth poisoned Oakenscowl, warped its behavior, and spread taint through the surrounding wildlife. The tumor was severed to end the beast's rampage and give local researchers a chance to examine the blight. They hope to learn how the malady took root in the boughs of the newly grown World Tree.

item:garrick-s-head.text: Garrick's Head. At Northshire's vineyards, Garrick Padfoot's severed head proves the cutthroat is dead. The authorities at Northshire Abbey require it before they pay the bounty. For weeks, Garrick Padfoot and his gang harassed Northshire Valley's farmers and merchants. Stormwind's defenses were stretched thin, and local guards were busy with kobolds and Defias bandits. So Garrick hid in a shack near the vineyards and raided passing trade. Deputy Willem offered a bounty for the outlaw's death, seeking someone to kill him and bring back proof.

item:gazlowe-s-ledger.text: Gazlowe's Ledger. In Ratchet, Gazlowe checks his trade records against the harbor manifest when a shipment from Booty Bay goes missing. Gazlowe tracks trade goods in Ratchet with a personal ledger. It records imported crates, outbound cargo, and warehouse stores. When a shipment from Booty Bay is missing, Gazlowe compares his expected inventory with the dock records kept by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

item:gem-of-anacondra.text: Gem of Anacondra. The Gem of Anacondra is one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders within the Wailing Caverns. Carried by Lady Anacondra, it serves as tangible proof of her defeat and the curbing of the Nightmare's spread over the Barrens. When Naralex entered his deep slumber to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens, the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts and warped his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators abandoned their traditional ways to become the Druids of the Fang, twisting their noble restorative purpose into a toxic delusion. The Gem of Anacondra is one of the four dream gems carried by these serpentine leaders, focusing their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchoring the nightmare within the cave system.

item:gem-of-cobrahn.text: Gem of Cobrahn. The Gem of Cobrahn is a dream gem carried by Lord Cobrahn, one of the corrupt leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. It serves as both a focus of his corrupted reverie and physical proof needed by Nara Wildmane to confirm his defeat. When the night elf druid Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the barren plains of Kalimdor, his nightmare twisted both the Wailing Caverns and his disciples. Among them was Cobrahn, who abandoned the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle to take the shape of the serpent. Lord Cobrahn carries one of the four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways, using it to channel the twisted dreams that threaten to transform the Barrens into a venomous marsh.

item:gem-of-pythas.text: Gem of Pythas. The Gem of Pythas is one of four corrupted dream gems carried by the leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Held by Lord Pythas, it fuels the nightmare twisting the subterranean oasis and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens, his noble vision was twisted into a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him, styling themselves the Druids of the Fang and seeking to remake the surface world into a venomous jungle. Lord Pythas carries this resonant stone, one of four dream gems anchoring the corruption within the caverns. The gem serves as a conduit of their dark design and proof to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas's twisted trance has finally been broken.

item:gem-of-serpentis.text: Gem of Serpentis. The Gem of Serpentis is a dream gem carried by Lord Serpentis, one of the four leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. It acts as a focal conduit for the twisted nightmare reshaping the cave network and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex's slumber inside the Wailing Caverns succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare, his most devoted followers were warped into the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis is one of the cabal's four leaders. Like the other three, Serpentis carries an enchanted dream gem that anchors their collective will to the corrupted vision. Recovering this gem breaks Serpentis's hold over the cavern's ecosystem, striking directly at the leadership directing the corruption spreading across the Barrens.

item:gerenzo-s-mechanical-arm.text: Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm. In the Stonetalon Mountains, goblin operatives seek Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm as proof while clearing out competition. Taken from rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the grafted limb marks his death. Above Cragpool Lake, rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle grafted whirring gears and metal onto his failing body. The renegade gnome replaced his natural limbs with intricate machinery. Goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks seeks Gerenzo's elimination to impress his superiors, and this distinctive arm is the trophy he needs as indisputable proof of the engineer's death.

item:ghost-hair-comb.text: Ghost Hair Comb. Madame Eva sends Ghost Hair Comb to Blind Mary at her lonely home on Duskwood’s outskirts. The comb stirs grief, then yields ghostly hair for Eva to spin into thread. Madame Eva of Darkshire sends Ghost Hair Comb to Blind Mary, who lives in a lonely, dilapidated dwelling on Duskwood’s outskirts. At the sight of it, the ghost recoils in horror. She must face that she is no longer the lovely living woman she remembers. Grief-stricken, Mary thrusts the comb away, leaving strands of her ghostly hair tangled in its teeth.

item:ghost-hair-thread.text: Ghost Hair Thread. In Darkshire, Madame Eva spins Ghost Hair Thread from the spirit world. Its occult powers can bind spirits or stitch life into inanimate things. Abercrombie asks for it to ward his shack against restless ghosts. Madame Eva spins Ghost Hair Thread in Darkshire, where its strange powers are known. Eva says the spectral strand can bind malevolent spirits or stitch vitality into inanimate objects. In Duskwood, it can be used in rituals and wards.

item:ghoul-fang.text: Ghoul Fang. In Duskwood, Ghoul Fang is gathered from the undead for Madame Eva’s protective talismans. The fangs are essential to her work in Darkshire, where travelers face the forest’s encroaching darkness. Ravenous undead haunt Duskwood’s shadowed woods and graves. Flesh Eaters lurk near the burial grounds, while Rotted Ones roam among the trees. Taking a fang from these creatures is grim work, and proof of survival against the dead threatening Darkshire’s borders. Madame Eva, Darkshire’s fortune teller and mystic, sees terrible omens around travelers who cross Duskwood. She combines ghoul fangs with skeletal fingers and arachnid venom to enchant the Totem of Infliction. The charm turns the forest’s dark forces against violent assault, protecting the one who bears it.

item:ghoul-rib.text: Ghoul Rib. In Duskwood, ghouls roam the groves and cemeteries, and Abercrombie asks for their ribs. The hermit says he needs them to build an effigy that will ward off the flesh-eating horrors near his shack. Ghouls haunt Duskwood, among them Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones, and Plague Spreaders. Abercrombie lives alone in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery and asks travelers for their sturdy, rotted ribs. He says he lives beyond the Night Watch’s protection in Darkshire and needs a fearsome effigy to frighten the dead away from his home.

item:giant-crocolisk-skin.text: Giant Crocolisk Skin. In the Wetlands, giant crocolisks yield thick hides that Menethil Harbor tradesmen need for leatherworking. Taking one is perilous work, and more than one hunter has been maimed. The Wetlands' bogs and waterways shelter enormous crocolisks with hides dense enough to resist the marsh's damp rot. In Menethil Harbor, artisans such as James Halloran rely on steady shipments of skins to make rugged leather goods. Reaching a full-grown giant crocolisk means braving deep water and facing a fierce swamp predator, so every hide comes hard-won.

item:gloom-weed.text: Gloom Weed. In Tirisfal Glades, Gloom Weed grows in the fields between Deathknell and Brill. Gordo, a lumbering Forsaken abomination, gathers it by mistake while searching for doom weed. Gloom Weed grows in the fields west of Brill and east of Solliden Farmstead. The plant is harmless, with none of the alchemical strength sought by the Royal Apothecary Society. Gordo, an abomination, wanders the road pulling weeds with his clumsy hands. He misunderstood his master's orders and keeps gathering Gloom Weed instead. Then he asks travelers to carry it to Master Holland in the Brill graveyard, much to the apothecary's annoyance.

item:glowing-ember.text: Glowing Ember. At the Shrine of Eternal Flame, a Glowing Ember kindles the brazier for a shaman's trial. It comes from a Minor Manifestation of Fire on Durotar's crags. A rising shaman drinks fire sapta to see the fiery spirits on the ridge near Telf Joolam. There, the initiate faces a Minor Manifestation of Fire. When the elemental falls, only a smoldering ember remains of its physical form. Raw elemental heat still pulses within it, carrying the living spark needed to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

item:glowing-fruit.text: Glowing Fruit. On Teldrassil, a strange fruit glows beneath unusual fronds. Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth studies its strange reaction to the World Tree's soil. The Glowing Fruit hangs beneath unusual fronds on Teldrassil, bright and round. Botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth recognizes it as foreign to the World Tree. He thinks its seeds came from distant lands across the sea. Its reaction to Teldrassil's rich, enchanted soil shows how foreign plants can affect the young World Tree.

item:glowing-gem.text: Glowing Gem. At Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem lies among the murlocs after Teronis fell seeking it. The stone holds magic needed to restore Dartol's rod. Murlocs near Lake Falathim hold the Glowing Gem, a stone with latent magic. Teronis, a young night elf from Astranaar, went after it to find a way to push back the corruption spreading through Ashenvale's forests. Teronis died at the lake, but the stone remained intact among the scavengers along the shore.

item:glowing-soul-gem.text: Glowing Soul Gem. In Ordil'Aran, the Glowing Soul Gem serves the Cult of the Dark Strand's work in northern Ashenvale. Shadow sorcery fills the stone, which holds the spirit of an unwitting victim. Northeast of Maestra's Post, the ruins of Ordil'Aran shelter members of the Cult of the Dark Strand and their shadowy masters. The cult's operatives carry Glowing Soul Gems, enchanted vessels that trap and torment the souls of the dead. These stones channel magical energy and bind spirits to the cult's ends.

item:glutton-shackle.text: Glutton Shackle. In Silverpine Forest, Glutton Shackles lend strength to Arugal’s flawed sorcery. The mad archmage crafted these enchanted restraints for Moonrage Glutton worgen. Feral worgen infest Silverpine Forest, and the Forsaken’s trained mages see them as proof of poor arcane work. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished arcanist stationed at the Sepulcher, holds Archmage Arugal in contempt and calls him an incompetent hack unworthy of the Kirin Tor. Dawnweaver found that Arugal relied on enchanted relics to shore up his fragile spells. The heavy Moonrage Gluttons that roam northern Silverpine wear Glutton Shackles, magical anchors that reinforce the curse binding the beasts.

item:glyph-of-azora.text: Glyph of Azora. From the Tower of Azora, Theocritus watches threats beyond Elwynn. His glyphs carry the Eye of Azora's power farther, so he can read enemies' thoughts and plans. From his tower in Elwynn Forest, Theocritus watches hostile powers. The Eye of Azora lets him see far away, but it cannot reach the minds or plans of his adversaries. So he places small focuses called Glyphs of Azora on distant surfaces. Each one anchors his magic, letting him read enemy intentions and project his voice across miles to speak with field agents.

item:glyphic-letter.text:
Glyphic Letter. At Northshire Abbey, Glyphic Letter calls promising novitiates to arcane study. After serving the garrison, they are summoned upstairs to Khelden Bremen, the resident mage trainer. Khelden Bremen seals Glyphic Letter with his own insignia. Apprentice spellcasters receive it after proving their discipline in Northshire Valley. The summons draws them from basic field duties into dedicated magical instruction within the abbey.

Before they take up the arcane, Bremen tests each student's resolve. Its forces are dangerous, its scrutiny unyielding, and its burdens heavy.

item:glyphic-memorandum.text: Glyphic Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, the Glyphic Memorandum calls novice mages to Anvilmar. Marryk Nurribit wrote it to guide new spellcasters into formal arcane instruction. Novice spellcasters receive the Glyphic Memorandum after their first tasks in Coldridge Valley. Marryk Nurribit, the local mage trainer, summons them inside Anvilmar. He gives plain counsel: learn your incantations, save coin for training and tavern ale, and keep clear of Gnomeregan, ruined by radiation.

item:glyphic-scroll.text: Glyphic Scroll. In Deathknell, the Glyphic Scroll calls newly raised Forsaken magi to the church. Isabella’s seal marks the summons, which invites fledgling spellcasters to begin their arcane training in undeath. Newly awakened Forsaken mages find a sealed scroll after culling mindless Scourge in Deathknell’s graveyard. Isabella, the settlement’s mage trainer, marks it with her seal and calls them to the ruined parish sanctuary. There, new magi begin learning the arcane under the Forsaken banner. Death has freed them from mortal weakness, but magic’s corrupting temptations remain.

item:glyphic-tablet.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives the Glyphic Tablet to novice Darkspear troll mages. Its summons sends them to Mai'ah for instruction in arcane magic. New Darkspear initiates with an affinity for arcane power receive the Glyphic Tablet in the Valley of Trials. Gornek passes it to young recruits as they handle early tasks around the red canyons. On the slate, Mai'ah, a seasoned troll mage outside the Den, invites them to meet her. The Darkspear follow arcane traditions unlike the scholarly academies of humans or high elves. Mai'ah offers instruction and a solemn warning: raw magic corrupts and deceives, and its dangers to a mage's mind exceed those of any enemy soldier.

item:glyphs-of-summoning.text: Glyphs of Summoning. In Orgrimmar, apprentice warlocks use the Glyphs of Summoning to call a voidwalker. Transcribed from the ancient Tablet of Verga, the inscriptions draw one from the Nether into a summoning circle and bind it to the warlock’s service. In the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks study the dark arts far from the prying eyes of the Warchief’s guards. For an aspiring warlock learning from Gan'rul Bloodeye, commanding a voidwalker marks an important step. The Glyphs of Summoning come from knowledge inscribed on the Tablet of Verga, and bridge Azeroth and the Nether. In Neeru Fireblade's tent, the warlock lays them within a summoning circle. They open a threshold and draw a creature of the Void into the mortal realm. Before Gan'rul teaches the final methods of binding, the warlock must defeat the summoned creature in combat.

item:gnoam-sprecklesprocket.text: Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. Deep in the Deadmines, Gnoam Sprecklesprocket powers a plan to reach Gnomeregan. Shoni the Shilent seeks it for drilling machines that could breach the rock around the lost gnomish home. Sneed's shredder runs deep in the Defias stronghold. The goblin taskmaster Sneed pilots the machine, whose compact power core supplies energy for heavy logging and cutting blades. Its steady output makes the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket valuable salvage in the tunnels of Westfall. In Stormwind City, the gnomish inventor Shoni the Shilent has chosen the Deadmines shredder for a larger effort. Gnomish forces seek to reclaim Gnomeregan from the troggs who overran it, but sealed underground approaches block the way. Shoni plans to power heavy gyrodrillmatic excavationators with the Sprecklesprocket. They could bore through the bedrock around the lost techno-city and open an unexpected route for an underground assault.

item:gnoll-paw.text:
Gnoll Paw. At Sentinel Hill, Gnoll Paw bounties help defend Westfall’s farmsteads from Riverpaw packs. The People's Militia pays for proof that patrols have slain gnolls. The People's Militia defends Westfall from Sentinel Hill. The royal army is absent, and the crown seems blind to troubles in the countryside. So ordinary citizens and volunteers face outlaws, rogue mechanoids, and Riverpaw gnolls.

Captain Danuvin offers bounties for proof that gnolls have been slain. Their paws show that patrols have searched the scrublands instead of resting beneath the watchtower.

item:gnomeregan-gumdrop.text: Gnomeregan Gumdrop. At Hallow's End, Gnomeregan Gumdrops reach travelers from the exiled gnomes. One sweet helps sick Jesper celebrate at the Stormwind orphanage. At Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel gives travelers Gnomeregan Gumdrops when they play along with his Hallow's End tricks. Alliance innkeepers offer treats from their own lands, but the exiled gnomes have no capital inn of their own. The radioactive disaster drove them from their underground kingdom. Still, they share their distinct sweets with the Alliance. Sick Jesper stays at the Stormwind orphanage in Cathedral Square and cannot travel the continents to trick-or-treat. So travelers gather four regional sweets from Alliance capitals and bring them to him: Gnomeregan Gumdrop, Stormwind Nougat, Ironforge Mint, and Darnassus Marzipan.

item:gnomish-tools.text: Gnomish Tools. Along Durotar's coast, Gnomish Tools lie among the wrecks of Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde seeks the salvaged devices to study Alliance engineering and adapt its innovations for survival. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet brought vast supplies of modern equipment to Durotar. Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to its shores, with sophisticated gear made by their gnomish allies aboard. After the fleet was destroyed along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, the delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Waterproof toolboxes still lie among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows. Gar'Thok, who oversees Razor Hill, sent Horde scouts to recover tools from the watery grave of Proudmoore's navy. The orcs know humans and gnomes are skilled in engineering, especially siege engines, shipwrighting, and clockwork mechanics. They send the kits by caravan to craftsmen and scholars in Orgrimmar. There, the Horde means to study Alliance contraptions, learn to counter enemy war machines, and adapt foreign innovations for its own survival.

item:gold-dust.text: Gold Dust. In Elwynn Forest, Gold Dust passes from kobold hands to local buyers. Miners still seek whole veins of ore. Kobolds dig through the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines beneath Elwynn Forest. Rather than refine the gold dust they find, they keep it in pockets and pouches. Local peddlers and fences want those scraps, hoping to profit without paying official smelting tariffs.

item:golm-fragment.text: Golm Fragment. At the southern Wetlands dig, Golm Fragment lies among the four missing pieces of the Goaz Stone. Dwarven archaeologists need it to piece together the ancient Titan inscriptions. Golm Fragment lies among the remains of Whelgar's excavation in the southern Wetlands. Prospector Whelgar found the monumental Goaz Stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back. Its inscription had been severed in four places. When the dig was overrun, the fragment remained amid dirt and overturned crates, hidden inside an ancient relic box until explorers could retrieve it.

item:gordon-s-crate.text: Gordon's Crate. Weapons are bound for the Forsaken forces in Silverpine Forest, packed in Gordon's Crate in the Undercity. The shipment is meant for the remote garrison at the Sepulcher. The Forsaken keep a steady flow of supplies from the Undercity to hold Silverpine Forest. Gordon's Crate carries weapons for Deathguard Podrig's defenders at the Sepulcher. The outpost sentries face worgen, wild beasts, and human remnants in the woods. Overland roads from the capital are dangerous and slow, so valuable shipments travel with the Undercity's bat handlers. Gordon's Crate is handed to Michael Garrett, the bat master above the city's trade quarter. He arranges passage on a trained flying bat to Karos Razok's roost back at the Sepulcher.

item:grape-manifest.text: Grape Manifest. At Northshire Abbey, Milly Osworth's recovered harvest is bound for the stores after brigands seized it. Northshire Abbey depends on nearby farms for its food and drink. The lost harvest put its stores in danger. Now the crates are reclaimed, and the quartermasters can balance supplies and ready barrels for fermentation. Milly Osworth's manifest records the quantity they need to plan. Brother Neals oversees Northshire Abbey's food and drink. He enjoys sampling its wine in the quiet of the bell tower. Knowing the grapes are coming helps keep the monks and visiting recruits supplied with drink. Each saved bushel strengthens the abbey's stores and brings a blessing from the Holy Light.

item:gray-bear-tongue.text: Gray Bear Tongue. In Hillsbrad Foothills, gray bear tongues are raw reagents sought by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill for experimental toxins. Gray bears roam the wilds around Tarren Mill in several sturdy varieties. Their tongues hold heavy muscular tissue and fluids that Apothecary Lydon uses as a base ingredient for lethal solutions, including the Elixir of Suffering.

item:gregor-s-remains.text: Gregor's Remains. Coleman Farthing seeks Gregor's Remains to settle an old score. The bones belonged to Gregor Agamand, once a member of Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest family. Before the Third War, the Agamands held great wealth and broad lands across northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the family patriarchs chose pride over flight. They fortified their mills and urged their loyal laborers to stand against the undead. The defense failed. The estate fell, and those who stood their ground were butchered and raised into undeath. Gregor Agamand became a mindless servant of the Lich King, haunting the mills his family had ruled. Some who escaped the Lich King's control joined the Forsaken, but the memory of that defense still wounds them. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker now stationed in Brill, blames the Agamands' pride for trapping his soul in eternal rot. Farthing seeks Gregor's remains as personal retribution against the master who led his household into damnation.

item:grelin-s-report.text:
Grelin's Report. In Coldridge Valley, Grelin's Report carries word of the Frostmane trolls to Kharanos. It joins the scouts at Anvilmar with Senir Whitebeard and Ironforge. Grelin Whitebeard has watched the Frostmane trolls in Coldridge Valley and judges them no great threat. Mountaineers already stationed there can handle them, with mercenaries paid from Senate funds. So Grelin entrusts his report to a capable traveler instead of his fumbling apprentice. The journey leads through trogg-infested Coldridge Pass.

The paper shows Mountaineer Thalos that you travel on urgent business. With it, you may pass his blockade and enter the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. At the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard receives Grelin's field report for Ironforge. His brother has invoked King Magni Bronzebeard's name throughout the document, and Senir takes note with amused resignation. Grelin claims the King's sanction for his actions. Senir expects that appeal to royal authority to ruffle feathers in the Ironforge Senate.

item:grelin-whitebeard-s-journal.text: Grelin Whitebeard's Journal. Grelin Whitebeard records Frostmane troll activity in a field journal in Coldridge Valley. Grik'nir the Cold steals the journal and carries it into the troll cave. Grelin Whitebeard watches the Frostmane trolls near Coldridge Valley and writes down what they do. His leatherbound notebook records their strength, their organization, and the danger they pose. Grik'nir the Cold takes the journal during a confrontation or ambush. The marked troll brute carries it into the troll cave, leaving Grelin without the notes he needs to finish his report. So he asks passing adventurers to retrieve the book.

item:grell-earring.text: Grell Earring. In Bashal'Aran, Grell Earring carries traces of the seal binding Asterion. Wild Grells and Vile Sprites in Bashal'Aran gather scraps among the ruins and make earrings from them. Most mortals see only worthless trinkets. Asterion, an ancient night elf bound there as a tormented phantom, studies the magic lingering on the earrings. He hopes those traces will lead him to the ancient seal that imprisons him.

item:grenka-s-claw.text: Grenka's Claw. Grenka's Claw is a physical trophy taken from the formidable harpy Grenka Bloodscreech in the depths of Roguefeather Den. Presented to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, it serves as undeniable proof that an aspiring adventurer has endured a grueling physical trial in the canyon heights. Within the winding caverns of Roguefeather Den, west of Freewind Post, harpies cache food and violently defend their territory against outsiders. To test the physical resilience of young champions, Dorn Plainstalker tasks them with invading the deep roosts and destroying the flock's food reserves. Such brazen provocation inevitably draws the fury of Grenka Bloodscreech. Severing and returning her wicked talon proves that a warrior can withstand wave after wave of enraged harpies and survive the vicious onslaught of their matriarch.

item:grimtotem-satchel.text: Grimtotem Satchel. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Grimtotem Satchel remains in Maur Grimtotem’s grasp. Troggs killed the tauren in Ragefire Chasm, but he shielded the pouch as he died. Its return to Thunder Bluff brings Magatha Grimtotem’s interest to light. Maur Grimtotem fell to troggs deep inside Ragefire Chasm, beneath Orgrimmar. The tauren still clutched the simple leather pack when his body was found. He had fought to protect it while the troggs surrounded him. What could it hold that made him guard it with his life?

item:grizzled-bear-heart.text: Grizzled Bear Heart. In Silverpine Forest, sturdy bears yield hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works without pause to create an engineered blight that can exterminate both the Scourge and living humanity. In Silverpine Forest's woodlands, Apothecary Renferrel found that toxins from a grizzled bear's heart make a remarkably lethal concoction when joined with arachnid ichor. Couriers and Forsaken loyalists hunt ferocious grizzled bears, giant grizzled bears, and the roaming beast Old Vicejaw. They carve out the hearts and carry them to Master Apothecary Faranell, deep within the Undercity's Apothecarium.

item:grizzled-scalp.text: Grizzled Scalp. In southern Darkshore, grizzled thistle bears roam the forests south of Auberdine. Their thick, furred hides reach Wizbang Cranktoggle, a gnome tinkerer with a use for them.

item:gryshka-s-letter.text: Gryshka's Letter. Innkeeper Gryshka sends a note of thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads after receiving fresh meat. The letter also introduces young Horde couriers to the wind rider flight network. Innkeeper Gryshka thanks Zargh for the steaks he sends from the Barrens to Orgrimmar's central tavern. She recalls the time he lost a finger while preparing meat, then teases that he looks handsome even when bloodied by his trade. To return Gryshka's Letter to the Crossroads, you report to Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's plateau. Show him that you have already checked in with Devrak at the Crossroads, and Doras introduces young couriers to the wyvern flight paths linking settlements in Durotar and the Barrens.

item:gunther-s-spellbook.text: Gunther's Spellbook. Bethor's enchantment now marks Gunther's Spellbook in Tirisfal Glades. The tome may show its owner that other mages have escaped the Lich King's control.

item:gyromechanic-gear.text:
Gyromechanic Gear. In Kharanos, inventors seek Gyromechanic Gears for a bold experiment. They hope to reverse the mutations of leper gnomes. Radiation swept through Gnomeregan while gnomes fought to drive out the troggs. Many survivors became mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket will not abandon their twisted kin, so they have planned the Recombobulator. The machine is meant to undo radiation's effects.

Its prototype needs precise mechanisms that can bear the volatile pressure inside, including Gyromechanic Gears and Restabilization Cogs. Gnomeregan's fall ended local manufacturing. Now the inventors must salvage these delicate parts from hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-letter.text: Hallowed Letter. In Northshire Valley, Priestess Anetta calls young priests to Northshire Abbey. Her letter begins their study of the Holy Light. Priestess Anetta’s personal mark appears on the Hallowed Letter. It reaches fledgling priests after their first trials against the kobold camps of Northshire Valley. She sees a spark of the Holy Light in each novice and urges them to enter the abbey and serve it. Dark forces still linger across Azeroth after the Third War. The priesthood gathers those who can heal, protect, and guide an empire struggling to keep order.

item:hallowed-rune.text: Hallowed Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder sends novice priests the Hallowed Rune to begin their training at Anvilmar. The Hallowed Rune bears teachings of the Holy Light. A young priest proves their resolve by aiding the valley’s mountaineers and defenders. Then Branstock sends them to Anvilmar, where he teaches them to mend wounds and wield holy power against the troggs threatening Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-scroll.text: Hallowed Scroll. In Deathknell, the Hallowed Scroll calls newly awakened Forsaken priests to the ruined chapel. Sealed by Dark Cleric Duesten, it begins their training in faith, willpower, and shadow. Newly risen Forsaken priests feel their bond with the world change violently. As Deathknell is reclaimed amid ongoing chaos, the Hallowed Scroll sends them to seek guidance in the settlement’s ruined chapel. Dark Cleric Duesten’s seal marks the parchment. It introduces the new priests to formal instruction and directs them to report for it, beginning their study of the practical beliefs that shape Forsaken priesthood. Dark Cleric Duesten tells priests who answer the summons to leave old teachings behind. The Holy Light, ancestral spirits, and demonic pacts cannot be their crutches. Instead, the scroll begins a discipline grounded in each priest’s own will. Its teachings call on them to survive and rule through conviction, making faith a means of self-command and mastery.

item:hallowed-sigil.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Hallowed Sigil summons young night elf initiates to Aldrassil. Shanda sends it to call them into service to Elune. Young night elf priests in Shadowglen receive the Hallowed Sigil from a woodland messenger. Holy markings are engraved on the token, which carries a personal summons from Shanda, the priest trainer at Aldrassil. Read it, then go up to the great hollow of Aldrassil. There, the summons brings the acolyte to the Sisterhood of Elune and begins their service to the Kaldorei as new travelers arrive across Teldrassil.

item:hallowed-tablet.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, the Hallowed Tablet calls young Darkspear priests to Ken'jai. Its words begin their lessons in communing with the spirits. Gornek gives the Hallowed Tablet to a promising troll priest taking their first steps through the Valley of Trials. The words carry a personal invitation from Ken'jai, the priest trainer outside the Den. Ken'jai reads signs and hears the spirits' whispers, sensing when young Darkspear with spiritual potential arrive in Durotar. The tablet tells the initiate to read its message and seek Ken'jai's guidance in channeling spiritual authority.

item:hand-of-dextren-ward.text: Hand of Dextren Ward. Darkshire demands proof that Dextren Ward has been executed in the Stormwind Stockade. The severed hand is bound for town, where grieving families await justice for their dead. Dextren Ward was sentenced to death by Lord Ebonlocke after he was caught digging up bodies in Duskwood cemeteries and selling them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Stormwind intervened before the town could execute him and took him to the Stockade. For Darkshire's grieving families, Ward's hand proves the defiler has been executed, despite the House of Nobles' unwanted leniency.

item:handful-of-oats-classic.text: Handful of Oats (Classic). In Westfall, Old Blanchy needs oats after the Furlbrows' wagon breaks down. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Now its farms lie overgrown or under the control of Defias bandits and rogue harvest golems. Sacks of grain and oats remain by barns and outbuildings, and in overgrown fields. Travelers and refugees whose wagons break down along the dusty roads can gather the leftover oats for their weary draft horses.

item:handful-of-stardust.text: Handful of Stardust. In the Ruins of Stardust, a pale frost gathers on the bushes south of Astranaar. Night elven healers use the powder to cool intense fevers. Stardust clings to shrubs in the Ruins of Stardust, south of Astranaar. The fine powder shines like frost. Lingering elemental spirits haunt the ruins, yet plants thrive among the broken stones and take in a rare glow. Night elven healers make the residue into poultices for dangerous, persistent fevers. They turn to it when ordinary salves and moonwell waters bring no full relief.

item:hardened-tortoise-shell.text: Hardened Tortoise Shell. Hardened Tortoise Shells are remarkably durable carapaces harvested from the sparkleshell tortoises wandering the Shimmering Flats. Coveted by gnomish racers at the Mirage Raceway, these rugged organic plates offer unmatched resistance against volatile and corrosive experimental fuels. The sun-scorched expanse of the Shimmering Flats is home to various breeds of sparkleshell tortoises, including snappers and borers, whose carapaces have evolved into exceptionally tough defenses against the harsh desert salt and wandering predators. Out on the salt flats, standard metal alloy fuel tanks frequently corrode or rupture under the strain of gnomish experimental chemistry. Mechanics like Wizzle Brassbolts prize these shells not for armor or shields, but as organic raw material tough enough to be retrofitted into makeshift, acid-resistant fuel tanks capable of containing volatile rocket propellants.

item:hardened-tumor.text: Hardened Tumor. Forsaken researchers seek a Hardened Tumor for their work on the New Plague. Apothecary Berard first studied the growth before Arugal's curse made him a mindless servant. Along Lake Lordamere, Vile Fin murlocs sometimes develop a rare, calcified growth. Apothecary Berard recorded the abnormality while studying wildlife along Silverpine Forest's eastern borders. The growth appears only in mature specimens along the shoreline and the Dawning Isles. Its cause remains uncertain, but the Royal Apothecary Society took notice of the dense tissue.

item:harpy-lieutenant-ring.text: Harpy Lieutenant Ring. In the Dry Hills, Harpy Lieutenant Rings mark the Witchwing Slayers who command the flock. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads asks for them as proof of death. Witchwing Slayers direct attacks on Horde travelers in the Barrens. Their rings mark their place among the flock’s leaders, above the ordinary raiders who fight with little coordination. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger and the defenders need the rings taken from fallen slayers to confirm that this part of the harpies’ leadership has been broken.

item:head-of-arugal.text: Head of Arugal. At Shadowfang Keep, Head of Arugal is taken from the mad archmage who commands the worgen. The Forsaken at the Sepulcher seek it as proof that he has fallen. Archmage Arugal commands the worgen from Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher gives the order to claim his severed head. The Forsaken see Arugal's fall as a blow against the beasts that hinder Lady Sylvanas's hold over Silverpine. Bringing the head to Dawnweaver proves the archmage's sorcery has been cut from the land.

item:head-of-bazil-thredd.text: Head of Bazil Thredd. Warden Thelwater demands proof that the Stockade uprising has been crushed. The severed head of Bazil Thredd is meant to show that the rebellion's leader is dead and Defias control of Stormwind's prison has ended. Bazil Thredd led the uprising in the Stockade beneath Stormwind City. From his cell block, he directed the riots with the help of loyal Defias inmates. Warden Thelwater distrusts outsiders and struggles to keep order. He demands Thredd's head as proof that the ringleader is dead and to test the adventurer's allegiance to Stormwind.

item:head-of-deepfury.text: Head of Deepfury. At the Stormwind Stockade, Kam Deepfury’s severed head marks the end of a Dark Iron conspirator. His death in the prison riots answers the grievance of the dwarven defenders at Dun Modr. Kam Deepfury was held in the Stormwind Stockade for political reasons, spared immediate execution by human diplomacy. Roggo uncovered that Deepfury had orchestrated the attack on the Thandol Span, which cost the lives of King Magni’s soldiers and Longbraid the Grim’s kin. The Ironforge mountaineers at Dun Modr could not accept his continued imprisonment. Bound to his post, Motley Garmason sent Alliance champions into the rioting prison to take Deepfury’s head and deliver dwarven vengeance.

item:head-of-gath-ilzogg.text: Head of Gath'Ilzogg. Claiming Gath'Ilzogg's severed head proves the Blackrock warlord has been slain. His fall breaks the leadership behind the siege of Stonewatch Keep and brings desperate relief to Lakeshire. Gath'Ilzogg led the Blackrock assault that took Stonewatch Keep, drove out its defenders, and left the valley under constant raids. Lakeshire stood near ruin, while Stormwind sent almost no military help. Magistrate Solomon offered a bounty on the warlord. Gath'Ilzogg fell in the keep's fortified upper levels, and claiming his head breaks the local Blackrock leadership. For Lakeshire, it is the first step toward reclaiming the keep for the kingdom.

item:head-of-grimson.text: Head of Grimson. At the Deep Elem Mine, Grimson the Pale's severed head proves the Forsaken have secured its riches. Dalar Dawnweaver receives the trophy at the Sepulcher, and the mine's minerals can supply Varimathras's military campaigns. Forsaken scouts called Darkstalkers found a strategic threat brewing in the southeastern hills. Archmage Arugal's shadowy enchantments had corrupted workers in the Deep Elem Mine and driven its overseer, Grimson the Pale, mad. From the Sepulcher, Dalar Dawnweaver sent champions to kill Grimson and bring back his severed head. The trophy confirms the mine is free of rogue magic, leaving its underground wealth for Varimathras's forces.

item:head-of-kelris.text: Head of Kelris. Agents of the Argent Dawn seek Kelris's severed head to confirm his fall and the end of his sacrifices. In Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight Lord Kelris led sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God. Taking his head marks the end of his rule over the Twilight's Hammer cultists and their naga allies in the cavern. The head must reach the surface so leaders can know his bloody ceremonies have ended. The Argent Dawn had presumed Kelris dead or lost for months before his influence returned with Kalimdor's encroaching shadows. His head, brought to agents in Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, settles lingering bounties and confirms that his attempt to plunge the world into primeval chaos has been stopped.

item:head-of-targorr.text: Head of Targorr. In the Stormwind Stockade, Targorr the Dread awaits an execution stopped by nobles in Stormwind. Once Gath'Ilzogg's supreme executioner in the Redridge Mountains, the captured orc is now the subject of Guard Berton's demand for proof of his death in Lakeshire. Targorr the Dread earned infamy across Redridge as the Blackrock clan warlord Gath'Ilzogg's brutal executioner. He tortured and slaughtered defenders of the Kingdom of Stormwind before his capture and death sentence in the Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind nobles intervened and mysteriously suspended the sentence. Guardsmen like Berton suspect foul play and corruption in the capital. Guard Berton fears Targorr could become a political pawn or arrange an escape, so he hires an outside champion to enter the volatile prison and finish what the courts delayed. Taking Targorr's head bypasses the stalled legal system and gives closure to grieving families and Lakeshire's besieged defenders, who suffered under the executioner's blades.

item:head-of-vancleef.text: Head of VanCleef. At Sentinel Hill, VanCleef's severed head proves the Defias leader has fallen. Carried from the depths of the Deadmines, it brings the People's Militia hard-won vengeance. Westfall's settlers need proof that their danger has passed. For months, Edwin VanCleef directed the Defias Brotherhood's terror from the deepest sanctum of the Deadmines, guarded by armed outlaws, goblin engineers, and a massive war juggernaut. Gryan Stoutmantle, leader of the People's Militia, demands physical proof before declaring the countryside safe. VanCleef's severed head, brought out into daylight, assures the exhausted defenders that the architect of their ruin can no longer threaten Westfall.

item:heart-of-isha-awak.text: Heart of Isha Awak. Hunters seek Isha Awak’s heart along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. Mahren Skyseer wants it as proof that the Deep Doom has been overcome. Isha Awak prowls the sea off the Merchant Coast, south of Ratchet. Sailors and coastal folk revere and fear the massive thresher, known as the Deep Doom. It has killed many human trespassers along the shore. Mahren Skyseer, a tauren mystic, sees an honorable predator, not a mindless menace. She believes its fierce spirit dwells in its heart. Mahren charges brave hunters to plunge into the waves, defeat Isha Awak in its own domain, and claim the heart as both trophy and spiritual offering.

item:heartswood.text: Heartswood. In northwestern Ashenvale, Heartswood is cut from a tree rooted among the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. The tree grew where two ancient lovers died, and its wood draws succubi when warlocks seek to summon them. Among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale, a peculiar tree took root. Legend says Anathera and Latherion, two lovers, fell side by side there during the War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. The Heartswood tree grew from the earth where they died. Even now, wood cut from it carries the memory of their devotion. Those who study emotional and spiritual bonds are curious about it.

item:heartswood-core.text: Heartswood Core. Beneath Stormwind, warlocks use the Heartswood Core to summon a succubus. Gakin the Darkbinder provides the enchanted focus, made from an ancient tree’s wood, to open a passage to the Twisting Nether. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, warlocks perform rites beyond the city watch’s gaze. The Heartswood Core channels the magic that begins a binding ritual. Made from an ancient tree’s wood, it holds enough lingering power to pierce the veil between worlds. At a consecrated summoning circle, an initiate focuses dark arts through the core and opens a passage to the Twisting Nether. A succubus crosses the divide.

item:heavy-leaden-collection-phial.text:
Heavy Leaden Collection Phial. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt offers the Heavy Leaden Collection Phial for decontamination research. It is meant to draw in unstable irradiated discharge from mutants deep inside Gnomeregan and keep it contained. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial draws volatile residue from living, irradiated creatures in Gnomeregan. Keeping the fallout inside is difficult. A suitable sample may take several attempts to collect. Ozzie Togglevolt provides the phial to help his research into reversing the terrible mutations afflicting leper gnomes. Earlier samples from surface troggs were too weak for useful chemical analysis.

With the leaden phial, researchers hope to gather samples from virulent beasts, including irradiated slimes and lurkers in the Hall of Gears. They seek the active elements in the city's toxic fallout, then hope to make an effective antidote.

item:hezrul-s-head.text: Hezrul's Head. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark leads the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens. His head is carried to Regthar Deathgate west of the Crossroads as proof their chieftain has fallen. Hezrul Bloodmark leads his Kolkar centaur clan from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. The Kolkar hold the Barrens' oases and threaten Horde supply routes and young settlements. Regthar Deathgate, an orc veteran charged with securing the land west of the Crossroads, sees their fierce rage but little discipline. He demands Hezrul's severed head to break the clan's command and throw its surviving fighters into disarray, weakening their attacks on the Horde.

item:high-potency-radioactive-fallout.text:
High Potency Radioactive Fallout. In Gnomeregan's depths, researchers seek potent radioactive fallout. They hope to learn how the sludge afflicted the leper gnomes and find a cure. Deep in the Hall of Gears, irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes roam Gnomeregan's lowest tiers. Researchers outside the fallen capital need fallout drawn from these living creatures. Samples scraped from contaminated scavengers outside are too weak for their work.

The sludge decays quickly. It must be sealed in a leaden phial and reach the researchers before its potency fades. Ozzie Togglevolt and his colleagues seek a cure for the leper gnomes. They believe the secrets of the irradiated sludge may show them the way. During the trogg invasion, toxic venting deformed these survivors and drove them mad.

The leper gnomes remain trapped in a living nightmare. For the researchers, dangerous expeditions into the ruins are worth the risk.

item:highborne-relic-classic.text: Highborne Relic (Classic). In Darkshore, Highborne Relics remain in the hands of spirits haunting Ameth'Aran. Night elf scholars seek them for destruction before their dormant magic can cause more harm. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne caste brought ruin upon ancient Kalimdor through reckless arcane magic. Their estates lie in shattered ruins across Darkshore. At Ameth'Aran, wailing apparitions wander among the crumbling columns, still clutching the implements of their old sorcery. The relics bind arcane taint to the spirits, who will not release the objects tied to their undoing. Night elf society largely renounced arcane magic after the Great Sundering, and scholars see these relics as a grave hazard. Acting on reports from the Sentinels, Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine sends travelers to wrest them from the cursed spirits. Once gathered, the relics are destroyed so the Highborne's ancient evils and catastrophic mistakes cannot be repeated.

item:highperch-venom-sac.text: Highperch Venom Sac. Highperch Venom Sacs are harvested from the wild wyverns nesting upon the towering spires of Highperch in Thousand Needles. While orcs prize wyverns as aerial mounts, select apothecaries and traders value their potent stingers even more than the living beasts. The high spires of Thousand Needles house thriving prides of wild wyverns, particularly around the elevated crags of Highperch. These winged predators rely on powerful venom delivered through their barbed tails to paralyze and kill prey. While the Horde often domesticates these creatures as loyal wind riders, their venom sacs command a remarkably high price among alchemists, hunters, and opportunistic merchants across Kalimdor. Though native to the deep canyons of central Kalimdor, this venom draws interest far beyond them. In the port town of Theramore, the high elf Fiora Longears pays handsomely for fresh sacs collected from Highperch's broods. She seeks samples swollen with venom—typically found only on young wyverns or fertile females—fueling trade in dangerous reagents far from the beasts' natural desert habitat.

item:highperch-wyvern-egg.text: Highperch Wyvern Egg. Highperch Wyvern Eggs are clutch eggs gathered from the nesting grounds atop the high mesas of Thousand Needles. They are sought after by aspiring Horde wind riders to raise and train new aerial mounts. The high plateau of Highperch in Thousand Needles provides a natural sanctuary for native wyverns to roost and raise their young. Accessible only via steep winding paths up the canyon walls, these nesting grounds are fiercely guarded by adult beasts. The eggs laid among these roosts are sturdy and warm, holding developing hatchlings capable of adapting to the harsh skies of Kalimdor. Across Kalimdor, the demand for trained wyverns continually outstrips supply as the Horde expands its courier and scouting networks. At Freewind Post, trainees like the tauren Elu seek out intact eggs directly from wild aeries. By raising the hatchlings from their shells, handlers hope to forge the deep bonds required to train trustworthy winged mounts for the Horde's wind riders.

item:hildelve-s-journal.text:
Hildelve's Journal. In Dun Morogh, Hildelve's Journal bears the last words of a dwarf lost to a fierce bear. Its pages tell of the attack and his plea for vengeance. Dwarven pilot Hildelve went alone into Dun Morogh after his steam tank broke down. He left his partner, Hammerfoot, with the tanks and searched the snow-swept crags for rumored chiron ore. In his journal, Hildelve writes that Mangeclaw, a monstrous ice claw bear, stalked him for days before attacking.

Hildelve fought bravely and drove the bear off, but Mangeclaw mauled him and left him gravely wounded in the cold. His final hours were agonizing. Before the bear returned, Hildelve made one plea: whoever found his body should hunt Mangeclaw and avenge his death.

item:hillsbrad-human-skull.text: Hillsbrad Human Skull. Across the Hillsbrad Foothills, Forsaken gather the skulls of slain humans. At Tarren Mill, they keep them as grim mementos of the assault on local settlements. Forsaken forces from Tarren Mill fight the humans of Southshore and nearby settlements. During the Battle of Hillsbrad, Deathstalkers and soldiers carry out the purge Darthalia ordered. Guards left on watch want a share of the slaughter. Deathguard Samsa collects skulls from the fighters on the front lines, taking pleasure in keeping the remains of people the Forsaken once lived among. These trophies are proof of the killing as the conflict rages.

item:hillsbrad-town-registry.text: Hillsbrad Town Registry. In Hillsbrad Fields, the town hall keeps a ledger of the settlement's surviving citizens and landowners. The Hillsbrad Town Registry records civic matters, and the Forsaken seek it during their offensive against the human stronghold. The Hillsbrad Town Registry records the town's people and rights. It rests in the town hall near the podium of Magistrate Burnside. From Tarren Mill, the Forsaken press to break human resistance in the foothills. Darthalia sends Horde champions into the town hall to kill the council and seize the ledger. Its records cover Hillsbrad's population, households, and administrative rights. The registry would strip the town of its civic order and give the Undercity intelligence on the surviving population and their assets.

item:hollow-vulture-bone.text: Hollow Vulture Bone. Hollow Vulture Bones are lightweight, durable skeletal remains harvested from the scavengers of the Shimmering Flats. At the Mirage Raceway, goblin mechanics prize them as specialized building materials to lighten their rocket cars without sacrificing structural integrity. Speed is everything out on the salt, and weight is the enemy of speed. While standard engineering leans heavily on iron and copper, the goblin pit crews at the Mirage Raceway turn to whatever the desert provides to gain an edge. Vulture bones are naturally hollow yet remarkably sturdy, providing the perfect strength-to-weight ratio for internal brackets, steering rigs, and minor structural supports. For chief tinkerers like Pozzik, harvesting bones from local scavengers is a practical and cheap shortcut to shaved seconds on the track.

item:honorary-picks.text: Honorary Picks. In Ironforge, Honorary Picks are bound for Brock Stoneseeker’s mining apprentices in Thelsamar. Gryphons carry the ceremonial tools to Loch Modan, where they mark students ready to work its ore veins. Mining keeps the great forges burning and brings dwarves the iron and stone they need. In Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker teaches young apprentices to mine. Honorary Picks from Ironforge mark the students ready to work the open ore deposits across Loch Modan. The picks travel through the Alliance gryphon network, linking Ironforge with its outlying settlements. At Ironforge’s Great Forge, Gryth Thurden receives the shipment. He sends it over the mountains to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar.

item:horn-of-arra-chea.text: Horn of Arra'chea. Across Mulgore, Arra'chea roams while Cairne Bloodhoof calls young hunters to prove their worth. The kodo's horn confirms a hunter can track prey and provide for the Shu'halo. Passing the Rites of the Earthmother earns a youth a place atop Thunder Bluff, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof still expects his people to prove their worth. For the tauren, the hunt binds identity to lasting harmony with the land. Cairne sends young hunters to track Arra'chea, a massive, solitary kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking the bull's horn shows mastery of tracking prey across vast distances. Bringing Arra'chea's horn to Thunder Bluff does more than display strength; it helps sustain the community. Tauren use every part of a slain beast. The trophy tells the High Chieftain where Arra'chea fell, so gathering parties can go down into the plains and harvest the kodo's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

item:horn-of-awakening.text: Horn of Awakening. In southern Darkshore, Kerlonian Evershade keeps a horn close at hand. It rouses him whenever sleep overtakes him on the road to Ashenvale. Kerlonian Evershade has only recently awakened from centuries in the Emerald Dream, and wakefulness still weighs on him. The Druid of the Claw travels south toward Maestra's Post and entrusts the horn to travelers willing to escort him. When exhaustion takes him along the wilderness trail, a clear blast jolts him awake and gets him back on his feet before wild beasts or cultists can reach him.

item:horn-of-echeyakee.text: Horn of Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn gives hunters the Horn of Echeyakee. Sounded among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement, it calls the legendary white predator of the Barrens. Hunters who are being tested in the hunt receive the horn. Its call summons Echeyakee, whose name means “Whitemist” in Taur-ahe. Taure n hunters revere the king of the savannah cats as both mercy and death. He strikes so swiftly that his quarry feels neither terror nor suffering. The horn belongs at the predator’s lair, among giant kodo bones behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

item:huge-gnoll-claw.text: Huge Gnoll Claw. In southwestern Elwynn, Hogger's death is proven by his huge claw. Stormwind's authorities in Goldshire require it before paying the bounty. For months, Hogger has terrorized the southern woodlands of Forest's Edge. Patrols have failed to stop him, and the local garrison cannot corral or subdue the brute. The Stormwind Army is stretched thin across Elwynn, so it has posted an open bounty on his head. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire requires clear proof before paying. Hogger's oversized claw leaves no doubt that the notorious marauder has fallen.

item:humbert-s-sword.text: Humbert's Sword. At Dun Garok, Humbert's Sword lies among the dwarves who took it from his camp. Deathguard Humbert left his post to gather firewood while scouting the stronghold. Deathguard Humbert left his hidden post near Dun Garok one morning to gather firewood for boiling water. High Executor Darthalia had sent him to watch the dwarven presence there. While he was away, a dwarven patrol found his campsite and plundered his gear, including his personal blade. With so many dwarves to search, Humbert needs Horde agents to enter the fortress and recover it. Dun Garok's defenders carried Humbert's belongings behind the stronghold's barricades. Riflemen, mountaineers, and priests pass supplies around the garrison. Finding the thief means searching among the defenders in the trenches and redoubts.

item:hyacinth-mushroom.text: Hyacinth Mushroom. In Shadowglen, Hyacinth Mushrooms grow at the roots of trees across Teldrassil. Night elf herbalists use them for medicine, and grell and grellkin forage for them. Hyacinth Mushrooms grow in Shadowglen among the trees and roots of Aldrassil. Forest healers use them in remedies for young night elf sentinels and trainees harmed by venomous creatures. The spiders of Shadowthread Cave are among the dangers they face, and the mushrooms go into soothing draughts and antivenoms. Corrupted grell also hoard them.

item:hypercapacitor-gizmo.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. The Hypercapacitor Gizmo is an eccentric piece of engineering recovered from the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. Once dangling from the neck of a caged beast in a ruined caravan, its true purpose remains a mystery even to the tinkerer who claims to own it. When centaur marauders ambushed a goblin caravan traveling through Thousand Needles, they plundered nearly everything in sight. The sole survivor, Wizlo Bearingshiner, managed to crawl his way to safety at Whitereach Post, leaving behind his best gizmo: the Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Strangely, the gadget wound up secured around the neck of a ferocious, enraged panther locked inside a transport cage. The raiding centaur feared the beast enough to leave the cage entirely alone amidst the burning wreckage, unwittingly preserving Wizlo's odd machine. While Wizlo proudly calls the device his best gizmo, he admits upon its recovery that he has no real idea what it actually does. Like many goblin contraptions, the Hypercapacitor Gizmo is a tangled mass of ambition and volatile parts, destined to keep its owner occupied with endless tinkering rather than serving any practical, understood function.

item:ignition-key.text: Ignition Key. At Sludge Fen, the Ignition Key is held by Supervisor Lugwizzle at the Venture Company drilling operation. Wizzlecrank needs it to unlock an advanced shredder's movement column and activate its controls. Sputtervalve of Ratchet sent an operative to steal a Venture Company shredder from Sludge Fen, but the plan stalled. The undercover pilot, Wizzlecrank, climbed into the cockpit and found the movement column locked. He pretended the machine had mechanical trouble so the foremen would not grow suspicious while he waited for someone to fetch the Ignition Key. Supervisor Lugwizzle keeps the key high atop the central oil derrick, where access to the shredder's arm, speed, and rotation controls is held.

item:ilkrud-magthrull-s-tome.text: Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome. At Fire Scar Shrine, Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome draws Delgren the Purifier's attention. Its pages connect the warlock to the cultists at the Tower of Althalaxx. Ilkrud Magthrull holds the Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, where demonic influence has poisoned the site. The formidable orc warlock is surrounded by summoned minions. His personal tome records foul rituals and shadowy communications. The Argent Dawn paladin Delgren the Purifier has long known of Magthrull's presence, but the ties between the warlock and the dark cultists gathering at the Tower of Althalaxx make the book urgent to recover.

item:incantations-from-the-nether.text: Incantations from the Nether. Beneath Orgrimmar, Searing Blade cultists hold Incantations from the Nether, a grimoire of demonic magic. Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras seek its fel knowledge for the Forsaken. The Searing Blade is a subterranean sect tied to the Shadow Council, working in the fiery tunnels of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar's red stone streets. Its cultists prize Incantations from the Nether, a spellbook of demonic rites given by agents of the Burning Legion. They use its secrets to plot treason in the Orcish capital. Word of the tome has reached the royal quarters of Undercity.

item:incendia-agave.text: Incendia Agave. Beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle, Incendia Agave grows in the Boiling Pool. A skilled shaman can enchant it to kindle the sacred fire of life. In Thousand Needles, Incendia Agave grows in and around the waters of the Boiling Pool, beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle. Wandering steam elementals guard the scarce plant, making it difficult to harvest. Though it grows underwater, the plant holds natural elements suited to rituals of flame.

item:incendia-powder.text: Incendia Powder. On Thunder Bluff, Incendia Powder is prepared to call a sacred spirit into the open. Magatha Grimtotem enchants it for use at Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. Incendia Powder carries shamanic magic to the sacred fire atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Magatha Grimtotem entrusts it to travelers on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Scattered across the consecrated brazier where the dead are laid to rest, the powder calls forth Arikara, a vengeful winged serpent.

item:insane-scribbles.text: Insane Scribbles. In Darkshore, cultists carry Insane Scribbles torn from the Twilight Tome, a fragment of dark literature. The dancing text and distorted scrollwork cause dizziness and mental strain. Ancient forest protectors study the fragments to learn the Twilight's Hammer's motives. Reading the Twilight Tome can endanger a mortal's sanity. Its script writhes across the parchment, and graceful scrollwork warps into grotesque images before the reader's eyes. Tearing out even one sheet, called Insane Scribbles, leaves the bearer lightheaded and disoriented. Though the writing makes little sense, the parchment hums with primal, deeply ancient magic tied to dark powers long buried beneath Azeroth.

item:inscribed-bark.text: Inscribed Bark. In Teldrassil, Inscribed Bark carries word of the World Tree's state to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. The Oracle Tree entrusts it with news of the boughs and the threats troubling the woods. The Oracle Tree sends Inscribed Bark to the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus. After you drive the harpies from their nests, the ancient tree gives you its message, wary of sending ordinary couriers along Teldrassil's tainted paths. The report tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm of recent victories and the deeper blight still gripping the woods.

item:intact-raptor-horn.text: Intact Raptor Horn. Across the Barrens savannas, raptors are hunted for their intact horns. Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet wants them for a scheme built on rumors of raptor intelligence. Hunters prize raptor hides, talons, and trophies, but whole horns are harder to take in the field. Mebok Mizzyrix, an eccentric goblin alchemist in Ratchet, believes the Barrens raptors are more cunning than their kin elsewhere. He suspects their intellect lies in their horns. By grinding whole horns and brewing them into tonics, Mebok hopes to bottle that supposed genius in commercial drinks. A horn fit for brewing must come from a particularly vicious predator, not just any young raptor. Sunscale Scytheclaws prowl the southern plains and the northern borders near Ashenvale. Takk the Leaper and the elusive Ishamuhale are notable terrors of the veldt, and their stout horns can survive the clash of the hunt intact.

item:intrepid-strongbox-key.text: Intrepid Strongbox Key. On the wreck of the Intrepid, Captain Halyndor still guards the key to his strongbox. The rusted iron key once kept a mysterious item locked away aboard the doomed Alliance vessel off the Wetlands. The Intrepid was wrecked with the Third Fleet off the Wetlands, and its crew became restless, cursed spirits. Captain Halyndor watched over a mysterious item inside the ship’s heavy strongbox. Now his ghost prowls the waterlogged deck, still clutching the rusted key that opens it.

item:invisibility-liquor.text: Invisibility Liquor. Maybell Maclure slips from her family's sight with Invisibility Liquor to meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. Their households remain bound by a bitter feud. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks a quiet meeting with Maybell Maclure. But their families' feud keeps the households apart, and their kin watch closely. Ordinary secrecy will not do. Invisibility Liquor lets its drinker cross the disputed farmland unseen.

item:iron-pike.text: Iron Pike. In Lakeshire, Iron Pike supplies are needed to repair the Everstill Bridge. The shipment from Stormwind was seized by Redridge gnolls, leaving the town short of iron. Lakeshire spent its metal reserves forging armor, blades, and ammunition after recent attacks by the Blackrock orcs. Builders requested more iron from Stormwind City, but Redridge gnolls hijacked the caravan on the road. They carried crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, stopping repairs on the Everstill Bridge. Foreman Oslow oversees the bridge's reconstruction and needs the stolen hardware back.
