Without the heavy pikes to reinforce its stone and timber frame, the bridge leaves Lakeshire partly cut off from the northern road and open to further incursions.

item:iron-pommel.text: Iron Pommel. In Ashenvale, the Iron Pommel is the last missing piece of Dartol's Rod. The long-dead wizard Dartol made the rod, and the night elves of Astranaar seek it to slow the furbolg attacks on their people. Druids at Dor'Danil Barrow Den kept the pommel safe until their sanctuary was overrun and they were slaughtered. Dartol's Rod was split apart and scattered across Ashenvale to guard its mystic power. Night elf druids near the road south toward the Barrens took charge of the Iron Pommel. Their circle was massacred at Dor'Danil Barrow Den, and their shelter fell silent in ruins. The pommel vanished amid the destruction, swallowed by the bubbling oozes now moving through the defiled glade.

item:iron-rivet.text: Iron Rivet. Iron Rivet shipments from Stormwind now lie in gnoll camps north of Lake Everstill. Foreman Oslow needs them to mend Lakeshire's damaged bridge. Lakeshire's iron stores went into weapons and armor when Blackrock orcs attacked. After the assaults eased, Foreman Oslow asked Stormwind for supplies to mend the damaged Everstill Bridge. Redridge gnolls ambushed the caravan before it reached town. They dragged its wagons and pack beasts into the hills north of Lake Everstill, scattering iron rivets and pikes among their camps. The Everstill Bridge needs heavy iron rivets to hold its stone and timber framework together under the weight of carts and travelers. Foreman Oslow cannot safely carry out repairs without them. The bridge links Lakeshire to the western valleys, and its repair will help secure the town's perimeter against further incursions.

item:iron-shaft.text: Iron Shaft. Near Felwood, the Iron Shaft waits in a locked chest. It is one piece of Dartol's Rod, sought by Teronis to slow the furbolg assaults on Ashenvale. Dartol made the rod, then its pieces were scattered across Ashenvale. One was placed in the care of the druids of Dor'Danil. The Iron Shaft is the rod's sturdy metal core, kept in a locked chest in a glade near Ashenvale's northern border, close to Felwood.

item:ironband-s-progress-report.text: Ironband's Progress Report. In eastern Loch Modan, troggs have brought Prospector Ironband's excavation to a halt. His report asks for more blastpowder, though the Explorers' League sent supplies weeks ago. Jern Hornhelm receives the dispatch in Thelsamar and forwards it to the Explorers' League in Ironforge. Ironband reports that work has stalled and asks for heavy munitions. The League leaders are baffled. They sent him plenty of blastpowder weeks ago, and now wonder where it went.

item:ishamuhale-s-fang.text: Ishamuhale's Fang. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer awaits Ishamuhale's Fang from the feared sunscale raptor Speartooth of the Barrens. The tooth proves the hunter bested one of Kalimdor's deadliest natural predators. Across the central savanna, hunters fear Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor alive. Some say the apex hunter kills from predatory passion, not hunger. Fresh zhevra meat draws the beast into the open beside a withered tree northwest of Ratchet, where it gives no quarter. Taking its massive fang proves to the Horde's hunting instructors that a traveler has overcome the savagery of the plains.

item:ivar-s-head.text: Ivar's Head. In northern Silverpine, Ivar's Head proves Ivar the Foul is dead. Rane Yorick seeks it so her wounded brother Quinn can recover safely. Rane and Quinn Yorick were scouting northern Silverpine Forest on High Executor Hadrec's orders when Ivar the Foul ambushed them at an abandoned farmstead. The Forsaken Deathstalkers drove the feral ghoul off, but Quinn was badly mauled. Rane stayed at the ruined farm to watch over him and could not safely leave to finish their mission. Ivar's severed head proves the ghoul will no longer threaten the estate, giving Quinn time to recover under Rane's care.

item:iverron-s-antidote-item.text: Iverron's Antidote (item). In Shadowglen, Iverron's Antidote must reach a young night elf before it spoils. Dirania Silvershine brews it to counter the lethal venom of local Webwood spiders, but it lasts only five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the antidote in Aldrassil for Iverron, a young night elf bitten by Webwood spiders. Its volatile ingredients and herbal catalysts give the draught a shelf life of only five minutes. Couriers must hurry north to the Webwood cave and deliver it before it spoils.

item:jade-phial.text: Jade Phial. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage entrusts the Jade Phial to young initiates. It carries sacred water from Teldrassil’s moonwells to replenish the druids’ central well in Darnassus. The Jade Phial gathers water from a moonwell near Starbreeze Village. Teldrassil’s many moonwells channel lunar and natural energies that matter to night elf society and druidic worship. From time to time, the druids replenish their central moonwell in Darnassus with water from wells across the great bough. Corithras Moonrage entrusts the phial to young initiates, who use it to collect pure water without disturbing the moonwell’s spiritual potency.

item:jennea-s-flask.text:
Jennea's Flask. At the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind, Jennea Cannon sends apprentices to Mirror Lake for water. They bring a sample back for arcane study. Arcane currents have been torn from their ancient channels by magical struggles across Azeroth. Jennea Cannon wants to learn how these shifts have affected Elwynn Forest. She gives promising apprentices a glass flask and sends them southwest of Stormwind's gates, to the base of Mirror Lake's waterfall.

The flask protects the water sample on the journey back to the Wizard's Sanctum. There, Jennea can examine it for arcane disturbances. With Jennea's flask, Stormwind's mages can test whether shifting ley lines have tainted Mirror Lake. Harmful magic in the water could bring strange afflictions to the surrounding life and to anyone who drinks from it. A sample may reveal magical residue before tainted currents spread through the countryside.

item:jitters-completed-journal.text: Jitters' Completed Journal. Jitters gives up his completed journal, hoping to clear his name and expose the sinister forces haunting Duskwood. The reclusive man fears Sven Yorgen's vengeance after fleeing the massacre at Sven's farm.

item:johaan-s-findings.text: Johaan's Findings. Apothecary Johaan sends his findings south from Brill to the Sepulcher. His research carries recent alchemical work from Tirisfal Glades to Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine Forest. Apothecary Johaan sends his research from Brill to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society works under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's demand for a New Plague that can destroy both the living and the Scourge. Its researchers are scattered across Lordaeron's contested ruins, so they must share their findings between outposts. Renferrel directs the Society's efforts from Silverpine Forest, while Johaan records his local tests in Brill. His documents join the Society's wider work to refine its deadly brews.

item:johaan-s-special-drink.text: Johaan's Special Drink. At Brill, Apothecary Johaan offers a drink with a deadly purpose. Disguised as a common refreshment, it tests the Royal Apothecary Society’s developing plague. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan prepares a brew from venomous components and local reagents. Though it looks like a tavern drink, the mixture is made to test how virulent the plague is against living beings. Johaan hands it over as if to quench a captive’s thirst. The work serves the Forsaken apothecaries’ effort to create a weapon potent enough to fulfill Sylvanas Windrunner’s designs for Azeroth.

item:jordan-s-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Ore Shipment. In the northeastern hills of Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres hold Jordan's Ore Shipment. The ore came by caravan from the Wetlands for Bailor Stonehand to refine into an alloy for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell's ore was bound for Bailor Stonehand, a dwarf who would refine it into his special alloy. The caravan carried it south through the mountains from the Wetlands into Loch Modan. Then Mo'grosh ogres ambushed the travelers and dragged the shipment to their stronghold in the wilderness. The surviving guards died of their wounds, and Jordan's smithing project waits for the ore's return.

item:jordan-s-refined-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment. Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment arrives in Ironforge for the Test of Righteousness. The metal is prepared for blacksmith Jordan Stilwell to forge a holy weapon. Jordan Stilwell needs rare materials for a weapon worthy of a paladin. He requires a Purified Kor Gem, sturdy Whitestone Oak lumber, his lost smithing hammer, and refined ore. The shipment brings the metal to Ironforge for this sacred labor.

item:jordan-s-smithing-hammer.text: Jordan's Smithing Hammer. Jordan Stilwell waits outside Ironforge for his father's hammer, lost within Shadowfang Keep. Jordan Stilwell is a human blacksmith who works outside Ironforge. His father’s hammer lies within Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Without it, Jordan cannot forge a sacred weapon fit for a holy champion, the masterwork he hopes to make.

item:kadrak-s-flag.text: Kadrak's Flag. At the edge of the Barrens and Ashenvale, Kadrak gives the Horde a mark to carry into enemy ground. The flag is planted in the Talon Den after Keymaster Rynthariel is killed. Kadrak sends the Horde flag into the Talon Den on Stonetalon Peak. The dryad Rynthariel, Keymaster of the Den, has sent communications across the border, and Kadrak decides her death alone will not answer them. He gives you the crimson banner to plant deep inside the Den. The Horde colors there carry a warning to the night elves and dryads: incursions across the Barrens will meet retaliation on Alliance soil.

item:keg-of-shindigger-stout.text: Keg of Shindigger Stout. In Dun Garok, Shindigger Stout fills the dwarves’ kegs and draws interest from Tarren Mill. The Royal Apothecary Society wants the ale for a purpose far darker than drink. Dwarves of Ironforge hold Dun Garok in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills. Within its barracks and mess halls, defenders share Shindigger Stout through the cold and the siege against their regional enemies. The brew is a staple of the garrison’s daily life.

item:ken-zigla-s-draught.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Ken'zigla prepares a bitter draught for the gravely wounded. A careful half dose restores enough strength to move, while more can make a patient bleed out. Ken'zigla prepares the draught in the Stonetalon Mountains for those near death. Its strength must be measured with care: more than half a dose at once can make the patient bleed out as their circulation surges. Half a dose gives a wounded person enough vigor to move and flee danger. The rest must wait until the body steadies after a full night's rest.

item:khazgorm-s-journal.text: Khazgorm's Journal. At Bael Modan, Prospector Khazgorm leads the Ironforge dwarven excavation in the southern Barrens. His field ledger records the Explorers' League's work on lands claimed by the Stonespire tauren. Prospector Khazgorm directs the heavy machinery and blasting that cut into the southern Barrens hillsides. His notes show an excavation far from the Explorers' League's promised search for knowledge: its work has displaced the Stonespire tribe. The tauren tried to settle matters peacefully, but the dwarves refused. Gann Stonespire wants the journal to understand the Ironforge presence in his homeland and find a way to break it.

item:klaven-mortwake-s-journal.text: Klaven Mortwake's Journal. SI:7 operatives recover Klaven Mortwake's Journal from the Defias tower. It records the Brotherhood's search for a way to raise the dead. Master Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's intelligence service, SI:7. He sought Mortwake's journal to trace the Brotherhood's wider alliances. The notes confirm experiments in reanimation and illicit support linking Duskwood, the Venture Company, and the Defias. For rogues serving the crown, recovering the research is a step toward mastering poisons.

item:kodo-horn.text: Kodo Horn. In the Barrens, Kodo Horns are gathered from the roaming kodos. Tonga Runetotem uses them in herbal remedies for poisoned wildlife. Across the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem uses intact kodo horns in his herbal remedies. He works from the Crossroads, where the horns help strengthen his salves. Chips and fragments lack the strength he needs, so he gathers whole horns from mature kodos wandering the plains.

item:kodo-liver.text: Kodo Liver. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn needs Kodo Liver for a strange ale. He learned to brew trogg ale from the wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout. Kodos roam the Barrens, where tauren and predators hunt them for their hides and meat. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn uses a fresh Kodo Liver with thunderhawk saliva glands and lightning glands to make trogg ale. Chen Stormstout taught Drohn the recipe, and Drohn says the blend packs a potent kick for adventurous travelers. The ingredients come from the wilds of central Kalimdor.

item:kodobane-s-head.text: Kodobane's Head. Near the Forgotten Pools, Barak Kodobane's severed head proves the cunning chieftain's death. The orc warlord Regthar Deathgate receives it as proof that the centaur threat there has been broken. Kolkar bands in the Barrens have long been divided, but ambitious warlords now threaten to gather them into an army. Barak Kodobane made his camp by the lush waters of the Forgotten Pools, where the oasis offers vital resources and nearby paths lie open to raids. Regthar Deathgate, stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads, demands Kodobane's severed head as proof that this commander can no longer rally his kin against the Horde.

item:kravel-s-crate.text: Kravel's Crate. Kravel's Crate is a heavy package dispatched by Kravel Koalbeard from the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Destined for the Nesingwary expedition in Stranglethorn Vale, it contains specialized hunting ammunition designed to bring down the jungle's deadliest game. Handed out by the shrewd entrepreneur Kravel Koalbeard at the Mirage Raceway, Kravel's Crate represents an unfinished business transaction across continents. Ordered weeks prior by a wealthy dwarven patron, the shipment was delayed long enough for its buyer to depart Kalimdor entirely. Rather than lose out on the favor of a wealthy customer who already paid for forwarding, Kravel entrusts passing adventurers to haul the crate all the way to northern Stranglethorn Vale. Despite its nondescript appearance and the crust of salt dust it gathers in the Shimmering Flats, the crate carries lethal cargo: heavy, special-gauge ammunition tailored specifically for hunting rifles. When received at the expedition camp north of Grom'gol, the recipient notes that the potent rounds are prized by big-game hunters and vital for survival against the predators roaming the jungle canopy.

item:kreenig-snarlsnout-s-tusk.text: Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk. At the Crossroads, Thork seeks proof that Kreenig Snarlsnout has fallen. His tusk marks the end of the Razormane leader's attacks on Horde caravans in the northern Barrens. Horde caravans traveling west from Durotar face constant attacks in the Barrens. Those raids grew bolder under Kreenig Snarlsnout, a fierce Razormane leader. Thork, commander of the Crossroads watch, ordered Kreenig killed to disrupt the quilboars' coordination. His tusk offers proof that the leader is dead and insults the Razormane, weakening their resolve and leaving their fighters without central direction.

item:kron-s-amulet.text: Kron's Amulet. Along the Southfury River, Kron’s amulet recalls a young orc hunter who went missing.

item:kuz-s-skull.text: Kuz's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Kuz's Skull marks the end of a feared Razormane raider. Kuz came from Razorfen Kraul and helped lead attacks on Horde outposts before a captive former kin sought vengeance. Kuz, Nak, and their chieftain Lok Orcbane led Razormane attacks across the southern Barrens. Sent from Razorfen Kraul, the three raiders struck travelers and settlements such as the Crossroads. Their betrayal of Mangletooth, a fellow quilboar, turned one of their own against them. They left Mangletooth to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo. From that cage, he revealed Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to kill the raider and take her head.

item:laced-pumpkin.text: Laced Pumpkin. At Apothecary Johaan's hand, Laced Pumpkin turns an ordinary gourd into a deadly test of Forsaken alchemy. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society seeks weapons against the Scourge and living human forces. In Tirisfal Glades, the pumpkin looks like ordinary produce salvaged from blighted soil. Apothecary Johaan in Brill treats it with experimental toxins meant to realize the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks weapons against the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south. Even a simple harvest can carry infection and chemical death.

item:laird-s-response.text: Laird's Response. Along Teldrassil's shores, Laird's Response carries a puzzle for Nessa Shadowsong. The fish there are larger and more plentiful than those along mainland Darkshore. Laird compares catches from across the Veiled Sea. Fish from Teldrassil's coast are larger and more plentiful than those from Darkshore's mainland beaches. In his reply to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird of Auberdine offers a theory: the newly planted World Tree's unusual presence and vitality may be changing the surrounding sea life. Travelers carry his letter across the water to Rut'theran Village, where the fisherfolk greet the news with wonder and quiet curiosity.

item:lake-creeper-moss.text: Lake Creeper Moss. Around Lake Lordamere’s southern Dawning Isles, Lake Creeper Moss grows on aquatic beasts. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks the organic compound as a vital reagent for engineering a lethal new plague. Lake Creeper Moss grows on the hides of freshwater beasts in the waters by the southern Dawning Isles. Lordaeron’s blighted waters shape its unusual properties. Before Arugal’s curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard recorded the moss in his journal. He noted its resemblance to traces found on fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. Forsaken agents send recovered samples to the Apothecarium in the Undercity, where Master Apothecary Faranell uses them in his research.

item:lake-skulker-moss.text: Lake Skulker Moss. In northern Lake Lordamere, Lake Skulker Moss draws the Royal Apothecary Society's attention. Apothecary Berard identified it as an organic part of research into brewing a New Plague before Arugal's curse claimed his mind. Lake Skulker Moss is gathered from Lake Skulkers and Elder Lake Skulkers on the Dawning Isles. Before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard cataloged the plants and creatures of eastern Silverpine Forest. In his journal, he wrote that Lake Skulker and Lake Creeper mosses could stabilize or react with other ingredients. After Berard became Arugal's mindless servant, his journal was recovered from Pyrewood Village for Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel sent Forsaken champions to gather moss and a rare tumor from local Vile Fin murlocs, then deliver both to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

item:large-candle.text: Large Candle. In Elwynn's mines, kobolds carry Large Candles for light and wax. Apothecaries value the wax for their work. Kobolds follow candlelight through the dark shafts beneath Elwynn Forest. They fasten the tapers to their heads, and Kobold Miners, Tunnelers, and Geomancers defend them fiercely from intruders. Large Candles from Fargodeep Mine and Jasperlode Mine hold valuable wax, though they are crudely made. Surface tradesmen cannot produce much wax at once, so the candles serve both as tools for kobolds and as a commodity for alchemists. William Pestle, an apothecary operative from Stormwind City, gathers Large Candles at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. His family runs an apothecary, and he needs rendered wax for its concoctions, balms, and ointments. Pestle hires passing adventurers to clear the infested mines and take candles from the kobolds.

item:large-soran-ruk-fragment.text: Large Soran'ruk Fragment. The Large Soran'ruk Fragment rests in Shadowfang Keep, far from the other shards. Its broken orb once held a disgraced demon of the Burning Legion. Disgraced demons of the Burning Legion may be condemned to imprisonment in enchanted orbs. Mages and warlocks aligned with the Legion receive these vessels and draw on the fel forces trapped within. Even when an orb is shattered, its bound fiend's lingering essence still radiates power. Each fragment draws ambitious practitioners of shadow magic. The orb of Soran'ruk was cracked into two halves long ago. Cultists elsewhere scattered one half into smaller pieces. A sorcerer in the cursed Shadowfang Keep claimed the larger half. The Shadowfang Darksouls carry the Large Soran'ruk Fragment, which holds the bound spirit until someone seeks to reforge the ancient vessel.

item:laughing-sister-s-hair.text: Laughing Sister's Hair. In Ashenvale, laughing sisters' hair draws weavers seeking its natural magic. Kil'hala at the Crossroads uses the gathered locks to make enchanted robes. Near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale, laughing sisters are dryads whose hair holds natural magic. Dryads protect the woods and are linked to Cenarius and the night elves. Horde craftsmen prize their hair as a potent crafting material. Kil'hala, a troll tailor at the Crossroads, spins the locks into enchanted robes for Deino's promising pupils of the arcane.

item:legacy-of-the-aspects.text: Legacy of the Aspects. Legacy of the Aspects is an ancient tome hidden deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in southern Ashenvale. Retrieved during a Horde trial of the intellect, the volume contains essential lore concerning the Great Aspects that shaped ancient Azeroth. While earlier trials set forth by tauren elders test physical endurance and resolve, the pursuit of Legacy of the Aspects is designed to challenge the mind. Tasked by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to the Talondeep Path in the Stonetalon Mountains, an aspirant must delve into the haunted barrow dens of Dor'Danil. Guarded by the restless spirits of fallen druids and the vicious creatures that slew them, the ancient text rests upon a stone pedestal. Claiming the volume is only the first step; the seeker must commit its contents to memory before relinquishing the book, as they are tested on its historical lessons.

item:letter-to-delgren.text: Letter to Delgren. Balthule Shadowstrike sends a warning from the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. His letter to Delgren the Purifier describes the Dark Strand cult's demonic work and must reach Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the Dark Strand cult gather around the Tower of Althalaxx ruins. He cannot destroy the cult alone, so he writes to Delgren the Purifier, his tutor in the Holy Light, asking for aid. The cult's foul rites threaten more than Darkshore's coast. The letter must travel south through the region into western Ashenvale, where Delgren works with night elf Sentinels against demonic and undead threats.

item:letter-to-jin-zil.text: Letter to Jin'Zil. At the Crossroads, Letter to Jin'Zil carries word of Serena Bloodfeather's defeat. Darsok Swiftdagger sends it to the Darkspear witch doctor in the Stonetalon Mountains, telling him the northern Barrens are free of the Bloodfeather threat. After the harpies at the Dry Hills are wiped out and Serena Bloodfeather is slain, Darsok Swiftdagger writes to an old comrade. The harpies of the Barrens first roosted in the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. Darsok sends news of the fallen matron to Jin'Zil, a witch doctor, and introduces a promising warrior to the wider frontier.

item:letter-to-jorgen.text: Letter to Jorgen. In Stormwind City, a sealed letter calls Jorgen to help find a missing diplomat. A diplomat bound for Theramore never arrived for talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Royal investigators moved quickly to keep the matter quiet. While official agents searched the capital, other channels stirred. The letter bypasses military ranks and seeks Jorgen, a gruff veteran who fishes beneath the great statues in the Valley of Heroes. It invokes old obligations and draws him into a covert inquiry amid rumors of a Defias conspiracy.

item:lewis-note.text: Lewis' Note. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis sends a courier by gryphon to seek armor for Westfall's garrison. The order goes to a private armorer in Stormwind. The People's Militia at Sentinel Hill receives little support from Stormwind's House of Nobles. Skirmishes with the Defias Brotherhood keep wearing down its small supply of gear. So Quartermaster Lewis turns to private trade to keep the defenders equipped. His order goes outside the kingdom's military channels. An Alliance courier must fly by gryphon to Old Town and present it to Osric Strang, who owns Limited Immunity.

item:lieutenant-s-insignia.text: Lieutenant's Insignia. Near Orgrimmar, cultists bear Lieutenant's Insignia and the Burning Blade's mark. Horde adventurers recover it from them. Cultists at Skull Rock on Durotar's eastern shore carry Lieutenant's Insignia. The mark names its bearer an officer of the Burning Blade. Warchief Thrall will not suffer traitors in his new nation. Yet a purge might scatter the cult before its masters are exposed. So he entrusts the badge to a champion, to test those suspected of infiltrating beneath Orgrimmar.

item:lightning-gland.text: Lightning Gland. In the Barrens, Lightning Glands are taken from stormhides roaming the plains. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet needs them for trogg ale, a fiery brew Chen Stormstout taught him to make. Stormhides roam the Barrens savannas among other predators touched by the elements. Their flesh holds lightning glands, organs charged with latent electricity. These glands are poor fare on their own, but brewers prize them for the sting they bring to a brew. Brewmaster Drohn keeps Chen Stormstout’s brewing traditions alive in Ratchet. To make trogg ale, a potent brew, Drohn needs five lightning glands, a thunderhawk saliva gland, and a fresh kodo liver. The finished drink has a sharp kick that adventurers find invigorating and potent.

item:logging-rope.text: Logging Rope. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, Logging Rope keeps the mills and machinery supplied. Furbolg tribes have stolen shipments across Ashenvale, leaving the Warsong to recover the line they need. Logging Rope shipments meant for the Warsong Lumber Camp have been stolen. The Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolgs intercepted the line before it reached the loggers. The tribes keep the ropes in their encampments across northern and central Ashenvale. Corruption has driven the furbolgs mad, and they fiercely defend their ancestral woods. Locke Okarr at Splintertree Post seeks to recover the stolen supplies before work at the Warsong Lumber Camp stops. The heavy rope lets the Horde secure timber, bind logs, and rig saw machinery. Furbolg resistance continues across the forest.

item:lok-s-skull.text: Lok's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Lok's Skull marks the fall of a feared Razormane leader. Lok Orcbane led fierce quilboar raids against Horde supply routes, and the skull is his severed head. Lok Orcbane led aggressive Razormane assaults on Horde supply lines in the southern Barrens. He emerged from Razorfen Kraul with his lieutenants Nak and Kuz. After betraying Mangletooth and leaving him captive at Camp Taurajo, Lok became known to orcish defenders for ruthless raids they struggled to contain. Mangletooth directs Horde champions to Lok's camp, where claiming Lok's skull avenges the captive and strikes at the leadership driving the Razormane offensive.

item:lonebrow-s-journal.text: Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is a weathered diary found clutched in the skeletal remains of the dwarven explorer Henrig Lonebrow at the base of the Great Lift. Its pages detail the final grim journey of Lonebrow through the Barrens and point toward dangers lurking within Razorfen Kraul. Henrig Lonebrow met an unfortunate end near the base of the Great Lift connecting the Barrens to Thousand Needles. Lying abandoned on a rocky ledge, his skeletal remains still grip this weathered journal. The diary serves as a testament to his final travels and directs whoever discovers it to bring word to the night elf druid Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, the border outpost leading into Feralas. Lonebrow's notes shed critical light on the quilboar menace brewing in the southern barrens.

item:lorgalis-manuscript.text: Lorgalis Manuscript. The Lorgalis Manuscript lies hidden beneath Ashenvale in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. The ancient text concerns the Old Gods, and dark scholars covet its words about powers that sleep. The Lorgalis Manuscript lies at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, where long-dead elves once lived before their city fell. Lorgalis wrote of the Old Gods, who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained and sleeping. The text praises Aku'mai, a servant of the Old Gods who dwells in the Deeps. Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient beings sleeping deep beneath the world. The manuscript rests in a pitted iron chest among the flooded corridors, drawing the attention of cultists and shadow scholars alike.

item:lunar-fungus.text: Lunar Fungus. Lunar Fungus grows in Darkshore's caves, where druids gather it for healing. Mixed with Earthroot and water, it helps make a salve for sick deer. Lunar Fungus grows from Lunar Fungal Blooms in Darkshore's underground caverns. The Cenarion Circle values its amplifying effects. Mixed with soothing water and common Earthroot, it lends potency to a salve that counters debilitating afflictions. Damp caves where it grows are also frequented by territorial moonkin, so gathering it means navigating carefully. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong has young druids gather Lunar Fungus as part of their studies in nature's healing arts. They see how physical ingredients such as this fungus can counter poisons in local deer. By learning how herbal remedies work, initiates prepare to channel natural antidotes through shapeshifting and spiritual power.

item:lurker-venom.text:
Lurker Venom. In Loch Modan, dwarven defenders need Lurker Venom to counter Dark Iron sabotage. Predatory spiders in the rocky hills and woods provide the toxin. Lurker Venom helps dwarves disarm explosives planted by the Dark Iron. Ashlan Stonesmirk, an explosives expert, named spider poison as an ingredient in the mixture Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. The solvent joins the venom with rare minerals and tears from the loch’s crocolisks. Together, they form a reactive compound that can disarm complex explosives.

Lurker spiders range from common wood lurkers to the matriarch Shanda the Spinner. Their bites threaten travelers and mountaineers across Loch Modan’s hills and crags.

item:lydon-s-toxin.text: Lydon's Toxin. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon has made a toxin to disrupt the Venture Company's logging in the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde adventurers carry it to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, who must devise a way to spread it. Apothecary Lydon made the toxin in the Hillsbrad Foothills to fight the Venture Company loggers despoiling the Stonetalon Mountains. He says the compound is lethal on contact and may spread from one target to another. Before it can be used against the goblins near Windshear Crag, the mixture must cross continents to Thunder Bluff. Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative there, needs the raw toxin to devise a wide-dispersal device called the Toxic Fogger.

item:macgrann-s-dried-meats.text: MacGrann's Dried Meats. In Dun Morogh, Old Icebeard has carried off Tundra MacGrann’s winter meat. Tundra MacGrann hunted game and salted it for the winter. He packed weeks of provisions into a sturdy chest inside a thorium meat locker, to keep scavenging bears and prowling predators from his homestead. Yet he never expected an intruder strong enough to carry away the whole chest. Old Icebeard raided MacGrann’s camp while the dwarf tracked deer. The yeti dragged the heavy chest to his den in Chill Breeze Valley. Its solid thorium plating holds, but MacGrann’s injured leg keeps him from making a swift rescue into the cavern. Without help retrieving his cache before winter, the stranded hunter faces starvation in the mountain snows.

item:mackreel-s-moonshine.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. On the broken Thandol Span, Foggy MacKreel brews moonshine strong enough to fell a sentry. Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore takes a batch to settle Foggy's debt. Foggy MacKreel brews his moonshine while stationed as a guard on the Thandol Span. The liquor has a fierce reputation, and even hardened dwarven sentries can be laid low after a night of drinking it. They wake with headaches like siege engines rolling overhead. Travelers value its warmth against the damp chill of Lordaeron and Khaz Modan. Foggy MacKreel owed an unsettled debt to Brewmeister Bilger, Southshore's tavern keeper and master brewer. He sent a batch of moonshine instead of coin to clear his tab. Bilger accepts the liquor in place of gold and adds MacKreel's potent brew to his stock for the chilly coastal days of the Hillsbrad Foothills.

item:maggot-eye-s-paw.text: Maggot Eye's Paw. At Garren's Haunt, Maggot Eye's Paw proves the gnoll chieftain is dead. The paw is carried to Brill as proof of his execution for stealing corpses for the Scourge. Maggot Eye raided graves and pillaged the countryside near Garren's Haunt, supplying corpses to the Lich King's armies. The Forsaken posted a death sentence and bounty in Brill. To collect the bounty and close it, hunters must bring the gnoll's severed paw back to town. Executor Zygand accepts that proof in place of rumors of Maggot Eye's death.

item:maggran-s-reserve-letter.text: Maggran's Reserve Letter. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder sends orders to relieve a guard at the Great Lift. The letter promises Grish Longrunner leave to visit his family. Maggran Earthbinder sends orders from Sun Rock Retreat to the Great Lift. Grish Longrunner, a Horde sentry at the post, is to be relieved by a replacement warrior. The Great Lift's wooden winches stand far to the south, where Grish has kept watch. With the new warrior taking his place, he can leave his post and return home to visit his family.

item:mangy-claw.text: Mangy Claw. In Dun Morogh, Mangy Claw marks the end of a deadly hunt. The great ice claw bear Mangeclaw killed a stranded dwarven pilot, and the severed claw proves the beast was slain. Pilot Hildelve’s steam tank broke down in Dun Morogh’s frozen hills. He searched for ore on foot and faced the mountain wilderness alone. In his journal, he tells how he fought off Mangeclaw, an ice claw bear, but was savagely mauled. The bear returned and killed the weakened pilot. Hildelve’s final entry pleaded for vengeance. Taking Mangy Claw from the fallen bear fulfills his request.

item:marshal-haggard-s-badge.text:
Marshal Haggard's Badge. In the hills of Elwynn Forest, Marshal Haggard lives retired from Stormwind's service. Dead-tooth Jack tricked him into surrendering his old badge, which the Defias could use to impersonate city officials. Dead-tooth Jack came to Haggard's farm one night in a Stormwind tabard. The Defias rogue pretended to be Marshal Dughan, Goldshire's garrison commander, and said Haggard's former peers needed the insignia for official business.

The aging marshal handed it over without suspicion. Jack fled into the woods before Haggard saw through the ruse. In Defias hands, the badge still carries the authority of Stormwind's marshals. Outlaws could use it to pass checkpoints or confuse local patrols.

item:mary-s-looking-glass.text: Mary's Looking Glass. In Duskwood, Mary’s discarded looking glass passes from a ghoul to a stargazer. Blind Mary once treasured the polished mirror. After her death and the loss of her eyes, her reflection became an agonizing reminder of what she had lost. She cast the looking glass away behind her barn, where Duskwood's gloom closed in. An Insane Ghoul found it among the ruined outskirts and carried it south to the crypts of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. In Darkshire, the stargazer Viktori Prism'Antras dreams of seeing through Duskwood's eternal twilight to the clear heavens above. His telescope needs special optical lenses and reflective glass. Mary sends adventurers after the feral undead in the cemetery's ruined chapel to recover her looking glass. Viktori needs it as a reflector in his machine for viewing the stars.

item:mathystra-relic.text: Mathystra Relic. Among Mathystra’s overgrown ruins in northern Darkshore, ancient night elven relics still hold traces of magic. The Twilight's Hammer cult has taken an interest in them. Mathystra once stood on the Kalimdor coast as a city and bastion of elven civilization. Before the Great Sundering, it was a proud place. Now toppled columns and cracked stones lie half-swallowed by brush and sea mist, with restless spirits and lurking beasts among them. Relics from that age are scattered through the ruins. Ten thousand years of neglect have worn them, but traces of elven arcane craft remain, and they are dangerous in careless hands.

item:melenas-head.text: Melenas' Head. At Fel Rock, Melenas' Head marks the end of a lingering demonic threat on Teldrassil. Taken as a bounty from Lord Melenas, the satyr commander encamped there, it is proof of his death. Satyrs on Teldrassil’s new World Tree shame the night elves who guard Shadowglen and the surrounding reaches. Lord Melenas made his lair in Fel Rock’s twisted caverns, just north of the elven settlements, and rallied aggressive grell warriors to his banner. The kaldorei prize discretion when dealing with corruption so close to their heartlands. Melenas' Head is private proof that his schemes have ended before his influence could spread.

item:menethil-statuette.text: Menethil Statuette. Off the Wetlands coast, the Menethil Statuette lies lost from a shipwreck. The rare silver likeness honors Lordaeron's fallen king. King Terenas Menethil II appears in his youth, a long-haired paladin lifting a hammer toward the heavens. He was humble and disliked personal monuments, so few statues or likenesses were made in his honor. The Scourge's fall of Lordaeron destroyed almost all of them. This surviving effigy is extraordinarily valuable to the Alliance. The Blind Princess carried the statuette toward the Alliance harbor of Menethil. Bluegill murlocs attacked the merchant vessel off the marshy coast, scattering its cargo. The statuette became trapped in a half-buried barrel on shore. With Dragonmaw orcs and other local threats nearby, defenders hurried to send the recovered icon south to Stormwind City. There, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon entrusted it to the Cathedral of Light.

item:merrin-s-letter.text: Merrin's Letter. At the Whelgar's Excavation site, Merrin Rockweaver sends an urgent message from the Wetlands. Raptors have overrun the dig, but Merrin assures her loved ones that she survived. Merrin Rockweaver writes from the ruined dig at Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands. The dwarven expedition had been uncovering enormous prehistoric fossils and relics when they disturbed a nest of Mottled Raptors. The beasts swarmed the trenches, killed several workers, and cut off the surviving researchers. Amid the chaos, Merrin sends word to her husband Tarrel at Menethil Harbor. She, Prospector Whelgar, and Ormer Ironbraid survived behind a barricaded shelter.

item:middle-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Middle of Gelkak's Key. Off Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast’s key lies in three pieces after threshadons sank his ship. Greymist murlocs took the middle fragment from the shore. Gelkak Gyromast’s winding key broke when threshadons dragged his ship beneath the waves. The gnome pirate came ashore with his belongings shattered on the rocky shoals. The specialized key was made for his mechanical first mate, but the wreck split it into three pieces scattered along the strand. Coastal beasts carried off the top and bottom. Greymist murlocs prowling the Darkshore surf took the middle piece and kept it in their camps and among the wreckage they hold.

item:milly-s-harvest.text: Milly's Harvest. In the Northshire Vineyards, Milly's Harvest lies abandoned after the Defias arrive. Crates and buckets of grapes risk theft or being crushed beneath the abbey guards' boots. Milly Osworth gathers grapes in the Northshire Vineyards. The harvest matters to local vintners and the abbey community. When armed brigands in red masks enter the fields, Milly flees to the abbey grounds. Her fresh-picked grapes lie scattered between the rows. Stormwind guards watch the valley entrance, but their small numbers leave Northshire vulnerable. The garrison promises to drive out the Defias. Milly fears a long fight between guards and thieves will ruin her harvest. The crates may be trampled or carried off as provisions, costing Northshire one of its few peaceful harvests.

item:miners-gear.text: Miners' Gear. In northern Loch Modan, Miners' Gear waits in the Silver Stream Mine. Kobolds have overrun the tunnels, and the Miners' League wants its tools recovered before the local guards attack. The Silver Stream Mine ran out of ore, so the Miners' League made its quiet tunnels a depot for mining equipment. Kobolds overran the mine, seized the stored goods and made nests among the crates. The league fears an assault by the Mountaineers could wreck the dwarven gear, or scavengers could ruin it. Enter the mine and bring the crates to safety before either fate befalls them.

item:miners-union-card.text: Miners' Union Card. In Moonbrook, union cards mark the laborers lost beneath the earth. Workers once carried them through the mines, and now the cards remain with skeletal dead in the dark drifts. Before the Defias Brotherhood took control of Moonbrook, miners worked below ground for the guild, drawing valuable ore for the kingdom. A tunnel collapse crushed a major shaft and killed dozens beneath the rock. The dead rose as skeletal miners, excavators, and dynamiters. Union cards remain in their bony pockets, the last proof of who they were. In Stormwind, surviving colleagues seek the cards to learn the dead workers' identities and bring closure to their families.

item:minshina-s-skull.text: Minshina's Skull. On the Echo Isles, Minshina's Skull holds the bound soul of Minshina, a Darkspear troll and brother of Master Gadrin. Zalazane trapped him there after driving the tribe from the isles, and uses the skull to fuel dark rituals. Minshina was captured and slain when Zalazane seized the Echo Isles and drove out the Darkspear. The traitorous witch doctor bound his victim's soul to Minshina's severed skull instead of letting him pass into death. The skull lies within a circle of power on the southernmost isle, tethering Minshina to Zalazane's magic. Tormented by dreams of his brother calling to him, Master Gadrin seeks brave travelers to enter the occupied islands, reclaim the skull, and break Zalazane's hold over Minshina's spirit.

item:mirror-lake-water-sample.text:
Mirror Lake Water Sample. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, water is gathered for Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. The mages will test it for signs that the arcane currents have altered local water. Jennea Cannon sends promising apprentices to collect water from Mirror Lake. The lake lies just southwest of the Stormwind Gate, where they fill a specially prepared flask at the foot of its waterfall.

The Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind fears the world's mystic channels remain unsettled after catastrophic conflicts. Its mages will examine the sample for stray magical taint in the waterways people nearby use.

item:mist-veil-s-lockbox.text: Mist Veil's Lockbox. Off Darkshore, Mist Veil's Lockbox lies in the sunken night elven vessel. It holds the captain's log and personal effects, lost when coastal murlocs ambushed and sank the ship. The night elven vessel Mist Veil sank while sailing toward Auberdine. Coastal murlocs ambushed it alongside its sister ship, the Silver Dawning, and overwhelmed both vessels. The captain perished in the attack. Their logbook and personal belongings remain sealed in the lockbox in the flooded hold, surrounded by murlocs. Surviving sailors reached Auberdine, but the loss of their vessel and commander still grieves them. Gorbold Steelhand seeks Mist Veil's Lockbox so the captain's final effects can be honored and laid to rest. Recovering it from the flooded wreck may bring some solace to the survivors on the mainland.

item:mo-grosh-crystal.text: Mo'grosh Crystal. In northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh ogres mine and guard rare crystals with unusual alchemical properties. Dwarven engineers use them to neutralize Dark Iron explosives. Mo'grosh ogres mine the crystals at their stronghold in northeastern Loch Modan. Though the clan favors brute strength over delicate metalwork, its members prize these stones. Enforcers, mystic shamans, and towering leaders carry them. The crystals are uncommon, so the ogres guard them closely within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

item:modr-fragment.text: Modr Fragment. At Whelgar Excavation Site, Modr Fragment lies among the relics and loose earth of a raptor-overrun dig. The ancient Titan script on it is one of four missing pieces of the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone, a massive tablet marked with ancient Titan writing, at his Wetlands dig. Vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from the site before they could finish their work. The translated inscription broke off at four gaps, hiding warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. Modr Fragment is one of the missing pieces, left among the relics and overturned soil when the diggers fled for their lives.

item:moldy-tome.text: Moldy Tome. Along the Hillsbrad coast, the Moldy Tome lies ruined after a shipwreck. Once part of the Tome of the Cabal, it still draws warlocks seeking its lore on demonic summoning. The Tome of the Cabal was a rare work of dark arts held in Lordaeron. Someone vandalized it and tore it in two. One half, now called the Moldy Tome, sailed south toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The ship never arrived. It sank in the dangerous waters west of Southshore, and the half that survived washed ashore south of Azurelode Mine. Damp and surf ruined its pages as murlocs scavenged along the Hillsbrad coast.

item:moonpetal-lily.text: Moonpetal Lily. Around Teldrassil’s freshwater pools, Moonpetal Lilies offer petals prized for their restorative power. Healers use them in remedies and healing draughts. Moonpetal Lilies grow along the moist banks of freshwater pools and ponds. They are common northwest of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Like other plants atop the young World Tree, they draw on the essence of Teldrassil’s sheltered groves. Their broad petals shine beside the water, where the moisture lets them thrive. Night elf healers and herbalists prize Moonpetal Lilies for their healing properties. Mixed with forest plants such as Hyacinth Mushrooms, the lilies help soothe and stabilize. Healers brew antidotes from them for deadly toxins, including the venom of Webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave.

item:moonstalker-fang.text: Moonstalker Fang. Near Auberdine, travelers gather Moonstalker Fangs for Wizbang Cranktoggle's sampling devices. The teeth come from the moonstalkers of Darkshore. Moonstalker Fangs come from saber cats that hunt along Darkshore’s forest fringes. Their long teeth can shear flesh and bone. Wizbang Cranktoggle, an eccentric gnome tinkerer, uses them in a different way. North of Auberdine, near the bridge, Buzzbox 323 crushes the durable fangs to dust for his ecological surveys.

item:moonwell-water-tube.text: Moonwell Water Tube. At Auberdine, water from the moonwell carries purifying nature magic. The vial is used to test a mysterious red crystal set among Darkshore’s eastern ridges. Water from Auberdine’s moonwell fills the tube. The sacred pool is tied to Elune and holds restorative, purifying magic. Even a small amount can be used against corruption or to test strange mystical forces.

item:mossy-tumor.text: Mossy Tumor. Around Wellspring Lake, mossy tumors mark Teldrassil's spreading corruption. Carved from the bark and flesh of corrupted timberlings, these poisonous growths show the malevolence taking hold in the young World Tree. Teldrassil's timberlings were made to nurture and tend the great tree's boughs, but many have grown hostile and diseased. Mossy tumors are signs of that sickness made flesh. Thick with toxins, they spread across the Mire Beasts, Tramplers, and Elder Timberlings around Wellspring Lake. Rellian Greenspyre and the keepers in Darnassus send travelers to cut away the tumors and burn them thoroughly, so their poison cannot take deeper root in the island's soil.

item:mountain-lion-blood.text: Mountain Lion Blood. Across Hillsbrad and Alterac, Mountain Lion Blood draws Apothecary Lydon’s interest. In Tarren Mill, Lydon seeks fresh blood to make the Royal Apothecary Society’s dreaded Elixir of Pain. Mountain lions prowl the highlands and foothills of Hillsbrad and Alterac. Hunters prize their pelts and claws, while the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society seek the blood in their veins. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill believes fresh mountain lion blood can form the base of a potent brew meant to bring misery to the living. Apothecary Lydon’s experiments in Tarren Mill support the Royal Apothecary Society’s work to perfect the Forsaken’s New Plague. Lydon gathers blood from vigorous wild beasts to refine a concoction called the Elixir of Pain, testing how local organic compounds can be turned against the enemies of the Dark Lady.

item:mudsnout-blossom.text: Mudsnout Blossom. Mudsnout Blossoms grow in Nethander Stead, south of Tarren Mill. Mudsnout gnolls guard the foul, toxic mushrooms, and Apothecary Lydon seeks them for his elixir research. South of Tarren Mill, Mudsnout Blossoms grow in Nethander Stead. Despite their name, they are large, foul-smelling mushrooms that flourish in soiled dirt among the local Mudsnout gnolls' camps. The gnolls defend the territory fiercely. The mushrooms' spores and flesh poison living things, causing agony and rapid bodily decay.

item:mudsnout-composite.text: Mudsnout Composite. At Tarren Mill, Mudsnout Composite is prepared for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a new plague. Apothecary Lydon makes it from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills and sends it to the Undercity. Apothecary Lydon makes Mudsnout Composite from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The paste is noxious on its own, but Master Apothecary Faranell must bind it with a colloid of decay to bring out its deadlier qualities. Together, the ingredients form a key chemical component in the Dark Lady's Elixir of Agony.

item:mudsnout-mixture.text: Mudsnout Mixture. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell prepares a base for a deadly Forsaken poison. Mudsnout Mixture begins with mushrooms sent north from Tarren Mill. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon. He sends a composite made from Mudsnout Blossoms north to the Undercity. The toxic mushrooms grow at Nethander Stead, held by gnolls. Master Apothecary Faranell sees promise in the composite and adds his own colloid of decay. The resulting Mudsnout Mixture is volatile. It steadies the mushroom compound and prepares its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement in the foothills.

item:murloc-head.text: Murloc Head. Along the Western Strand, Murloc Head is grim proof of a threat Southshore wants brought under control. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle collects the severed heads for Marshal Redpath, who requires evidence of the murlocs being culled. Southshore's fishermen and coastal travelers face an immediate threat from aggressive murlocs along the Western Strand. Alliance fighters often clear the beaches, but Marshal Marcus Redpath wants proof before he approves reports of the threat being reduced. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle hires fighters to bring him murloc heads. Farren finds the work repulsive, and the sight has spoiled his appetite for Southshore's seafood.

item:musquash-root.text: Musquash Root. Beneath the Stonewrought Dam, Musquash Root grows in the Wetlands. Few gather it, though a hidden coven beneath Stormwind needs it for a brew. Musquash Root grows in the damp ground beneath the Stonewrought Dam's falls. Mist and seclusion make it hard to gather. Few herbalists seek it, but practitioners of the darker arts prize its chemical and alchemical properties.

item:mysterious-fossil.text: Mysterious Fossil. Along Darkshore's coast, Prospector Remtravel uncovers the Mysterious Fossil. The Explorers' League sends it across the sea for study. Prospector Remtravel uncovers an unusual fossil while working along Darkshore's wild coast. He arranges for dwarven scholars to receive it instead of leaving it in the wilderness. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sees an extraordinary find among the stones of Kalimdor.

item:nak-s-skull.text: Nak's Skull. In the southern Barrens, Nak leads Razormane warbands against the Horde. His skull proves his defeat and gives Mangletooth a means to avenge betrayal by his former kin. Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane lead raids from Razorfen Kraul across the Barrens. Their warbands strike Horde settlements and roads, while defenders at the Crossroads do not know the three commanders are planning attacks beyond ordinary tribal skirmishing. At Camp Taurajo, the captive Razormane Mangletooth has been left to die in a cage by his own people. He now seeks revenge against those former brethren. Mangletooth demands proof that Nak and his companions are dead: their severed skulls, delivered by Horde adventurers. He means to use that proof to break the southern raiding parties.

item:nek-rosh-s-head.text: Nek'rosh's Head. In the Wetlands, Nek'rosh's Head proves the Dragonmaw chieftain has fallen. Captain Stoutfist receives it as proof that the threat to Menethil Harbor has been broken. The Dragonmaw clan gathers forces and siege weapons across the marshlands, threatening the Alliance port of Menethil Harbor. After the clan's catapults are burned, the port's defense depends on killing Chieftain Nek'rosh. His severed head gives Captain Stoutfist and the Ironforge authorities proof that the warlord's hold over the Wetlands is broken.

item:neru-fragment.text: Neru Fragment. Unearthed from disturbed earth, the Neru Fragment carries part of the Goaz Stone's ancient Titan script. The relic was discovered at Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, and its words tell of Azeroth's primeval history. Prospector Whelgar led the dwarven expedition that discovered the Goaz Stone. The relic broke into four pieces: Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. Raptors overran the dig, halting the work, and the Neru Fragment remained beneath loose soil among the aggressive beasts. Once recovered, it can join the other pieces and restore the tablet. Its surviving words speak of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy, giving dwarven scholars a record to decipher.

item:nessa-s-collection.text: Nessa's Collection. At Rut'theran Village, fish bones and scales gathered from nearby waters are prepared for study by Laird in Auberdine. Nessa's Collection shows the great size of aquatic life around Teldrassil's roots. Nessa Shadowsong lives in Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base, where she gathered fish bones and scales to compare island sea life with that of mainland Kalimdor. Catches from the waters around the Great Tree grow to striking size. Nessa sent physical proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant along Auberdine's docks. The parcel travels through Vesprystus, Rut'theran's hippogryph master, and offers practical evidence of Teldrassil's growing vitality. In Darkshore, Laird finds that the specimens far outsize their mainland counterparts. The collection holds jawbones nearly twice the size of those from fish native to the Darkshore coast, and scales as large as a clenched fist. For coastal night elves, the package offers a clear look at how greatly the waters around Teldrassil differ from northern Kalimdor's somber shores.

item:nether-gem.text: Nether Gem. Across Tirisfal Glades, the Nether Gem carries Gunther Arcanus’s image to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Gunther entrusts it to an emissary after his lost spellbook is returned, opening a path to the Forsaken.

item:ng-5.text: NG-5. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Gaxim Rustfizzle needs NG-5 for his explosive plans. The volatile chemical is Nitromirglyceronium, the ignition compound he needs to set off wagons loaded with dynamite as a distraction. Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome operative in the Stonetalon Mountains, needs NG-5 for his engineering plans. The compound is formally known as Nitromirglyceronium, a hazardous chemical solution that demands care—or reckless gnomish enthusiasm. Gaxim says it provides the reaction needed to detonate entire wagons loaded with dynamite, creating a massive explosion to distract his adversaries in the region.

item:nida-s-necklace.text: Hilary's Necklace. In Lakeshire, Hilary searches for the necklace she lost in Lake Everstill. Her father gave it to her when she was young, and it slipped beneath the water while she and the other children fished by the docks. Hilary lost her necklace while fishing with her friend Shawn along the Lakeshire shore. Her father had given it to her, and she treasures the gift. Fierce beasts and aggressive murlocs live in the lake's depths, so local children stay on the docks. The necklace remains beneath the water, buried in the lakebed silt.

item:nightmare-shard.text: Nightmare Shard. In the Wailing Caverns, a glowing shard bears a taint Falla Sagewind cannot ignore. She binds its pure, disturbed essence of the Emerald Dream into the Nightmare Shard and sends it to senior druids for a warning kept from others. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Falla Sagewind examines a mysterious glowing shard and finds its energy darker than she expected. It reflects an unnatural affliction in the Emerald Dream, like a waking nightmare. Falla binds this tainted essence into the Nightmare Shard and orders it carried without delay to elder leaders of the Cenarion Circle.

item:nightsaber-fang.text: Nightsaber Fang. In Teldrassil, hunters take fangs from the nightsabers prowling the forest. Woodland residents also seek these teeth as reagents. Nightsabers hunt beneath Teldrassil’s canopy, among the deadliest natural predators of northern Kalimdor. Night elves revere them for their agility, ferocity, and deep spiritual bond with Elune. A hunter who kills one can take its sharp fangs as proof of skill. Some figures in the forest seek those fangs for darker rites.

item:nissa-s-remains.text: Nissa's Remains. Nissa's remains belong to a noblewoman of the once-wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal Glades. Slain and made mindless servants of the Scourge during the Third War, Nissa and her family are now hunted by former laborers seeking vengeance. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest and most influential dynasty. Their prosperous mills stood across the northern hills. When the Plague of Undeath spread through Lordaeron, the family patriarchs refused to flee. They fortified their estates and persuaded their retainers and laborers to stay and fight. Their pride cost them their lives. The Scourge slew the Agamands, then raised them as mindless thralls bound to the Lich King's will. In Brill, survivors who later broke free under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner still remember the Agamands' fatal pride. Coleman Farthing, once a laborer in their mills, resents his former masters for luring the workers into undeath. He charges adventurers with putting down the risen Agamands and retrieving their physical remains, including Nissa's. For Farthing and other Forsaken, destroying these relics offers a grim sense of closure and revenge.

item:nitroglycerin.text: Nitroglycerin. At Bael Modan, Nitroglycerin helps the dwarves drive their excavation through tauren lands. Their soldiers and officers carry the volatile chemical, which can also be used against the fortress. Bael Modan's dwarves dig into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tauren with heavy drillers and volatile chemicals. At the excavation site and its fortified keep, they keep nitroglycerin close to blast deep holes and break apart hills. Soldiers and officers, including Lord Cyrik Blackforge, carry vials of the fluid as the digging continues.

item:nondescript-letter.text: Nondescript Letter. Calvin Montague sends a Nondescript Letter east from Deathknell to Innkeeper Renee in Brill. He gives it to newly awakened Forsaken as an excuse to leave the valley and reach the Gallows' End Tavern. Calvin Montague asks newly arisen Forsaken near Deathknell to carry an unmarked envelope east to Brill. He claims he is tired from fighting zombies and spiders, and says the letter is for an innkeeper named Renee. His promise of rich compensation sounds hollow, and the errand takes travelers out of the valley toward the Gallows' End Tavern.

item:nori-s-mug.text: Nori's Mug. In Dun Morogh, Nori Pridedrift sends a mug of mornbrew to Anvilmar. Travelers bring the drink to Durnan Furcutter, then return the empty mug to its owner. Nori Pridedrift lends his mug for a delivery through Dun Morogh's freezing passes. It carries hot mornbrew to Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar, where the drink comforts him against the bitter cold. After Durnan drains it, the mug returns to Nori. He reminds travelers that mugs do not grow on trees and expects his sturdy drinking vessel back.

item:notched-rib.text: Notched Rib. At Agamand Mills, Notched Ribs prove the Forsaken are breaking the Scourge's hold on Tirisfal. Across northern Tirisfal Glades, the Scourge gathers skeletons in ruined armor. Cracked Skull Soldiers and Rattlecage Soldiers attack any living being or creature with free will they meet. Blades leave their brittle bones pitted and scored. Deathguards demand proof that Forsaken scouts and volunteers are killing these mindless intruders. A battle-marked rib shows that another of the Lich King's thralls has been shattered. Northwest of Brill, the Agamand Mills hold a key position. If the Scourge settles among the ruined farmsteads and windmills, the undead gain a base from which to strike deep into Tirisfal. Deathguard Dillinger watches the northern roads and sends champions to break up the skeleton ranks before they can gather strength. The notched ribs brought back to Brill show that the Forsaken line holds as it wears down the Scourge vanguard bone by bone.

item:nugget-slug.text: Nugget Slug. Tool buckets at the Sludge Fen hold nugget slugs the Venture Company uses in its heavy equipment. Tinkerers seek the seventeen-point-five-gauge fasteners for work on volatile machinery. At the Venture Company’s extraction sites, nugget slugs fasten heavy equipment. They are made for demanding industrial assemblies and sized at seventeen-point-five gauge. Ordinary trade brings them little use. Yet tinkerers need them for custom goblin hardware.

item:ogre-s-monocle.text: Ogre's Monocle. In southern Duskwood, Zzarc'Vul wears an immense monocle. Its lens has the exact dimensions Viktori Prism'Antras needs for a stargazing telescope in Darkshire. Zzarc'Vul, an ogre, wears a huge monocle tailored to his massive stature. When Viktori Prism'Antras of Darkshire began building a stargazing instrument from blueprints by the gnome engineer Cog, ordinary lenses proved too small. Zzarc'Vul's eyewear is the only polished glass in the region with the size and curve needed to focus light through the finished telescope. The Vul'Gol Ogre Mound lies in the shadow of southern Duskwood, where Zzarc'Vul lives among his brute brethren. The brute shows little wish to give up his distinctive accessory. To claim the lens, you must defeat him on his own ground, then carry the glass back to Darkshire so Viktori can turn his gaze to the night skies.

item:okra.text: Okra. At Saldean's Farm, Okra helps feed Westfall's homesteaders. The crop grows in the farm's plots and thickens the stews that sustain them. Saldean's Farm still yields vegetables while much of Westfall lies fallow, threatened by Defias outlaws and rogue harvest golem attacks. Okra grows in the tilled plots around the farm and persists through the harsh conditions. It nourishes local homesteaders when trade and supplies from Stormwind run dry. Salma Saldean's famous Westfall Stew depends on okra. She combines sliced pods with whatever meat settlers can hunt across the dusty plains, including vulture flesh, goretusk snouts, and coastal murloc eyes. The pods break down in the heat, thickening thin broth into a filling, restorative meal. For settlers clinging to their homesteads, fresh okra turns sparse scavenging into a hot supper.

item:ordanus-head.text: Ordanus' Head. At Raynewood Retreat, Ordanus' Head is claimed as proof that Keeper Ordanus has fallen. Blood elf magi Braelyn Firehand seeks it in Ashenvale. Keeper Ordanus was an ancient keeper of the grove and one of Cenarius's elder sons. Braelyn Firehand climbed the heights of Stonetalon Mountains on her master's orders, seeking to end the druids' stifling of magic at the peak and take vengeance on Ordanus. Before she could strike, the keeper was spirited away to the heart of Ashenvale. Braelyn used arcane scrying to peer through the forest canopy and found his sanctuary in the boughs of Raynewood Retreat. She demanded his severed head as proof that the wild demigod's arrogance had been answered.

item:orendil-s-cure.text: Orendil's Cure. In northern Ashenvale, Orendil Broadleaf brews a draught for a child in Astranaar. He uses rare Bathran's Hair to treat Relara Whitemoon's mysterious, deathly sickness. Relara Whitemoon, still young, fell deathly ill in Astranaar, and ordinary remedies failed. Her father, Pelturas Whitemoon, sought help from Orendil Broadleaf, a hermit and master of natural medicine who lives in northern Ashenvale. Orendil used bundles of rare Bathran's Hair gathered from the haunted ruins of Bathran's Haunt to brew a draught for Relara. When the vial arrives, it gives Pelturas hope. Yet the cure only slows the disease, so he must seek the further remedies Orendil suggested.

item:oslow-s-toolbox.text: Oslow's Toolbox. Foreman Oslow needs tools for Lakeshire's defenses, but they lie beneath Lake Everstill. Sent from Goldshire, the chest went down when Blackrock orcs struck its boat with a catapult. Foreman Oslow needs construction tools to keep Lakeshire's defenses and buildings in repair. Blackrock orcs besiege the Redridge Mountains, and the bridge into town lies destroyed. The tools came from Goldshire, so the shipment crossed Lake Everstill in a rowboat. Blackrock forces struck the vessel with a catapult, sending the boat and Oslow's heavy chest into the depths among the murlocs.

item:osric-s-crate.text: Osric's Crate. At Sentinel Hill, Osric's Crate brings fresh armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia. The defenders face the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls without the Stormwind army. Quartermaster Lewis receives the shipment and shares the protective gear among the volunteer fighters. The crown gives the People's Militia no formal support. These freshly made suits are meant to help the volunteers hold their position. From Dungar Longdrink's roost in Stormwind's Trade District, a gryphon carries the crate to Thor at Sentinel Hill. The flight avoids dangerous roads through Elwynn Forest and across the Westfall border, where bandits may ambush travelers. Gryphons help keep frontier garrisons supplied during wartime.

item:package-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Package of Empty Ooze Containers. In Ironforge, a package of empty ooze containers is bound for dangerous sampling in Felwood. Laris Geardawdle supplies jars that can hold tainted and cursed ooze without dissolving. Laris Geardawdle sends a dozen empty jars with travelers bound for Felwood. Six are for cursed ooze and six for tainted ooze. Raw specimens are caustic, and ordinary luggage can be eaten away by them. Sturdy, sealed glass keeps the acidic residue contained on the journey across continents to Laris's workbench in Ironforge. Laris Geardawdle's interest in ooze reaches beyond an eccentric hobby. He has seen Forsaken researchers from the Royal Apothecary Society harvesting these strange organisms across Azeroth, and wonders what they know. He suspects slimes may be primordial secretions tied to the world's creation. Field agents gather evidence in his jars, which he hopes will win him acclaim within the Explorers' League.

item:painted-gnoll-armband.text: Painted Gnoll Armband. At Westbrook Garrison, Painted Gnoll Armbands prove Riverpaw gnolls have been slain. Their packs press against Elwynn Forest's western border. Riverpaw warriors and scavengers wear rough bands marked with crude tribal patterns. These armbands come from Riverpaw gnolls along Elwynn Forest's wilderness borders. Stormwind's defenders face a growing threat near Stone Cairn Lake and in the woods south of Westbrook Garrison. Stormwind's Army is stretched thin across the kingdom, leaving Westbrook Garrison hard pressed to guard the western border. Deputy Rainer offers a standing bounty for slaying Riverpaw Outrunners and Riverpaw Runts. The painted bands let the deputies tally bounties and thin the packs near nearby farmlands.

item:panther-cage-key.text: Panther Cage Key. The Panther Cage Key is a small metal key held by Wizlo Bearingshiner at Whitereach Post. It unlocks a reinforced cage holding an enraged, captive predator within the wreckage of an ambushed caravan in Thousand Needles. When a traveling caravan was attacked and ransacked by centaur raiders north of Whitereach Post, the goblin tinker Wizlo Bearingshiner barely escaped with his life. Amid the ruins of wagons and plundered cargo, the marauders left one thing entirely untouched: a sturdy cage housing a ferocious, rare panther. Around the predator's neck hung Wizlo's prized invention, a hypercapacitor gizmo. Unwilling to approach the snarling beast, the centaur gave the cage a wide berth, leaving Wizlo's key as the only way to open the door and retrieve the device.

item:parker-s-lunch.text: Parker's Lunch. Darcy packs Parker's Lunch in Lakeshire for Guard Parker's patrol. The meal offers a glimpse of the bonds and modest comforts among Redridge's defenders. Darcy, a waitress at the Lakeshire inn, packs a meal for Guard Parker. He patrols the exposed road south toward Duskwood while Redridge faces attacks from gnolls and Blackrock orcs. The garrison is stretched thin and cut off from Stormwind's aid, leaving guards to keep long, lonely watches. Darcy's small gesture keeps Parker fed and begins a bashful courtship between the two townspeople.

item:partially-filled-vessel.text: Partially Filled Vessel. Tenaron Stormgrip gives young night elf initiates the Partially Filled Vessel in Aldrassil. It carries blessed moonwell water from Shadowglen toward Dolanaar. Young kaldorei initiates gather blessed water from Shadowglen’s secluded moonwell. In Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip pours a sample into the vessel for its journey across Teldrassil. More water from the tree’s moonwells must be gathered to tend to the island’s health. Carry the vessel south through the valley gates, then follow the cobblestone roads west to Dolanaar. The journey takes a young adventurer beyond Shadowglen’s protected nursery and into Teldrassil’s wider wilds. At Dolanaar’s central moonwell, Corithras Moonrage takes the vessel and directs the next part of the ritual.

item:pendant-of-shadow.text: Pendant of Shadow. At the Tower of Ilgalar, Morganth carries the Pendant of Shadow as he pursues the Scythe of Elune. Theocritus wants the talisman brought to the Tower of Azora as proof Morganth has been slain.

item:pendant-of-the-sea-lion.text: Pendant of the Sea Lion. At the Shrine of Remulos, druids join the Pendant of the Sea Lion's two halves. The completed talisman marks an initiate's readiness to learn an aquatic form. A druid must master the water's dangers to claim the sea lion's aquatic aspect. The pendant has two halves, one embodying the agility to slip past aquatic predators, the other the endurance to withstand prolonged submersion. At the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, the pieces are joined into one. After the pendant is forged, an initiate brings it to an elder mentor. Turak Runetotem waits on the rises of Thunder Bluff, while Mathrengyl Bearwalker is in Darnassus. The talisman proves the initiate has completed trials under Dendrite Starblaze, allowing the elder to teach the secrets of taking an aquatic form.

item:perenolde-tiara.text: Perenolde Tiara. In the ruins of Alterac, the Perenolde Tiara has surfaced again. Dwarven craftsmen of Ironforge made the emerald-studded heirloom, and collectors in Stormwind seek it. The Perenolde family ruled Alterac until the kingdom fell during the Second War. Among their treasures was a delicate tiara, made by master jewelers in Ironforge and set with brilliant emeralds. After King Aiden Perenolde’s treachery brought Alterac to ruin, the tiara vanished amid the devastation of the high crags. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage, unearthed the tiara while searching Alterac’s ruins for abandoned wealth. Word of the relic reached Count Remington Ridgewell, a wealthy noble in Stormwind who collects famous relics for his family museum. Now the count seeks to take the tiara from the ogre.

item:phial-of-scrying.text: Phial of Scrying. In Darkshore, scouts use the Phial of Scrying to reach Onu from afar. The ancient of lore provides the enchanted vessel, which calls forth a bowl for scrying across corrupted woodlands. The Phial of Scrying carries mystical waters that form a temporary bowl on the ground. Scouts investigating deep within Darkshore use it for long-distance divination. From perilous places such as the Master's Glaive, they can speak directly with Onu instead of returning to his grove.

item:piece-of-krom-zar-s-banner.text: Piece of Krom'zar's Banner. At Regthar Deathgate's bunker west of the Crossroads, a torn banner marks the broken assault. Warlord Krom'zar led the Kolkar retaliatory force from Desolace. Warlord Krom'zar led a warband east from Desolace to strike back. Kolkar chieftains across the Barrens had fallen, and the furious centaurs attacked the defensive bunkers west of the Crossroads. A strip cut from Krom'zar's fallen standard gives Regthar Deathgate proof that the assault was crushed and the southern trade routes were preserved for the Horde.

item:plainstrider-beak.text: Plainstrider Beak. Across the Barrens, hunters bring Plainstrider Beaks back to the Crossroads. Huntmasters use them as proof that birds threatening local provisions have been culled. Plainstriders forage around the Crossroads and threaten its supplies. Greater, fleeting, and ornery plainstriders roam the surrounding savannah. Sergra Darkthorn asks arriving hunters to bring back their beaks as proof that the flocks have been culled away from supply lines and storehouses.

item:plainstrider-feather.text: Plainstrider Feather. On Red Cloud Mesa, young hunters gather Plainstrider Feather from the birds roaming Mulgore’s plains. Camp Narache uses them for clothing and tribal adornments, honoring the creatures that provide for the village. Young tauren on Red Cloud Mesa learn to track and hunt for what the tribe needs. Plainstriders roam the grassy plateau, providing food and useful feathers. Camp Narache makes garments and gear from their plumage. Young hunters bring feathers and fresh meat to Grull Hawkwind to meet the camp’s needs. The offering is their first test before Chief Hawkwind recognizes them and welcomes them in Thunder Bluff.

item:plainstrider-kidney.text: Plainstrider Kidney. Across the Barrens, hunters harvest Plainstrider Kidney for Kalimdor's unusual brewing traditions. The organ is unappetizing to most travelers, yet essential to an exotic brew. The vast, arid plains of the Barrens are home to tall, flightless plainstriders. Hunters often take their feathers and meat for tools and simple rations, while Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks their internal organs for another purpose. Drohn says plainstrider kidneys are needed to recreate Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. He claims the kidneys give the brew a unique kick, in a tradition passed down through an unconventional line of brewmasters.

item:plainstrider-meat.text: Plainstrider Meat. Across Red Cloud Mesa, Plainstrider Meat helps feed Camp Narache. Young tauren hunt the birds for food and feathers, proving their skill and self-reliance. Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa depends on game from the surrounding grasslands. Plainstrider meat helps feed the village when food stocks run low. The birds also provide feathers for clothing and ceremonial adornments. Tauren life depends on the land, and survival means taking what is needed while respecting nature. Grull Hawkwind sends young hunters across Red Cloud Mesa to track the swift plainstriders. They gather meat and feathers to prove their tracking skill and self-reliance. Then they appear before Grull's father, Chief Hawkwind.

item:plainstrider-scale.text: Plainstrider Scale. Across Mulgore, Plainstrider Scale is sought for a remedy Maur Raincaller prepares in Bloodhoof Village. The tough scale helps counter a spreading infection. Plainstriders roam Mulgore with tough scales covering their powerful legs. The scales protect them, though only some are firm enough to grind for folk remedies.

item:plainstrider-talon.text: Plainstrider Talon. Across Mulgore, tauren shamans gather Plainstrider Talon for cleansing totems. The sharp claws come from large, flightless plainstriders native to the region, and help cleanse corrupted water. Large, flightless plainstriders roam Mulgore’s open grasses, using powerful legs and sharp claws to forage through tough prairie earth and defend against predators. To the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, every part of a hunted beast carries spiritual resonance. When goblin ventures tainted sacred sources such as the Winterhoof Water Well, shaman Mull Thunderhorn sought plainstrider talons alongside prairie wolf paws. In tauren ritual crafting, reagents from native predators and foragers channel the land’s spiritual essence into totems that can purge unnatural poisons.

item:podrig-s-order.text: Podrig's Order. At the Sepulcher, Podrig's Order calls for fresh weapons from the Undercity. Deathguard Podrig found the Sepulcher's stores mostly adequate after an inventory ordered by Executor Hadrec. Replacement weapons were running desperately low. His dispatch lists the blades and arms needed by the Deathguards holding the outpost in Silverpine Forest, a frontier threatened by the Scourge, feral beasts, and other dangers. The order goes to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, because the damp crypts of Silverpine make forging weapons difficult.
