Couriers carry the document to bat master Karos Razok, using Forsaken flight paths to speed the shipment from the capital.

item:pork-belly-pie.text: Pork Belly Pie. In Elwynn Forest, Billy Maclure waits for a pie from Stonefield Farm before he speaks of a missing necklace. Auntie Bernice bakes it despite the families’ long feud. The Stonefield and Maclure families have quarreled over land and pride for years. Young Billy Maclure has a weakness for Auntie Bernice’s pork belly pie. When a valuable Stonefield family necklace goes missing, Billy refuses to share what he knows until an adventurer brings him a warm slice. Bernice bakes it reluctantly, wishing the greedy boy would choke on it.

item:powdered-azurite.text: Powdered Azurite. In Hillsbrad Foothills, Powdered Azurite is taken from the Azurelode Mine. Thun'grim Firegaze needs it to forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors. Powdered Azurite comes from the mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. Human workers dig the blue stone from Azurelode Mine, then grind and pack it for trade and metalworking. A skilled smith mixes the dust with dense metals to make armor more durable and resilient. Horde blacksmiths prize Powdered Azurite for its strength in metalworking, though it comes from human-held tunnels across the Great Sea. Thun'grim Firegaze, an aging orc armorer in the Barrens, asks for small amounts alongside refined iron and fiery reagents. Mixed into the smelt, the powder helps him hammer out the heavy plating of his Brutal Armor.

item:powers-of-the-void.text: Powers of the Void. In Northshire, a stolen tome draws Drusilla La Salle's attention. A novice took Powers of the Void from a guarded wing of Northshire Abbey's library while leaving to join the Defias Brotherhood. Drusilla seeks the book for her own study of dark magic. Powers of the Void was kept behind guarded shelves in Northshire Abbey's library. The abbey archives hold holy scripture and clerical records, as well as scholarly works on shadow and nether energies. The archmage Khadgar is believed to have penned the tome. Its subject was dangerous, so abbey authorities kept it under guard and away from casual visitors. That kept Drusilla La Salle, Northshire's warlock mentor, from browsing it without drawing the priesthood's suspicion. A Northshire novice carried the tome away when he abandoned his vows to join the Defias Brotherhood. As he fled into the neighboring vineyards, he took several valuable volumes from the abbey. Drusilla sends promising warlock initiates to the Defias bandit camp to recover the book from their tents. She wants its dark knowledge for her own study. The effort tests whether an initiate has the nerve to bind otherworldly demons.

item:prairie-alpha-tooth.text: Prairie Alpha Tooth. Around Thunder Bluff, prairie wolf alphas roam Mulgore’s open plains. Mull Thunderhorn needs their teeth to cleanse the Wildmane Well. Mulgore’s wells sustain the tauren, and keeping them pure calls for rites of respect and sacrifice. Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village needs teeth from the prairie wolf alphas that prowl beneath Thunder Bluff to cleanse the Wildmane Well. These fierce pack leaders embody the strength of the wild. Their teeth honor the balance between hunter, prey, and the spirits of the earth.

item:prairie-wolf-heart.text: Prairie Wolf Heart. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village needs a Prairie Wolf Heart for a remedy against venom. Maur Raincaller lives in Bloodhoof Village and is suffering from the venom of Mazzranache, the legendary plainstrider. The bite brings fever and threatens to spread poison through him. Maur seeks the heart of a prairie wolf, along with cougar bone and bird gizzard, for a traditional plains remedy meant to stop the infection before delirium proves fatal.

item:prairie-wolf-paw.text: Prairie Wolf Paw. Across Mulgore, Prairie Wolf Paws are gathered from the wolves that hunt the plains. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village uses them with plainstrider talons to make a cleansing totem. Prairie wolves hunt in packs across Mulgore’s rolling grasses, alongside prairie stalkers and their pack alphas. They threaten young hunters and local livestock, and their place in the spiritual balance of the plains matters to tauren shamans. The shamans see the paws as more than trophies: they carry the land’s innate vitality. When goblin ventures tainted Mulgore’s sacred water reserves, shaman Mull Thunderhorn needed the land’s physical aid against the pollution. Joined with plainstrider talons, wolf paws provide the spiritual resonance for cleansing totems. With one made, the work of purifying the Winterhoof Water Well can begin.

item:pridewing-venom-sac.text: Pridewing Venom Sac. Around Mirkfallon Lake, Pridewing Venom Sacs are sought by the night elves of Astranaar. Reports suggest Horde agents harvest the poison for covert attacks, and the Sentinels mean to deny them that supply. Pridewings hunt from the crags south of Ashenvale, especially around Mirkfallon Lake. These airborne predators are native to the Stonetalon Mountains, and their venom can be gathered from the glands in their bodies. Reports from Theramore suggest Horde assassins are taking that poison to coat blades for covert attacks on night elf settlements. In Astranaar, Sentinels send scouts to hunt the wyverns and collect their venom glands before Horde agents can claim them.

item:prismatic-punch-card.text:
Prismatic Punch Card. In Gnomeregan, the Prismatic Punch Card bears the highest security clearance. Gnome refugees in Ironforge seek the records it unlocks. When the gnomes fled Gnomeregan, troggs and toxic irradiation drove them from the city. Vast stores of research and civic records remained in its depths. The gnomes guarded high-level systems behind tiers of clearance. To reach the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D in the lower Engineering Labs, a card must pass through a series of terminals.

The card begins white, then advances through yellow, blue, and red. At the final terminal, it is stamped Prismatic. Its encoded clearance is listed as awaiting the invention of an entirely new number.

item:pristine-spider-silk.text: Pristine Spider Silk. In Duskwood, venomous spiders yield the fine thread Stormwind mages need for robes that endure enchantments. Stormwind mages need silk strong enough to bear enchantments and an adept’s wear. Tailors use common spider silk, but strands from carrion recluses and black widow hatchlings in Duskwood are more resilient. Mages from the Wizard’s Sanctum send rising adepts into those woods to gather it. Master tailor Wynne Larson then weaves the silk into a robe for an adept.

item:prowler-claws.text: Prowler Claws. Across the Barrens, Prowler Claws are carried back to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. They show that a hunter can track and defeat the prowlers stalking the plains. Savannah Prowlers hide in the Barrens’ tall grass, waiting to strike with patience and cunning. These large cats ambush creatures that enter their hunting grounds, unlike grazing plainstriders and zhevra. Taking their curved claws means facing predators that rely on stealth and defend their territory. For Horde warriors and scouts, the hunt tests whether they can track a stalker through its own ground and make it the prey. Sergra Darkthorn, the huntress at the Crossroads, asks initiates to bring back Prowler Claws before facing greater trials. The claws show that a hunter can follow tracks through the savannah grass and withstand a predator’s attack. Those who return with them have proved they can stay alert among the dangerous beasts of the plains.

item:pure-hearts.text: Pure Hearts. In the Undercity, Pure Hearts draw a succubus from the Twisting Nether. Carendin Halgar gives these ritual reagents to Forsaken warlocks, who use them to manifest the demon and attempt to defeat and bind her. Carendin Halgar gives Pure Hearts to warlocks who summon a succubus in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. Set on the summoning circle, these untainted spiritual essences lure the demon across the Twisting Nether and into the mortal realm. Once she appears, the warlock must resist her enthralling mind-charms and strike her down. Defeating the succubus asserts mystical dominance and sends her back to the Twisting Nether. Carendin then teaches the warlock the spell to summon her at will.

item:purified-kor-gem.text: Purified Kor Gem. At Jordan Stilwell’s forge outside Ironforge, a Purified Kor Gem is needed to shape a weapon of the Light. First, elven magic must cleanse the corrupted stone. Naga hold the Corrupted Kor Gem in Blackfathom Deeps, beneath Ashenvale’s coast. A paladin carries it to Thundris Windweaver, a night elf in Auberdine. There, Thundris draws on arcane and natural arts to purge its aquatic and shadowy taint. The stone emerges purified, ready to channel holy power. Jordan Stilwell, a human weaponsmith outside Ironforge, needs the gem for a masterwork weapon. He has long held designs for a weapon worthy of the Silver Hand, but lacked the rare materials to forge it. The Purified Kor Gem, Whitestone Oak Lumber, and rare ore give the weapon its spiritual core, to channel a paladin’s righteous wrath.

item:putrid-claw.text: Putrid Claw. Putrid Claws reach Deathguard Dillinger as proof that the Scourge near Brill is being held back. Mindless undead roam the woods west of town, especially by the old bridge. The mindless Scourge keeps crossing into Tirisfal Glades. Rotting dead and ravaged corpses wander the eastern borders, gathering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. Deathguards place bounties on these horrors to protect travelers and garrison supply lines. A severed putrid claw proves that one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

item:pyrewood-shackle.text: Pyrewood Shackle. At Pyrewood Village, enchanted shackles bind its beleaguered inhabitants to Archmage Arugal's strange magic. The bands are tied to the dark fate that grips the townsfolk when night falls.

item:quinn-s-potion.text: Quinn's Potion. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel brews Quinn's Potion to help an injured scout recover. Quinn Yorick needs it after a disastrous patrol in Silverpine Forest. Apothecary Renferrel brews a remedy for Deathstalker Quinn Yorick. Word reached the Royal Apothecary Society at the Sepulcher after Quinn was badly hurt and left unable to move near the Ivar Patch. Renferrel made the draught to help him recover. Though minor field casualties rarely draw Renferrel from his darker research for Lady Sylvanas, he supplied the remedy so the scout could regain enough strength to travel.

item:ran-bloodtooth-s-skull.text: Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. In Ashenvale, Ran Bloodtooth's Skull bears proof that a corrupted furbolg chieftain has fallen. The night elves of Astranaar receive it as a sign that a fierce threat to their woodland realm has ended. The furbolgs of Ashenvale have fallen into murderous madness under demonic taint and wilderness corruption. Ran Bloodtooth led one of the fiercest tribes. His skull gives the night elf Sentinels proof that he has fallen and his hold over the local furbolgs is broken, bringing some respite to Astranaar.

item:raptor-head.text: Raptor Head. Across the Barrens, Raptor Head trophies answer a bounty from Gazrog at the Crossroads. The guard payroll vanished from a watchtower, and a wild raptor was caught in the theft. A stolen chest of guard payroll has left the Crossroads watchtower without its silver. The defenders caught a wild raptor red-handed, to their disbelief. Gazrog has put a bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the Barrens. Bring their severed heads to the outpost, and the predators will be culled before they can pilfer more Horde supplies.

item:rare-earth.text: Rare Earth. At Dolanaar, Rare Earth waits for delivery to Denalan's camp near Lake Al'Ameth. The mineral-rich soil came from Darnassus for his botanical experiments on Teldrassil. Rare Earth is late reaching Dolanaar from Darnassus. Denalan, an eccentric botanist on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, requested the parcel to study plants in Teldrassil's young ecosystem. Herbalist Syral Bladeleaf now entrusts the soil to travelers heading south, hoping it reaches Denalan before its potency fades.

item:rattlecage-skull.text: Rattlecage Skull. In Deathknell, novice Forsaken warlocks gather skulls from mindless undead. Venya Marthand asks for them as a test of their will before teaching them the dark arts of summoning. In Deathknell, Venya Marthand guides newly raised Forsaken who have a gift for dark magic. She sends them to subdue Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy and bring back their severed skulls. The trial tests whether a fledgling warlock can bend creatures from beyond this world to their command. It also lays the groundwork for breaching the void and binding a first demonic servant.

item:raven-claw-talisman.text: Raven Claw Talisman. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Raven Claw Talisman is kept among relics needed to awaken sleeping druids. The sacred night elf relic is one of four Relics of Wakening used to guide the Druids of the Talon safely back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman rests in a designated chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den, where Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered deep meditative sleep. Their hibernation is a delicate spiritual threshold. Without the proper ceremonial focus, a druid whose link to the waking world is broken may remain stranded in the Emerald Dream. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs this talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting to perform the awakening ritual and bring the sleepers back safely. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, putting its sacred chests and sleeping druids in peril. Their desecration has cut the sanctuary off from outside aid, and the relics may be lost or destroyed. Athridas Bearmantle calls on Teldrassil's defenders to brave the den's winding earthen corridors and secure the Raven Claw Talisman before the displaced druids are lost to the Dream forever.

item:razorflank-s-medallion.text: Razorflank's Medallion. Charlga Razorflank's medallion lies deep within Razorfen Kraul, carried by the crone who rules the stronghold. Its return gives the night elf sentinels proof that she has fallen. Charlga Razorflank carries the medallion as the leader of the Razorfen quilboar. At Thalanaar, Falfindel Waywarder learns of fallen explorers such as Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow, then sends Alliance adventurers against the quilboar leader. The medallion confirms Charlga's death to the night elf sentinels guarding Feralas's borders. They can know that the gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

item:reagent-pouch-shaman.text: Reagent Pouch (shaman). Burning Blade cultists in Durotar carry reagents for a shaman's first fire sapta. Telf Joolam uses them with fire tar from Razormane quilboar to make the draught that lets a young shaman see the realm of fire. Burning Blade cultists carry reagents for a young shaman's first fire sapta. The hermit Telf Joolam uses the powders and oils in their pouches with fire tar from Razormane quilboar. Together, these components make a draught that grants sight into the realm of fire and attunes the shaman to the spirits of flame. Burning Blade cultists turn flame toward destruction and fel sorcery, yet the elements in their pouches still belong to heat and combustion. Shaman teach that elemental forces exist in tension: fire creates as well as destroys. A shaman can take the cultists' tools and use those elements to awaken true communion with the spirits.

item:reconstructed-tome.text: Reconstructed Tome. In warlocks’ hands, the Reconstructed Tome gathers the scattered teachings of the cabal. Its pages hold the rites for summoning and binding a felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Warlocks of the Alliance and Horde search for the torn leaves of the Tome of the Cabal. They piece the grimoire back together and consult occult scholars, who are eager to glimpse its rare teachings before the finished book is surrendered.

item:recruitment-letter.text: Recruitment Letter. Takrin Pathseeker sends promising adventurers from Durotar west to serve in the Barrens. His letter directs able-bodied volunteers to the border outpost run by Kargal Battlescar. Takrin Pathseeker watches young warriors and scouts prove themselves around Razor Hill. He chooses those who seem strong enough for frontline service and gives them a letter for duty in the Barrens. Across the Southfury River bridge, recruits leave Durotar’s sheltered red dirt and join the Horde’s guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Kargal Battlescar receives the recruits at the outpost just across the river. The grizzled veteran manages the post and evaluates each conscript before signing off on their enlistment. A signed recruit is soon sent farther west to the Crossroads, where the frontier outposts are stretched thin.

item:red-burlap-bandana.text: Red Burlap Bandana. Near the abbey vineyards in Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves. The cloth marks the Brotherhood's low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs of the Defias Brotherhood wear red burlap masks. The cheap, rough cloth hides their faces and marks their allegiance to the growing rebellion. They carry these scarves into the eastern orchards, where local guards recognize the red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

item:red-leather-bandana.text: Red Leather Bandana. In Westfall, the Red Leather Bandana marks those who defy Stormwind’s Crown. The Defias Brotherhood wears it to cover their faces and show their cause.

item:red-linen-bandana.text: Red Linen Bandana. Across Elwynn Forest, the red linen bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood and hides its wearers' faces. Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp wants the cloth for garments and bandages. In Northshire Valley, initiates and common thugs wear coarse burlap masks. The crimson linen marks the allegiance of full operatives to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals rebellion against Stormwind's crown. Sara Timberlain asks travelers to gather bandanas from outlaw encampments. The masks are tied to bandits, but their linen is respectable. Washed and worked with a needle, the cloth can become sturdy clothing and bandages for the forest's working folk.

item:red-wool-bandana.text: Red Wool Bandana. Inside the Stormwind Stockade, Red Wool Bandana scraps mark Defias brotherhood. Imprisoned cutthroats tear them from jailhouse wool blankets and wear them as emblems of defiance behind bars. In the Stormwind Stockade, Defias Brotherhood inmates hold fast to their identity. They secretly tear scraps from prison wool blankets and stitch them into red bandanas to wear as their colors. Guards treat the scarves as contraband, and their discovery can spark fatal mutinies. For the prisoners, each bandana declares that their brotherhood and rebellion endure, even in chains. Red Wool Bandanas became known for the death of Mac Raskol, a fourteen-year-old prison guard. He caught inmates shredding blankets to make the scarves and tried to discipline them. Defias convicts stabbed him in the back. His grieving grandmother, Nikova, now seeks adventurers to enter the rioting dungeon, cull the rioters, and bring back the crimson cloth as proof of vengeance.

item:remaining-drops-of-purest-water.text: Remaining Drops of Purest Water. Across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, shaman gather what Brine needs for a draught. Its last drops wait for a perilous journey. Brine prepares a water draught in the Barrens from water gathered across Kalimdor and Lordaeron. Part of it gives shaman vision of distant elements. The remaining drops are kept for a harder purpose. Shaman carry them to the coast of Silverpine Forest, near the Sepulcher, where the Brazier of Everfount stands. There, the drops are burned with the bracers of a fallen, tainted elemental. The pure water cuts through the undead plague’s corruption, calling an untainted water spirit to commune with the shaman and complete their communion with the element.

item:remedy-of-arugal.text: Remedy of Arugal. In Silverpine Forest, Dalar Dawnweaver seeks Arugal's spell to learn how his worgen magic works. Before taking Shadowfang Keep, Archmage Arugal sheltered at an abandoned wheat farm north of the river bridge in Silverpine Forest. He recorded his strange arts in spellbooks left among the farm tools and rotting floorboards. One scroll, the Remedy of Arugal, describes early methods and magical formulas from his experiments with the transmutations that cursed the local people. Dalar Dawnweaver, a Forsaken spellcaster at the Sepulcher, thinks little of Arugal's standing and considers his intellect fragile and transparent. Still, Dawnweaver needs to understand the worgen curse's workings. Recovering the Remedy gives Forsaken agents the arcane knowledge Dawnweaver seeks to counter Arugal's spreading menace and secure Silverpine for Lady Sylvanas.

item:rendered-spores.text: Rendered Spores. Across the Barrens, Rendered Spores are being rushed from Apothecary Helbrim to Thunder Bluff before they decay. Apothecary Zamah must stabilize the emulsion beneath the city. Apothecary Helbrim makes Rendered Spores from fungal spores gathered near the Barrens’ damp oases. He processes the strange spores into an active chemical emulsion, but it is unstable. After forty-five minutes, it breaks down and becomes useless for scientific study. Apothecary Helbrim cannot finish refining the emulsion at his remote outpost. It must reach his Forsaken colleague, Apothecary Zamah, beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. In the Pools of Vision, Zamah has the equipment and reagents to reseal and finish processing the spores for the Royal Apothecary Society.

item:renferrel-s-findings.text: Renferrel's Findings. In Silverpine Forest, Renferrel's Findings carry research south to Tarren Mill. Apothecary Renferrel gathered the notes at the Sepulcher for Apothecary Lydon, who is helping brew the Forsaken's New Plague. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel records his work on the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society labours under direct orders from Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Dark Lady. Researchers scattered across Lordaeron must work together to achieve a breakthrough. Renferrel sends his findings south to Tarren Mill, where fellow researchers can build on his results. The papers link Silverpine Forest to Hillsbrad Foothills and the Forsaken's alchemical network. Apothecary Lydon awaits Renferrel's notes in Tarren Mill, where he can compare them with his own work against the living and the Scourge. Reliable couriers must cross Hillsbrad's contested roads; without them, the Society's scattered research would quickly stall.

item:report-on-the-defias-brotherhood.text:
Report on the Defias Brotherhood. At Stormwind Keep, the findings on the Defias Brotherhood reach the royal court. City Architect Baros Alexston entrusts the report to the adventurer who uncovered the conspiracy. City Architect Baros Alexston prepared the report for Stormwind's leaders after a long investigation into unrest in Westfall and nearby lands. He entrusted it to the adventurer who unraveled the conspiracy.

The report is carried to Stormwind Keep for a personal audience. There, the findings concern the conspirators' schemes and the danger they pose to the kingdom.

item:resonite-crystal.text: Resonite Crystal. In Boulderslide Cavern, kobolds are digging frantically for Resonite Crystal. Their work has drawn Mor'rogal's concern at Sun Rock Retreat.

item:restabilization-cog.text:
Restabilization Cog. At Gnomeregan's gates, leper gnomes still carry Restabilization Cogs. In Kharanos, tinkerers need intact cogs for a machine meant to reverse leper mutation. Radiation flooded Gnomeregan in a failed attempt to wipe out the invading troggs. Countless gnomes fell sick and hostile, then fled their home as exiles. Even in their madness, they carry intricate gnomish machinery.

Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket believe the terrible change can be undone. Their prototype Recombobulation Device needs parts taken from the afflicted outside Gnomeregan's gates. Intact Restabilization Cogs will balance its inner combustion systems.

item:ring-of-zoram.text: Ring of Zoram. At Zoram, the ring of the city's rulers has surfaced again after millennia beneath the sea. The naga now hold it, and Talen seeks the key to an ancient statuette. Before the Well of Eternity collapsed, Zoram stood on Kalimdor's western coast as a jewel of the night elven empire. Its rulers wore the Ring of Zoram, whose inner band bears a strange code in the night elven language. The Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago, and the ring sank with the city beneath the tides. It lies beneath the waters of what is now the Zoram Strand. For millennia, silt and ruins hid the ring. Then naga began scouring Ashenvale's coast, and Ruuzel, a naga leader who dwells on an islet off the northern strand, uncovered it among the sunken debris. The night elf scholar Talen seeks the ring for more than its age. It is the only key that can unlock relics salvaged from the depths, including ancient statuettes sealed on the sea floor.

item:robo-mechanical-guts.text:
Robo-Mechanical Guts. In Stormwind, Shoni gathers parts from Gnomeregan’s roaming machines. She needs them to repair tunneling vehicles built to help reclaim the city in Dun Morogh. After High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the surviving gnomes fled Gnomeregan, thousands of machines remained behind. Automated mechanisms, clockwork sentries, and industrial robots still roam the radioactive city’s corridors.

In Stormwind City, tinker Shoni is assembling gyrodrillmatic excavationators to break through Gnomeregan’s defenses and reclaim the lost city. She sends adventurers into the contaminated halls to salvage working parts from the robots, including springs, wires, and gyro-components.

item:rocket-car-parts.text: Rocket Car Parts. Rocket Car Parts are the scattered, twisted metal remains of high-speed collisions across the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Constantly generated by reckless gnome and goblin racers pushing experimental speeders past their limits, these salvaged scraps are harvested by opportunists looking to turn racetrack accidents into quick coin. The Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats is the staging ground for an unending, combustible rivalry between goblin and gnome engineering. In their pursuit of unmatched land speed, racers regularly suffer catastrophic breakdowns, explosive misfires, and high-velocity crashes that scatter metal across the salt flats. These discarded remnants—ranging from bent cylinders and burnt gears to crushed sheet metal—do not stay abandoned for long. Scavengers and merchants, most notably the opportunistic dwarf Kravel Koalbeard, hire passing adventurers to comb the blinding white expanse and collect the debris. Because both racing teams are perpetually desperate for spare machinery to patch together their next prototype, scavenged wreckage can easily be resold directly back to the very teams that wrecked it.

item:rod-of-channeling.text: Rod of Channeling. In the Wetlands, the Rod of Channeling is carried by Dragonmaw spellcasters. Warlocks seeking to summon a felhunter gather three for Strahad Farsan's acolytes to steady the ritual circle in Ratchet. Warlocks need more than willpower to bind a volatile felhunter. Strahad Farsan asks for three matched rods so his acolytes can channel magic together and steady the summoning circle while the warlock binds the beast. Dragonmaw darkcasters carry these rods for their own workings. Bonewarders and shadowwarders bear them at Angerfang Encampment and in the surrounding Wetlands ruins. Combat leaves the rods worn and nicked, but they still focus chaotic nether energy.

item:rolf-and-malakai-s-medallions.text: Rolf and Malakai's Medallions. In eastern Elwynn, Rolf and Malakai's Medallions bear the realm's insignia, though their owners vanished on patrol. Guard Thomas seeks the tokens to learn what became of his men. Guard Thomas commands the station in eastern Elwynn. When Rolf and Malakai vanished along the riverbanks, he feared the worst. Their medallions confirm the guards died at the hands of encroaching murlocs. The Stormwind garrison has lost soldiers who held the line against wilderness threats while the kingdom's military was stretched thin. Human guards carry identification medallions on city watch and rural patrols. The tokens show their allegiance and authority under the crown. Returning Rolf and Malakai's medallions to Guard Thomas lets him account for his missing men and record their sacrifice in his field report. He can also warn of aggressive murloc tribes settling near the trade roads.

item:rot-blossom.text: Rot Blossom. Rot Blossoms grow among Duskwood's desecrated graves, fed by blighted soil and undead remains. Their foul alchemical properties make them sought after. In Duskwood, Rot Blossoms grow in the defiled earth of graveyards such as the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Local rumors say the blooms can take root inside the cracked skulls of Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends stalking the barrows. For people in Darkshire, gathering them is grim and dangerous. Disturbing the soil means facing the unrested dead. Rot Blossoms provide an ingredient for local brews. Their dark essences are needed to make Zombie Juice, a foul draft tied to Duskwood's efforts to survive. Those sent to gather the flowers often aid the Night Watch as they cut down restless skeletons wandering the haunted graves.

item:rot-hide-ichor.text: Rot Hide Ichor. On Fenris Isle, Rot Hide Ichor draws the Royal Apothecary Society’s attention. Apothecary Renferrel gathers it at the Sepulcher to learn what corrupted the gnolls and how to oppose them. On Fenris Isle, Rot Hide gnolls are no ordinary beasts. Their bodies are decomposed and twisted by an unnatural blight, and a noxious ichor flows through their veins to sustain their animated flesh. The Royal Apothecary Society suspects the fluid may reveal how the pack was corrupted and who commands them from within the ruined keep. At the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel gathers vials of the ichor for study. The Forsaken hope to isolate the chemical and magical forces that fuel the gnolls, then find their weaknesses before sending troops across Lordamere Lake in a full assault.

item:rough-quartz.text: Rough Quartz. In Durotar, a Rough Quartz comes from a Minor Manifestation of Earth. A shaman brings the stone to an elder, who binds it into the first Earth Totem. Rough Quartz is a gift from a Minor Manifestation of Earth to a shaman who communes with the spirits in Durotar or Mulgore. To the untrained eye, it looks like an ordinary desert pebble. The stone represents endurance, patience, and unwavering strength. At the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller binds it into carved wood to make an Earth Totem. The quartz becomes the spiritual focus joining a young shaman to Azeroth's living soil.

item:rumbleshot-s-ammo.text:
Rumbleshot's Ammo. Near the Grizzled Den, Rumbleshot's Ammo lies abandoned in the snow. Its courier fled from hungry wendigos before the crate could reach gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot in Dun Morogh. Hegnar Rumbleshot keeps a roadside arms shop on the mountain path from Coldridge Pass toward Anvilmar. Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar teams drill in the snowy heights, so his supplies run low as quickly as powder burns.

Loslor sent the shot from Kharanos, but the shipment never reached the shelves. Its courier camped too close to the Grizzled Den. When the wendigos attacked, the courier fled in panic and left the heavy crate in their hunting grounds.

item:rune-inscribed-parchment.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek hands aspiring orc shamans a message from Shikrik. It calls them to become spiritual leaders and conduits for elemental spirits. New orc shamans begin training under veteran overseers in the Valley of Trials. While an initiate performs initial trials for Gornek, he hands them a rune-covered document sent by Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor. The message summons them to deeper communion with the elements. Among the orcs, shamans mediate between the living and their ancestors. The writ marks a move from brute strength toward disciplined reverence for ancestors.

item:rune-inscribed-pendant.text: Rune-Inscribed Pendant. In Silverpine Forest, a Rune-Inscribed Pendant arrives at the Sepulcher in a shipment bound for Ambermill. The Kirin Tor use pendants like it to channel arcane power. A Rune-Inscribed Pendant is found among cartographic supplies bound for the Dalaran enclave at Ambermill. Its fine arcane inscriptions reveal its purpose: to focus and strengthen a wizard’s spells. More channeling pendants are arriving in the region, and the Forsaken at the Sepulcher wonder what the Kirin Tor are preparing.

item:rune-inscribed-tablet.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives young Darkspear troll shamans a stone message. It sends promising mystics to Shikrik to begin formal communion with the elements. Gornek gives the rune-carved stone to initiates who prove their mettle in the Valley of Trials. The troll shaman Ishi-yo sent it to direct them to Shikrik, the shaman trainer. For Darkspear trolls, the tablet begins a shared path with the orcs, joining their old spiritual traditions with the shamanic heritage Warchief Thrall has renewed.

item:rune-of-nesting.text: Rune of Nesting. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the Rune of Nesting lies among four sacred relics. It helps Athridas Bearmantle prepare the ritual that safely awakens the Druids of the Talon from the Emerald Dream. The Rune of Nesting lies in the Chest of Nesting, deep in the winding chambers of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Night elf druids hibernate in underground barrow dens to commune with nature through the Emerald Dream. To return safely, the Druids of the Talon need a precise awakening ritual guided by sacred relics. The rune is one of four: the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. Together, the relics help call the sleeping druids back to the waking world. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, putting its sleeping defenders in peril. Without the relics, the druids risk remaining trapped in the Emerald Dream while invaders desecrate their sanctuary. Recovering the Rune of Nesting and its companion artifacts allows Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar to prepare the ritual that can safely awaken them.

item:runes-of-summoning.text: Runes of Summoning. In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar gives warlocks runes for summoning a voidwalker. The ritual draws an unbound voidwalker into a circle, where an aspiring warlock can bend it to their will. Carendin Halgar gives the Runes of Summoning to warlocks ready to command a voidwalker. In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Forsaken practitioners study how to manipulate the Nether. A warlock casts the runes in the active summoning circle below Halgar's station. The ritual tears through the Void and draws forth a creature to be overpowered and bound into servitude.

item:sack-of-murloc-heads.text: Sack of Murloc Heads. Along the Hillsbrad beaches, a gruesome sack of Murloc Heads is gathered as proof of military action against local shore pests. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle hands the bundle to passing adventurers for delivery to Marshal Redpath in Southshore. Southshore faces constant attacks from Syndicate outlaws, Forsaken skirmishers, and wild murlocs along the coast. Local officers must show town leaders that coastal threats are being culled to secure funding and favor. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle collects severed heads as proof, but finds the cargo distasteful. His squeamishness leads him to hand the sack to travelers instead of bringing the grisly evidence to Marshal Redpath himself.

item:sack-of-supplies.text: Sack of Supplies. A caravan shipment bound for Rezlak lies scattered among the harpy roosts of Razorwind Canyon. Dustwind harpies intercepted the goods as they crossed Durotar. Rezlak needs steady supplies for his work outside Orgrimmar. The goblin engineer, contracted from Ratchet by Gazlowe, builds for the Horde. A caravan carrying a promised shipment passed near the canyon road south of Orgrimmar, where Dustwind harpies ambushed it. They dragged the cargo into their roosts in Razorwind Canyon, scattering sacks among dirt and scree beside their nesting sites.

item:salty-scorpid-venom.text: Salty Scorpid Venom. Salty Scorpid Venom is a caustic fluid harvested from the scorpids stalking the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Packed with natural salts from the desert floor, it is prized by gnomish rocket racers attempting to engineer volatile, ultra-hot fuel. The scorpids crawling the arid expanse of the Shimmering Flats have adapted to an intensely mineral-rich environment. Over generations, the venom of beasts like the Scorpid Reavers and Scorpid Terrors has absorbed enormous quantities of local salt. Rather than brewing antidotes or standard poisons, gnomish tinkers like Fizzle Brassbolts prize this caustic compound as a prospective additive for high-combustion engine fuel. Out at the Mirage Raceway, the engineering competition between gnomes and goblins drives inventors to test increasingly dangerous materials in their rocket cars. Fizzle Brassbolts believes boiling down the salted venom, treating it with specialized catalysts, and mixing it into propellant tanks will deliver the blazing heat necessary to outrun goblin racers on the salt pans.

item:samophlange-item.text: Samophlange (item). In the Barrens, Samophlange is hidden inside an automated control console. Goblin mechanics cannot explain what the strange component does. Samophlange lies inside a control console in the Barrens, behind a maze of wiring and hollow tubes. It takes careful searching to free the component from its housing. It looks like a vital part of clockwork and steam machinery, but goblin tinkerers cannot make sense of its purpose. They mean to send it to the Tinkers' Union in Undermine, though the fragile piece may not survive rough handling.

item:samophlange-manual.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob seeks the scattered pages of the Samophlange Manual. The handbook holds instructions for repairing and operating the Venture Company's samophlange. Boss Copperplug guarded the Venture Company's knowledge of the samophlange. The ambitious overseer kept the manual's pages from most workers, giving scattered leaves only to his most loyal subordinates. When the device slipped from company hands, no one could repair it without gathering the torn documentation from Copperplug and his crew at the Boulder Lode Mine. Rilli Greasygob left the Venture Company and settled in Orgrimmar to learn how the samophlange was built. Copperplug had never favored him, so Rilli depends on enterprising travelers to retrieve the manual's cover and loose leaves. Reassembled, the handbook gives goblin tinkerers working alongside the Horde a rare look at Venture Company engineering.

item:sample-ichor.text: Sample Ichor. In Silverpine Forest, Sample Ichor carries traces of necromancy and warlock sorcery. Apothecary Renferrel refined it from the fluid that sustains the Rot Hide gnolls. Apothecary Renferrel sent Sample Ichor to the Undercity for closer study. He recovered samples from the Rot Hide gnolls and their lingering remnants, then reduced the foul liquid to its base components. His analysis showed that the ichor was made through necromantic rites woven with warlock magic. Since its craft reaches beyond simple alchemy, Renferrel sent the sample to Bethor Iceshard for divination.

item:sample-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. A courier carries Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture across the sea to Tarren Mill. The brew came from the witch doctor Zanzil and leaves its carrier weakened. Serge Hinott may find a cure and uncover the poison's workings. An operative carries the mixture after infiltrating the Venture Company's tower near the Sludge Fen in the Barrens. The sample came from a cache in Gallywix's lockbox, and Zanzil's brew has left the agent afflicted. Shenthul sends the stricken operative across the Great Sea with the sample. At Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills, apothecary Serge Hinott has the rare skill to isolate the toxin and learn its components.

item:sample-snapjaw-shell.text: Sample Snapjaw Shell. Across the Barrens, Sample Snapjaw Shells carry lingering vitality from freshwater oases. Tauren druids send them across the Great Sea to help heal Silverpine Forest. Snapjaws thrive in the lush, strange oases of the Barrens. Their durable shells keep a faint inner glow and pulse with energy long after separation from the creature. Tauren druids watching the land's swift changes see in these carapaces the resilient spark of Kalimdor's wilderness. Their vigor shows how life can flourish even in harsh, arid surroundings. Tauren naturalists send couriers across the sea with shells for Mura Runetotem at the Sepulcher. Stationed in Silverpine Forest's blighted expanses, Mura seeks ways to help the Forsaken heal the northlands. She studies the life-force preserved in the snapjaw's armor, hoping to find what can renew an ailing forest and bring growth back to dying soil.

item:samuel-s-remains.text: Samuel's Remains. Near Deathknell, Samuel's Remains are gathered from a Scourge thrall and laid beside Marla. Samuel Fipps and his wife Marla lived peacefully in Tirisfal Glades before the plague of undeath swept across Lordaeron. Samuel succumbed to the contagion and became the Scourge's mindless servant. Marla escaped undeath, but Samuel struck her down. With her dying breath, she asked to be buried beside him once his cursed form was put to rest. Novice Elreth in Deathknell sends newly awoken Forsaken northeast of the settlement to find Samuel's wandering form, recover his bones, and bury them in the front row of the local cemetery.

item:sapphire-of-aku-mai.text: Sapphire of Aku'Mai. Along Blackfathom Deeps, the naga are harvesting the glowing Sapphires of Aku'Mai. Water spirits cling to the crystals, and Je'neu Sancrea seeks help confiscating them before their arcane power can be exploited. Blackfathom Deeps holds Sapphires of Aku'Mai in its watery cavern entrances along Ashenvale's Zoram Strand. Water spirits cling to the crystalline formations, rich in elemental energy, making them potent aids in magical workings. When scouts reported the subterranean naga quarrying the gems from cavern walls, Je'neu Sancrea, a shaman, sought adventuring help to confiscate them. In naga hands, the stones could fuel devastating arcane rites.

item:sapphire-of-sky.text: Sapphire of Sky. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Sapphire of Sky helps call sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. It is one of four sacred Relics of Wakening kept by the night elves. Druids of the Talon sleep in hibernation within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, deep among Teldrassil's roots, while they commune with the wilds. Waking from that deep trance is perilous. Four sacred relics protect the passage: the Black Feather Quill, the Raven Claw Talisman, the Rune of Nesting, and the Sapphire of Sky. The gem completes the harmony needed to call the sleeping spirits back from the Emerald Dream. Without it, they risk being trapped there forever. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den, leaving the sacred relics in their repositories. The Sapphire of Sky is secured inside the Chest of the Sky, along the winding underground corridors. The druids still sleep as the furbolgs rampage around them. Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar needs the sapphire and its companion relics to wake the sleepers before they are lost forever.

item:sara-balloo-s-plea.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. In her grief, Sara Balloo asks an Alliance champion to carry her handwritten appeal to King Magni Bronzebeard. Grief keeps Sara from facing the High Seat, so she entrusts her words to an adventurer loyal to the Alliance. She asks King Magni to remember the private mourning and sacrifices of ordinary dwarven families who serve the kingdom.

item:sarilus-foulborne-s-head.text: Sarilus Foulborne's Head. Across the border from the Barrens, Sarilus Foulborne's Head reaches Ashenvale as proof of the sorcerer's death. The undead mage defiled Ashenvale's waters, and the Sentinels demanded his head.

item:sarkoth-s-mangled-claw.text: Sarkoth's Mangled Claw. Across the southern bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth's Mangled Claw bears the mark of a wounded hunter. Hana'zua's crushing blow scarred the scorpid's pincer before its venomous sting struck him down. Hana'zua, a young Darkspear troll, met Sarkoth while hunting in the Valley of Trials. The massive scorpid's venomous stinger pierced his chest, leaving him bleeding beneath a nearby tree. Before the blow landed, Hana'zua crushed the beast's pincer. Its severed, battered claw proves Sarkoth has been slain. For the wounded hunter, that scar on the beast is proof his desperate strike left its mark, and a last hold on his warrior's honor as venom courses through his veins.

item:sarltooth-s-talon.text: Sarltooth's Talon. Above Whelgar's Excavation Site, Sarltooth's Talon marks the end of the raptor's attack. Ormer Ironbraid wants the claw as proof that the beast has been slain. Ormer Ironbraid watched from the ridge as raptors overran Whelgar's Excavation Site and butchered the dwarven expedition. He could not stop the slaughter. One massive raptor, Sarltooth, seemed to Ormer the likely pack leader. Seeking vengeance for his fallen kin, Ormer demanded the beast's death and one of its talons as proof. The claw marks the end of Sarltooth's reign over the ancient dwarven ruins.

item:sathrah-s-sacrifice.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah's spirit a chance at peace. Her silvery spinnerets come from the mighty spider who dwells in Teldrassil. Lady Sathrah was a venerable creature of Teldrassil, until creeping madness and corruption spread through the great tree's boughs and took hold of her. The Sisterhood of Elune asks you to bring back her silvery spinnerets as a consecrated offering, not a trophy. At the fountain in the Temple of the Moon, the remains are bathed in holy water. The rite washes away the taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind and frees her troubled soul. Her spirit then appears peacefully within the sanctuary, with the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

item:satyr-horns.text: Satyr Horns. In Ashenvale, Satyr Horns draw dryads seeking vengeance and traders bound for Ratchet. The horns come from satyrs whose corruption has taken root in the ancient forest. Ashenvale’s satyrs bear horns that mark their demonic corruption. At the Shrine of Aessina, the dryad Illiyana gathers them in grief and vengeance for her lost sister Anilia. Pixel, a traveling goblin resting at Splintertree Post, seeks them for trade. Demand for satyr horns has risen in Ratchet, where hunters can sell these remnants of slain demons. Satyr Horns must be cut from the beasts themselves; ordinary suppliers do not sell them. Satyrs hold strongholds across Ashenvale, including the corrupted groves of Xavian, the hollows of Satyrnaar, and the ruins of Night Run. Clearing these enclaves drives back the lingering demonic taint and supplies grieving guardians and eager merchants with proof of the cull.

item:savannah-lion-tusk.text: Savannah Lion Tusk. In the Barrens, Savannah Lion Tusks go from hunting trophies to ingredients in Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. The great cats roaming the Barrens carry sharp, heavy tusks. Prowlers, huntresses, prides ruled by patriarchs, and beasts like Humar the Pridelord all bear them. Travelers often take the teeth as proof of a successful hunt. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet uses the tusks with plainstrider kidneys and thunder lizard horns to recreate Chen Stormstout's famous namesake brew, a potent ale with a legendary kick few mortal gullets can withstand.

item:scaber-stalk.text: Scaber Stalk. In Darkshore, Barithras Moonshade seeks Scaber Stalks from a hidden cavern behind Cliffspring Falls. Scaber Stalks grow in a subterranean cave behind Cliffspring Falls, among the northeastern mountains of Darkshore. The pale mushrooms thrive in the damp, secluded cave network, far from ordinary forest growth. Their remote, hazardous home makes them rare to gather, and Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine commissions scouts to brave its darkness.

item:scale-of-old-murk-eye.text:
Scale of Old Murk-Eye. Along Westfall's coast, Captain Grayson seeks proof that Old Murk-Eye is dead. The ghost haunts Westfall Lighthouse, where the murloc's attacks left the beacon dark. Old Murk-Eye made Westfall's coast a killing ground. Captain Grayson, the ghost bound to Westfall Lighthouse, says the cunning murloc rallied weaker-minded murlocs to raid the shore. Murk-Eye drove away the keeper's family, leaving the beacon dark when Grayson's ship struck the rocks.

When the family returned to relight the flame, Murk-Eye attacked again and slaughtered them. Grayson seeks one of the creature's scales as proof that the shore is clear of its fiercest predator.

item:scarlet-armband.text: Scarlet Armband. In Deathknell, Scarlet Armbands mark the zealots pressing into Forsaken territory. Executor Arren demands them as proof that the newly risen have struck back. Scarlet Armbands mark the Scarlet Crusade's followers, from Initiates to fresh converts. The Crusade's red insignia warns newly risen Forsaken in Deathknell that danger waits close by. Crusaders make no distinction between the Scourge's mindless servants and the free-willed subjects of the Dark Lady. To them, every walking corpse must burn. Executor Arren gathers the armbands to confirm that enemy scouts southeast of Deathknell have died and that new Forsaken can defend their fledgling nation.

item:scarlet-crusade-documents.text: Scarlet Crusade Documents. At the Crusade's camp near Deathknell, a messenger carries Scarlet Crusade Documents through Tirisfal. The intercepted orders name field commanders and direct their forces, giving the Forsaken military leadership intelligence on Scarlet positions across the Glades. Meven Korgal carried the documents from the Crusade's encampment southeast of Deathknell. By order of the Highlord, they direct the captains of the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command. Captain Perrine must further fortify the southwest tower and gather information on the undead in Brill. Captain Vachon must crush undead movement near the northern tower, while Captain Melrose watches the borders of the Plaguelands. The orders name Scarlet field officers, their posts, and their duties across Tirisfal Glades. Executor Arren sees that Deathknell's local forces cannot use the full breadth of this intelligence. The captured documents become a newly awakened Forsaken's passport out of Deathknell. Carry them northeast, past Cold Hearth Manor, to Brill, and deliver them to Executor Zygand outside Brill Town Hall. With the orders in hand, Forsaken military leaders plan swift strikes against Scarlet commanders entrenched across the Glades.

item:scarlet-insignia-ring.text: Scarlet Insignia Ring. In Tirisfal Glades, Scarlet Insignia Rings mark the Crusade's members. In Brill, the Forsaken collect them as proof that another zealot has fallen. Every Scarlet Crusade fighter in Tirisfal Glades carries an insignia ring, from new neophytes and zealous friars to captains Melrache and Perrine. The Crusade's fiery sigil marks each ring, identifying members within an order consumed by paranoia. To outsiders, the rings identify Lordaeron's most fanatical human remnant. Deathguard Burgess in Brill collects the rings under orders from Varimathras, Lady Sylvanas's dreadlord lieutenant. The Forsaken see the Scarlet Crusade as a pestilence across their newly claimed homeland. Recruits bring the rings back to Brill as proof of a Crusader's death and of their loyalty to the throne of the Undercity.

item:scavenged-goods.text: Scavenged Goods. Around Deathknell, Forsaken gather Scavenged Goods from equipment boxes. Newly risen undead rely on these discarded supplies to arm and clothe the recruits who follow. New Forsaken rise in Deathknell's graveyard with little more than rotting burial shrouds. Nearby settlements and kingdoms offer the undead no aid, so they must salvage what they need. Deathguard Saltain gathers discarded weapons, tools, and garments from supply crates across the village, then gives them to the next recruits to rise.

item:scavenger-paw.text: Scavenger Paw. In Deathknell, Scavenger Paw comes from the young, ragged wolves roaming the hills. Newly awakened Forsaken gather the severed paws for local caretakers to stitch into crude protective gear. Deathknell's newly returned Forsaken have little to spare. The Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade press against Tirisfal, so every scrap of hide and bone goes to practical use. Novice Elreth assists Shadow Priest Sarvis and gathers paws from scavenger wolves, along with bat wings. She uses them to make serviceable garments and armor for Forsaken who have just risen from their graves, still disoriented by their return.

item:scorched-spider-fang.text: Scorched Spider Fang. Across the Wetlands, Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers carry Scorched Spider Fangs. Furen Longbeard in Stormwind needs fifty to strengthen mail for Alliance warriors. In Stormwind, blacksmith Furen Longbeard strengthens mail by unusual means. He needs fifty scorched fangs from the Wetlands' giant spiders. Their dense, venomous substance has toughened in the heat. Furen works it into the mail links as he tempers them. Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers bear the fangs Furen needs. They live in the Wetlands' sunken valleys and burrows, amid damp and rot. Their mandibles are hardened and scorched. Gathering fifty means venturing into deep hollows and facing the spiders in their swarms.

item:scroll-of-messaging.text: Scroll of Messaging. In Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle has a plan for the Scroll of Messaging. The gnome engineer means to use its sending spell to trigger remote explosives. Gaxim Rustfizzle plans to turn a message into a blast at the Venture Company's logging operation. He will combine the scroll's transmission incantation with volatile NG-5 charges. The explosion is meant to distract the guards, giving operatives time to slip past and steal engineering schematics and confidential correspondence.

item:sea-creature-bones.text: Sea Creature Bones. On Darkshore, Sea Creature Bones come from massive marine carcasses washed ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers skeletal samples for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where the cause of the strandings is under investigation. Massive sea creatures have begun flinging themselves onto Darkshore’s shallows, where they perish. Among them are giant threshers far larger than those native to the local waters. Night elves see the sudden increase as an ominous portent. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, sent by the Temple of the Moon to Auberdine, gathers bones from the beached creatures. Hippogryphs carry the specimens to Darnassus for close examination. The immense carcasses attract local scavengers. Greymist murlocs gather around the dead and dying creatures, feeding on their remains and fiercely defending the feeding grounds. The murlocs are too weak to hunt beasts of this size, but investigators and adventurers must fight through their packs along Mist's Edge to recover bone fragments for study.

item:sea-turtle-remains.text: Sea Turtle Remains. Along Darkshore, giant sea turtles lie dead on the coast and beneath the waves. Their remains go to researchers in Auberdine, who study the growing number of strandings. Giant sea creatures are washing ashore along Darkshore, while others lie beneath the water near sunken wrecks. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde oversees the collection of bone fragments and tissue from the bodies. The Temple of the Moon in Darnassus urgently requests these samples. Its scholars and priestesses fear the creatures may be fleeing an unnatural disturbance in the waters around Teldrassil. Recovering the remains is dangerous. Murloc tribes along the coast routinely gather around the huge carcasses, picking bones clean and nesting beside them. Scholars need fresh bone fragments and tissue before the scavengers destroy evidence that could explain the creatures' fatal migration.

item:sealed-description-of-thredd-s-visi.text: Sealed Description of Thredd's Visitor. Warden Thelwater seals a report on the man visiting Bazil Thredd in the Stormwind Stockade. The confidential account may help investigators follow someone moving through Stormwind’s political and criminal circles. For years, prisoner Bazil Thredd received no visitors in the Stockade. Then a quiet man began coming once or twice each week with valid papers under the name Maelik. Warden Thelwater took note and recorded the man’s appearance. He sealed the description so meddling eyes could not read it before proper investigators acted.

item:sealed-envelope.text: Sealed Envelope. Fizziks has sealed Venture Company secrets inside the Sealed Envelope for delivery to Sputtervalve in Ratchet. After the Venture Company cast goblin engineer Fizziks out of its logging operations in the Stonetalon Mountains, he smuggled out company secrets. The envelope holds internal manuals, operating procedures, and technical specifications. Among them are schematics for the Super Reaper 6000, a machine built for industrial clear-cutting. Fizziks sends the documents south to Sputtervalve, an engineer in the neutral goblin port of Ratchet. The Steamwheedle Cartel's business rivals have little personal love or trust for Fizziks, yet the designs have undeniable engineering value. They reveal Venture Company mechanical ingenuity and give independent engineers a chance to exploit its advanced logging technologies.

item:sealed-note-to-elling.text: Sealed Note to Elling. In Stormwind, Jorgen sends a sealed dispatch to Elling Trias, proprietor of Trias' Cheese. The fisherman’s message draws Trias into a quiet inquiry about a vanished diplomat. Jorgen gives a strict charge for the sealed note in Stormwind: place it in Elling Trias's hands and keep silent. The stakes leave no room for careless talk. Trias runs a cheese shop in the Trade District. There, Jorgen's message brings the inquiry into the diplomat's disappearance to his counter.

item:sealed-note-to-watcher-backus.text:
Sealed Note to Watcher Backus. In Stormwind, Elling Trias sends a sealed note to Watcher Backus in Duskwood. He asks the Night Watch guard to report Defias activity near Darkshire. Elling Trias agrees to use his contacts to help find the missing diplomat. He seals a note for Watcher Backus, a Night Watch guard stationed in Duskwood.

Trias sends a traveler south through the forest to deliver it by hand. He hopes Backus will report any Defias seen near Darkshire.

item:searing-collar.text: Searing Collar. At Skull Rock in Durotar, Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars in their rites. The heated torcs burn their flesh as the cultists attune themselves to demonic power. The Burning Blade gathers for dark rites in Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs wear Searing Collars around their necks, enduring heat that brands and sears their skin. Margoz, a hermit, studies the cruel devices. He suspects the burning and the enchantments bound to the metal attune the wearers to demonic energies. What part do these collars play in the corruption spreading through orc society under the Horde’s nose?

item:searing-coral.text: Searing Coral. Along the Wetlands coast, Searing Coral is gathered from living iron coral beneath the sea. Tinkerers and smiths prize its heat-resistant mineral for strengthening armor. Searing Coral grows in the cold sea south of Menethil Harbor. Living iron coral thrives in saltwater and yields mineral-rich material that withstands extreme heat. Harvesters must pry the hardened growths loose while wild murlocs and other aquatic beasts roam nearby. Dwarven smiths do not traditionally work Searing Coral. In Ironforge, curious gnome craftsmen such as Klockmort Spannerspan follow methods from veteran armorsmith Furen Longbeard. They smelt the coral and hammer it into metal alloys, making lightweight, durable armor for aspiring warriors.

item:secure-crate.text: Secure Crate. In the Barrens, a Secure Crate waits for a traveler to carry it to Ratchet. Potions and alchemical goods inside are bound for the Eastern Kingdoms. Couriers, caravans, and goblin ships carry trade between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. When a Barrens caravan misses its departure, travelers take fragile cargo like this Secure Crate down to the coast. It holds potions, alchemical goods, and reagents for associates across the Great Sea. The crate is sealed against the Barrens trails and the sea spray on its voyage. The crate’s land journey ends at the Ratchet docks, where Wharfmaster Dizzywig oversees shipping. Ratchet is a neutral port for goods crossing the sea, including cargo bound for Blackwater Cove. Dizzywig works under the Steamwheedle Cartel’s ledger, recording parcels and freight before loading them onto the next departing vessel. Ratchet links the Old World with the frontier.

item:senir-s-report.text:
Senir's Report. In Dun Morogh’s cold foothills, Senir Whitebeard sends his findings on the Frostmane trolls to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Senir’s report gathers what mountaineers saw while scouting the Frostmane trolls in Dun Morogh’s crags. He also includes his brother Grelin’s account of Coldridge Valley. Grelin acted there with King Magni Bronzebeard’s sanction.

Senir sends the findings to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge’s High Seat. He advises couriers to leave out how much outside help he needed to compile them.

item:serena-s-head.text: Serena's Head. At the Dry Hills in the northern Barrens, Serena Bloodfeather's head is sought as proof of her death. Darsok Swiftdagger plans to display it on a Horde supply wagon as a warning against further harpy raids.

item:serpentbloom.text: Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a rare, subterranean herb found growing only in the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Its potent natural properties have drawn the keen interest of the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society. Serpentbloom grows exclusively within the damp, shadowy tunnels of the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens. Rooted in an ecosystem warped by unrestrained Emerald Dream energies, the plant thrives far from sunlight and often harbors venomous serpents nesting among its stems. Because the cave system is overrun with hostile beasts and corrupted druids, few who venture inside ever return with viable specimens. Operating from the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah collects Serpentbloom on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society of Undercity. The Forsaken continuously seek out virulent, strange, and chemically potent vegetation across Kalimdor to fuel their research for the Dark Lady. Zamah believes that harvesting Serpentbloom in significant quantities could yield valuable breakthroughs for Forsaken alchemy.

item:sethir-s-journal.text: Sethir's Journal. On Teldrassil, Sethir's Journal was recovered through stealth. Its pages confirm that corruption from mainland Kalimdor has reached the World Tree.

item:sevren-s-orders.text: Sevren's Orders. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren sends a proven Forsaken agent to the Undercity. The orders direct the agent to Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter. Skilled Forsaken agents who prove themselves against the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades are summoned south as their people strengthen their hold on Lordaeron. Magistrate Sevren writes the orders as an introduction and credentials for Bethor Iceshard, one of the Dark Lady's foremost arcane practitioners in the Magic Quarter. Sevren knows only that the assignment concerns reaching out to an errant lich. The Undercity's high mages give the summons their full authority.

item:shadowhide-pendant.text: Shadowhide Pendant. In Redridge, Shadowhide Pendant charms pass among gnolls working with Morganth. Lakeshire accepts ten as proof that its law has been enforced. Shadowhide Pendant charms pass among the Shadowhide warriors, brutes, and spellcasters. Deep in Redridge's hills, the clan has gathered under Lieutenant Fangore and fallen under the sway of Morganth, a rogue wielder of the Arcane. To Lakeshire's townspeople, the crude charms mark an organized threat harassing settlements for an enemy of the Crown. Stormwind law, upheld by Magistrate Solomon, sets death as the sentence for actively aiding a known criminal of the realm. Royal reinforcements are too few, so Bailiff Conacher at Lakeshire Town Hall relies on adventurers to keep the peace. Ten Shadowhide Pendants prove that gnolls obeying Morganth's orders have faced frontier justice.

item:shaman-voodoo-charm.text: Shaman Voodoo Charm. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans wield the Shaman Voodoo Charm. Its vile magic can sever a sleeping druid's spirit from the body. The Gnarlpine tribe has fallen into madness and corruption on Teldrassil. Within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, its shamans wield magic beyond ordinary wilderness sorcery. Their voodoo charms let them tear a sleeping druid's consciousness from the mortal realm and trap it in the Emerald Dream. The furbolgs then animate the empty body. Night elf protectors become mindless guardians, killing anyone who enters the barrows.

item:shard-of-water.text: Shard of Water. Along the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer receives the Shard of Water from a shaman who has faced corruption. Shamans must understand balance, life, and preservation to master water. In the Call of Water, they travel to corrupted springs, even crossing the sea to blighted Silverpine Forest. After purifying the tainted waters, a shaman receives the Shard of Water. Returning the crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky Barrens shore proves the initiate's worth and provides the final key to forge a Water Totem.

item:shaw-s-report.text: Shaw's Report. In Westfall, Shaw's Report carries SI:7 intelligence to Gryan Stoutmantle. Written by Master Mathias Shaw, it tells of the Stonemasons Guild, Edwin VanCleef, and their grievance with the crown after Stormwind was rebuilt.

item:shimmering-frond.text: Shimmering Frond. In the Oracle Glade, a strange plant casts a twisting, shimmering aura. Its fronds come from a species native to the Swamp of Sorrows, far across the Great Sea. A radiant plant grows among the trees near the Oracle Glade. Its aura pulses, and its fronds shimmer in the woodland light. Denalan, who tends planters beside Lake Al'Ameth, recognizes the leaves as belonging to a species from the Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How seeds from that distant marsh crossed the Great Sea and took root on Teldrassil remains a mystery. Denalan is growing specimens in his own soil to study them.

item:shimmerweed.text: Shimmerweed. On Shimmer Ridge, Frostmane trolls gather shimmerweed for their rituals. Rejold Barleybrew of Brewnall Village wants to test its sharp flavor in his stout. High above Dun Morogh's lowlands, Frostmane trolls tend shimmerweed on Shimmer Ridge's icy crags. They harvest the plant and keep it in woven baskets throughout their camps. There, it fuels their sacred rituals. Few mountaineers beyond troll society pay the herb much mind, though inventive outsiders have taken an interest. In Brewnall Village, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew suspects shimmerweed may be the missing piece in his attempt to brew the ultimate dwarven stout. He has detected the herb's pungent, unmistakable flavor and wants to test it in his fermenting vats. So Rejold hires travelers to slip into Frostmane camps, evade the hostile trolls and bring back bushels.

item:shindrell-s-note.text: Shindrell's Note. In Astranaar, Shindrell Swiftfire writes a missive about corruption near the town and along Ashenvale's coast. She sends the intelligence report east through the forest to Kayneth Stillwind. Sentinels and druids coordinate to watch Ashenvale's borders as unrest spreads through the forest. In Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire writes of troubling disturbances along the western coast and among the central canopies. She addresses her report to Kayneth Stillwind, a druid at the shrine of Forest Song in the Nightsong Woods to the east. Couriers carry Shindrell's firsthand observations to aid Kayneth's investigation of corruption creeping through the sacred groves.

item:shipment-of-boots.text: Shipment of Boots. Off the Barrens coast, Shipment of Boots lies in a Southsea encampment south of Ratchet. Drizzlik sent the crate from Booty Bay for Gazlowe's trade network, but the pirates seized it before it reached port. Gazlowe arranged for Drizzlik, a clothing merchant in Booty Bay, to send boots to Ratchet. Southsea Freebooters patrolling the Merchant Coast ambushed the ship and carried the crates to their beach encampments south of the harbor. They scattered the stolen goods among their tents and shanties, and the shipment remains there, far from Ratchet's docks.

item:shipment-of-iron.text: Shipment of Iron. In Hillsbrad Fields, a crate of raw iron waits at the human smithy. The metal feeds local arms production, making the shipment a target for Forsaken forces seeking to cut the supply lines that arm the townsfolk. Across the Hillsbrad Foothills, human peasants have mounted stiff resistance against Tarren Mill. Much of their strength comes from the smithy at the southwestern edge of Hillsbrad Fields, where Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices work round the clock, making weapons and armor from heavy shipments of iron. Forsaken commanders ordered the forge put out, its smiths killed, and its stored metal seized for the Horde war effort, hoping to break the farmers’ resolve.

item:shipping-schedule.text: Shipping Schedule. At Jerod's Landing, the Defias Brotherhood sends contraband along Elwynn's waterways. Its dockmaster guards a schedule of shipments between Redridge and Westfall, and SI:7 wants it. South of Goldshire, Jerod's Landing lies on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River. The Defias Brotherhood seized it as a hub for river traffic. From there, they carry contraband between Redridge and Westfall by waterways beyond the Stormwind Guard's notice. Their dockmaster keeps the Shipping Schedule close, recording each shipment. Master Mathias Shaw leads SI:7, Stormwind's intelligence agency, and ordered the schedule stolen. It can reveal Defias supply lines, and taking it tests new operatives. The theft must happen inside the dock house, from the dockmaster's pockets. If the operative is caught, SI:7 denies any connection. No trail leads back to its barracks in Stormwind.

item:sida-s-bag.text: Sida's Bag. In the Wetlands, Sida's Bag lies swallowed in an ooze near Ironbeard's Tomb. Sida, a resident of Menethil Harbor, fled after throwing her satchel at one of the slimes during her weekly visit; the bag and its contents must be recovered from the acidic creatures. Sida visits Ironbeard's Tomb near Dun Modr each week. Dreadful, dripping oozes ambushed her there, and panic drove her to fling her satchel at one of them. The ooze absorbed the bag into its body. The distraction gave Sida time to escape alive and return to Menethil Harbor, while her possessions remained trapped inside an unknown slime. The oozes around Ironbeard's Tomb range from crimson to monstrous, and look much alike. Sida's Bag can be found by cutting down the marsh slimes until the swallowed satchel emerges intact. Acidic muck has soaked the durable sack, but its contents remain preserved. Sida reclaims her belongings, then discards the ruined, slime-coated exterior and offers the washed-out container to whoever braved the marsh on her behalf.

item:signed-recruitment-letter.text: Signed Recruitment Letter. Kargal Battlescar sends the Signed Recruitment Letter west from the Far Watch Post. His mark directs new recruits to report for duty at the Crossroads. At the Far Watch Post, Kargal Battlescar prepares recruits for service in the Barrens. The post stands east of the Southfury River, where newcomers cross from Durotar. When a conscript proves ready to Kargal, he stamps and signs a letter of introduction. The orders send recruits west along the road to the Crossroads. There, Sergra Darkthorn coordinates supplies and the defense of the dry plains. Kargal's orders carry his personal contempt for the officer who awaits the recruit. He calls Sergra Darkthorn an abrasive shaman who talks in circles around soldiers. Kargal openly questions Warchief Thrall's high opinion of her. Even so, the dispatch must reach Sergra's hands before any further assignments at the Crossroads are granted.

item:silithid-egg-the-barrens.text: Silithid Egg (The Barrens). Across the Field of Giants, silithid eggs lie buried beneath the soil. Horde researchers gather them to learn about the swarm spreading through the southern Barrens. Silithid mounds rise from the Field of Giants as strange insect-like creatures churn the earth. Their eggs lie beneath the hardened soil, guarded by territorial silithid. The Horde knows little about these creatures, but scouts at the Crossroads have seen signs of coordination and intelligence beyond that of ordinary wild beasts. Unhatched eggs may help scholars in Orgrimmar learn about the silithid’s life cycle and nature. Silithid eggs must be dug from the mounds with an adapted digging claw. The creatures defend their underground nurseries fiercely, swarming anyone who threatens their unhatched young. Korran, a troll researcher, needs intact specimens for study before the swarm spreads farther across Kalimdor.

item:silixiz-s-tower-key.text: Silixiz's Tower Key. Foreman Silixiz carries the key to the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Shattered Hand operatives must take it from his pocket as part of an undercover sabotage assignment. North of the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company keeps its tower under tight security. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix oversees the isolated lookout, while goblin mercenaries patrol the compound. Outside, Foreman Silixiz carries the tower key. A Shattered Hand operative from Orgrimmar must steal it and keep it. Force will not do: the operative must enter unseen and pick Silixiz's pocket, proving their stealth before climbing into the tower's toxic upper levels.

item:silver-dawning-s-lockbox.text: Silver Dawning's Lockbox. Off the Darkshore coast, Silver Dawning's Lockbox lies in the wreck of a ship lost to coastal murlocs. Inside are the fallen captain's personal effects and ship log. The Silver Dawning sailed across the sea toward Auberdine when coastal murlocs attacked. They drove the ship beneath the waves north of the harbor, and the captain died in the assault. The flooded hull still holds the captain's personal lockbox, with the ship's log and private belongings inside. Recovering them could bring a final measure of peace to the surviving crew ashore.

item:silvery-spinnerets.text: Silvery Spinnerets. Near Wellspring Lake, Silvery Spinnerets are harvested from Lady Sathrah in northern Teldrassil. Her silver webs once gathered healing evening dew for the Temple of the Moon. The Sisterhood of Elune seeks the spinnerets for a sacred rite honoring her soul. Lady Sathrah once spun shimmering webs by moonlight near Wellspring Lake. Her silver silk gathered evening mist into healing dew prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. But corruption reached her in Teldrassil, driving her into violent madness. Sathrah threatened her brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end her suffering and recover her spinnerets, bringing mercy to a once-revered creature of the great boughs.

item:simple-memorandum.text:
Simple Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, novice gnome warriors are sent to train with Thran Khorman in Anvilmar. They prepare for the war to take back Gnomeregan. Young gnome fighters face wildlife and troggs in Coldridge Valley with letters of introduction in hand. The Simple Memorandum directs its bearer to Thran Khorman, the warrior trainer in Anvilmar.

Gnomes bring intellect and contraptions to battle, but taking back Gnomeregan calls for strength and martial discipline. The memorandum sends its bearer beyond early training to learn the art of war from Thran.

item:simple-rune.text: Simple Rune. In Coldridge Valley, Thran Khorman sends promising young dwarven warriors to Anvilmar for training with the Simple Rune. Young fighters who have begun clearing threats from Coldridge Valley receive Thran’s formal summons. The rune’s martial marks hold no magic; they tell each recruit to report to Thran inside Anvilmar. There, he teaches basic combat and gives practical advice for surviving Dun Morogh’s hostile wilds.

item:simple-sigil.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, a Simple Sigil calls novice night elf warriors to training with Alyissia. It marks their first step into Teldrassil’s defense. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine guides young night elves as they seek their calling. A runner brings a Simple Sigil from the warrior trainer Alyissia, and Ilthalaine gives it to fledgling warriors. Its inscription tells each recruit to report for instruction. The token marks the start of their martial training as troubling times come to the World Tree. Alyissia uses the sigil to speak with recruits about the kaldorei’s pressing needs. Teldrassil’s recent growth, corruption spreading among forest beasts, and the rediscovery of distant lands such as Feralas have stretched night elven protectors thin. The sigil holds no power. It welcomes a recruit among the guardians charged with shielding their people from emerging threats.

item:simple-tablet.text: Simple Tablet. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives new troll warriors a message to take to Frang. Gornek gives new troll warriors a message from Tar'sere, addressed to Frang, the warrior trainer near the Den. It introduces the recruit to combat training in Durotar and asks them to present themselves to Frang. The message calls on them to take up weapons for the Horde.

item:singed-scale.text: Singed Scale. In Durotar, Singed Scale comes from the charred plates of electrified thunder lizards. Horde warriors bring the scales to prove their endurance and learn defensive combat. Horde veterans judge a warrior by the blows they can bear while shielding allies. In Thunder Ridge, a canyon in western Durotar, lightning hides and thunder lizards crackle with storm energy. Hunting these beasts means enduring relentless electrical shocks and crushing blows. Their blackened scales show that a fighter can withstand punishing assaults and hold firm under pressure. At the Far Watch Post, on the border between Durotar and the Barrens, the veteran warrior Uzzek asks initiates for five scales before teaching them. He believes they need physical toughness before they can learn stances and tactical defense. Bringing the scales proves they have the fortitude to join thick hide, heavy armor, and careful footwork into a firm defense against the Horde’s enemies.

item:skeleton-finger.text: Skeleton Finger. In Duskwood, Skeleton Finger is gathered from the restless dead.
