Madame Eva of Darkshire collects these remains with ghoul fangs and spider venom to make protective talismans. The dead rise throughout Duskwood, from skeletal raiders and warriors to necrotic mages and fiends. Most travelers leave their foul remains untouched, but fortune tellers and mystics prize their cold essence. Madame Eva, the seer of Darkshire, gathers the bony fingers to bind their lingering necrotic energies into the Totem of Infliction, a ward that strikes back at attackers.

item:skin-of-sweet-rum.text: Skin of Sweet Rum. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Skin of Sweet Rum is bound for Lakeshire, where war has thinned the tavern's stores. Lakeshire's tavern supplies are running low as the Blackrock orc invasion cuts off the roads into the Redridge Mountains. Barkeep Daniels needs drink for the town guards and refugees, so he sends travelers to gather regional specialties. Among them is a waterskin of sweet rum from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire.

item:skittering-blood.text: Skittering Blood. Skittering Blood feeds the Royal Apothecary Society's work on a New Plague. The reagent comes from arachnids in the Skittering Dark of Silverpine Forest, where Forsaken alchemists seek a weapon against the Scourge and humanity. Skitterweb lurkers, strikers, and their broodmother Krethis the Shadowspinner yield a venomous blood. Apothecary Renferrel found that, refined with toxins from grizzled bear hearts, it forms the base of an exceptionally lethal elixir. Its contaminating agents make it useful in the Apothecarium's chemical experiments. In the Undercity, Master Apothecary Faranell directs the Royal Apothecary Society's search for a New Plague. The Forsaken face Scourge hordes and hostile human remnants, and turn to biological warfare to even the odds. Faranell studies the blood's toxic strength as he works toward a contagion that can destroy unlife and living flesh alike.

item:sleepers-key.text: Sleepers' Key. At Stonetalon Peak, Sleepers' Key helps guard a sacred druidic vault. Night elf druids made it one of three enchanted keys for the Talon Den Hoard. The Talon Den rises on Stonetalon Peak as a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor. To guard sacred relics and potent treasures from unwanted attention, night elf keepers built a system of locks and hidden caches. Sleepers' Key is one of three keys that together form a protective ward. The key lies in a secluded cache deep in the den, opened with the Gatekeeper's Key hidden near the threshold. The Claw Key and the Barrow Key complete the set. Set all three into the Talon Den Hoard's stone locks, and the ward fades, revealing the ancient items within.

item:smoky-iron-ingot.text: Smoky Iron Ingot. At the Windshear dig sites, kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots from ore they pull from the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcish armorers prize the bars as raw material for sturdy mail gear for Horde warriors. Kobolds smelt Smoky Iron Ingots in the Windshear Crag tunnels of the Stonetalon Mountains. They dig ore from the rocky slopes and heat it over crude, smoking fires. Residue and charcoal cling to the bars, but the metal remains dense and strong. Thun'grim Firegaze, a near-blind orc armorer, works from a rugged camp overlooking the Barrens. He asks for these ingots to make armor for proven Horde warriors. Alongside refined iron bars, powdered azurite, and volatile phlogiston, the smoky metal forms a resilient core for Brutal Hauberks.

item:smoldering-embers.text: Smoldering Embers. In the Charred Vale, Smoldering Embers remain after fire elementals are extinguished. Night elf Sentinels gather them as proof that the fires are being subdued. Venture Company logging and industry set the Charred Vale ablaze and stirred destructive forces from deep within the earth. Burning Ravagers, Burning Destroyers, and Rogue Flame Spirits then swept across the scorched basin. When an elemental is extinguished, its ash-covered core remains as a Smoldering Ember. These cinders show that the fires overrunning the vale are being brought under control.

item:snellig-s-snuffbox.text: Snellig's Snuffbox. At the Lost Fleet, Snellig's Snuffbox remains with its undead owner among the wrecks. First Mate Fitzsimmons in Menethil Harbor wants it as proof his cursed crewmate has been put to rest. First Mate Snellig still clutches his snuffbox in a wreck off the northern Wetlands. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras ran aground there, its sailors and officers drowned beneath a mysterious power tied to a hidden treasure aboard the ships. Bound by that power, the drowned crew rose again as tortured spirits and skeletal undead. Snellig haunts the rotting hold of the wreck closest to the coastline. His snuffbox is a small, ordinary reminder of his mortal life at sea. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the disaster's sole living survivor, wants this possession returned as proof that at least one lost shipmate has found release from torment.

item:snufflenose-command-stick.text: Snufflenose Command Stick. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix sends trained gophers after blueleaf tubers in Razorfen Kraul. Mebok Mizzyrix has trained snufflenose gophers to find blueleaf tubers deep in Razorfen Kraul. The roots lie hidden beneath the thorny tunnels, where finding them is nearly impossible without help. Mebok, a merchant in Ratchet, avoids entering the quilboar dens himself. He gives adventurers the Snufflenose Command Stick to direct the gophers. From up to fifty paces away, the stick guides them to sniff out and uncover the roots.

item:snufflenose-owner-s-manual.text: Snufflenose Owner's Manual. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix keeps Snufflenose Owner's Manual beside him. Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc. wrote the booklet to explain how to send a trained Snufflenose Gopher after Blueleaf Tubers in Razorfen Kraul. Marwig Rustbolt, owner of Snuff Inc., wrote a guide to handling the company's trained snufflenose gophers. Their keen noses can detect Blueleaf Tubers buried underground from fifty paces away. The manual explains how to release a gopher from a ventilated crate and guide its rooting with a command stick. Prospectors direct it through Razorfen Kraul's thorns and quilboar tunnels to find the tubers.

item:sodium-nitrate.text: Sodium Nitrate. At Bael Modan, Sodium Nitrate helps the dwarves blast through the southern Barrens’ stone. Gann Stonespire seeks the chemical for charges against the fortress. Dwarven excavators at Bael Modan use Sodium Nitrate to break through the southern Barrens’ rock. The Bael'dun expedition entered the Stonespire tribe’s ancestral lands with earthmovers and blasting reagents. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry the chemical inside the excavation works and nearby fortress.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-darkshire.text: Solomon's Plea to Darkshire. Magistrate Solomon asks Darkshire for aid as Lakeshire faces mounting threats. His urgent letter to Lord Ello Ebonlocke requests the Night Watch to help defend Redridge. Lakeshire faces attacks from Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, with few reinforcements arriving from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon sends a formal plea to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire, asking him to send Night Watch militia north into Redridge. With central military support failing across southern Azeroth, human settlements must seek help from one another to survive.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-westfall.text: Solomon's Plea to Westfall. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent appeal to Westfall for help against Blackrock orcs and gnolls. He asks Gryan Stoutmantle to send the People's Militia while Stormwind's royal army fails to answer. Blackrock orcs and hostile gnolls threaten Redridge, and Magistrate Solomon is isolated in Lakeshire. Stormwind's royal army has not arrived in force to defend the region's borders. With no time to wait for support from the capital, Solomon writes to seek help beyond the regular army. Word has reached him of a volunteer defense force forming in Elwynn to the west, so he appeals to the People's Militia. Solomon addresses his message to Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran warrior organizing Westfall's frontier defense. He hopes Stoutmantle can spare fighters for Lakeshire until Stormwind sends regular reserves. An adventurer carries the document. With Stormwind's outlying territories poorly coordinated, local magistrates must arrange mutual aid on their own.

item:soran-ruk-fragment.text: Soran'ruk Fragment. In Blackfathom Deeps, cultists hold shards of Soran'ruk, a shattered prison orb. The pieces still carry fel energy from the demon once bound inside. Soran'ruk's prison orb was broken apart after the demon fell from favor with the Burning Legion. Demons who displease their masters may have their spirits sealed in orbs, then given to fel spellcasters as sources of power. The Twilight's Hammer cultists in the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps possess smaller shards from one half of the orb. They draw on the lingering demonic essence for their own workings.

item:southsea-treasure.text:
Southsea Treasure. Southsea Treasure lies aboard a pirate ship south of Ratchet, where Wrenix the Wretched seeks the hoard. The Tide Razor's lowest hold sits beneath the Southsea Freebooters' training ground. The Tide Razor lies anchored along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet. The Southsea Freebooters use it as a forward base and training ground. Their plunder, called the Southsea Treasure, waits in the lowest hold.

Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin scoundrel in Ratchet, sets the theft as a test for aspiring pickpockets. He says the last five operatives sent after the chest came back in pieces. Alert pirates guard the ship, and a fierce creature watches the hold.

item:spectral-comb.text: Spectral Comb. At a ruined farmstead south of Darkshire, the Spectral Comb gathers ghost hair from Blind Mary. Ghostly hair lies beyond the reach of ordinary combs, leaving mortal craftsmen few ways to gather such fibers. The Spectral Comb can pass through a spirit’s intangible tresses. Carried south of Darkshire to a ruined farmstead, it is offered to Blind Mary, a weeping ghost who wails alone. Grooming brings her solace, and she willingly uses the comb. The spectral fibers she leaves behind can be woven into Ghost Hair Thread.

item:spells-of-shadow.text: Spells of Shadow. Beneath Orgrimmar, Spells of Shadow rests in the hands of Searing Blade cultists. The Forsaken leadership in the Undercity wants the grimoire recovered. Searing Blade cultists keep Spells of Shadow among their guarded treasures in Ragefire Chasm. The splinter cult is tied to the Shadow Council, and its members wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. The book holds shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks keep it close as they plot beneath the Horde in Durotar. Word of the Searing Blade's demonic gifts reached the Undercity's royal quarters. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, decided the relics were wasted on cultists with lesser vision. Varimathras sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm to seize Spells of Shadow and its companion tome, Incantations from the Nether. Their power is meant to serve the Forsaken cause against the Scourge and the Lich King.

item:spotted-sunfish.text: Spotted Sunfish. At Lake Everstill, Spotted Sunfish draw fishers and hungry murlocs alike. The fish bring trade to Lakeshire, though murlocs make the shallows dangerous. Spotted Sunfish bring trade to the Lakeshire piers. Dockmaster Baren buys them from the lake's steady catch, supplying food and commerce to a town under strain. Aggressive murloc tribes prowl the shallows and disrupt fishing. They gather sunfish at their camps, where travelers can take the fish by force.

item:stalker-claws.text: Stalker Claws. Across Mulgore, Stalker Claws are taken from prairie stalkers for a cleansing rite. Tauren shamans bind them into totems used to purify tainted wells. Prairie stalkers hunt across Mulgore’s grassy steppes. Their stealth and lethal precision make them deadly predators, yet they keep an essential balance within the Earth Mother's design. Mull Thunderhorn needs their claws to help heal the blighted land. He seeks no harm to the beasts; the natural force of their hunt holds the spiritual strength needed to counter artificial corruption. Goblin drilling and mining across central Kalimdor have sent chemical poisons into the underground waters that feed ancestral tauren wells. The Thunderhorn Water Well has been tainted by vile muck. Tribal shamans bind Stalker Claws and Cougar Claws into a Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem, a spiritual conduit that scours the unnatural sludge from the earth's springs.

item:steelgrill-s-tools.text: Steelgrill's Tools. At Steelgrill's Depot, Beldin Steelgrill needs fresh tools to keep his workshop at work. He puts siege engines and equipment through hard use, so Kharanos keeps sending replacements. Beldin Steelgrill is one of Dun Morogh's finest siege engine technicians. Merchants know his rough touch, though. He works without pause on armored tanks and mechanical contraptions, and delicate tools soon break in his hands. Arclight spanners snap and fang-ratchets wear out, so he keeps ordering replacements from Kharanos for his repair benches. At his depot northeast of Kharanos, Beldin services combat vehicles for experienced drivers such as Pilot Stonegear. The tools keep Ironforge's war machines in working order. Fresh wrenches and ratchets keep repairs moving on the siege engines assembled there, supporting local defenses.

item:steelsnap-s-rib.text: Steelsnap's Rib. In Thousand Needles, Steelsnap's Rib marks the end of a feared hyena's reign. Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff wants the bone brought to Hunter Rise as proof that Steelsnap has been slain. Tauren hunts often seek food, honor, or harmony with nature. Steelsnap is different. The alpha hyena roams the canyon floor south of Camp E'thok in Thousand Needles, terrorizing peaceful wildlife and rallying lesser predators to bloodshed. Hunt master Melor Stonehoof, on Hunter Rise, marks Steelsnap for death. He asks for the hyena's rib as proof the tyrant is slain and the canyon cleansed of its blight.

item:stolen-silver.text: Stolen Silver. At the Crossroads, a strongbox of Horde silver has gone missing from the guard tower. Sunscale raptors carried the coins to their nests at the Raptor Grounds south of Ratchet. Sunscale raptors carried a strongbox of silver from the Crossroads guard tower. The coins were meant as pay for the garrison guards. The raptors dragged the lockbox to their communal nests at the Raptor Grounds, south of Ratchet. Gazrog and the other overseers cannot explain why the predators took it. The theft leaves them wondering whether the raptors prize shiny things or possess a cunning beyond that of ordinary wild beasts.

item:stone-of-relu.text: Stone of Relu. In the Wetlands, the Stone of Relu is lost to a raptor after an ambush. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it can unlock secrets within ancient fossils. Explorers' League work uncovered the Stone of Relu. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it can decipher prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. He means to use it on his Wetlands specimens and on the fossil Prospector Remtravel unearthed in Darkshore. Archaeologist Flagongut was traveling along the Wetlands roads to meet Prospector Whelgar when mottled raptors ambushed him. In the scramble, the relic was lost and swallowed by one of the beasts. The League now seeks the marsh raptors so the ancient stone can be cut from their gullets.

item:stonetalon-sap.text: Stonetalon Sap. Near Mirkfallon Lake and Stonetalon Peak, sap beasts carry the sap Jin'Zil seeks. The Darkspear witch doctor uses it in a brew for his caged night elf prisoners.

item:stormpike-banner.text: Stormpike Banner. Alliance recruits enter Icewing Cavern to earn the Stormpike Banner. The trial lies southwest of Dun Baldar in Alterac Valley, where harpies guard the standard. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends new Alliance soldiers into Icewing Cavern southwest of Dun Baldar. Before they face the Frostwolf orcs, recruits must brave the harpies, seize the Stormpike Banner, and bring it back alive. Those who return earn the rank and insignia of an initiate in the Stormpike Guard.

item:stormpike-s-request.text: Stormpike's Request. From Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike sends Furen Longbeard a commission for a fine dwarven shield. Mountaineer Stormpike stands watch in Loch Modan, where the dwarven frontier brings danger. He needs a sturdy shield and trusts no ordinary smith with such work. Furen Longbeard is the armorsmith whose craft he admires. Furen left Ironforge and now lives among the humans in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Stormpike assumes a king's ransom drew him south, so he relies on travelers to carry his request across the kingdoms. Furen Longbeard receives Stormpike's letter in Stormwind's Dwarven District and agrees to make the shield. The Stormpike clan is proud and established, known across Khaz Modan for martial grit and wealth. Word and business from his northern homeland are welcome. So Furen sets to work on the mountaineer's order.

item:stormwind-armor-marker.text: Stormwind Armor Marker. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain accepts a Stormwind Armor Marker from those who aid the realm. It lets them claim crafted gear from artisans commissioned by Stormwind. Stormwind's commanders issue armor markers to those who serve the realm. Keeping order across Elwynn Forest strains Stormwind's resources. So commanders sometimes use these official slips in place of standard gear at military outposts. A marker confirms the bearer's service and allows a contracted local craftsman to provide tailored armor. Sara Timberlain and other artisans work under commission from the Stormwind Army at Eastvale Logging Camp. The camp lies on Elwynn's eastern frontier, where they use local materials to make protective cloth and leather garments. Present a marker there to receive custom-fitted defense for guarding the surrounding woodlands.

item:stoutmantle-s-response-to-solomon.text: Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon. From Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle sends word to Lakeshire that no soldiers can be spared for Redridge Mountains. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks Sentinel Hill for help as Blackrock orcs and gnolls press his town. Gryan Stoutmantle answers in writing and mourns Lakeshire's losses. Yet Westfall faces a war of its own. The People's Militia formed after the Crown withdrew its garrison, and farmers and volunteers now fight the Defias Brotherhood alone. Stoutmantle's forces are already bleeding and stretched thin, with no men to spare for another abandoned frontier.

item:strange-smelling-powder.text: Strange Smelling Powder. In Loch Modan, Strange Smelling Powder has alarmed engineers investigating sabotage. Chief Engineer Hinderweir fears it may be explosive and seeks an expert's judgment. Strange Smelling Powder was found amid signs of sabotage against Loch Modan's infrastructure. Chief Engineer Hinderweir fears it may be an engineered explosive, unlike the powder usually used in mining. He cannot identify its mixture or origin, and will not tamper with it himself. Even a small spark could bring disaster.

item:strangely-marked-box.text: Strangely Marked Box. Along Darkshore, a Strangely Marked Box is found among cargo on dead sea turtles. Its runes point to the naga and show that the turtles did not come ashore by chance. Dead sea turtles and other sea creatures wash up on Darkshore's beaches. Some carry broken harnesses and carriages strapped to their shells. Sealed boxes marked with foreign, winding runes lie among the wreckage. Greymist murlocs often shelter in the hollow ribs and broken wagons, feeding on the carcasses and guarding what remains.

item:strigid-owl-feather.text: Strigid Owl Feather. Strigid Owl Feathers are gathered from the owls in Teldrassil's boughs. Zenn Foulhoof seeks them for his covert dealings.

item:sturdy-dragonmaw-shinbone.text: Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbone. At the Angerfang Encampment, renegade Dragonmaw orcs provide sturdy shinbones for armor. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely needs them to frame leg guards for warriors. Velora Nitely needs bones that can bear the strain of brutal leg guards. The renegade Dragonmaw orcs at the Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands have thick, sturdy frames, and their shinbones can brace the armor. Each bone must be tested by hand. Warriors discard any that snap under pressure.

item:sully-balloo-s-letter.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. Beneath the Thandol Span, Sully Balloo's Letter carries a soldier's farewell to Sara in Ironforge. His words hold the love he bore her through his final days. Beneath the Thandol Span, the road from the Wetlands crosses toward the Arathi Highlands. Under the rushing water, a dwarf's skeletal remains lie pinned. A fragile, waterlogged envelope rests in his grasp. Inside, the letter begins, “My dear Sara...” The parchment has suffered beneath the water, yet the ink still bears the care of the dwarven defender in his final days or hours. He never returned to Ironforge.

item:sunscorched-shell.text: Sunscorched Shell. Beneath Highperch, wyvern eggs leave shells hardened by Thousand Needles' desert heat. Armorer Mathiel in Darnassus uses them to make lacquer for mail links. Highperch wyverns lay eggs on the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor. Beneath their roosts, discarded shell fragments bake in the desert sun and searing winds. Their brittle remains hold a natural resilience that draws the attention of skilled artisans. In Darnassus, armorer Mathiel studies methods pioneered by his colleague, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard. Mathiel processes the shells into a fine lacquer for mail armor. Applied to the metal links, the coating strengthens them without burdening the wearer.

item:super-reaper-6000-blueprints.text: Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. In Windshear Crag, the Venture Company’s Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints are coveted by goblin rivals. They hold the technical schematics for an enormous mechanized woodcutter deployed in Stonetalon Mountains, designed under gnome engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle’s supervision. Venture Company operators carry the Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints through Windshear Crag. The plans show how to build the massive mechanized lumber harvesters driving the company’s relentless clear-cutting. To the dismay of traditional goblin engineers, the Venture Company put Gerenzo, a gnome, in charge of designing the model. When goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks was ousted from the operation, Sputtervalve quickly hired him to steal the designs. Yet Gerenzo’s dense, eccentric gnomish notations are almost as hard to decipher as the plans are to take by force.

item:supplies-for-sven.text: Supplies for Sven. Darkshire sends provisions to Sven Yorgen's camp in northwestern Duskwood. The Carevin family keeps his small band supplied as they hold their watch against the shadows. Sven Yorgen and his few followers camp in the northwestern wilderness, far from Darkshire. Their numbers are too low, and their watch too demanding, to spare anyone for the journey into town. The Carevin family sends food, bandages, and other necessities to the isolated camp, helping the band hold its ground.

item:surena-s-choker.text:
Surena's Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder seeks the bloodstone choker he gave his former apprentice, Surena Caledon. She fled with Erlan Drudgemoor to join the Defias Brotherhood, and Gakin now sends aspiring acolytes to take it back by force. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder once trained Surena Caledon in the dark arts. He saw promise in her youthful charm and magical talent, and gave her a valuable bloodstone choker to aid her studies. But Surena left her training and fled with Erlan Drudgemoor, a rogue aligned with the Defias Brotherhood.

Gakin will not let a traitor keep such a potent artifact. Now he sends initiates seeking mastery over the void to find her at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and reclaim the choker by force. Their deed will prove where their loyalty lies.

item:swoop-gizzard.text: Swoop Gizzard. Across Mulgore, swoops soar as predatory birds, and their gizzards go into traditional remedies for deadly toxins. Swoops hunt across Mulgore’s plains and mesas, with keen eyes and a taste for scavenging. Tauren use their feathers and meat in daily life, while herbalists and healers prize their internal organs, especially the gizzard. Dense and muscular, it helps counter venomous bites and festering infections when combined with cougar bones and wolf hearts. In Bloodhoof Village, Maur Raincaller tends the wound Mazzranache left on his shoulder. The legendary plainstrider’s venom drives Maur into delirium as the poison creeps through him. To make a poultice that can expel the lethal venom, Maur needs a swoop gizzard, a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, and a plainstrider scale.

item:tablet-of-verga.text: Tablet of Verga. In Skull Rock, the Tablet of Verga lies in Burning Blade hands, its demonic runes sought by warlocks in Orgrimmar. The Tablet of Verga bears ritual runes for summoning creatures of the Nether and bending them to a master's will. The Burning Blade cult stole the stone and hid it in a chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Warlocks in the Cleft of Shadow seek it to study the markings and learn to summon a voidwalker. Recovering it also keeps the cult from gaining that same advantage.

item:tainted-heart.text: Tainted Heart. In Teldrassil, Denalan gives adventurers a heart still troubled by corruption. Though its outer foul moss is gone, lingering energies remain, and he seeks to cleanse them with rich soil. Teldrassil's natural balance is troubled by a malady that warps its plants and beasts. After foul moss is stripped from a blighted growth, Denalan gives adventurers the Tainted Heart within. Darkness still clings to its tissue. Denalan hopes specially prepared, nutrient-rich earth can counter the taint and restore what was corrupted.

item:tainted-keg.text: Tainted Keg. At Tarren Mill, Tainted Keg carries stolen dwarven stout laced with a lethal Forsaken brew made by Apothecary Lydon. Sent to imprisoned human farmers as refreshments, it tests poisons being developed by the Royal Apothecary Society. Dun Garok's dwarven riflemen lost a barrel of Shindigger Stout to thieves. Apothecary Lydon mixed the stout with his newly refined Elixir of Agony. The Forsaken chose an ordinary drink to carry the poison, hoping it would escape suspicion. A familiar ale became a swift death sentence.

item:tainted-letter.text: Tainted Letter. Near Northshire Abbey, Drusilla La Salle sends human warlock initiates a sealed summons for secret tutelage, beyond watchful eyes. Initiates returning from nearby kobold camps carry Drusilla's summons toward Northshire Abbey. Priests, paladins, and soldiers train openly across its lawns, but fel practitioners must keep their path quiet. Town guards and clerics may grow suspicious if novice warlocks draw attention while seeking their mentor near the abbey grounds. Drusilla La Salle meets her pupils on the fringes, where sentries are less likely to pry. Elwynn’s ordinary folk distrust warlocks, and the letter begins a lesson in discipline. Arcane and nether magic risk corruption. Those who commune with denizens of the Twisting Nether must temper ambition with patient self-control.

item:tainted-memorandum.text:
Tainted Memorandum. In Coldridge Valley, Alamar Grimm urges novice gnome warlocks to leave old paths behind and seek power through the dark arts. At Anvilmar, few celebrate fel practitioners, and many distrust them. Alamar Grimm gives the Tainted Memorandum to young gnomes who study forbidden arts. He rejects the Holy Light and ordinary weapons. To him, Gnomeregan’s fall proves that old ways and tinkering failed their people.

Grimm sees reliance on dwarven charity as a dead end. He urges gnomes to claim undeniable power and summon minions who obey without question. Only then, he believes, can they secure their own future.

item:talisman-of-corruption.text: Talisman of Corruption. In Darkshore, Xabraxxis uses the Talisman of Corruption to turn the Blackwood furbolgs against their former allies. The satyr keeps it in his personal pouch, where its magic binds the tribe to fel madness. Auberdine's night elves have long sought the cause of the Blackwood furbolgs' turn against their former allies. Thundris Windweaver found that satyrs had brought about the tribe's fall. With talismans like this, demonic agents spread corrupting sorcery through the wilderness, tainting food and twisting peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. The devices channel fel magic that grips the minds and wills of local tribes.

item:tallonkai-s-jewel.text: Tallonkai's Jewel. On Teldrassil, Tallonkai's Jewel is lost from its druidic talisman. Ferocitas the Dream Eater prizes the emerald, which is needed to mend the Emerald Dreamcatcher. Tallonkai Swiftroot received the Emerald Dreamcatcher from Gaerolas Talvethen, warden of the druids in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The talisman is a powerful focus that draws energy from the Emerald Dream. When it was damaged, someone pried its radiant central emerald free and carried it into eastern Teldrassil. Ferocitas the Dream Eater, a corrupted Gnarlpine leader, took the jewel and made it into a necklace. Its green light glimmered in the forest gloom, but its harmony with the Emerald Dream meant nothing to the furbolg. To Ferocitas, it was only a trophy until it could be recovered.

item:taming-rod.text: Taming Rod. In Durotar, Taming Rods help novice hunters learn to command beasts. Trainers give them to students so they can practice before forming lasting bonds with animal companions. In Razor Hill, trainers such as Thotar give Taming Rods to aspiring orc and troll hunters. These enchanted tools help novices who cannot yet bind a wild creature permanently. A rod pacifies a regional predator, such as a dire mottled boar or an armored scorpid, so the hunter can practice giving commands and fighting beside an animal companion. The bond lasts only briefly, leaving the student free to learn without forming a lasting tie to the beast. Each Taming Rod's magic fades after a short while, and each is attuned to specific kinds of wild beasts. Novices face successive trials against different temperaments, from docile foragers to aggressive venomous hunters. When a student has shown they can command them, the rod goes back to the trainer. The trainer then teaches the student to tame, call, and dismiss lifelong companions without an artifact.

item:taragaman-the-hungerer-s-heart.text: Taragaman the Hungerer's Heart. Beneath Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade seeks Taragaman the Hungerer's Heart as proof that the demonic presence is gone. The trophy comes from the felguard ruling Ragefire Chasm's depths.

item:tattered-manuscript.text: Tattered Manuscript. In Thousand Needles, Tattered Manuscript lies hidden in Splithoof Hold. Its torn pages came from the Tome of the Cabal, and warlocks seek them to learn how to summon a felhunter. Once, the Tome of the Cabal was a unique, whole volume kept in the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. An unknown defiler tore almost half its pages from the binding. The spine and pages left behind became known as the Moldy Tome. They were sent south toward Khaz Modan, then lost at sea. The torn leaves crossed the Great Sea to Kalimdor and came into the hands of the Galak centaur inside Splithoof Hold. A battered chest deep in the caverns of Splithoof Hold holds the manuscript. There it endured the dry winds of Thousand Needles. Alliance warlocks work with Krom Stoutarm in Ironforge, while Horde practitioners aid Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Both groups brave the aggressive centaur to reunite the leaves with the Moldy Tome. Together, the books hold dark rituals for summoning and binding a demonic felhunter.

item:tazan-s-satchel.text: Tazan's Satchel. Near Ratchet, Tazan carries a locked satchel as he deals with pirates along the coast. The Shattered Hand wants the secret information inside. Tazan deals with pirates camped along the Barrens coast near Ratchet. Therzok, a guild master of the Shattered Hand beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, takes notice. The guild seeks covert power beyond Warchief Thrall's cautious diplomacy, and marks Tazan for elimination to seize the intelligence in his satchel.

item:tear-of-the-moons.text: Tear of the Moons. At Bael Modan in the southern Barrens, dwarven excavators have unearthed the Tear of the Moons. Its strange power draws Feegly into obsession, while General Twinbraid fears what the crystal can do. Dwarven excavators unearthed the Tear of the Moons during the first digging at Bael Modan. The crystal's strange radiance captivated the miners, especially Feegly. He claimed it gave him great strength, then grew unstable and turned against his comrades. General Twinbraid, commander of the expedition, feared the relic's influence and declared it cursed. He took the crystal and locked it in his personal strongbox at Bael'dun Keep. Then he cast Feegly out into the Barrens.

item:tear-of-tilloa.text: Tear of Tilloa. Near Darkshire, the Tear of Tilloa draws those seeking rare alchemical reagents. The flower grows on the Mistmantle estate in Duskwood. Outside Darkshire, the Tear of Tilloa grows on Stalvan Mistmantle’s estate. Duskwood’s soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, yet the small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. Rare and secluded, it draws those seeking uncommon reagents beyond lawful markets.

item:techbot-s-memory-core.text: Techbot's Memory Core. In Gnomeregan, Tinkmaster Overspark seeks Techbot's Memory Core to study the automaton's corrupted behavior. Before Gnomeregan fell, Techbot aided Tinkmaster Overspark and his fellow inventors with devices and knowledge. During the city's fall, an errant electrical discharge jolted Techbot and turned its positronic brain to a hostile negatronic state. Now the automaton wanders Gnomeregan's tainted halls and attacks anyone in sight. Overspark hopes the memory core will help him understand the fault and restore his creation to its senses.

item:telescopic-lens.text: Telescopic Lens. Gazlowe needs the Telescopic Lens to finish the observatory telescope above Ratchet’s harbor. Southsea pirates took it from a ship, and the lens remains in their camp south of town. Ratchet is known chiefly for ruthless commerce, but its overseer and chief engineer, Gazlowe, has greater mechanical ambitions. His observatory rises above the harbor to house a telescope for watching maritime traffic and the stars. The larger lens came safely overland from Durotar. The smaller, vital lens traveled by sea, where Southsea Freebooters prey on merchant lanes off the Barrens coast. The Southsea Freebooters took anything of value when they raided the transport ship, including the delicate optics. The pirates may have left the lens among the clutter of their beachside camp south of Ratchet because they could not appreciate its craft or did not know how to pawn it. Gazlowe needs the unblemished glass brought back so his observation deck can come into focus.

item:teronis-journal.text: Teronis' Journal. Teronis' Journal follows a scout's search through Ashenvale for a gem tied to a rod he hoped could slow furbolg attacks. Teronis, a longtime friend of Raene Wolfrunner, aided the Sentinels and searched Ashenvale for a gem. He believed it belonged to a rod that could slow the furbolg attacks on his people. Near the shore, aggressive creatures brought his journey to an end. The journal was recovered from his personal effects in remarkably good condition. Its findings about a radiant gem that once formed part of the rod give Astranaar's defenders a trail to follow in his unfinished search.

item:tharil-zun-s-head.text: Tharil'zun's Head. Tharil'zun's Head reaches Lakeshire as proof that the commander terrorizing the Redridge approaches is dead. He led the Blackrock Outrunners occupying Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs at Stonewatch Keep have pressed Lakeshire hard, raiding farms and ambushing travelers on the roads. Tharil'zun directed the Blackrock Outrunners at the head of these attacks. Lakeshire's garrison cannot risk acting on rumors or partial victories, so Marshal Marris demands proof that Tharil'zun is dead. His severed head shows that the Outrunners' coordinated ambushes from the keep have suffered a major blow.

item:tharnariun-s-hope.text: Tharnariun's Hope. In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender seeks a way to study the sick thistle bears and find a cure. His trap calms them long enough to bring them to his camp. Tharnariun Treetender made a calming trap to study the sick thistle bears. Across Darkshore, a mysterious affliction has left the animals increasingly frenzied and violent. Tharnariun hopes to cure them rather than see them killed. Set on the ground, Tharnariun's Hope casts a soothing light. A rabid thistle bear that crosses it grows calm for a time and can follow a traveler back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

item:the-book-of-ur.text: The Book of Ur. Ur's book now lies in Shadowfang Keep, where Archmage Arugal found it before Forsaken scholars in the Undercity took interest. The Dalaran mage wrote of strange beings from other planes. Ur was a Dalaran mage known for studying other planes and their creatures. Before the Scourge came, the Kirin Tor knew his work well. Ur was fascinated by magic beyond this world, yet he chose to write down his findings instead of breaking through the veil recklessly. Caution and restraint shaped his research. When the Scourge attacked Dalaran, neither his magic nor his care could save him.

item:the-collector-s-schedule.text:
The Collector's Schedule. Near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, The Collector's Schedule marks the passage of illicit gold shipments through Elwynn Forest. Gnolls carry its handwritten itinerary, and Marshal Dughan recognizes the name it records. Gold still leaves Elwynn's mines on a schedule, though Stormwind has not officially worked them for months. Banditry and creature incursions drove the miners away. The itinerary names the days and hours when a figure called The Collector receives each shipment.

The trail leads to a camp near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn Forest. Marshal Dughan recognizes the Collector's name when he sees the schedule. Who pays for the stolen gold remains unknown.

item:the-embalmer-s-heart.text: The Embalmer's Heart. In Duskwood, Eliza's buried corpse holds a heart that still beats. The Embalmer placed his own heart in his dead wife through dark magic, and it became the anchor of his power. Darkshire's tales remember the Embalmer as a gentle alchemist. When his wife Eliza died, grief shattered his mind. He turned to foul sorcery, cut out his own heart, and placed it in her lifeless chest. The magic stirred her corpse to unlife, but the return twisted Eliza into a ravenous creature with an insatiable hunger for living human flesh. Horrified by what he had done, the alchemist buried her again.

item:the-general-s-response.text: The General's Response. In Lakeshire, General Marcus Jonathan answers a plea for aid as Redridge faces danger. His dispatch acknowledges Magistrate Solomon’s appeal against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, but sends no immediate reinforcements from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon asks Stormwind City for troops to defend Redridge from gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands. General Marcus Jonathan replies that he has sent the plea to the throne, but no soldiers are coming now. He orders the letter returned to Lakeshire. Solomon is troubled by the delay and suspects something is wrong with Stormwind’s leaders.

item:the-lich-s-spellbook.text: The Lich's Spellbook. On Brightwater Lake's island, a spellbook draws Bethor Iceshard's attention. He hopes its pages will reveal the lich's skill and who he was in life. A free-willed lich guards an island in Brightwater Lake with skeletal minions. He distrusts the outside world and mistakes other undead for Scourge thralls, ordering his guardians to kill anyone who approaches. Bethor Iceshard seeks skilled necromancers for the Forsaken beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. He sends an emissary into the island camp to take the lich's spellbook. Bethor hopes its pages will reveal the master's power and identity before death took Lordaeron.

item:the-state-of-lakeshire.text: The State of Lakeshire. In Lakeshire, Magistrate Solomon's report calls for help before the town falls. It urges General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind to send royal army reinforcements against the crisis in Redridge. Magistrate Solomon writes of the attacks threatening Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls press the town, whose defenders cannot hold the borders indefinitely. Couriers carry his dispatch west along the road to Elwynn Forest. Solomon asks the Stormwind Army to intervene and protect the kingdom's eastern reach. General Marcus Jonathan receives Solomon's report at Stormwind's gates. He respects the magistrate's standing and understands the danger, but cannot move the army on his own. Deployments need the crown's consent, so Lakeshire's plea must wait for a council with the young King and regent Bolvar Fordragon.

item:theramore-medal.text: Theramore Medal. At Northwatch Hold, Theramore Medal marks service among the marines and officers defending the outpost along the Merchant Coast. The insignia bears Theramore’s mark and identifies the Alliance garrison. Marines, marksmen, commandos, and officers serving from Northwatch Hold carry stamped medals bearing Theramore’s mark. The soldiers are loyal to Lady Jaina Proudmoore’s realm. For the human troops on the cliffs above the Barrens, the medals show that their service is legitimate and their authority comes from Theramore. Others see the tokens as trophies from an overzealous foreign garrison, one that treats every vessel approaching the coast as a mortal threat. Northwatch Hold’s gun batteries menace ships along the Merchant Coast, often bombarding privateers and merchantmen alike. After losing ships to the guns, Ratchet privateer Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun seeks the medals. He wants proof that Northwatch’s trigger-happy ranks have paid in blood for sinking his ships, and that the soldiers responsible have been slain in retribution.

item:thick-bear-fur.text: Thick Bear Fur. In Dun Morogh, Thick Bear Fur helps travelers and soldiers endure the mountain cold. Bears roam the snowfields, and their pelts make insulated clothing and bedding. Bears roam Dun Morogh's ridges through some of the harshest snowfields in the Eastern Kingdoms. Their thick coats shield them from blizzards, and locals and travelers put the pelts to use. Hunters gather them to line clothing, insulate drafty outposts, and pad cold sleeping rolls. Pilot Bellowfiz outfitted his siege tank, Jetsteam, at Steelgrill's Depot for a month in the field on a long mission for the Siege Brigade. Cold iron offered little comfort in the high snowbanks, so he hired local scouts to gather thick bear fur from the snowfields south of the Grizzled Den. The pelts would make warm bedding for his cabin quarters.

item:thistlenettle-s-badge.text: Thistlenettle's Badge. Foreman Thistlenettle's badge is all that remains after the collapse in the Deadmines. Before the Defias Brotherhood sealed Moonbrook and the tunnels beneath it, dwarven prospectors from Ironforge's Explorers' League worked the old gold mines of Westfall. Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew were deep underground when a tunnel collapsed and split them apart. His brother Wilder escaped to Stormwind City, but the foreman and several laborers were left trapped below.

item:thresher-eye.text: Thresher Eye. Along Darkshore, Wizbang Cranktoggle wants Thresher Eyes for his Buzzboxes. He uses them to repair Buzzbox 411 on the beach north of Auberdine. Darkshore Threshers hunt the surf and outer shallows off Darkshore. They threaten local fishermen and travelers, and their large eyes have caught the interest of Wizbang Cranktoggle. The gnome engineer is stationed nearby and fond of crawler wine. He needs the eyes to repair Buzzbox 411, a far-speaking communication machine on the beach north of Auberdine. Wizbang does not explain how the slimy eyes repair delicate machinery. They might serve as crude lenses, chemical agents, or biological gears. Whatever the method, three eyes placed in Buzzbox 411's maintenance hatch restore its communication link, and Wizbang sends supplies through static-choked transmissions.

item:thule-s-head.text: Thule's Head. At the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec demands proof that Thule Ravenclaw is dead. His severed head confirms the commander of the Scourge forces on Fenris Isle has fallen and helps the Forsaken hold Silverpine Forest.

item:thunder-lizard-blood.text: Thunder Lizard Blood. In the southern Barrens, hunters bring back Thunder Lizard Blood as proof of survival. The blood comes from the great beasts that roam the plains. Thunder lizards go by the names Stormsnouts, Stormhides, and Thunderheads across the plains. Their heavy steps shake the earth, and their crushing weight can flatten unwary hunters. Bringing back their blood shows the skill to hunt them and the endurance to survive beneath their thundering feet.

item:thunder-lizard-horn.text: Thunder Lizard Horn. In the Barrens, Brewmaster Drohn seeks a Thunder Lizard Horn for Chen Stormstout's legendary brew. Thunder lizards roam the Barrens, their crested bodies crackling with lightning. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet values their horns as an ingredient for Stormstout ale. His mentor learned the recipe from the wandering pandaren Brewmaster Chen Stormstout and passed it down to Drohn. The horn gives the drink its potent kick.

item:thunderhawk-saliva-gland.text: Thunderhawk Saliva Gland. Across the Barrens, greater thunderhawks yield a gland prized by Brewmaster Drohn. He needs it to recreate Chen Stormstout's fiery Trogg Ale. Greater thunderhawks hunt across the Barrens' arid savannas. These winged serpents are known for harnessing storms, and the older, more dangerous ones produce a saliva gland charged with natural potency. Travelers keep clear of the deadly beasts, but brewmasters value the gland as a rare base for exotic drinks. Brewmaster Drohn settled outside Ratchet after Chen Stormstout traveled through Kalimdor. Drohn studies the wandering brewmaster's fermentation methods and needs a fresh thunderhawk saliva gland, stormhide lightning glands, and kodo liver to brew Trogg Ale. The fiery spirit has an unmistakable kick and is meant to fortify hardy adventurers.

item:thunderhawk-wings.text: Thunderhawk Wings. Across the central and southern Barrens, hunters claim Thunderhawk Wings from the wind serpents that soar overhead. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer receives them as proof of a hunter’s strength, cunning, and endurance. Hunters stationed at Camp Taurajo prize a pair of intact Thunderhawk Wings. Wind serpents, whom local hunters call thunderhawks, are fierce winged reptiles that strike swiftly from above. Tracking them across the open plains and claiming their wings in combat tests a hunter’s skill. For an initiate, bringing back the wings proves readiness to follow the lifelong path of an accomplished hunter.

item:thunderhorn-cleansing-totem.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. Mull Thunderhorn prepares the Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem in Bloodhoof Village. Ancestral magic in the totem is meant to purify the Thunderhorn Water Well. Mull Thunderhorn entrusts a prepared totem to travelers in Bloodhoof Village. They carry it north to the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring, where foul agents have tainted the water. The ancestral wells dug by the tauren tribes nourish their herds and hunting grounds. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the water's disturbed spirits and cleanses the site.

item:thurman-s-remains.text: Thurman's Remains. At Agamand Mills, Thurman's remains bear witness to the family's failed stand against the Scourge. The once-wealthy mill owner fell to the Plague and now wanders his ruined estate as an undead thrall. Before the Third War, the Agamands were Tirisfal Glades' wealthiest landowners, with extensive mills and dozens of local workers. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, Thurman Agamand and his kin fortified their estate instead of fleeing. Certain their wealth and strong mills could withstand the attack, they persuaded their loyal workers to take up arms beside them. The defense failed. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered and made mindless servants of the Lich King. Coleman Farthing, a former worker who rose as Forsaken, now demands the destruction of his former masters. He seeks Thurman's remains as proof that the foolish patriarch paid for dooming his household.

item:thurman-s-sewing-kit.text: Thurman's Sewing Kit. At Larson Clothiers, Thurman's Sewing Kit is needed for the day's tailoring. Young apprentice Thurman Schneider left it at his family's home by the Canals, hoping to spend the day at leisure. Thurman's Sewing Kit holds the needles, shears, and thread he needs for tailoring. Young Thurman studies at Larson Clothiers, deep in Stormwind's Mage Quarter near the Mage Tower. His mother, Rema Schneider, knows he cannot work without the kit. So she asks passersby along the Canals to carry it to the shop. When Thurman gets his tools, his reaction reveals he left them behind on purpose. He hoped to trade a day of stitching garments for leisure.

item:timberling-seed.text: Timberling Seed. Across Teldrassil, Timberling Seeds are gathered from plant spirits that have grown hostile. Naturalists and druids study them to learn why the forest's plant life has turned aggressive. Timberlings are nature elementals of Teldrassil, and their temper reflects the World Tree's balance. Lately they have grown hostile and angry, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists such as Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth suspect trouble in the soil. They gather seeds from wild timberlings, hoping that purified, carefully tended soil might let docile offspring sprout.

item:timberling-sprout.text: Timberling Sprout. Along Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts take root already touched by corruption. Night elf wardens pull them before they grow into aggressive timberlings. Timberlings are plant spirits bound to Teldrassil's natural vitality. Along Lake Al'Ameth, the night elves find seedlings that sprout tainted and aggressive instead of healthy and in harmony with the wild. The young sprouts seem beyond cleansing or natural healing, so the caretakers gather and destroy them. They hope to stop hostile timberlings from spreading across the fragile boughs of the newly planted World Tree.

item:tirisfal-pumpkin.text: Tirisfal Pumpkin. At Solliden Farmstead, living humans still tend pumpkins in blighted Tirisfal. The Forsaken take them for the Royal Apothecary Society’s mixtures. West of Brill, crops still grow despite the corruption spreading across Lordaeron. At Solliden Farmstead, living human farmers work the soil and grow large orange pumpkins under the watch of the nearby Scarlet Crusade. The harvest feeds these farmers. To the Forsaken of Brill, the pumpkins are targets for sabotage and raw materials for Apothecary Johaan. Deathguard Simmer sends young Forsaken into the contested fields to steal pumpkins from under the farmers’ noses. The vegetables do not feed the dead; they go into the Royal Apothecary Society’s cauldrons. Apothecaries test how natural plants react to plagues and experimental mixtures, using Lordaeron’s remaining crops against the living.

item:token-of-thievery.text: Token of Thievery. In the Redridge Mountains, rogues face a test set by Lucius at Alther's Mill. A locked footlocker holds the Token of Thievery, proof of skill recovered during their training. In Lakeshire, Lucius tests promising rogues in the field. He hides the Token of Thievery in a locked footlocker among the ruins of Alther's Mill, where Blackrock orcs threaten the area. Recovering it tests whether an initiate can pick a lock under mortal danger. Success earns a Certificate of Thievery.

item:tome-of-the-cabal-quest-item.text: Tome of the Cabal (quest item). Warlocks in Ratchet receive the Tome of the Cabal from Strahad Farsan after gathering dangerous components. Its pages hold the incantations for drawing a felhunter across the Twisting Nether and binding it. A felhunter is a vicious beast from the chaotic Twisting Nether, feared for devouring mana. Subduing one marks a passage for seasoned warlocks. The Tome of the Cabal holds the rites for opening a path to such a demon. Strahad Farsan, an experienced conjurer in Ratchet, gives the tome to an aspirant only after they gather the rare and dangerous components its magic requires. Strahad Farsan establishes the primary summoning circle in his sanctum, while his acolytes use rods of channeling to form a greater protective boundary. The warlock recites the tome's exact incantations and drags the felhunter into our world. The demon must be battled at once and subdued, binding it to the warlock's will.

item:top-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Top of Gelkak's Key. A giant foreststrider carries the Top of Gelkak's Key into the woods near Darkshore. It is one of three broken pieces of a mechanical key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome Gelkak Gyromast. Threshadons attacked Gelkak Gyromast's ship off Darkshore and sent it beneath the waves. The gnome washed ashore with the winding key for his mechanical first mate. The impact against the coastal rocks broke it into three pieces. Before the dizzy pirate could gather his wits, beasts scavenged the wreckage. A giant foreststrider carried the ornate upper piece into the woods.

item:torch-of-the-dormant-flame.text: Torch of the Dormant Flame. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, a shaman prepares to kindle the Torch of the Dormant Flame. The unlit torch waits for a fire spirit's ember, earned on a mountaintop in Durotar. A shaman seeking fire's favor carries the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame up the peaks above Durotar. Fire sapta lets the shaman see a Minor Manifestation of Fire on the mountaintop and challenge it. When the spirit falls, its glowing ember goes into the weathered brazier at the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. The shaman touches the torch's head to the white-hot blaze, and the wood awakens as a burning emblem of elemental mastery.

item:torn-fin-eye.text: Torn Fin Eye. Along Hillsbrad's coast, Torn Fin Eyes draw the Royal Apothecary Society's attention. The Forsaken seek them for alchemical work on new plagues. The Royal Apothecary Society puts rare biological components to use in its work on the Forsaken's New Plague. Torn Fin Eyes come from murlocs along the Western Strand of Hillsbrad Foothills. Their organic properties help activate volatile alchemical compounds. Mixed with Daggerspine naga scales, restorative troll elixirs, and gnoll-derived sludge, the eyes help stabilize and trigger toxic mixtures meant to spread death through enemy lands.

item:torn-murloc-fin.text: Torn Murloc Fin. Along eastern Elwynn's waterways, murlocs crowd the banks and the Stormwind Army's bounty is being answered. Murlocs have grown numerous along eastern Elwynn's streams and lakes. So the Stormwind Army offers a bounty to thin their numbers. Guard Thomas watches the bridge over the eastern river and gathers severed fins as proof. With soldiers stretched thin by unrest at home and nearby threats, local authorities rely on travelers to show that murloc camps have been cleared.

item:totem-of-hawkwind.text: Totem of Hawkwind. At Camp Narache, young tauren receive the Totem of Hawkwind before departing for Bloodhoof Village. They present it to Baine Bloodhoof as proof that they have completed their first trials and are ready to continue the Rites of the Earthmother. Chief Hawkwind carves the Totem of Hawkwind atop Red Cloud Mesa for youth coming of age. The token introduces its bearer and proves their passage. Tauren rarely use formal writ; meaningful symbols and familiar tribal craft carry a leader's intent. After a youth completes the first trials at Camp Narache, Hawkwind sends them onward with the totem, along the road into the wider lands of Mulgore. Its distinct carvings identify the bearer to Baine Bloodhoof and show they have the spirit and strength for the next trials, on the way to seeking the blessing of Thunder Bluff.

item:tough-wolf-meat.text:
Tough Wolf Meat. In Northshire and Coldridge, wolves prowl their valleys and provide meat for hungry locals. Tough Wolf Meat is coarse and stringy. People in Elwynn Forest eat it, and dwarven outfitters in Dun Morogh use it to stock their supplies. Wolves prowl near Northshire Valley and Dun Morogh. They threaten nearby settlements, yet their meat offers a hard-won source of food. Coarse, stringy and chewy, it is prized by resource-strapped frontiersmen.

Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner hates the vicious beasts but cooks their meat into steaks. He trades basic supplies and gear to those who cull the packs.

item:tourmaline-phial.text: Tourmaline Phial. At the Pools of Arlithrien, the Tourmaline Phial gathers blessed moonwell water for Teldrassil's rituals. Corithras Moonrage gives the Tourmaline Phial to travelers for rituals that tend the World Tree. Druids in Dolanaar use gemstone vials to collect pure moonwell water across Teldrassil. This phial is meant for the moonwell beside the Pools of Arlithrien, southeast of the road to Darnassus, where hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs are growing more troublesome.

item:toxic-fogger.text: Toxic Fogger. In Stonetalon, the Toxic Fogger is bound for the Venture Company's air routes. The Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society filled the device with lethal poison to contaminate the company's flights. Apothecary Zamah sends the Toxic Fogger against the Venture Company's mining work. Apothecary Lydon brewed its toxin in Tarren Mill, and Zamah dispatched it from Thunder Bluff. She suspects the goblins use courier flying machines to carry messages and light cargo between Stonetalon and their headquarters. Her plan is to release the poison where those machines land and refuel. The Forsaken aim to strike the company's supply route instead of fighting its mercenary crews in drawn-out skirmishes.

item:treshala-s-pendant.text: Treshala's Pendant. In Razorfen Kraul, a pendant carries the bond between Treshala and Heralath Fallowbrook. Heralath brought it from their home in Darnassus into southern Kalimdor, where the quilboar tore it from him as he lay dying. Heralath Fallowbrook carried the pendant close when he left Teldrassil on perilous journeys. The necklace reminded him of home and of his beloved wife, Treshala, and the devotion they shared.

item:trogg-stone-tooth.text: Trogg Stone Tooth. In Loch Modan's hills, Stonesplinter troggs leave rugged, mineralized teeth behind. Dwarven defenders use each tooth as proof that the troggs are being hunted along the southern frontier. Captain Rugelfuss calls for volunteers to hunt Stonesplinter troggs near Loch Modan's southern gate. With the Ironforge Reserve committed to the Alliance Front, local dwarven garrisons are stretched thin across Khaz Modan. Rugelfuss cannot spare the soldiers at the southern gate guard tower to patrol the nearby hills. So volunteers hunt the lurking troggs and bring back Trogg Stone Teeth as crude, undeniable proof of each beast slain.

item:troll-charm.text: Troll Charm. In Ashenvale, Troll Charms have been taken from fallen Darkspear travelers. The Thistlefur furbolgs seized the sacred amulets after ambushing the party on its way to Zoram'gar Outpost. Darkspear trolls carry spiritual charms as marks of dignity. Scout Mitsuwa says a troll without one is as diminished as an orc without battle scars. A party of Darkspear kin traveled through Ashenvale's canopy toward Zoram'gar Outpost when corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs ambushed and slaughtered them. Their spirits were commended to the afterlife, while the furbolgs took the charms as trophies and stashed them in chests deep within Thistlefur Hold.

item:trophy-swoop-quill.text: Trophy Swoop Quill. Across Mulgore, swoops circle above the plains, and their quills mark a hunter’s skill. Tauren bring these feathers to Harken Windtotem in Bloodhoof Village. Swoops ride high above Mulgore’s grasslands, where they are hard to track. Young tauren hunters and travelers in Bloodhoof Village seek a trophy quill to prove their cleverness and resolve. Bringing one to elders such as Harken Windtotem honors the hunter’s clan and shows the sharp senses needed to thrive on the plains.

item:twilight-pendant.text: Twilight Pendant. In Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight Pendants mark the cultists who serve the Twilight's Hammer. The Argent Dawn seeks them as proof of the cult's work along Ashenvale's coast. Beneath the drowned ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, the Twilight's Hammer gathers with the naga to honor the chaotic Old Gods. Shadowmages, aquamancers, reavers, and loreseekers all wear Twilight Pendants as signs of devotion to their shadowy patrons. The cult keeps to the ruins of the former night elf temple, so these pendants offer outsiders one of the few ways to learn how many cultists gather there and hinder their plans. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus seeks Twilight Pendants as evidence that the growing darkness is being driven back. Blackfathom Deeps once held a pristine moonwell, and its desecration by void-worshipers threatens Kalimdor. Gathering the pendants shows that the Twilight's Hammer foothold in Ashenvale is being dismantled before its patrons can unleash greater terror.

item:twilight-whisker.text: Twilight Whisker. In Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil gathers Twilight Whisker for his brew. Twilight runners carry the whiskers in the northern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Twilight runners prowl the high crags near Stonetalon Peak. Hunters prize their pelts, while Witch Doctor Jin'Zil of Malaka'jin wants their stiff whiskers for a darker purpose. He seeks vengeance on night elves captured after defending these woodlands. To mock and poison his captives, Jin'Zil gathers resinous sap, countless eyes, fey dragon scales, and Twilight Whisker for a lethal draught he calls forest magic.

item:twitching-antenna.text: Twitching Antenna. In the southern Barrens, silithid antennae still twitch after they are cut free. Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo seeks them as proof of a young warrior’s speed and skill in combat before the nerves go still. Silithid Grubs, Swarmers, Harvesters, and Creepers carry antennae that twitch after they are cut from the head. The spasms fade soon after the insects are slain. A young warrior must hunt silithid in the southern wastes and hurry back across the scrublands while the antennae still twitch. Bringing them back in time tests both speed and skill, making the hunt a rite of passage for Horde warriors. The silithid antennae also point to a threat that troubles Camp Taurajo’s hunters. Silithid are not native to the Barrens, and their new burrowing mounds at the Field of Giants unsettle the camp. Ruga Ragetotem wants the specimens to study the danger and prepare Horde warriors for the alien menace moving into the plains.

item:ukor-s-burden.text: Ukor's Burden. At the Valley of Trials, Ukor's food is turned away, and he needs help bringing it back to Razor Hill. Ukor, an orc peon, rarely acts on his own, but he carried provisions from the inn in Razor Hill to help young recruits in the Valley of Trials. The journey led him through Durotar's red dust and dangerous wildlife. The overseers and instructors refused the food, believing hardship and hunger make true warriors. Now Ukor waits outside the canyon's mouth, afraid of the beasts along the trail back. He has entrusted the sack to passing travelers, asking them to return it to Innkeeper Grosk.

item:uncloven-satyr-hoof.text: Uncloven Satyr Hoof. In Ashenvale, satyrs gorge themselves on the ancient forest’s magic. Their swollen hooves hold the power they steal, and Ula'elek uses it to forge armor in Sen'jin Village. Satyrs haunt the corrupted groves of northeastern Ashenvale, feeding on the ancient forest’s magical purity. The more they consume, the more corruption distorts their demonic bodies. Their hooves swell and lose their natural cleft, becoming dense stores of absorbed energy. Skilled shamans and leatherworkers can harvest that volatile power. At Sen'jin Village on Durotar’s coast, the troll armorer Ula'elek turns demonic corruption into strength for Horde champions. He takes hooves from satyrs that have fed on the forest and draws out their trapped magic. Then he channels that stolen power into brutal gauntlets, armor for young warriors facing the rigors of Kalimdor.

item:underbelly-whelp-scale.text: Underbelly Whelp Scale. South of Lake Everstill, Underbelly Whelp Scale trades hands among Redridge craftsmen. Black dragon whelps provide the pliable scales, and local artisans value them when coin is scarce. Black dragons bear tough scales, but facing a full-grown one is deadly for ordinary folk. South of Lake Everstill, black dragon whelps nest among the crags. Their back plates can be brittle or coarse, while the softer scales beneath their bellies bend more readily and still offer protection. Those qualities make Underbelly Whelp Scale valuable in local trade. Craftsmen prize it, and creditors can accept it in place of coin. In Lakeshire, craftsmen sometimes barter when coin runs short or trade routes are strained. Verner Osgood, the local blacksmith, owes a heavy debt to Argus, a blacksmith in Goldshire. The debt began with a shipment of shoes brought in from Goldshire. Argus favors rare trade goods, so Verner depends on travelers to gather underbelly whelp scales. They can help settle what he owes and keep his workshop in good standing.

item:unidentified-ore.text: Unidentified Ore. At Windshear Crag, Unidentified Ore draws the Venture Company's attention. Piznik recovered a sample and passed it to Ziz Fizziks for study in Undermine. The Venture Company's clear-cutting and strip mining at Windshear Crag exposed unusual mineral strata in the Stonetalon Mountains. The site's new boss, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, ordered large amounts of strange gold-green ore mined. Demoted goblin worker Piznik remained loyal to his fired former boss, Ziz Fizziks, and secured a sample while plotting his exit from the outfit. He handed it to a traveler bound for the crag's western ridge. Ziz planned to send most of the ore to Undermine for study and keep a small cut for personal profit.

item:unrefined-ore-sample.text: Unrefined Ore Sample. In Thousand Needles, an unusual ore draws the Horde's attention. Tatternack Steelforge seeks a sample to judge whether the raw mineral can strengthen the weapons of Warchief Thrall's armies. South of the Barrens, Gravelsnout kobolds dig through the stone beneath the canyon walls of Thousand Needles. Travelers returning north found a curious mineral among slain vermin, unlike the usual veins of Kalimdor. They refused to surrender their prize to the Horde. The kobolds who dig and survey the depths carry raw chunks of the ore from their excavations. At Camp Taurajo, weaponsmith Tatternack Steelforge works under orders from Warchief Thrall to improve the Horde's arms. Travelers who kept knowledge of the deposit angered him; he saw their refusal as an insult to the Horde's war effort. With a raw sample, Tatternack plans to test the mineral's strength and temper, then smelt it and forge a prototype blade for Orgrimmar's approval.

item:ur-s-treatise-on-shadow-magic.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Stormwind's mages once guarded Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic, fearing what its pages could bring. Now the tome lies hidden in the Tower of Ilgalar, stolen by Morganth. Ur of Dalaran wrote of shadow magic and its subtle, corruptive nature. The mages of Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum feared these arts could bring doom to the unwary, so they sealed the volume against readers. After Morganth gave himself to dark arts and Stormwind's magical circle exiled him, he carried the tome east into the Redridge Mountains. There he made his stronghold in the Tower of Ilgalar.

item:urgent-message.text: Urgent Message. The Urgent Message is a sealed dispatch penned by Brave Moonhorn warning Freewind Post of escalating centaur violence across Thousand Needles. Carried by travelers descending into the canyon, the letter alerts the tauren garrison that their supply lines and scouting parties are under immediate threat. Penned by Brave Moonhorn near the great lift that descends from the Barrens into Thousand Needles, the Urgent Message represents the first line of defense for travelers crossing the border. Moonhorn monitors the jagged canyons below, where aggressive centaur tribes have renewed their relentless raids against Horde travel. Addressed to Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post, the missive sounds the alarm about emboldened attackers striking dangerously close to crucial roadways, urging the local garrison to brace for sustained conflict and guard against secondary threats like the unpredictable Grimtotem clan.

item:valdred-s-hands.text: Valdred's Hands. In southern Silverpine Forest, Valdred Moray's severed hands become proof of Raleigh Andrean's vengeance for his wife's murder. Raleigh seeks them in the Undercity as a grim trophy. The plague consumed Lordaeron and ended the friendship between Valdred Moray and Raleigh Andrean. Valdred had murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. Raleigh died and rose as one of the Forsaken, claiming he could no longer truly grieve. Yet he still wanted vengeance. When Valdred fled south past the Greymane Wall toward Gilneas, Raleigh sent an emissary after his former friend. He demanded Valdred's severed hands as proof that the deed was done.

item:velinde-s-journal.text: Velinde's Journal. Velinde Starsong's personal journal records her duties and the mystery of her departure from Darnassus. The Night Elf priestess's journal is stored in the Sentinel bunkhouse. When Night Elf priestess Velinde Starsong left Darnassus, her belongings were locked in a footlocker at the Sentinels' bunkhouse in the Tradesmen's Terrace. Among them was her personal journal, a record of her responsibilities and duties. The Sentinels respected Velinde and believed she had left to attend to private matters. Her journal's contents suggest her unexplained absence is more troubling than they first believed.

item:velinde-s-key.text: Velinde's Key. In Darnassus, Velinde's Key guards the writings of a vanished priestess. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver entrusts it to those who bring proof of their interest in Velinde Starsong's fate. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps Velinde's Key in Darnassus. The simple key secures Priestess Velinde Starsong's personal belongings in a footlocker in the Sentinel bunkhouse above the Tradesmen's Terrace. Velinde left night elf lands without warning, and her possessions were set aside. Bladeweaver gives the key only to those who bring genuine evidence of their interest in learning her fate, such as revelations found in the Tome of Mel'Thandris.

item:venomtail-antidote.text: Venomtail Antidote. In Durotar, Venomtail Antidote is urgently needed to save a scout from scorpid poison. Kor'ghan brews the remedy in Orgrimmar for Rhinag, who lies stricken near Durotar's northwestern border. Durotar's venomtail scorpids can kill a warrior within an hour of a deep sting. Rhinag, a troll scout, was envenomed near the northwestern border, far from aid. His only chance is a remedy from Kor'ghan, an apothecary in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Finding Kor'ghan means making your way beneath Orgrimmar. He knows desert toxins and harsh remedies, and prepares a vial to purge the venom before it turns fatal. The draught stops the poison and spares Rhinag a humiliating death in the wilderness. Kor'ghan still demands further trials and hunts from the scout to atone for his carelessness.

item:venomtail-poison-sac.text: Venomtail Poison Sac. In Durotar, a scorpion’s venom can bring a hunter near death, while its poison sac holds what alchemists need to make a cure. Scorpids roam Durotar’s red rocks, including Venomtail Scorpids, Corrupted Scorpids, and the Death Flayer. Their tail sacs hold a fast-acting venom that can overwhelm even seasoned warriors if left untreated. The same sacs contain the primary compounds alchemists need to make an antidote. When a scorpion stung the hunter Rhinag outside Orgrimmar, local alchemists needed four fresh poison sacs to make a remedy and neutralize the venom in his veins.

item:venture-co-documents.text: Venture Co. Documents. In eastern Mulgore, Venture Co. Documents confirm illegal strip-mining in tauren lands. The papers were recovered from a crate amid a ruined caravan and detail the company's operations. Venture Co. Documents were found atop mined ore in a ransacked wagon. The ledgers show the goblin-led cartel has quietly established drilling and mining outposts in Mulgore's eastern foothills. Across Kalimdor, the Venture Company is known for ruthless deforestation and uncontrolled excavation. Morin Cloudstalker and the tauren Outrunners use the seized records to judge the threat to their sacred ancestral plains and rally hunters to drive out the trespassers.

item:venture-co-engineering-plans.text: Venture Co. Engineering Plans. At Windshear Crag, the Venture Co. Engineering Plans reveal how the logging machinery is built. Alliance operatives recover the schematics from the goblin mill. Inside the lumber mill south of Cragpool Lake, the Venture Co. Engineering Plans show the construction, strengths, and flaws of the timber-harvesting machines. The Venture Company uses those machines to strip the forests of Stonetalon, while smoke hangs over Windshear Crag.

item:venture-co-letters.text: Venture Co. Letters. At Windshear Mine, Venture Co. Letters carry word of the cartel's work in Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered amid explosive distractions, they give the night elf Sentinels intelligence on goblin operations. Venture Company machines cut timber and strip-mine the ancient woodland around Windshear Crag. Alliance operatives set off covert sabotage to distract the workers and enter Windshear Mine. The letters they recover hold private messages and logistical records of the company's local work. Sentinel leaders can learn how the defilers arrange their workforce and supply lines from those records.

item:verdant-note.text: Verdant Note. In Camp Narache, Verdant Note calls young tauren druids to begin their training. Sent for Gart Mistrunner, it guides them toward the rites of the Earthmother. Young tauren with a gift for nature receive Verdant Note soon after their trials begin in the Red Cloud Mesa. A messenger carries Gart Mistrunner's brief summons to Camp Narache, where the initiate must report to the mentor. Restless spirits and shifting elements trouble Mulgore, and the elders need new druids trained quickly. Gart Mistrunner teaches initiates to commune with nature. He warns that night elves share a bond with the wild but keep their distance from tauren, guarded by ancient pride. Tauren druidism centers on reverence for the Earthmother. Initiates learn to hear the land's restless ancestral voices and serve as her living instruments.

item:verdant-sigil.text: Verdant Sigil. In Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives young night elf druids the Verdant Sigil as a summons to begin training. Young night elves in Shadowglen who feel the call of the wild receive the Verdant Sigil from Conservator Ilthalaine. A messenger brings it from Mardant Strongoak, the druid trainer, and it directs novices to climb into Aldrassil's boughs. The token invites them to leave basic chores behind and begin serious study of communion with nature spirits and the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Presenting the Verdant Sigil to Mardant Strongoak begins a young druid's lifelong craft. Novices are not yet ready to walk the sleeping trance of the Emerald Dream, but the token marks the start of their mentorship. Under Mardant's instruction, they learn to read the wilderness's whispers and practice early shapeshifting and healing arts in service of Teldrassil.

item:verna-s-westfall-stew-recipe.text:
Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe. As the Furlbrows prepare to leave their Westfall farm, Verna sends her stew recipe to Salma Saldean. Its familiar comfort may remain for those who stay. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow have made their home in Westfall for years. Now the Defias Brotherhood and rogue harvest golems run rampant across the countryside. The Furlbrows wait for their wagon to be repaired so they can flee toward Stormwind.

While they wait, Verna writes down her beloved Westfall Stew formula. She entrusts it to travelers bound for her neighboring friend, Salma Saldean. That way, those left behind may still know the stew's familiar comfort.

item:verner-s-note.text: Verner's Note. In Redridge, Verner Osgood sends a written requisition west to Smith Argus in Goldshire. It describes Lakeshire’s iron shortage and asks the Elwynn smith for horseshoes. Lakeshire’s defense has consumed nearly all of Verner Osgood’s iron. The town’s blacksmith has used his reserves to arm and armor the Stormwind Guard, who are stretched thin against invading gnolls and local perils. Meanwhile, Lakeshire’s stables have fallen into neglect, without even basic horseshoes for their mounts. Verner asks Smith Argus in Goldshire to send prepared shoes from Elwynn, so the town can shoe its horses.

item:verog-s-head.text: Verog's Head. Regthar Deathgate seeks Verog's Head as proof of the Kolkar leader's death. The chieftain commands forces around the Stagnant Oasis, and his defeat is meant to weaken the tribes threatening the Barrens. The Kolkar centaur threaten Horde travelers and supply routes across the northern Barrens. Verog the Dervish roams the arid scrubland, leaving his command tent at the Stagnant Oasis vulnerable. Horde operatives attack his forces around the pavilion until an alarm sounds. Verog rushes back to defend his camp, where he is slain and decapitated. Regthar Deathgate receives his head as proof that another dangerous Kolkar chieftain has fallen. Barak Kodobane's head is already on display beside it.

item:vial-of-innocent-blood.text: Vial of Innocent Blood. Syndicate shadow mages gather Vial of Innocent Blood in the ruins of Durnholde Keep. The Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill seeks it as a catalyst for experimental toxins. Syndicate shadow mages gather innocent blood in the ruins of Durnholde Keep. The Syndicate's fallen human nobles practice dark arts within the crumbled walls. Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill wants untainted blood for an experimental pacifying agent. He means to use it against the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, and sees the Syndicate's stores as a convenient source.

item:vial-of-phlogiston.text: Vial of Phlogiston. At Razorfen Kraul, phlogiston draws smiths from the Alliance and Horde. Master armorers use it to temper mail for promising warriors, while quilboar guard it in their stronghold. Phlogiston bears volatile fire and has a place in esoteric metalwork. Furen Longbeard, a dwarven smith in Stormwind, needs it, as does Thun'grim Firegaze, a near-blind orc armorer in the Barrens. Both use it to harden warrior armor beyond ordinary physical limits. Without this alchemical agent, neither can complete the specialized forging of Fire Hardened Mail or the Horde's Brutal Armor.
