A vial of phlogiston lies deep in Razorfen Kraul, amid the tangled thickets at the southern tip of the Barrens. The geomancer Roogug holds it in the bristling redoubt. Whether it is bound for Furen in Stormwind or for Thun'grim's anvil across the dust, reaching it means a perilous descent into hostile quilboar territory.

item:vial-of-purest-water.text: Vial of Purest Water. In the southern Barrens, Brine blesses a vial of pure water for a shaman initiate. Its contents help Islen Waterseer prepare a water sapta for seeing elemental spirits. Brine guides the initiate through trials of patience and cleansing before sealing the water in the vial. The water holds an uncorrupted elemental purity. Carry it across the Barrens to Islen Waterseer, who keeps watch on a solitary shore. She needs it to brew a water sapta. Without such pure water, a shaman cannot commune with spiritual guardians in places far from the sunbaked flats.

item:vial-of-spider-venom.text: Vial of Spider Venom. In Duskwood, spiders carry venom that Madame Eva needs for a protective ward. She gathers it with undead remains to make a Totem of Infliction. Duskwood's thickets shelter venomous spiders, from pygmy venom webs and green recluses to black widows and Naraxis. Their fangs carry poison potent enough to paralyze travelers and decay flesh. Those who kill the spiders can draw the fluid into intact vials. In Darkshire, fortune teller Madame Eva sees ominous portents for travelers setting out into the dark world. She needs five vials of spider venom, ghoul fangs, and skeleton fingers to craft a ward of retribution. Her craft turns the venom’s biting nature against attackers, making the Totem of Infliction return harm to anyone who strikes its bearer.

item:vicious-night-web-spider-venom.text: Vicious Night Web Spider Venom. In eastern Tirisfal, Vicious Night Web Spider Venom carries an old contagion. The Royal Apothecary Society prizes it for holding historical disease strains, and uses it in work on the Forsaken's New Plague. Apothecary Johaan in Brill studies old texts about a plague that killed thousands. The contagion behind that outbreak endured for centuries inside the venom of local Night Web spiders. Apothecaries hunt the vicious breed in Venomweb Vale, south of the Scarlet Monastery, and draw out the preserved contagion for their alchemical experiments.

item:vile-familiar-head.text: Vile Familiar Head. Near the Burning Blade Coven, Vile Familiar Heads mark a grim test for young Horde warlocks. Under Ruzan's guidance, they gather the gruesome trophies as proof of readiness to bind their first demonic minions. The test demands discipline and respect for the lethality of the beings they mean to summon. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Ruzan asks novices seeking to learn summoning to bring him six Vile Familiar Heads. Vile familiars are fiery imps with dangerous elemental cunning, found outside the Burning Blade Coven. Novices must face and defeat them, proving they can subdue demonic life rather than be overcome by it. Warlocks are barely tolerated within Thrall's Horde, so their training calls for care. A novice slain by a conjured creature only deepens the dishonor and suspicion cast upon practitioners of the dark arts.

item:vile-fin-scale.text: Vile Fin Scale. Vile Fin Scale comes from murloc tribes prowling Tirisfal’s northern coasts and waterways. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society studies these samples as it works on a plague meant to strike the living and the Scourge. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks a blight that can spread through the living and the Scourge. Simple toxins are easy to brew, but an infectious disease needs properties that help it pass from one population to another. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan studies Vile Fin scales for their natural resilience and mucous coatings. He hopes these traits can help stabilize his experimental contagions and carry them onward. The Vile Fin tribe inhabits Tirisfal Glades’ northern shores and western shallows, where its members threaten travelers and press into Forsaken territory. Gathering their scales helps keep the feral murloc populations in check and supplies Johaan’s laboratory with fresh organic material for tests in biological warfare.

item:voodoo-charm.text: Voodoo Charm. In Teldrassil’s barrows, the Voodoo Charm can break the Gnarlpine enchantment holding Oben Rageclaw’s body.

item:wailing-essence.text: Wailing Essence. Wailing Essence is a strange, concentrated substance found within the ectoplasms roaming deep inside the Wailing Caverns. Suspected of fueling the bizarre mutations spreading through the flora and fauna of the Barrens, it has drawn the attention of opportunistic alchemists eager to bottle its potent properties. The subterranean caverns beneath the central Barrens have grown thick with unnatural energy, warping beasts and giving rise to gelatinous ectoplasms. These oozing creatures concentrate a viscous substance known as Wailing Essence. While local druids observe these waters with growing dread, goblin entrepreneurs see only raw commercial opportunity. In the port town of Ratchet, an eccentric alchemist named Mebok Mizzyrix believes this essence is the missing active ingredient for a line of lucrative 'smart drinks' meant to enhance consumer intellect, utterly unconcerned with the nightmarish corruption it might actually harbor.

item:warsong-axe-shipment.text: Warsong Axe Shipment. At Booty Bay, the Warsong Axe Shipment waits for its voyage to Ashenvale. The newly forged axes are bound for the Warsong Outriders and the work at their lumber camp. Axes for the Warsong Lumber Camp wait in Booty Bay. The camp’s woodcutters need a steady supply of durable tools, and not every tool can be forged on the front lines. Orders cross the Great Sea to this neutral goblin port, where the crate is stored near Wharfmaster Lozgil. The sharpened axes are meant for Splintertree Post, where they can be sent onward to the camp. Keeping distant frontier camps supplied takes a long journey across the sea.

item:warsong-oil.text: Warsong Oil. At the Warsong Lumber Camp, Warsong Oil keeps the logging machinery running. A satyr ambush has carried a shipment into corrupted forest enclaves. Warsong Oil keeps the Warsong Clan's logging machinery running in Ashenvale. Goblin-engineered shredders and massive sawmills need a steady supply of the lubricant. Without it, timber cutting could halt, slowing the lumber needed to build Orgrimmar and fortify Horde settlements across Durotar and the Barrens. Satyrs ambushed a shipment of Warsong Oil before it could reach Splintertree Post and the logging camps. They carried the containers into corrupted enclaves, including Night Run, Satyrnaar, and Xavian, where they use the flammable lubricant in their rituals.

item:warsong-outrider-update.text:
Warsong Outrider Update. Along Ashenvale’s eastern border, a Warsong Outrider prepares the Warsong Outrider Update. Stationed there, the outrider records frontline intelligence for Horde couriers to carry. The reports help secure the crossing toward Azshara and strengthen the orcish foothold against night elf resistance. Beyond Splintertree Post, the eastern road crosses Ashenvale’s volatile borderlands toward the ancient ruins of Azshara. Mounted orcish vanguards patrol this frontier and record tactical sightings, patrol movements, and resource evaluations.

They send their field notes to Kadrak at the northern watchtower, which guards the Barrens border. The reports give Horde commanders a clear view of enemy troop concentrations and territorial threats beneath the forest canopy.

item:warsong-runner-update.text: Warsong Runner Update. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Warsong Runner Update carries reports from western Ashenvale to Kadrak. The Warsong runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches the coast and nearby threats in western Ashenvale. The dispatch records observations gathered by scouts at the outpost and reports on local activity. It travels to Kadrak's watchtower on the Barrens border, helping Horde leaders strengthen their position and plan their movements into the elves' ancestral woods.

item:warsong-saw-blades.text: Warsong Saw Blades. Warsong Saw Blades keep the Horde's lumber machinery cutting in Ashenvale. The Warsong Clan relies on goblin-made machines for its logging, and these blades supply its clear-cutting work. In Ashenvale, the Warsong Clan's logging depends on heavy machinery supplied and maintained by goblin engineers. Axes alone cannot meet the Horde's demand for Kalimdor lumber, so steam engines and circular saws cut through raw timber. Ashenvale's ancient hardwood quickly dulls and breaks ordinary blades. Replacement saw blades must keep arriving for the mills at the Warsong Lumber Camp to keep running. Getting mechanical parts through disputed territory brings constant trouble. Hostile furbolgs and satyrs often intercept other logging supplies, while goblin contacts such as Pixel at Splintertree Post handle the saw blade shipments. Lumber master Locke Okarr gathers the blades with rope, oil, and axes to keep the camp operating despite sabotage from Ashenvale's defenders.

item:warsong-scout-update.text: Warsong Scout Update. At Splintertree Post, a Warsong scout records what the Horde needs to know about Ashenvale. Warsong scouts watch the woods as the Horde seeks timber and supply routes through Ashenvale. From Splintertree Post, a fortified encampment, they track night elf sentinels and movements across the territory. Their observations reach Kadrak at the Barrens-Ashenvale border among routine orders. He uses them to judge troop readiness and coordinate supplies and travel through the contested woods.

item:water-of-the-seers.text: Water of the Seers. In Bloodhoof Village, young tauren drink the sacred Water of the Seers before their tribal trials. The draught opens the mind to the spirit world and summons a Plains Vision to guide them. Young tauren drink the Water of the Seers before the tribal fire in Bloodhoof Village. Tribal mystics prepare the draught for the ancient Rite of Vision. It opens the drinker’s spiritual sight, and the Plains Vision appears from the embers to guide the way to Seer Wiserunner.

item:water-pitcher.text: Water Pitcher. At Red Cloud Mesa, Water Pitcher carries fresh spring water from the local well to Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks young tauren to bring it back as a lesson in humility, service, and respect for tribal elders. Water Pitcher rests beside the well southeast of Camp Narache. Greatmother Hawkwind asks a novice to fill it and carry it to Chief Hawkwind. The chore tests their character and teaches young braves that no duty is beneath a tribal protector. Caring for the everyday needs of their kin matters as much as wielding a weapon on the hunt.

item:webwood-egg.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowthread Cave, Webwood Eggs lie in nests in Shadowglen. Naturalists seek viable eggs so they can study the young spiders in secure laboratories. A grown Webwood spider is venomous and too dangerous for one researcher to tame or subdue. So scholars like Gilshalan Windwalker collect unhatched eggs from clutches hidden in Shadowthread Cave. The eggs can be carried safely, and the spiderlings kept contained when they hatch. Naturalists can study them without facing the deadly fangs of adult spiders. Teldrassil’s native wildlife has grown unnaturally aggressive and corrupted, alarming scholars across the boughs. Eggs and gathered venoms secured at Aldrassil are bound for Darnassus. Researchers hope that raising and examining the spiders in controlled settings will reveal more about the dark affliction spreading through the World Tree’s boughs.

item:webwood-ichor.text: Webwood Ichor. In Shadowglen, Webwood spiders carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine needs their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to brew an antidote. Webwood spiders in Shadowglen carry venom that has left Iverron gravely ill. Dirania Silvershine asks for their ichor, hyacinth mushrooms, and moonpetal lilies to prepare an antidote.

item:webwood-spider-silk.text: Webwood Spider Silk. Webwood Spider Silk is gathered from Webwood Lurkers in the woods of Teldrassil. Crafters use spider silk in many ways, but these swatches draw the interest of suspicious figures among the World Tree’s boughs. Webwood Lurkers around Dolanaar spin a fine, strong thread that is dangerous to gather. Zenn Foulhoof, a satyr along the forest road, asks young adventurers to collect the silk with nightsaber fangs and strigid owl feathers. He says these rare reagents are needed for his forest business, and newcomers gather them without asking about his corrupt nature or true motives.

item:webwood-venom-sac.text: Webwood Venom Sac. In Shadowglen, Webwood Venom Sacs draw the attention of naturalists studying Teldrassil's growth. The sacs come from overgrown spiders, and their venom may show how the new World Tree has changed local wildlife. Webwood spiders live around and within Shadowthread Cave, and they are cousins to a much smaller breed found elsewhere. Their sudden growth and predatory aggression worry night elf researchers. Naturalists such as Gilshalan Windwalker study the venom in their sacs, examining its strength and composition. They hope to learn how Teldrassil's rapid, unblessed growth is changing the creatures that live on its boughs.

item:well-stone.text: Well Stone. Across Mulgore, Well Stones rest beside the water wells. Their earth and water magic helps prepare the Water of the Seers for tauren rites of passage. Well Stones rest in the soft earth beside Mulgore’s wells, where they absorb the spiritual resonance of the plains and the waters beneath them. Shaman and seers such as Zarlman Two-Moons know these stones as vessels of vital magic, not ordinary river pebbles. Combined with grounded Ambercorn beneath the plains’ mighty trees, their mineral properties temper the brew that awakens visionary trances in young tauren during the sacred Rite of Vision.

item:wendigo-mane.text: Wendigo Mane. Across Dun Morogh, wendigos roam the frozen crags, and their manes keep the mountain cold at bay. Pilot Stonegear has a use for them. Wendigos roam the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, their coarse fur guarding them from bitter drafts. Outside Kharanos, Pilot Stonegear sends adventurers to Grizzled Den for their heavy manes. He means to weave them into an insulating rug for the interior deck of Trollplow, his prized dwarven siege engine.

item:whitestone-oak-lumber.text: Whitestone Oak Lumber. Beneath Moonbrook, the Defias shape Whitestone Oak Lumber for their fleet. Its strength also draws Alliance smiths seeking a haft for a sacred weapon.

item:wildmane-cleansing-totem.text: Wildmane Cleansing Totem. At Mulgore’s Wildmane Water Well, one last cleansing remains. Mull Thunderhorn prepares a totem for the northern well after the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are cleansed. The Wildmane Water Well still needs cleansing. Goblin ventures have poisoned the land and fouled Mulgore’s scarce water, so the tauren turn to sacred ritual against the blight. After the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are cleansed, Mull Thunderhorn crafts a final totem for the well north of Thunder Bluff. Infused with natural spirits, it purifies the fetid water so life can nourish the plains again.

item:wiley-s-note.text: Wiley's Note. At Lakeshire, Wiley the Black writes a confidential note for Gryan Stoutmantle to repay a debt. Its contents point to alliances made by the Defias Brotherhood, drawing Stormwind's intelligence service into the inquiry. Wiley the Black, a rogue in Lakeshire, writes the dispatch in Redridge. He gives it to Gryan Stoutmantle to repay an old favor. In the note, Wiley tells what he knows of the Defias Brotherhood's plans. The Brotherhood has allies among regional gnolls, kobolds, and goblin operatives.

item:william-s-shipment.text: William's Shipment. In Goldshire, William's Shipment is bound for his brother Morgan in Stormwind, carrying candles from Elwynn's kobolds. William Pestle keeps trade moving between Goldshire and the capital. He gathers goods in Elwynn Forest, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot leave his duties to travel north, so couriers carry the wax and candles into the city. Kobold candles from Elwynn's mines fill William's shipment. He gathers the large candles for their wax and packs them for Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary. That wax joins the stock used in the capital's alchemical trade.

item:wine-ticket.text: Wine Ticket. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws customers to his family's shop with Wine Tickets. Present one to Suzetta Gallina for a complimentary bottle of Pinot Noir. Near Stormwind's Trade District, Renato Gallina hands out printed tickets to promote the Gallina Winery. The boutique vintage shop sits along the nearby canals. Each ticket offers a complimentary sample of Pinot Noir, drawing curious passersby and newly arrived adventurers to the family business in hope they become loyal customers.

item:winterhoof-cleansing-totem.text: Winterhoof Cleansing Totem. At Winterhoof Water Well, Venture Company poisons the water beneath Mulgore's plains. Mull Thunderhorn crafts a totem to cleanse it. Mull Thunderhorn crafts the Winterhoof Cleansing Totem in Bloodhoof Village. Venture Company goblins have tainted Mulgore's underground water with their operations. Mull imbues the carved wood with protective magic meant to wash away the foreign poisons. Carried past hostile goblin guards to Winterhoof Water Well, the totem channels a focused ritual that disperses the contamination. Pure drinking water returns for the plains' wandering herds and native tribes.

item:witchwing-talon.text: Witchwing Talon. In the northwestern Barrens, Witchwing Talons mark dead harpy raiders. Horde scouts at the Crossroads seek them as proof while they work to secure vital caravan routes. Witchwing harpies raid Horde supply caravans from their roosts northwest of the Crossroads. Scout Darsok Swiftdagger coordinates strikes against the flock's hierarchy. Darsok requires physical proof of each dead scavenger, and the talons provide it. With proof that raiders have fallen, the scouts can weaken the flock's ranks before striking higher in its command.

item:wolf-heart-sample.text: Wolf Heart Sample. Wolf Heart Sample is bound for the Crossroads, carrying diseased wolf tissue from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. The Royal Apothecary Society seeks to learn what northern toxins do to the Barrens’ native beasts. Wolf Heart Sample began with plagued wolves in Lordaeron’s ruins. Apothecary Renferrel gathered the hearts, and they were packed for the journey across the Great Sea. The Forsaken’s Royal Apothecary Society seeks greater knowledge of venom, blights, and biological reagents. A courier carries the parcel to the Crossroads in the Barrens, linking Undercity’s experiments in the scarred Eastern Kingdoms with Kalimdor’s frontier outposts. At the Crossroads, Apothecary Helbrim receives Wolf Heart Sample. Helbrim studies how toxins from Lordaeron’s Scourge-ravaged lands affect the native wildlife of Kalimdor. The toxicity preserved in the wolf hearts may reveal properties that can improve Forsaken poisons and elixirs far from home.

item:wolf-heart-samples.text: Wolf Heart Samples. In Silverpine Forest, wolf hearts hold a poison their living hosts endure. Apothecary Renferrel sends samples to the Royal Apothecary Society, whose members study them. Apothecary Renferrel found a deadly compound in certain wolf hearts while examining carcasses in Silverpine Forest. The poison saturates the tissue at a level that should kill the wolves, yet they live. Renferrel set tissue samples aside for delivery to Undercity. The Forsaken study organisms that withstand toxins as they seek to master biological warfare and prepare new reagents. Couriers carry the samples beneath the ruins of Lordaeron to Apothecary Zinge at the Royal Apothecary Society's headquarters in the Apothecarium. Zinge and her colleagues prize new toxins. They dissect and test the tainted tissue to isolate its virulent compounds and learn how the beasts survive them, hoping to use that knowledge in their alchemical work.

item:wood-pulp.text: Wood Pulp. At Bael Modan, Wood Pulp helps the dwarves prepare their blasting charges. The dwarven personnel stationed in the southern Barrens carry it as an absorbent base for stabilizing liquid explosives. At Bael Modan, Ironforge dwarves use earth-moving equipment and chemical explosives to tear into ancestral tauren hunting grounds. Liquid nitroglycerin is unstable on its own, so dwarven engineers soak it into porous wood pulp with sodium nitrate to make stable charges for excavation and combat. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers carry bundles for sapping and field munitions.

item:wooden-key.text: Wooden Key. In northern Ashenvale, the Wooden Key rests in the hands of maddened ancients near Felwood’s border. It opens a concealed chest with a remnant of Dartol's Rod. Crazed and Withered Ancients carry the Wooden Key along the shaded trails north of Raynewood Retreat. Shael'dryn once knew the local treants, but now says corruption has twisted their nature. One carries the key to a chest holding a piece of Dartol's Rod.

item:worn-parchment.text: Worn Parchment. At the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, Worn Parchment scraps offer clues to the cultists gathered there. North along Darkshore’s mist-shrouded coast, dark spellcasters and their followers have seized the ruined Tower of Althalaxx. Dark Strand Fanatics patrol the grounds outside and carry scraps of worn parchment among their belongings. One scrap holds only scattered writing and strange symbols. Gathered together, the fragments reveal a previously unknown organization called the Cult of the Dark Strand.

item:worn-stone-token.text: Worn Stone Token. Across the Alterac Mountains, Worn Stone Token enchantments have faded, though Dalaran crafted them to command elementals. The tokens remain with Dalaran personnel, from mages to laborers. Dalaran’s magi command elementals with talismans that bend beings from other realms to their will. Worn Stone Tokens are depleted versions of these implements. Theurgists and summoners carry them, as do Dalaran laborers and guards stationed around the ruins and internment camps of Alterac. Their presence shows how deeply elemental binding reaches into Dalaran’s daily work. At Tarren Mill, the Forsaken watch the nearby wizards. Magus Voidglare seeks Worn Stone Tokens to study Dalaran’s methods of enslaving elementals. Keeper Bel'varil directs agents to gather worn, inert tokens first. These let the Magus examine basic enchanting techniques safely before attempting more potent, volatile conduits.

item:woven-wand.text: Woven Wand. In the Undercity, the Woven Wand has returned to Bethor Iceshard. Three Dalaran apprentices made it as a pledge of brotherhood, before betrayal and the fall of Lordaeron scattered them.

item:xavian-water-sample.text: Xavian Water Sample. At Xavian, ancient waters hold arcane power sought by Horde mages in Orgrimmar. They seek it to unravel the latent magic preserved in Ashenvale's oldest sacred sites. Xavian was a fabled ancient elven city, and its old knowledge remains known among the learned. Even in ruin, its waters are said to hold great magical power. Deino, an arcane instructor in Orgrimmar, sends rising mages deep into Ashenvale to draw fresh water from the pool beneath Xavian's tallest waterfall. They must cross dangerous ground, for corrupt satyrs now guard the ruins fiercely and oppose spellcasters who meddle there.

item:young-crocolisk-skin.text: Young Crocolisk Skin. In the Wetlands, young crocolisks provide hides for trade from Menethil Harbor. Their softer skins are cured by local tanner James Halloran and shipped to distant ports. Menethil Harbor sends marsh goods to distant ports from the western coast of Khaz Modan. The town’s resident tanner, James Halloran, cures hides among its most lucrative exports. Full-grown crocolisks have thick, tough scales, while their young provide softer leather that is easier to work. The delicate skins are in high demand, so Halloran depends on local hunters and passing travelers to search the boggy marshes just outside town and keep his curing racks stocked.

item:yowler-s-paw.text: Yowler's Paw. In Lakeshire, Yowler's Paw is brought to Verner Osgood as proof the feared gnoll leader is dead. Yowler leads the packs menacing the hills above Lakeshire. Yowler leads the Redridge gnolls that terrorize the heights around Lake Everstill, their howls reaching Lakeshire. He is feared above all, a ruthless alpha driving the packs' expansion. Verner Osgood asks brave adventurers to bring him Yowler's paw, the customary proof of a bounty across human territories. Taking the paw marks the death of an unusually cunning predator and a blow against the chain of command among his disorganized followers. Yowler's Paw points to the danger facing Lakeshire. The Stormwind Army is consumed by the Blackrock orc threat entrenched around Stonewatch Keep, leaving civil authorities and townspeople to hire passing mercenaries for defense. Without regular royal garrisons, settlers such as Verner Osgood rely on proof that threats have been dealt with to keep local roads marginally safe for trade and travel.

item:zalazane-s-head.text: Zalazane's Head. Master Gadrin awaits proof that Zalazane has fallen. The Darkspear seek relief from the witch doctor who drove them from the Echo Isles. Master Gadrin asks for proof that Zalazane is dead. The witch doctor betrayed the Darkspear and seized control of their island home with mind-enslaving hexes. His magic drove Vol'jin's people to the shores of Durotar. From the Echo Isles, Zalazane still sends hexed thralls across the water to seize more victims. Sen'jin Village needs proof that his rule has ended. Returning Zalazane's severed head confirms his defeat and gives the displaced tribe a measure of peace, with hope of reclaiming their stolen islands one day.

item:zamah-s-note.text: Zamah's Note. Zamah's Note carries an urgent plea from Thunder Bluff to Tarren Mill. Zamah asks Apothecary Lydon for an alchemical way to drive the Venture Company from Stonetalon without direct bloodshed. The Venture Company has dug deep into the Stonetalon Mountains, felling trees and tearing up sacred land. Zamah wants a way to force the goblins out without slaughter. She turns to the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society for help. Her note tells her colleague, Apothecary Lydon, about the danger in Stonetalon. Lydon is in Tarren Mill, far away in the Hillsbrad Foothills of Lordaeron. The sealed note must cross continents to reach Lydon. Travelers from Kalimdor take a zeppelin to the Undercity, then travel south through Silverpine Forest into Hillsbrad. Lydon is intrigued by Zamah's specific request. Word has reached him from across the ocean, and he prepares an alchemical answer to the goblin problem.

item:zargh-s-meats.text: Zargh's Meats. At the Crossroads, Zargh prepares fresh meat for Gryshka in Orgrimmar. The parcel gives young Horde travelers a reason to learn the wind rider route. Zargh, an orc butcher and hunter at the Crossroads in the Barrens, prepares fresh cuts for Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The heat across the savannas can spoil fresh game quickly, so the parcel goes with couriers bound for the Crossroads roost. Wind Rider Master Devrak arranges a wyvern flight to Orgrimmar's Skytower, sparing travelers the long overland journey through Durotar. Zargh's delivery carries a personal sentiment along with its provisions. When Gryshka receives the meat, she recognizes Zargh's knack for winning a lady's favor with quality game. She is eager to prepare the cuts for the inn's patrons and guests. For newly arrived orc and troll travelers, the delivery offers an introduction to long-distance flight between Kalimdor's Horde settlements.

item:zhevra-hooves.text: Zhevra Hooves. Across the Barrens, zhevras graze in the open savannah. Their hooves prove a hunter can face swift, powerful prey. Zhevras graze across the Barrens, but their compact, muscular legs can strike hard. Sergra Darkthorn, the orc shaman in charge of the Crossroads, sends aspiring Horde scouts to gather hooves from zhevra runners. The hunt sharpens a fledgling hunter's instincts and resilience. A panicked runner can kick even a sturdy tauren flat. Intact hooves show a hunter can handle swift, kicking quarry before taking on Kalimdor's deadliest predators.
